# 0. Current state (V32 — 2026-11-04)

> **Read this section first.** Everything below §1 is a *dated record*: each pass wrote its audit, its
> implementation log and its gaps, and those sections are deliberately never rewritten — an audit that gets
> edited after the fact stops being evidence. The consequence is that the oldest sections describe the
> oldest product. §1's executive summary is the **2026-09-28** snapshot and says so; by V17 several of its
> statements (the API port, the payment provider, what the mobile apps can do) were simply no longer true of
> the running system. This section is the current answer to "what is Hangyul Univ today", and it is the one
> a new engineer should trust when it disagrees with anything earlier.

## 0.1 What it is

Hangyul Univ helps an international student get from "could I study in Korea?" to enrolled: discovery and
eligibility matching, applications, document preparation and review, essay/study-plan review, visa
preparation, housing and arrival. Students buy one-time plans; partner agencies do the counselling work in
their own console; partner universities see their applicant pipeline in theirs. **Hangyul never collects
tuition** — Korean MOE guidance requires it be paid by the student, in their own name, to the university.

## 0.2 Ports and processes (current)

| Process | Port | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| FastAPI API | **8001** | `npm run dev:api`. **V18 moved this from 8000**, which the owner's brief set as the intended port. Health: `GET /healthz` |
| Marketing site | 3100 | React 19 + Vite 7 |
| Student web | 3101 | also the payment-return origin (`toss_return_origin`) |
| Agency console | 3102 | |
| University console | 3103 | |
| PostgreSQL 16 | 5432 | native, not Docker |
| Redis | 6379 | native |

The Student, Agency and University apps proxy `/api` to the API same-origin, so auth cookies stay first-party; the
marketing site needs no API at all since §435 (static export + the Vercel fit function, §0.2a). Any document, script
or comment still naming `:8000` for the Hangyul API is stale; V18 migrated the dev scripts, the Vite proxy,
Playwright, the e2e helpers, the QA gates, the three Expo configs and the mobile bootstrap, and verified the
API answering on 8001.

## 0.2a Production deployment (V32 — current)

| Surface | Where | State |
|---|---|---|
| `univ.talkhangyul.com` | Vercel project `hangyul-univ` (apps/marketing-web) | **Live, fully public without any API**: directory, 425 university pages, scholarships, Quick Fit and the fit summary read a static export (`apps/marketing-web/public/data/public/`, `scripts/public-data/export.py`); Quick Fit's ranking runs the unchanged `server/app/services/fit.py` as a Vercel Python function (`apps/marketing-web/api/public-fit.py`, §435) |
| `app.` / `admin.` / `partner.univ.talkhangyul.com` | Vercel projects `hangyul-univ-{student,agency,university}` | Static builds live; `/api/*` rewrites to `https://api.univ.talkhangyul.com`, **which the owner has deferred** — until it exists the three apps show the localized service-unavailable state (§436), never demo data |
| Private API (FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, S3, ClamAV, workers) | — | **Not provisioned, by owner decision** (`docs/deployment/VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT.md`) |

Every production build emits `/build-info.json` (commit, built-at) so a stale deploy is visible from a browser. Per-app
`vercel.json` is generated (`scripts/ops/gen-vercel.mjs`) from `infra/csp.json`. `npm run qa:marketing-serverless` checks a
deployed marketing site end to end (local 23/23, production 22/22 at the last verification).

## 0.3 Products

**Four web products.** Marketing, Student, Agency Console, University Console — React 19, Vite 7, one
FastAPI API over PostgreSQL 16.

**Three native products (Expo SDK 57, React Native 0.86, expo-router), all on the V22 model since V23.**
`apps/student-mobile` — discovery and university detail, saved, matching, applications, documents with upload, messages,
notifications, visa, tasks, plan/services (checkout hands off to the web), housing and arrival (open the web page in the
student's language), profile, settings and language, and the verified four-step **sign-up** (§267). The student is served by
**한귤 유니브 상담팀** ("with {agency}" under it, as on the web). `apps/agency-mobile` — 오늘 · 학생 · 지원·서류 · 메시지 · 설정,
one role. `apps/university-mobile` — 지원자 · 메시지 · 현황 · 설정, one role. Staff apps use the V22 white/tangerine tokens.
**No build of any app carries a test sign-in, persona picker or `EXPO_PUBLIC_TEST_LOGIN` switch — V32 removed the
feature rather than hiding it** (§436); when the API cannot be reached the apps show the localized service-unavailable
state. The six V25 Android artifacts in `result/<app>-mobile/android/` predate V32 and are superseded: store binaries must be
rebuilt from the V32 source (V32 verified the Expo production exports leak-clean and ran the apps on the `hg35` emulator
through Metro). **iOS: not built** — EAS is not authenticated (`docs/qa/v23/IOS_BUILD_BLOCKER.md`). Full essay editing
remains web-only (§180).

## 0.3d What V26 changed (summary — §330–§352)

V26 was a forensic pass before it was an implementation pass: §330 reads V1–V25 as a defect history and names **29 root
causes** (`docs/qa/v26/ROOT_CAUSE_MATRIX.md`), each fixed at its cause and each with a gate. The product changes a user sees:

- **Every link lands on the record it names.** Agency TODAY items and rows carry `focus=<kind>:<id>` (request, reply, thread,
  document, essay, application, task, compose); the workspace opens the tab, scrolls, marks the record and focuses the
  composer. Student tasks and notifications open the exact requirement or document. University headline figures open the
  rows they count; the applicants list sorts decision-first by default (web and native).
- **Explore is grouped by university** with the fit facts first and the degree sentence said once; a 240-px tile per group.
  **Services** shows "지금 진행 중" — what is active, who acts next, and the one next action — before the plan matrix.
- **Copy**: a Korean particle post-processor (`을/를`, `이/가`, `은/는`, `과/와`, `으로/로`) ends the "{{doc}}을(를)" form everywhere;
  server action codes and client strings share one vocabulary; 50 new strings in all 33 locales (machine-drafted).
- **Design system**: the version-layer stylesheets (9/9/8/5 files) are gone — one canonical file per surface, 91 dead
  declarations removed; tangerine appears only on the primary action, the current item and focus (census 51 → 0 stray
  fills); every control meets the 24-px target size; `[data-focus]` is one shared rule.
- **Performance and correctness at scale**: the agency console at 1,071 students — TODAY figures 11.7 s → 0.3–0.6 s, ranked
  queue 2.9 s → < 1 s, an unknown filter value 500 → 422; CLS 0.671 → 0 on university pages, 0.16 → 0.01 on the applicants
  list; **RC-29**: a build rule keyed on file paths had silently stopped purging the marketing stylesheet (dev ≠ prod for
  nineteen releases) — fixed at source, entry CSS 246 KB.
- **QA hygiene** (V32: stronger — the development database holds reference data and **zero members**; fixtures exist only in test/e2e databases, `qa:v32-data-clean`): no test residue in development data, no future-dated history,
  the lint scope restored, the V21 payment check asserts its precondition, the e2e stack owns its upload directory.
- **Repository**: 7.75 GB of superseded evidence, build output, duplicate media and probes removed by a scripted, manifested
  cleanup (§350); the final logs in `docs/qa/v26/completion/logs/` come from the post-cleanup runs.
- Gate: `npm run qa:v26` (static · api · rendered, 91 checks) plus `qa:v26-scale`, `qa:v26-census`, `qa:v26-css`.

## 0.3a Identity, roles and tenancy (current — V22)

**Registration** is a four-step verified flow (Account → Verify → Consent → Complete). An account exists only after
the last step: both an **email one-time code** (Twilio SendGrid) and a **mobile one-time code** (Twilio Programmable
Messaging, Messaging Service, E.164 storage) have been entered, the password has been confirmed, a Cloudflare
**Turnstile** proof has been verified server-side (mandatory in production; production refuses to boot without the
keys), and the **granular consents** — [필수] 이용약관 · [필수] 개인정보 수집·이용 · [필수] 본인확인 국외 처리 고지 ·
[선택] 소식 수신 — have been recorded with version, locale, hashed IP, user agent and source. Rate limits (Redis) cover
register, login (progressive: CAPTCHA at 5 failures, growing delay at 20, never a permanent lock), forgot-password and
every OTP send/verify. Changing a verified email or phone requires a fresh code. §244, §253–§254, §263.

**One permission per tenant.** Partner agencies have exactly one role, `AGENCY_ADMIN`; university tenants exactly
one, `UNIVERSITY_ADMIN`. Several people may hold it; they all see and do the same things. The former
`AGENCY_OWNER/MANAGER/COUNSELOR/DOCUMENT_REVIEWER` and `UNIVERSITY_ADMISSIONS/REVIEWER/ANALYST` were migrated in place
(alembic `v22roles0001`) and survive only as enum aliases. Hangyul's own `HANGYUL_*` roles are unchanged. Hangyul
assigns university accounts to their university from `/hq/accounts`; a university admin never sees another
university (404 policy, re-tested in §258). §246–§247, §257–§258.

**Display identity ≠ audit actor.** A student is served by **한귤 유니브 상담팀 / Hangyul Univ team**: every staff
author in messages, essay comments, review history and the home card renders as that one identity; the real
`author_user_id` stays on every row and agency/HQ views show the real people. §246 A3, §257.

**Providers.** SendGrid, Twilio and Turnstile are configured only through server environment variables
(`SENDGRID_API_KEY`, `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_API_KEY_SID`, `TWILIO_API_KEY_SECRET`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`,
`TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID`, `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`, `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`, with or without the `HG_` prefix).
**As of 2026-10-23 none of these values is present on this development host**, so the live delivery smoke is
BLOCKED and development runs the "console" delivery mode (codes readable only through a dev-only route). §255.

**Legal.** `/privacy` now publishes three processors (Twilio Programmable Messaging, Twilio SendGrid, Cloudflare
Turnstile — all United States) with the 개인정보 보호법 제28조의8② transfer items; `/terms` 제9조 renders the statutory
refund rights from a canonical refund-policy model whose commercial schedule is `OWNER_POLICY_REQUIRED`; the checkout
records a versioned `PURCHASE_TERMS` consent. The legal pages are still **not production-ready** for the reasons in
§256.2 (identity fields, retention, refund schedule). §245, §256.

**Consoles.** White surface, hairline borders, ink text, tangerine only for the current/selected step and the primary
action; light menus everywhere (no navy). Agency: 오늘 · 학생 관리 · 지원·서류 · 메시지 · 통계 · 설정, home = clickable
process strip + work table. University: 지원자 · 메시지 · 통계 · 설정, home = clickable pipeline strip + applicant
table, analytics by four questions. Student: six-stage journey strip, one next action, team identity. §259–§261.

**University directory (V25).** 425 institutions; **166 with a real photograph of their own campus** (462 university photographs,
all with rights metadata, JPEG + WebP renditions and focal points), 3 led by an official film whose poster is a campus scene, 256
by a designed identity composition (4 with the institution's mark). See §320. *(V23 text, kept for history: 151 photographs,
79 film-led, 192 identity.)*

## 0.4 Payments (current)

One-time plan purchases — **Basic $179 / All-in-One $349 / Premium $599** — **never a subscription**. V29: plus
add-on orders (same card state machine); upgrades refused until an owner pricing rule exists (§401).

> **V19 corrected this paragraph.** It read "베이직 249,000 / 올인원 499,000 / 프리미엄 849,000 KRW" until
> this pass, and that had not been true of the product since V17 priced the plans in USD. The brief flagged
> the inconsistency; the audit found it was **documentation drift, not a product defect**. The single source
> of truth, `packages/types/src/plans.ts` → `shared/plans.json`, already carried `USD 17900 / 34900 / 59900`
> minor units, the API serves those, and the student's `/services` page renders `US$179 / US$349 / US$599`.
> Nothing was repriced; this prose was corrected to match the product (§199, §209).
>
> **Commercial price and live-payment readiness are two different things, and must not be read as one.**
> The public price is USD. Live USD checkout is **off**: `GET /me/payments/config` returns
> `env: "test"`, `live_usd_checkout_enabled: false` and all four readiness flags false. A student who
> reaches the pay button is told so in their own language — "해외카드 USD 결제가 아직 활성화되지 않았어요.
> 다른 통화로 청구하지 않습니다" — rather than being silently charged in KRW. Verified live this pass.
**How a plan is bought (V21, current).** `POST /me/orders` → Hangyul's **own** card form (card number and expiry only) →
`POST /me/orders/{id}/pay-with-card` → the server calls Toss Payments `/v1/payments/key-in` on the **`bill_talkoab1`**
foreign-card merchant (USD), with an order-derived idempotency key and 8 attempts / 300 s per student and IP. Nothing card-
related is stored except, if the student saves the card, the issuer and masked number Toss returns. *(Earlier text here
said only `HANGYUL` buys a plan and that a `bill_*` config must never be wired to one — V21 measured otherwise and reversed
it; this paragraph had not been updated until V23.)*

Merchant reality: four owner-provided Toss **test** configs; payments stay in **test mode** by agreement. Live keys, card
review and the overseas-card USD contract are owner/Toss items. The development paid-state bypass that earlier passes
documented here was removed in V32 (§436): a paid state for a test or e2e database is granted only by the fixture tooling
(`server/scripts/fixture_pay.py`, `app.seed.fixtures.grant_plan` / `pay_order`), which refuses any database whose name is
not a test/e2e one. Secrets live only in `server/.env`.

**Native payment is web-handled, by design (unchanged in V18).** The app opens the student web checkout in
the system browser and returns by deep link; there is one backend payment state machine and the Toss SDK is
not in the app bundle.

# 1. Executive summary

**What it is.** Hangyul Univ is a platform that helps international students study at Korean universities — from "which universities are realistic for me?" through documents, application, admission, visa, arrival and student life. It is operated by Hangyul (a Korean company whose brand is the tangerine "한결" BI) and connects four parties:

```
Student  →  Hangyul Univ (platform + data layer)  →  Partner study-abroad agency  →  Partner Korean university
```

**Business model.**
- Students: free explorer tier; paid service packages (Application Support, Premium Success) that include document review, application workflow and — for Premium — an assigned partner-agency counselor. Prices are stored in the database per region; payments run through a provider abstraction (demo provider in development; Stripe/Toss adapters exist but are not enabled).
- Universities: partnership contracts (recruitment fees / commissions / incentive tiers), seat quotas and co-funded "Hangyul Partner Scholarship" pools; in exchange they receive a pipeline of prepared applicants plus post-admission outcome data (visa, arrival, retention, graduation) by cohort, agency and nationality.
- Agencies: receive qualified, paid, documented cases matched to their specialties; work them in the Agency Console under SLA.
- Tuition is **never** collected by Hangyul (Korean MOE guidance: tuition paid in the student's own name to the university).

**Target users.** International students (Vietnam, China, Uzbekistan, Mongolia, Nepal, Myanmar, … — 14 nationalities in demo data), study-abroad agency counselors/managers/reviewers, Korean university international-admissions officers/analysts/management, Hangyul operations/finance.

**Four web products** (React 19 + Vite 7): Marketing site (:3100), Student platform (:3101), Agency Console (:3102), University Console (:3103), all backed by one FastAPI API over PostgreSQL 16. *(The API ran on :8000 at audit time; V18 moved it to **:8001** — see §0.2.)*

**Mobile products.** Three Expo (SDK 57, React Native 0.86, expo-router) native apps — Student, Agency, University — each a focused subset of its web counterpart (no document upload, onboarding or essay editing on mobile). *(Audit-time. The student app gained document upload before V17 and offline support in V18; see §0.3.)*

**Implementation status at audit time (2026-09-28).** Functionally broad and technically solid: 69 DB tables, ~120 endpoints, a real state machine, explainable matching, legalization (apostille/consular) routing, a task engine, tenant isolation, audit logging, 24 pytest + 93 vitest + 12 Playwright tests passing, 45 locales scaffolded (en/ko reviewed). Every screen renders without console errors or horizontal overflow at 390/768/1440.

**Strengths.**
- Honest data model: every time-sensitive fact carries `source_url`, `verified_at`, `verification_status`; demo data is labelled; match tiers instead of fake admission probabilities; analytics refuse to show rates with n < 5.
- Real workflow depth: document vault reused across applications, per-application checklists with plain-language actions (UPLOAD / FIX / LEGALIZE / RENEW), visa checklist driven by nationality-specific rules, essay review with anchored comments and suggestions, SLA-tracked agency assignment.
- Strong security posture: refresh-token rotation with reuse detection, HMAC-signed short-lived file URLs, 404-on-denial tenant isolation.

**Weaknesses (why the product does not feel premium).**
- The UI is a *generic AI-built SaaS dashboard*: everything is a rounded white card with a shadow; dashboards are grids of KPI tiles with coloured icon chips; badges/pills on nearly every line; tangerine used as decoration (eyebrows, section links, gradients, glows); a striped yellow demo banner on every page.
- Information architecture exposes the backend: the student home has ~11 equally weighted cards; the university detail page has 12 tabs; agency and university sidebars have ~20 items each (5 university items open the same page); agency Dashboard and Performance render the same analytics body; three different university detail pages exist.
- Screens do not answer one question each. The agency home shows 5 attention cards + 10 KPI tiles + 8 charts + a table; the university home shows 4 headline numbers + 10 KPI tiles + a 10-stage funnel + 6 more panels.
- Discovery is a 3-column wall of identical program cards with no eligibility signal for the logged-in student, even though the API can compute it.
- Typography has no discipline (≈355 literal font sizes, many half-pixel values, weights 550/650/750/780); spacing tokens are defined but used zero times.

**Major architectural decisions (existing, kept).** npm-workspaces monorepo; shared `@hangyul/*` packages (tokens, ui, types, api-client, auth, i18n, utils, validation, icons, mobile-ui); FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic; enums stored as VARCHAR; same-origin `/api` proxy so auth cookies are first-party; i18n via i18next with lazy JSON bundles; Recharts behind `React.lazy`.

**Major UX decisions (existing).** One "next action" for students; honesty rules; progressive onboarding with option cards; tables that turn into cards below 768 px; filters in drawers/bottom sheets; demo data always labelled.

# 2. Product vision

The intended ecosystem:

```
Student ──profile, documents, choices──▶ Hangyul Univ ──qualified, paid case──▶ Partner Agency
   ▲                                          │                                     │
   │     guidance, status, deadlines          │ verified information,               │ reviewed documents,
   └──────────────────────────────────────────┤ freshness, analytics                │ essays, submission
                                              ▼                                     ▼
                                     Partner University ◀──── complete, ready applications
                                     (admissions, offers, cohorts, outcomes)
```

| Party | Value proposition |
|---|---|
| **Student** | "Tell us about yourself once. We show which programs you can realistically get into, what it will cost, what you still need, and walk you — with a real counselor — through documents, application, visa and arrival." Removes the need to decode Korean admissions terminology (TOPIK, apostille, D-2 visa, 표준입학허가서) alone. |
| **Agency** | Pre-qualified students who have already paid and uploaded documents; a CRM where the daily question "who needs me today?" is answered automatically (tasks generated from deadlines, missing documents, SLA timers); faster document and essay review; fewer spreadsheets and chat threads. |
| **University** | A steady pipeline of *complete, pre-screened* applications with verified documents; transparent recruitment-channel quality (by agency and country); and — unlike email/Excel — outcomes after admission: tuition paid, visa issued, arrived, enrolled, retained, graduated, by cohort. |
| **Hangyul** | A marketplace and data network: partnership revenue, scholarship pools, and a compounding dataset of verified admissions information and outcomes. |

  agency-mobile/      Expo

packages/
  design-tokens/  colors, type, spacing, radius, shadows, status + chart palettes → tokens.css (generated)
  ui/             web components, shells (ConsoleShell, StudentShell), DataTable, charts (Recharts), global CSS
  icons/          lucide-react re-export + Hangyul brand marks (assets/brand)

                  to Hangyul, and is imported after eduan-ui. See §65, §69.1.
  eduan-ui/       V7 adapter for the Eduan template: verbatim Eduan SCSS + Bootstrap subset + Hangyul theme/glue; React ports (Ticker, Reveal, Offcanvas, SectionTitle, sticky header, Eduan line icons)
  ynex-ui/        V7 adapter for the YNEX template: verbatim YNEX SCSS + Bootstrap 5.3.3 subset + Hangyul theme + hg-* skin; React ports (YnexShell, PageHeader, YCard, StatCard, DateTimeline, ProgressRow, YTabs, SplitPane…)

                    for this project — since V10 the marketing foundation, ported through packages/koreanasha-ui. See §65.
themeforest-eduan/, themeforest-ynex/   licensed ThemeForest templates — V7 implementation sources (owner-authorised).
                    YNEX = console foundation; Eduan was the marketing foundation in V7–V9 and is now the shared chassis

## 3.2 Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Web | React 19.2.3 (pinned for Expo compatibility), Vite 7, React Router 7 (`createBrowserRouter`, route-level `lazy`), TanStack Query 5, TanStack Table 8, React Hook Form + Zod 4, Recharts 3, TypeScript 5.9 |
| Mobile | Expo SDK 57, React Native 0.86, expo-router, TanStack Query |
| Backend | Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2, Alembic, psycopg, argon2, PyJWT |
| Database | PostgreSQL 16 (native service, no Docker on this machine); Redis configured but unused |
| Fonts / icons | Pretendard Variable (npm, self-hosted dynamic subset); Lucide |

## 3.3 Auth

JWT access token (15 min, in memory) + rotating refresh token (14 days) in an httpOnly cookie `hg_rt_<client>` scoped to `/api/v1/auth` (mobile sends it in the body). Clients: `student`, `marketing`, `agency`, `university`; students cannot sign in to consoles and staff cannot sign in to the student app. Roles: STUDENT; HANGYUL_SUPER_ADMIN/OPERATIONS/COUNSELOR/FINANCE; AGENCY_OWNER/MANAGER/COUNSELOR/DOCUMENT_REVIEWER; UNIVERSITY_ADMIN/ADMISSIONS/REVIEWER/ANALYST. Tenant isolation in `server/app/services/access.py` (denials return 404).

## 3.4 API structure

All under `/api/v1` (`server/app/api/v1/`): `auth.py`, `catalog.py` (public catalog + saved/compare), `student.py` (`/me/*`), `documents.py`, `applications.py`, `collab.py` (essays, tasks, conversations, notifications, visa), `agency.py` (`/agency/*`), `university.py` (`/university/*`), `admin.py` (sources, freshness, audit). OpenAPI docs at http://localhost:8000/docs. Detail in §8.

npm run test:api | test:web | typecheck | build | test:e2e | i18n:check
node scripts/qa/visual-qa.mjs all 390,768,1440   # screenshot every route, report overflow/console errors

# 4. Current product map (as audited)

Quality scale: **A** credible · **B** functional but generic · **C** weak / confusing.

# 5. Existing user journeys

| Journey | What works | What does not |
|---|---|---|
| **Student onboarding** | Register → 7-step wizard (nationality with apostille hint + source, goals, education with GPA normalization, language, preferences, passport, sponsor), autosave, skip from step 3, finish screen with readiness | 7 steps is long before any value is shown; the finish screen shows a readiness % rather than "you qualify for N programs" |
| **University search** | Faceted search (degree, field, region, type, language, tuition, TOPIK/IELTS, intake, scholarship, dorm, partner, open) with debounced query | Results show no eligibility for the signed-in student; filters buried in a drawer; card wall |
| **Matching** | Explainable rules engine (`rules-2026.09`): hard eligibility then weighted fit → STRONG/COMPETITIVE/REACH/NOT_ELIGIBLE with reasons (met/missing/warning) | Lives on a separate page from search; terms not explained where shown |
| **Compare** | API compares 2–4 programs with match results | UI is a sticky-header spreadsheet; no "best for budget" / differences emphasis |
| **Document preparation** | Vault reused across applications; per-requirement checklist actions; legalization router (apostille vs consular, time-versioned by country); signed URLs | Presented partly as files; apostille guidance not surfaced at the point of need |
| **Essay review** | Versions, anchored comments, suggestions students can apply, internal notes, diff, deterministic pre-check | Visual quality only |
| **Application** | State machine with actor permissions; submission gate on required docs; history | Student view does not show "what is Hangyul / agency / university doing" |
| **Agency assignment** | Scoring by country, language, university, degree, workload, SLA; override with reason (Hangyul) | — |
| **Visa** | Checklist from nationality-specific VisaRequirement rows, dependency blocking, auto-created at admission certificate | Before admission the page is mostly prose |
| **University review** | Applicant list, detail with documents shared for the application, decisions via transitions, flags, CSV export | No explicit "request documents" action (only transition to ADDITIONAL_DOCUMENTS); list hard to scan |
| **Student lifecycle** | Enrollments, terms, outcomes, risk flags (attendance, standing, visa expiring, not registered); cohort retention/graduation | Split across 5 nav items |

# 6. Current design system (as audited)

- **Typography:** Pretendard Variable. Token scale 12/13/15/16/18/20/24/30/38/48/64, but CSS uses ≈355 literal sizes incl. half-pixels (10.5, 11.5, 12.5, 13.5, 14.5, 15.5, 16.5, 17.5) and weights 550/650/720/740/750/760/780/800. Headlines use heavy 750–800 weights with −0.03em tracking (marketing hero 82px/800).
- **Colors:** tangerine scale (FFF7E0…FF5000, but 50–600 are actually yellows/ambers), warm cream canvas `#FFFDF8`, cool grays, ink navy sidebar for University, 7 semantic tones. Tangerine is used for eyebrows, section links, KPI chips, funnel gradients, nav active state, hero stripes and glows.
- **Spacing:** 4px scale defined; `--hg-space-*` used **0 times**.
- **Radius:** tokens 4/6/10/14/20; CSS also uses 2,3,5,7,8,9,11,12,16,18,22,24,28. Cards 14px, marketing 24px.
- **Buttons:** 40/32/50px heights; primary has an orange glow shadow; 8 variants.
- **Cards:** white, 1px border, xs shadow, 14px radius — used for *everything* (sections, KPIs, lists, filters).
- **Badges:** 24px pills, heavily used (status, tier, partner, days-left, sample-data, degree).
- **Forms:** 44px inputs, blue focus ring.
- **Tables:** grey header band, 12px bold headers, sticky; card mode < 768px.
- **Charts:** Recharts, 8-hue rainbow categorical palette led by tangerine; gradient-filled area charts; donut charts.
- **Icons:** Lucide only (good) — but icons prefix nearly every heading, fact and KPI.
- **Responsive:** works without overflow; tables become cards; filters in bottom sheets; sidebars collapse to drawers.

**Why it does not work.** Every element carries equal visual weight (same card, same shadow, same badge), so hierarchy disappears and screens read as "a dashboard with many cards". Colour is decorative rather than semantic, so warnings do not stand out. Heavy display weights and pills make it look like a template. The consoles look like the ThemeForest YNEX admin they were modelled on (icon-chip KPI tiles, dark navy sidebar).

# 7. Current data model (summary)

69 tables (full generated reference: `docs/DATA_MODEL.md`). Conventions: UUID PKs, timestamps, enums as VARCHAR, `SourcedMixin` (source_url, verified_at, effective_from/to, verification_status default `DEMO`), `is_demo` flags.

| Domain | Entities |
|---|---|
| Identity | User, UserRole (global), Organization (HANGYUL/AGENCY/UNIVERSITY), OrganizationMember, AgencySpecialty, RefreshToken, LoginEvent, ConsentRecord, DataRequest |
| Reference | Country (apostille membership + effective date), Locale, Source, SourceSnapshot, FreshnessReview, LegalizationRule |
| Catalog | University, Campus, Program, ProgramIntake, AdmissionRequirement, DocumentRequirement, Dormitory, Scholarship, ScholarshipRule (College/Department unused) |
| Student | StudentProfile (pipeline_stage, targets, budget…), StudentEducation (gpa_percent normalized), StudentLanguage, SavedUniversity, MatchSnapshot, Appointment |
| Workflow | AgencyAssignment (score + SLA), Application (21 statuses) + StatusHistory, Document (legalization path/status) + DocumentVersion + DocumentReview, ApplicationDocument (shared_with_university), Essay/Version/Comment, Task (dedupe_key, engine-generated), Conversation/Participant/Message/MessageRead, Notification |
| Business | ServiceProduct/Price, Order, Payment, PartnerContract (guarantee terms), PartnerQuota, ScholarshipPool, ScholarshipAward |
| Lifecycle | VisaRequirement, VisaCase, HousingCase, ArrivalPlan, StudentEnrollment, StudentTerm, StudentOutcome, SupportTicket, ContentArticle, AnalyticsEvent, DailyMetric, AuditLog |

Key relationships: Student 1–N Application → Program/Intake/University; Application N–N Document via ApplicationDocument; Student 1–1 active AgencyAssignment → Organization + counselor; Application → VisaCase → StudentEnrollment → Terms/Outcome; University Organization ↔ University (tenant).

Application status flow: DRAFT → PROFILE_REVIEW → DOCUMENT_PREPARATION → READY → SUBMITTED → UNIVERSITY_REVIEW ↔ ADDITIONAL_DOCUMENTS / INTERVIEW → OFFERED / WAITLISTED / REJECTED → OFFER_ACCEPTED → TUITION_PENDING → TUITION_PAID → ADMISSION_CERTIFICATE_PENDING → ADMISSION_CERTIFICATE_ISSUED → VISA_PREPARATION → VISA_SUBMITTED → VISA_ISSUED → ENROLLED (WITHDRAWN any time). Actor permissions in `server/app/services/state_machine.py`.

# 11. Student perspective audit (before redesign)

*Persona: 19-year-old from Hanoi, knows little about Korean admissions, nervous about visas, doesn't know what an apostille is, limited budget, wants scholarships, comparing Korea with Japan and Australia, reads English on a phone.*

1. **Do I immediately understand what Hangyul Univ does?** Partly. "Your simplest path to studying in Korea" is clear, but the hero is dominated by a giant headline and floating mock cards with an orange orbit; the page then scrolls for 13 screens.
2. **Why should I trust it?** The sourced/verified-date idea is excellent but invisible on the landing hero; empty testimonial boxes actively *reduce* trust.
3. **Can I start without knowing terminology?** Onboarding is good (it explains apostille for my country with a source). The rest of the app uses TOPIK, D-2-2, "Reach", "Legalize" without explanation.
4. **Is onboarding too long?** 7 steps before I see any universities. Too long; value should appear after step 2–3.
5. **Do I always know what to do next?** The "Your next step" card is right, but it fights with a 42% ring, a journey bar, 3 lists and 6 more cards.
6. **Are recommendations understandable?** Reasons are good ("TOPIK 4 exceeds the minimum (level 3)"), but the same three reasons repeat on each card.
7. **Eligible vs recommended vs reach vs missing?** Only on the Matches page; not in search results or university pages.
8. **Is comparison useful?** It is a spreadsheet; I have to find differences myself.
9. **Is cost understandable?** A cost card on the home page for one program; tuition "/ semester" vs "yearly cost" on cards is confusing.
10. **Scholarships?** "14 you're eligible for" is good news buried in a card; list shows names without amounts.
11. **Timeline?** Deadlines list mixes application deadlines with essay tasks; no sense of the overall timeline.
12. **Apostille?** Explained in onboarding and in a document drawer; not where I see "Needs apostille".
13. **Visa progress?** Before admission, a prose list. Nothing tells me what I can already prepare (bank statement for Vietnam).
14. **Are documents overwhelming?** The vault is actually reasonable; "Needs a fix" + a red sentence is clear.
15. **Mobile?** Works; the home is 4,700px of stacked cards; bottom tabs are good.
16. **Trustworthy enough to upload my passport?** The privacy callout on Documents is good; the overall visual quality (striped demo banner, pills) feels less like a bank/Wise and more like a template.
17. **More useful than Google?** Yes in substance (eligibility, apostille by country, checklists) — but the UI hides it.
18. **Emotional confidence?** The greeting and "one step at a time" are nice; the density undermines calm.
19. **Unnecessary?** Readiness ring, cost card on home, scholarships card, duplicate Matches link, Notifications page, More page with 13 items.
20. **Missing?** Eligibility on every program; what my counselor/agency/university is doing; a simple overall timeline; "what can I prepare now" for visa.

# 12. Agency perspective audit (before redesign)

*Persona: manager at an agency with hundreds of students.*

1. **Saves time?** The engine-generated tasks, SLA timers and review queue do. The UI makes me hunt.
2. **Who requires attention?** The "Needs attention now" row exists but is visually equal to 10 KPI tiles below it; two of the five boxes say "All clear" and still take space.
3. **Pipeline useful?** Kanban is fine; duplicated by stage filter.
4. **Find a student in seconds?** Yes — global search combobox is good.
5. **Filter by country/counselor/university/intake/stage/missing docs/deadlines?** Country, counselor, stage, degree yes; university, intake, missing documents, deadline no.
6. **Today's workload?** Not on one screen.
7. **Overdue obvious?** Only as a number.
8. **Document review fast?** J/K/V/C shortcuts are good; the queue does not auto-open the first item; right panel empty on load.
9. **Essay review efficient?** Reasonable: comments, suggestions, internal notes.
10. **Communicate without switching tools?** Messaging with internal notes, mentions, templates, create-task — yes.
11. **Internal vs student-visible?** Supported (internal tag, yellow internal style).
12. **Dashboard leads to action?** Only the attention row does; the rest is statistics.
13. **Counselor workload?** Table at the bottom of the dashboard.
14. **Bottlenecks?** Task aging chart only.
15. **Metrics meaningful?** Defined and honest (n<5 suppression) but too many.
16. **Run daily operations inside?** Almost; missing saved views, bulk document actions, shared templates.
17. **What sends them back to Excel/Kakao?** Views like "deadline in 7 days + missing docs" (no saved views), shared templates, student-visible messaging on mobile chat apps, exporting by intake.

# 13. University perspective audit (before redesign)

*Persona: international admissions officer with limited time.*

1. **Why use it?** Complete, pre-reviewed applications plus outcomes after admission — valuable, but the dashboard does not say so.
2. **Beyond email/Excel?** Funnel through enrollment, channel quality by agency, cohort retention — real differentiators.
3. **Dashboard in 10 s?** No — 20+ numbers of equal weight; "99% Avg. readiness" and "9 Hangyul applicants" compete with "Graduation rate 82%".
4. **Identify incomplete applications?** "Waiting for extra documents 0" in the attention list; not in the applicant table.
5. **Review quickly?** Applicant table wraps into 4 lines per row; detail is long but complete.
6. **Communicate requests?** Message modal exists; no "request documents" action.
7. **Compare recruitment channels?** Agency table (with "Small sample" honesty) — good.
8. **Funnel conversion?** 10-stage bar funnel with mixed cohorts ("incl. earlier cohorts") — confusing.
9. **Enrolled cohorts?** Cohorts page is reasonable; split across 5 nav items.
10. **Post-admission data useful?** Yes, the differentiator.
11. **Metrics defined?** Yes (tooltips) — but hidden behind ⓘ icons.
12. **Credible for a president/director?** Not yet: dark navy template sidebar, rainbow icon chips, hatched "not enough data" tiles.
13. **Enterprise software?** Looks like an admin template.
14. **Cheap admin template signs?** Icon-chip KPI tiles, gradient funnel, hatched tiles, pills.
15. **Too much information?** Yes.
16. **Important info buried?** Pending decisions (5) sit mid-page on the right.
17. **What prevents adoption?** Trust in data quality (needs clear definitions and sample-size handling — present), SSO/export needs, and visual credibility.

# 14. Redesign strategy

## 14.1 Principles

Calm · Precise · Premium · Human · International · Trustworthy. **One screen answers one question.** Progressive disclosure. Reduce before adding. Colour means state. Tangerine means "act here" or "you are here".

| Product | The question its home answers |
|---|---|
| Student | "What should I do now — and where am I in the journey?" |
| Agency | "Who needs my attention today?" |
| University | "What is happening with our Hangyul applicant pipeline?" |
| Marketing | "Can this company get me into a Korean university without me figuring it out alone?" |

Benchmarked principles (not branding): Linear/Attio (dense but quiet tables, saved views, neutral chrome), Stripe/Mercury (ink-first charts, metric definitions, hairline dividers instead of cards), Wise/Airbnb (step-based guided flows, one CTA, plain language), Ashby (review queues with preview + decision), Vercel (restrained type scale).

## 14.2 Foundation (design system v2)

- **Tokens** (`packages/design-tokens/src/index.ts`): neutral near-white canvas; ink text `#16181C`; tangerine reserved for primary action/current step/focus; semantic colours for state only; type scale 12/13/14/15/16/18/20/24/28/36/48/64 with weights 400/500/600/700; radius 4/6/8/10/14; shadows only for overlays; ink-first chart palette; z-index + weights emitted as CSS variables.
- **Shared CSS** (`packages/ui/src/styles/*`): flatter cards (border, no shadow, 10px radius), 36px buttons without glow, quieter badges (6px radius, text + dot), white table headers, light neutral sidebars for both consoles (remove ink navy), slim neutral demo strip, consistent page header.
- **New shared patterns**: `Section` (title + optional action, no card), `ListRow`, `StatusText` (dot + label), `KeyValue`, `MetricRow`, `AttentionItem`, `JourneyRail`, `EmptyState` rewrite.

## 14.3 Student

- Nav: **Home · Universities · Applications · Documents · Messages**; everything else (Visa, Scholarships, Essays, Tasks, Housing, Arrival, Saved, Services, Support, Profile, Settings) in a single account/"More" menu grouped by journey stage.
- Home: journey rail (stages with ✓ / current / upcoming) → next best action (one dominant CTA, due date, why) → "Coming up" (next 4 dated items) → applications as rows with status in words and readiness → documents to handle → recommended programs (3 rows with verdict) → counselor strip. Remove readiness ring, cost, scholarship and visa cards from home (visa appears only once admitted).
- Universities: one discovery area with **For you** (matches by tier) and **All programs** (search). Desktop filter rail with the 5 filters that matter (degree, field, city/region, language & level, budget) + "more"; mobile search + filter sheet. Results as calm rows/cards showing verdict (Eligible / Reach / Not eligible yet / Sign in to check), tuition per year, deadline, language requirement, scholarship, partner.
- University detail: decision header (identity, program picker, verdict with reasons, 4 key facts: yearly cost, deadline, language, scholarship; primary CTA) then sections Programs · Admissions & documents · Costs & scholarships · Housing & campus · Sources.
- Compare: decision summary ("Lowest yearly cost", "Earliest deadline", "Best match") then rows where differences are emphasised and identical values dimmed.
- Application: workspace header (university, program, status, deadline, counselor) + "Next step" + tabs Overview / Documents / Essays / Timeline, with "who is doing what" (you / Hangyul & agency / university).
- Documents: requirement-centric rows ("Graduation certificate — Needs apostille — See instructions").
- Visa: numbered guided checklist before and after admission, blockers highlighted, sources with dates.

## 14.4 Agency

- Nav (≤12): Today · Students · Pipeline · Tasks · Reviews (documents / essays) · Messages · Applications · Consultations · Performance · Universities · Team & settings; Hangyul HQ group only for Hangyul staff.
- Today: attention list (overdue tasks, documents awaiting review, essays awaiting review, deadlines ≤7 days, SLA breaches, unread messages) — each a row with count, oldest item, and link to the filtered list; then pipeline strip (counts by stage group, clickable), upcoming deadlines, counselor workload. KPIs move to Performance.
- Students: saved views (All · My students · Needs attention · Deadline ≤14 days · Documents to fix · Waiting for university · Visa), columns Student · Nationality · Intake · Counselor · Stage · Documents · Next deadline · Next action · Last activity; search, sort, column config, bulk actions, CSV.
- Document review: auto-select first item; preview + requirement + checklist + decision with reason templates.

## 14.5 University

- Nav (≤12): Overview · Applicants · Offers & enrolment · Documents · Messages · Analytics · Students (cohorts) · Programs & rules · Partnership · Scholarships · Agencies · Exports/Settings.
- Overview: "Needs your decision" list first, then the admissions funnel as a precise table-bar (Submitted → Reviewed → Offered → Accepted → Tuition paid → Visa issued → Enrolled with conversion %), upcoming deadlines, yield, applicants by nationality and by program (compact bars), metric definitions inline.
- Applicants: quick-filter tabs (Needs review · Missing documents · Interview · Offer · Admitted · Enrolment pending · All), dense single-line rows, agency truncated, readiness as a short bar + %.

## 14.6 Marketing

- Hero: "Study in Korea, without figuring it out alone." + one-sentence promise + program search + primary CTA, next to a real product preview (next-step + match verdict). Trust line with sourced facts.
- Story: Discover → Get matched → Prepare documents → Apply → Visa → Arrive (one compact sequence with product snippets), trust section (sources with dates, privacy, human counselor, partner structure), for universities / agencies (two short columns), guides, final CTA. Remove placeholder testimonials, decorative orbs/leaves, repeated blocks.

# 16. Final state

## 16.1 What changed and why (summary)

Hangyul Univ now follows one design language — **calm, precise, neutral-first** — and every home screen answers one question:

| Product | Home answers | Primary pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Student | "Where am I, and what do I do now?" | Journey rail → one dominant next step → rows |
| Agency | "Who needs my attention today?" | Attention list → caseload by phase → coming up → workload |
| University | "What is happening with our Hangyul pipeline?" | Needs your decision → admissions funnel → coming up → origins/yield |
| Marketing | "Can they get me into a Korean university without figuring it out alone?" | Short promise + product preview → 6-step story → trust |

Premium comes from typography, hairlines, spacing and restraint instead of cards, shadows, pills, gradients and icon chips. Tangerine is used only for the primary action, the "you are here" marker and focus.

## 16.2 Before / After / Why / Impact — major screens

| Screen | BEFORE | AFTER | WHY | IMPACT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Student Home** (`apps/student-web/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx`) | ~11 equal cards (hero, 42% ring, bar journey, deadlines, apps, docs, 3 rec cards, counselor, scholarships, visa, cost) | Journey rail (✓ done / tangerine current / upcoming) → next step with one CTA and due date → applications as rows (status in words, readiness, closes) → recommendations with verdict and cost; side: coming up (dated), documents to handle, your team, one-line extras (visa/scholarships/profile) | One obvious action lowers anxiety; the rest is supporting context | Students |
| **Universities (search + matches)** (`pages/Explore.tsx`, `components/ProgramRow.tsx`) | Two places (Explore card wall, Matches page); no eligibility on search results; 13 filters in a drawer | One area: **For you** (verdict segments Eligible / Reach / Not yet with counts, plain-language summary, methodology on demand) and **All programs** (filter rail with 5 essentials + "More filters", quick chips, verdict overlaid on every result). Rows show only: program, university, city, degree, yearly cost, language requirement, deadline, verdict; reasons/compare/apply disclosed per row | "Which universities are realistic?" is the core question | Students |
| **University detail** (`pages/University.tsx`) | 12 tabs; first screen = "About" text | Decision panel first: program picker (ranked by fit), verdict headline (or the exact missing requirement), yearly cost, deadline + days left, language, scholarships, why Hangyul recommends it, Start application / Compare; then 5 sections (Overview, Admissions & documents, Costs & scholarships, Housing & campus, Sources) | Answer relevance, eligibility, cost and deadline before detail | Students |

- **Student:** Home · Universities · Applications · Documents · Messages; "More" grouped as Prepare (Essays, Tasks, Saved, Scholarships), Going to Korea (Visa, Housing, Arrival), Account (Profile, Services, Help, Settings). Mobile: same 5 bottom tabs.
- **Agency:** Today · Students · Pipeline | Work: Tasks, Messages, Applications, Consultations | Review: Documents, Essays | Insights: Performance, Universities | Team, Settings (+ HQ for Hangyul staff). Deadlines/notifications/templates/payments/audit reached from Settings.

## 16.4 Design system (v2) — final

- **Tokens** (`packages/design-tokens/src/index.ts` → `tokens.css`): neutral greys (`#16181C` ink → `#F7F7F8`), canvas `#FBFBFA`; tangerine `#FF6700` (primary), text-tangerine `#C24D00` (AA); status success/info/warning/danger/neutral/brand/teal (fg/bg/solid); **type scale** 12/13/14/15/16/18/20/24/28/36/48/64 with weights 400/500/600/700; **spacing** 4-px scale; **radius** 4/6/8/10/14; shadows only xs/sm (controls, next-step panel) and md/lg (overlays); weights, line-heights and z-index now emitted as CSS variables; dark theme for consoles re-derived from the same neutrals.
- **Chart palette** validated (lightness band, chroma floor, CVD ΔE ≥ 12, normal-vision ΔE ≥ 17) for light and dark: slate blue `#4A6FD1` (single series), tangerine (highlight), teal, ochre, violet, rose, grey "Other".
- **Components** (`packages/ui`): Button (sm 32 / md 36 / lg 44, no glow), Card (flat, 10px), Badge (6px radius, sparse), **StatusText** (dot + words), **Section**, **ListRow**/`hg-panel` lists, **Metrics** strip, **InfoTip**, **JourneyRail**, **UniMark**, **Bars**, Tabs (underline), Segmented, inputs 40px (44px + 16px font on phones), tables (white header, 12px medium labels, hairline rows), toasts above the mobile tab bar, calm single-column sign-in.
- **Removed patterns:** icon-chip KPI tiles, ink navy sidebar, striped demo banner, gradient funnels, orange glows, pill badges everywhere, eyebrow labels in tangerine, colored avatars.

## 16.5 Responsive

- Student: bottom tab bar; home stacks next step first; list rows wrap their status/progress under the title (`.hg-lrow` mobile rule); discovery uses search + filter sheet with the same rows (container queries switch to a table-like row ≥ 760px of list width); university page shows a sticky "Start application" on phones.
- Consoles: tables become list cards < 768px; filters in sheets; Today/Overview stack attention first.
- Verified: 0 issues (overflow, console errors, raw keys, heading count) on all 68 routes at 390/430/768/1024/1440 (340 views).

## 16.6 Stakeholder re-review (after redesign)

**International student.** I understand the service from the hero in one read and the product preview shows exactly what I'll get. After signing in, the home tells me where I am (Apply) and one thing to do. Universities › For you says "You meet the published requirements for 31 programs" and every row shows yearly cost, TOPIK level and deadline; I can open "why" without leaving the list. A university page answers am I eligible / how much / when in the first screen. Documents tell me "Needs apostille — see instructions" instead of listing files, and the visa page already shows my Vietnam-specific steps with sources. *Remaining friction:* onboarding is still 7 steps (value appears only after); the seed data shows 42% readiness on a "Ready to submit" application (demo inconsistency); cost is shown per program but there's no total-budget planner across choices.

**Agency.** Today tells me what needs me: 2 documents (oldest waiting 55 days), 5 essays, 8 deadlines, 2 unread conversations — each one click from the filtered list. The student list has the views I would otherwise keep in Excel, with next deadline and next action per student. Review opens the oldest document immediately. *Remaining gaps that still push work outside:* templates are per-browser, no bulk document actions, no upload-on-behalf, no message attachments, no WhatsApp/Kakao bridge; Tasks/Consultations/Team/Payments pages kept their earlier layout (restyled only).

**University.** The Overview says what needs a decision (3 awaiting review, 1 interview, 1 waitlisted, 17 enrolled students at risk) and the funnel is one consistent population with definitions and honest small-sample handling. Applicants is scannable in one line per person, and Request documents is an explicit action. It would not embarrass me in a director's meeting. *Remaining gaps:* the request note is not copied into the student's task title; analytics offer-rate and lifecycle blocks still use the older history-based counts (Overview/Offers use the funnel); no SSO; secondary pages (Scholarships, Partnership, Programs, Documents) restyled but not recomposed.

## 16.7 Remaining limitations / unresolved

1. **Native mobile apps** (`apps/*-mobile`) were not redesigned; they inherit the new token values (colours, status, chart palette) and typecheck clean, but screens are unchanged.
2. Secondary screens restyled by the foundation but not recomposed: student Onboarding, Housing, Arrival, Services, Profile, Settings, Essays list; agency Tasks, Consultations, Catalog, Team, Payments; university Scholarships, Partnership, Programs, Documents.
3. Dark mode (consoles) uses re-derived tokens but was not visually QA'd screen by screen; Recharts receives light-mode hex colours.
4. Demo-data inconsistencies: readiness % vs status for the main student; history-based yield vs current statuses (university analytics).
5. Product gaps unchanged: payments demo-only (Stripe/Toss not enabled), S3 storage and malware scanning stubs, no email/push, no agency upload-on-behalf, no message attachments, data requests recorded but not processed, legal pages are drafts, no real testimonials or outcomes data.
6. Korean strings for new UI were written by the implementer (not professionally reviewed); the other 43 locales fall back to English for new keys.
7. `/agency/students` row extras run several queries per student — needs aggregation before large caseloads.

## 16.8 Next recommended work

1. Shorten onboarding to 3 questions before showing matches (nationality, target degree, language score), deferring the rest.
2. Recompose remaining secondary screens with the v2 patterns (list above), then redesign native mobile screens with the same compositions.
3. Budget planner on Compare/Home (tuition + living + scholarships across the shortlist).
4. Agency: shared team templates (server-side), bulk document actions, upload on behalf, attachments.
5. University: include request note in the generated student task; migrate all analytics blocks to the funnel population; SSO; scheduled exports.
6. Professional Korean review of new strings; translation pipeline for other locales.
7. Dark-mode QA pass; pass CSS variables to Recharts.

## 16.9 How to run

```bash
cd /root/hangyul-univ
npm run dev          # API :8000 + marketing :3100, student :3101, agency :3102, university :3103
```

Demo password for every account: `Hangyul!2026` (student `student@demo.hangyul.kr`, agency `manager@lotus.demo.hangyul.kr`, university `admin@pusan.univ.demo.hangyul.kr`). Demo sign-in shortcuts appear in development builds (or with `VITE_DEMO_LOGINS=true`).

# 17. V3 Independent Audit

*Performed 2026-09-29 against the running system (not the claims above). Web apps inspected at 390×844, 430×932, 768×1024, 1024×768, 1280×800 and 1440×900. Native apps were run through Expo's web renderer (`expo start --web`, react-native-web) at 390×844 because no Android/iOS emulator exists on this machine — native-only behaviour (camera, push, secure store) cannot be verified here. Evidence screenshots: `docs/qa/v3/audit/`.*

## 17.1 What the previous pass claimed vs. what is true

| Claim in §16 | Verified reality |
|---|---|
| "Every home answers one question" | True on web (student, agency, university). **False on all three native apps**: still V1 layouts (student home: 42% readiness ring, 9-segment bar, orange eyebrow; agency & university: grids of icon-chip KPI tiles). |
| "0 issues on 340 views" | The automated check only covers overflow/console/raw keys. It missed: a runtime error overlay in the native student app (`<button> cannot contain a nested <button>` on Explore — card is a Pressable containing the save Pressable), and it cannot judge composition. |
| "Tangerine is restrained and accessible" | **Primary buttons fail WCAG AA since V1**: white on `#FF6700` = 2.92:1 (needs 4.5:1). Focus ring on white = 2.92:1 (needs 3:1). Tertiary text `#6B717B` passes, but the proposed V3 `#858B94` would fail (3.43:1). |
| "Consistent analytics" | **Yield has three values**: University Offers page 60%, Overview "3 of 4", native app 67% ("4 of 6"); native offer rate 100% ("6 of 6") vs web funnel 50%. Different code paths (history-based `kpis`, funnel-based endpoint, mobile using `kpis`). |
| "Coherent demo" | Main student has a **"Ready to submit" application at 42% readiness** (5 READY applications average 86%, min 42%). **E2E tests write into the demo database** — "Minh Anh E2E" appears in agency lists, payments and university applicants. |
| "Secondary screens restyled" | True but they still read V1: icon-chip header panels (Exports, Team), pill clusters (Programs: "Bachelor's · Taught in Korean · Business"), card-per-plan pricing, 7-step onboarding wizard, Housing/Arrival checklists as long lists without phase logic. |
| "Dark mode available (consoles)" | Never visually QA'd; charts receive light-mode hex values. |
| "Localized" | en complete; ko complete for student; **Arabic/Vietnamese/etc. show English sentences for all V2 copy** (RTL mirroring itself is correct: nav, rail, chevrons, arrows flip). |

| V3-7 | P1 | Admission result, offer decision, tuition and admission-letter steps are just status rows | Student |
| V3-8 | P1 | Agency: saved views are fixed tabs (no custom/team views), templates in localStorage, no attachments, no upload-on-behalf, no bulk review | Agency |
| V3-9 | P1 | `/agency/students` runs several queries per row (0.13 s for 12 students, 0.53 s for 64 as Hangyul admin — linear growth) | Agency |

## 17.3 Audience verdicts (before V3)

- **New visitor:** understands the promise quickly and sees authentic UI, but must commit (account + long profile) before any personal value. No quick eligibility.
- **Student (web):** strong primary flows; weak "after admission" story (offer, tuition, admission letter, housing, arrival feel like separate modules); no budget view; mobile app is a different, older product.
- **Agency:** web Today + list are good; daily work still leaks to spreadsheets (no custom views), chat apps (no attachments) and local files (templates); mobile is a KPI dashboard.
- **University:** web overview credible; trust undermined by inconsistent yield numbers and the incomplete document-request loop; secondary setup pages look older than the overview.

# 18. V3 Product Strategy

**Principle:** complexity inside the system, one next step in front of the user. V3 is not another restyle — it closes the loops the product promises.

| Audience | V3 promise | Key V3 capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| Visitor | "See your realistic options in 30 seconds, no account." | Public quick eligibility (nationality, degree, language) → counts + sample programs + "what TOPIK 3 would unlock" → account carries answers over |
| Student | "One journey, from shortlist to arrival, with the money explained." | Progressive profile with "what this unlocks"; unified discovery (For you / All / Saved) with plain match language; program decision page with cost breakdown; compare + **budget planner**; service choice by human support; application workspace with responsibility lanes, submission readiness, university-review explanations, **admission result + offer comparison + tuition + admission letter**; visa centre; housing & arrival flows; redesigned native app |
| Agency | "Run 500 students without a spreadsheet or a chat app." | Server-backed personal/team saved views; team templates; message attachments (channel-ready architecture); upload on behalf; bulk verify/assign; review SLA; recomposed Tasks/Consultations/Team/Payments/Settings; aggregated list queries; redesigned mobile around today/review/message |
| University | "Better-prepared applicants, and visibility after admission, with numbers you can defend." | One metrics service (numerator, denominator, population, time range) used by overview, offers, analytics and mobile; document request → requirement + student task with the exact note → completion back; applicant review with reasons; recomposed programs & rules, scholarships, partnership, cohorts/outcomes, exports (manual now, job-ready); SSO abstraction (OIDC/SAML) documented; redesigned mobile |

**Match vocabulary (student-facing):**
- **Strong match** — you meet every published basic requirement *and* it fits your budget and preferences.
- **Possible match** — you meet the published minimums; something needs attention (budget, deadline) or one item needs review.
- **Not eligible yet** — a published requirement is not met; the UI names it ("TOPIK 3 required — you have TOPIK 2").
- "Reach" is retired from student UI (API tier `REACH` is shown as "Not eligible yet — close" with the exact gap).

**Execution:** five parallel workstreams (student web, marketing + quick eligibility, agency + platform backend, university + analytics + SSO, native apps), one owner per app/namespace; shared design system, seed personas, i18n and this report owned centrally; Alembic revisions serialized (`/tmp/claude-0/hg-migrate.lock`) to keep one migration head.

# 19. V3 Design System

Refines V2; brand unchanged. Values verified with a WCAG contrast script.

| Token | V2 | V3 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Canvas | `#FBFBFA` | `#FAFAF8` | Spec; warmer |
| Surface / subtle | `#FFFFFF` / `#F7F7F8` | `#FFFFFF` / `#F6F6F3` | Warm-neutral grouping |
| Text primary / secondary / tertiary | `#16181C` / `#525862` / `#6B717B` | `#181A1F` (17.4:1) / `#5F646C` (5.96:1) / `#6E737C` (≥4.5:1 on canvas) | Spec direction; `#858B94` rejected (3.43:1) |
| Border / strong | `#E4E6EA` / `#CDD1D7` | `#E7E8EA` / `#D5D7DB` | Hairlines |
| **Action tangerine** (buttons, links, focus, current step) | `#FF6700` (2.92:1 with white — **fails**) | **`#CC4E00`** (4.51:1), hover `#B34400`, pressed `#9E3C00`, subtle `#FFF1E7` | AA for all button text; still unmistakably tangerine |
| Brand tangerine | `#FF6700` | `#FF6700` for logo and rare large brand moments only | BI preserved |
| Type | body 14 | caption 12/18 · meta 13/20 · UI label 14/20 · **body 15/24** · large 16/26 · section 18/26 · page 24/32 · large title 32/40 · display 36/42 (mobile) – 52/60 (desktop); weights 400/500/600, 700 rare | Readability for anxious readers; consoles keep 14px tables |
| Controls | buttons 36 · inputs 40 | buttons **40** (sm 32, lg 48 on mobile primary) · inputs **44** | Spec, touch comfort |
| Radius | 4/6/8/10/14 | 6 small · 8 control · 10 panel · 12–14 overlay | Unchanged principle |
| Shadows | xs on buttons | none on panels/buttons; md/lg for overlays only | Border + surface contrast |
| Widths | student 1160 | marketing 1200 · student 1120 · reading 720 · consoles fluid ≤1440 | Spec |
| Status | dot + words | unchanged (filled badges only for strong emphasis) | |
| Charts | validated palette | unchanged; tangerine = highlight only; charts read CSS variables | |
| Dark mode | toggle in consoles | **Removed** (light-only) until it can be QA'd to the same standard; tokens retained | Spec: light-only beats mediocre dark |

# 21. V3 Final Stakeholder Audit

*Method: each audience's core tasks were executed end to end against the running system — by Playwright scripts that click through the UI as that user (28 flows, listed in 21.5) and by hand with screenshots at 390 and 1440 (`docs/qa/v3/final/`, plus the per-workstream folders). No external participants were available, so this is an expert walkthrough, not a usability study; findings are stated as observed.*

## 21.1 New visitor (marketing)

| Task | Result |
|---|---|
| Understand what Hangyul is within the first screen | Pass — promise, who it is for, and the 3-question check are all above the fold at 390 and 1440. |
| Find out whether Korea is realistic for me without an account | **Pass (new)** — nationality, degree, language → "You meet the published requirements for N programs, M are one step away", sample programs, and the smallest language step that unlocks more. Never claims an admission chance. |
| Sign up without repeating answers | Pass — answers prefill registration and become the first profile entries; the signed-in count matches the anonymous one (21 met + 5 one step away in the verified case). |
| Decide whether to trust it | Mostly — every sample figure is labelled "Sample"/"Demo", partner logos are not faked, no testimonials. **Weak:** no real partner names, reviews or company details exist yet, so trust rests on transparency alone (a business gap, not a UI one). |

## 21.2 Student (web + native)

| Task | Persona | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Know the next step on opening the app | all four | Pass — one next step per state: profile unlock (Dilnoza), finish application with item count (Lan), **compare offers** (Hà, fixed in this pass), visa documents (Bảo). |
| Find programs I can actually get into, and why | Lan, Dilnoza | Pass — For you / All / Saved; Strong / Possible / Not eligible yet with the exact gap. |
| Understand the money | Lan | Pass — compare → budget planner with ranges, cash before arrival, and every line labelled Official / Sample / Estimate / Unknown. Unknown fees are shown as unknown, not invented. |
| Upload and fix documents | Lan | Pass — documents grouped as requirements with legalization steps and one next action each. |
| Respond to a university request | Lan (E2E) | Pass — the university's exact note arrives as a task and requirement; fulfilling it closes the loop on the university side. |

| Same on the phone | all | Web: pass at 390/430. Native: the redesigned apps were exercised through Expo's web renderer only (see §22). |

# 23. V4 Independent Product Audit

*Performed 2026-09-29 against the running system, before any V4 change. Method: every critical screen captured at first viewport and full page with `scripts/qa/v4-capture.mjs` (38 screens; key screens at 390×844, 430×932, 768×1024, 1024×768, 1280×800, 1440×900; others at 390 and 1440) as the four student personas (Lan preparing, Dilnoza early, Hà two offers, Bảo visa), the Lotus Bridge counselor, manager and reviewer, and the Pusan National admissions officer and admin. Every screenshot in `docs/qa/v4/before/` was looked at by eye; the same script recorded objective measures (`docs/qa/v4/before/metrics.json`). API responses and the database were queried directly to confirm each suspected defect. The §16–22 claims were treated as hypotheses.*

## 23.1 What the previous report claims vs. what a user actually sees

| Claim (§16, §21) | What I found |
|---|---|
| "Money explained: every line labelled, ranges not quotes" | **The same program has three unrelated prices.** Pusan BBA: Universities list "Per year ₩2x.xM" (a single engine figure, fake precision, tuition + 12 months living), program page "Tuition ₩8.9M … Estimated net ₩13.3M–₩21.7M", program list on the same page "₩4.4M / semester", Budget "₩13.3M–₩21.7M". SKKU shows "₩23.3M" on the list and a range on its page. A parent comparing screens cannot tell which is the cost. |
| "Program page answers relevance, eligibility, cost, deadline" | True for a new visitor. **Wrong for Lan:** she already has a Pusan BBA application, and the page still offers "Start application" (no "Continue your application"). |
| "Application workspace: who is doing what" | The lanes exist, but the page lists the same missing items **three times** (YOU lane, "3 items remain", "Still needed") and **contradicts itself**: YOU "Upload Personal statement" while HANGYUL "Reviewing your Personal statement"; "Upload Study plan" *and* "Write your Study plan". The hero asks "What needs to happen before submission?" and offers "Handle documents" — it never names the one thing to do. |
| "Documents: being checked, usually within 2 working days" | The student's bank certificate has been "being checked" for **2 months** (DB: uploads waiting 10–78 days). Nothing tells her it is late or that anyone has been told. This is exactly "Is anything happening?" |
| "Visa centre: calm, numbered, sourced" | The "What needs you now" headline is the raw sourced rule: *"Proof of funds per the Korean Embassy in Hanoi (reported: USD 15,000 held for 3 months — confirm before applying)"*. Four completed steps stay expanded; "Review due" warnings (an internal freshness state) are shown to the student with no explanation. |
| "Compare with budget" | Compare is **empty** for a student with 3 saved programs ("Pick at least two programs"); she must go back and toggle Compare per row. |
| "University applicants: single-line rows" | At 1440×900 the table is **wider than the page**: Agency is cut off, Submitted / Last update are off-screen. "Documents" shows a readiness bar ("100%") rather than what was verified. Enrolled students show "Below: TOPIK" in red (requirements changed after admission) — alarming and irrelevant after enrolment. |
| "Request loop verified" | It works, but **E2E runs leave data in the demo**: the demo applicant Priya Nair carries 6 requests titled "E2E bank certificate 1790618525316…". The global teardown purges E2E *accounts*, not rows E2E tests create on seeded applications. |
| "Analytics: each chart answers a question" | "Applications over time" is a **flat line at 0** for 26 weeks (the daily rollup has no rows for this tenant) while the funnel says 9 were submitted. The segment chart uses tangerine as an ordinary series colour. China: admitted 1 / arrived 3 (lifecycle columns mix application- and enrolment-based counts). |
| "Agency document review: fast" | The preview pane is a **blank white rectangle** at 1440; Verify is enabled with "0 of 5 checked"; details show raw values `SKIPPED` (virus scan) and `VI` (language); title and subtitle repeat "Bank balance certificate". |
| "Agency Messages" | Opens on "Pick a conversation" (one extra click every time); every row repeats the subject "Your study-in-Korea team". |
| "Agency Tasks: serious tool" | The "Waiting on" column is empty for every row; the page intro says "Views overlap: pick the question you're answering." |
| "Agency students: next action column" | Not in the default columns; a counselor's own list spends a column on "Counselor" (the same name on every row). |
| "Marketing hero: one clear action" | Three competing starts above the fold at 1440 ("Find universities for me", "Explore universities", "Show my options"); on a phone the 3-question check — the most valuable thing — starts **below** the fold, under two full-width buttons. |
| "No template signals" | Marketing still has a 4-column "trust" feature row and a 4-box "Who does what" grid; the university Overview is five bordered panels; "Needs your decision" shows **9 equal rows, 4 of them zero**, and puts "Enrolled students at risk" (not an admissions decision) in the decision queue. |

# 25. V4 Design & Interaction Strategy

**One sentence:** V4 removes contradictions and repetition before it adds anything — every screen gets one named next action, one cost model, one meaning per state, and the densest honest layout for its audience.

## 25.1 Principles applied to every screen

1. **One cost model.** A program's cost is always "First year, estimated: ₩A–₩B" (tuition + fees + living, before scholarship) from the budget service; tuition-only figures are labelled "Tuition per year"; semester figures only where the university publishes them, labelled as such.
2. **Say it once.** A missing item appears in one place per screen. Lanes (You / Hangyul & counselor / University) are the single checklist of the application workspace.
3. **Name the thing, then the reason, then the consequence.** "Fix your academic transcript — it needs an apostille. Your Pusan application can't be submitted until this is fixed. Due Oct 20."
4. **Time is information.** When a review exceeds its target, the student sees "Taking longer than usual — your counselor has been reminded" and the agency sees it in red; no silent 2-month waits.
5. **States map, enums never leak.** One state table (docs/STATE_MAP.md) drives student, agency and university wording.
6. **Density by audience.** Student 15–16 px body, generous rhythm; agency 13–14 px tables, 40 px rows; university 14 px, formal.
7. **Tangerine = act here / you are here.** Never a chart series.
8. **Rows over boxes; zeros collapse.** Queues hide empty categories into one "All clear" line.

| Student cost | Shared first-year range in discovery rows, program page, compare, budget, offers; offer shows "You pay ₩X by Oct 17 (tuition ₩Y − scholarship ₩Z)". |

| Microcopy: sentence case mid-sentence while keeping acronyms ("TOPIK", "GKS", "E2E" — a bug that produced "e2E" was found in E2E screenshots and fixed with a unit test) | Polish, trust | `lib/workspace.ts` `lc()` |

- **Home and application page name the same next step.** Home used the earliest task ("Write your study plan"), the application page the most urgent item ("Fix your academic transcript"). New shared rule `workspace_next()` (`services/readiness.py`, mirrors `lib/workspace.ts`: university request → fix → revise essay → legalize/renew → upload → write) and next-action code `APPLICATION_ITEM` with en/ko copy; web and native home render it. Test `test_v4_coherence.py`.
- Visa tasks on home are named by the requirement ("Bank balance certificate") with the embassy rule as the explanation.
- Deadline tasks name the program ("Submit your Business Administration (BBA) application to Chung-Ang University", `task.submitProgramApplication`) — agency Deadlines showed identical titles for two programs.
- Tasks of withdrawn/rejected/finished applications no longer appear on the student home (found as an order-dependent test failure; a real stale-item bug).

## 26.8 Native apps

- Deadlines formatted as the Korean calendar date on every screen of all three apps (`f.deadline`/`kstDayMonth` in `packages/mobile-ui`); the V3 "Oct 21 vs Oct 20" came from formatting KST date-times in the device time zone (reproduced with `TZ=Pacific/Auckland`).
- `taskTitle` helper keeps acronyms ("Review TOPIK certificate"); server fallback title fixed at the source.
- Student: home handles `APPLICATION_ITEM` (Lan's native home now matches web); "Coming up" no longer repeats the next action; application screen = one named next step + three lanes; late review state; visa leads with the requirement name and folds completed steps; discovery university-first with the first-year range; program page one cost model and "Continue your application".
- Agency: Tasks opens on the first view with work; Messages drops the repeated subject; Verify disabled until checks are ticked.
- University: home drops the duplicate row and three "Too few to rate" metrics; Pipeline defaults to the current intake; decision buttons no longer clip; status history in words.
- Verification level: see §27.6.

## 26.9 Final integration fixes (found during the gates)

- **Tier vocabulary was different on web and native.** For the same student, native showed "Strong 18 · Possible 13" and web "Strong 31 · Possible 0": web grouped engine COMPETITIVE with STRONG and called REACH (a requirement *not* met) "Possible match". Now everywhere — student web, native, agency Catalog, public quick check — **Strong match** = STRONG, **Possible match** = COMPETITIVE (meets the requirements, something needs attention), **Not eligible yet** = REACH (listed first, "one step away") and NOT_ELIGIBLE. The anonymous check labels REACH "One step away", never "Possible". Korean: 적합 / 확인 필요 / 아직 지원 불가 (native previously said "지원 가능", i.e. "can apply").
- **Two native-only crashes**, invisible in the web renderer, found by running the student app on an Android emulator: (1) `expo-notifications` throws on import in Expo Go (SDK ≥ 53) and took down the root layout — now loaded lazily and skipped in Expo Go, where in-app notifications remain the source of truth; (2) `transform: []` on SVG chevrons crashes react-native-svg on Android — new `flipStyle()` passes no transform in LTR (`packages/mobile-ui/src/theme.ts`).
- **Agency Messages 500** under concurrency: opening a thread could mark it read twice at once and hit the unique constraint. Now an idempotent upsert (`POST /conversations/{id}/read`), verified with 12 concurrent calls and a test.
- **Accessibility** (axe): invalid `aria-pressed` on radio-role buttons, a non-`li` child in the message list, non-focusable scroll region — fixed.

# 27. V4 Final Stakeholder Review

*Fresh walkthrough of the final build after `npm run db:reset`, by persona, at 390 and 1440 (and native on Android). Evidence: `docs/qa/v4/after/` (first viewport + `full/`), `docs/qa/v4/after/metrics.json` vs `docs/qa/v4/before/metrics.json`, `docs/qa/v4/after/mobile-android/`. Expert walkthrough — no external participants.*

## 27.1 Acceptance questions

| Question | Answer after V4 |
|---|---|
| Would a 19-year-old know what to do without explanation? | Yes for the core loop: home and the application page name the same single item with why, consequence and date ("Fix your academic transcript … can't be submitted until this is fixed · Due Oct 20"). Remaining jargon is explained where it appears (apostille steps per country). |
| Would a parent understand the total cost? | Yes: one "First year, estimated ₩A–₩B" range everywhere, cash before arrival, monthly living, what is not included, and on offers "You pay ₩3,138,800 by Oct 17 (tuition − scholarship)". |
| Would they trust it with a passport? | The privacy statement, verified-document reuse and honest late-review copy help; trust is still limited by being a demo with no real company proof (business gap). |
| Understand an apostille? | Yes — only the student's country path, with source and verification date, at the point of need. |
| Why a program fits / why they can't apply? | Yes — Strong / Possible / Not eligible yet with the exact requirement ("TOPIK 3 required — you have TOPIK 2") and what unlocks it. |
| What happens after admission? | Offer page lists the next five steps and the amount due; visa centre leads with the requirement name; housing/arrival activate from the visa stage. |
| Mobile primary? | Web at 390 is the reference design; native student app now runs on Android with the same next step, lanes and cost model. |
| Could a counselor manage 200 students here? | The list is a scannable single-line table with Waiting on + Next action, saved views, deadline filter and keyboard navigation; Today is a work queue whose every number opens exactly its records. At 1,000 students the list endpoint p50 is 34 ms (V3 benchmark, unchanged). |
| Manager understands risk in 30 s? | Today's queue + "Cases waiting on: 5 Us · 6 Student · 2 University" + caseload by phase. Case-ageing and capacity views are still thin (§28). |
| Review fast? | Document loop: 5 checks + V → next document in 189 ms, 0 mouse clicks; request correction C → 1 → Ctrl+Enter. |
| Internal vs external impossible to confuse? | Mode switch + audience line ("Hà will see this" / "Only your team sees this") + amber dashed surface + different send label. |
| Admissions faster than email? | Overview lists only real decisions; the applicant page answers eligibility (incl. language score) and documents in the first screen; request → exact note reaches student and agency and flows back. |
| Management trusts analytics? | Every rate shows numerator/denominator/intake/population; the funnel defaults to one intake; impossible counts and the empty chart are gone. |
| Hangyul's value visible to a university? | Yes: pre-verified documents ("7/7 verified"), requirement comparison, and the post-admission lifecycle (visa → arrival → enrolment → retention). |
| Does any screen still look like generated SaaS? | Much less: no KPI grids, zeros collapse, rows over boxes. Remaining template-feel: agency Performance still has five bordered blocks; some secondary pages (student Scholarships/Support, agency Consultations/Team) were not recomposed in V4. |
| Four products differentiated? | Yes — student is warm and spacious (15–16 px, one action), agency dense (40 px rows, keyboard), university formal (requirement tables, defined rates), marketing editorial (one interactive start). |
