# 54. V8 Final Hostile Re-audit & Remaining Gaps

Scorecard: `docs/qa/v8/SCORECARD.md`. V7 baseline 61 → **V8 87/100**. The evidence and the reasons points were withheld are in the scorecard.

**What a hostile reviewer would still say**
1. Nothing in V8 has been validated with a real student, counselor, admissions officer or parent. Every improvement is a measured proxy (screens, clicks, sideways tables, load) or an AI judgement.
2. The synthetic blind test did not show a clear visual preference for V8. The collapsed icon rail at 1024 px costs wayfinding; reviewers preferred a labelled sidebar.
3. The marketing hero and most section anatomy are still Eduan's. Only "Hangyul at work" is a Hangyul-native composition.
4. Five agency secondary pages (Catalog, Team, Templates, Providers/Services, Submissions) were verified but not recomposed.
5. University analytics is longer than in V7 (7.1 screens at 1024) because Overview content moved there; the review page's evidence table starts below the fold at 1024.
6. Three university tables still scroll sideways on phones.
7. ar/ur/fa students see a mix: student namespace partly or entirely English, with a banner. Ten new locales have only `common`.
8. Desktop LCP (about 2.0 s) is slower than V7's 1.66 s measurement and sits right at the aspirational target.

**Remaining gaps**

| Kind | Gap |
|---|---|
| Product | Agency secondary pages above; Today KPI strip/actions per row; university "select all matching"; analytics length; phone tables; student visa page 5+ phone screens; label-vs-rail trade-off |
| Business | Real service pricing (`is_demo` prices); partner agreements behind external channels; verified catalogue figures |
| External | WhatsApp/Zalo/KakaoTalk/email/SMS providers, payment providers (Stripe/Toss), storage/AV scanning, scheduled-jobs worker; all shown as not connected on `/hq/readiness` |
| Legal | MOE university–agency standard agreement; PIPA cross-border consent; recruitment-fee legality (unchanged from ROADMAP) |
| Human research | All four V8 protocols (student, agency, university, parent); human blind test; human translation review (no HUMAN_REVIEWED locale); iOS never run |

# 55. V9 Independent Final-Service Audit

*2026-10-10, before any V9 code change. Method: REPORT §1–54 and every linked document re-read as a list of claims; the V8 score (87/100) was not inherited. The running system (dev stack, fresh start, dev database as left by V8) was used as each persona; **436 baseline views** were captured with `scripts/qa/v9-capture.mjs` — every routed page as the right persona at 390/1024/1440 (consoles also 768), and the nine key screens at all ten widths 320–1728 — into `docs/qa/v9/before/` with metrics (`metrics.json`). Server answers were checked through the API (`/tmp` helper signing in through Demo access) and the database. Fresh research ran in parallel (§56).*

## 55.1 The question V9 asks

Not "what feature is missing" but "**which job does the user still finish outside Hangyul, or with avoidable work, mistakes or doubt?**" Each finding below names the job, the evidence and the work it still causes.

## 55.2 Top 30 problems (ranked by harm to the job)

| # | Who | Job | Evidence (2026-10-10) | Work / risk it causes today |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Student (no TOPIK) | "Can I realistically study in Korea?" | Quick check Nepal · Bachelor's · no test → **0 programs**, "21 more with TOPIK 3"; the 10 Korean-language-program routes that accept her today are never mentioned | The most common real student is told "no" and goes to an agency consultation or Google |
| 2 | Parent / student | "How much, to whom, when?" | `GET /me/budget` lines have amount + basis only — no payee, timing or refundability; insurance and visa fee "no reliable figure yet" although researched figures exist; visa **funds to show** (e.g. Myanmar KRW 20M, 6-month history) live only in the visa route | Parents learn the biggest money requirement at the visa stage; arithmetic by hand |
| 3 | Parent | Follow cost, dates and progress | No sponsor surface (V8: "not built") | Screenshots and chat forwarding; no privacy boundary |
| 4 | Student (non-en) | Use the app in my language | 38 of 55 locales have **no** student namespace; vi/ne/my: writing 24 %, success 62–63 %, concierge 67–68 %; ja 71 %, ru 57 %, zh-Hant 66 %; th, id, hi, bn, ur 0 % (`locales/_meta.json`) | English in the middle of the journey for most markets |
| 5 | Visitor | Trust the claims | Marketing counter "**46** languages supported in Hangyul Univ" — stale (55 exist) and an overclaim (most are marketing-only) | Trust damage the moment a student switches language |
| 6 | Student (Burmese, phone) | Read the home screen | `student/home-myanmar@390`: bottom-tab labels wrap to two lines and clip; photo credit overlaps the band title | Looks broken in the priority script |
| 7 | Student | Know who sees my passport | Dossier rows carry `applications[].sent` and consents exist, but no screen says who can see a document, where it was sent, retention, or what can be withdrawn | Hesitation at upload; agencies collect by chat instead |
| 8 | Counselor | Know who must act | Waiting-on values `us/student/university/external`; "Us" hides counselor vs agency team vs Hangyul; agency list shows "Next action: *Apply for your residence card*" (student voice) on a row that waits on **us** to reply | Wrong person chases; counselor re-reads threads |
| 9 | Counselor | Start the day | Two parallel views: ranked case queue (`/agency/today/queue`) and eight category counts (`/agency/today`); no work-type filter on the ranked list | Two mental models of the same work |
| 10 | Manager | Balance workload | Team = profile cards; capacity one agency number (60) split evenly; no expertise, availability, review/visa/service load | Assignment by memory; the Excel roster survives |
| 11 | Counselor (VN agency) | Send standard messages | 12 templates, all organisation scope, **en/ko only**, no payment/arrival/housing kinds | Retyped Vietnamese messages in KakaoTalk/Zalo |
| 12 | Counselor | Track submissions | "Ready to submit" shows only the authorised-submission fixture; guided submissions awaiting confirmation (every real university) are not a queue | Parallel spreadsheet of who submitted / who has a receipt |
| 13 | Counselor | Record a consultation | Meetings are a Tasks view; notes, decisions, follow-ups and next appointment are not one record on the student timeline | Notes in Notion/notebooks |
| 14 | Manager | 60-second operational truth | `/agency/ops` lacks first-class "unassigned paid case" and "oldest blocked case"; load ignores reviews, visa, services | Partial answers; drill by hand |
| 15 | Manager | Improve process quality | Outcome metrics exist (V5) but not as process quality (correction loops, revision loops, extra-document rates, turnaround, response time) with cohort + n | Quality depends on individual staff |
| 16 | Counselor | Know a message landed | No delivery state; thread not linkable to an application | "Did you see my message?" follow-ups |
| 17 | Agency staff @1024 | Find a page | Icon rail with dot separators at 1024 (`agency/today@1024`, `university/*@1024`) | Hover-to-read navigation (V8 blind test: labelled sidebar preferred) |
| 18 | University reviewer | Decide on evidence | `university/applicant@1024`: header + decision panel ("Make offer" as the dominant button) fill the first viewport; requirement ↔ evidence starts below the fold (3.9 screens) | Decision before evidence; scrolling per applicant |
| 19 | University reviewer (phone) | Read evidence | Sideways tables at 390/360: analytics, cohorts, partnership, **applicant @360** | Core content off-screen |
| 20 | University manager | Answer recruitment questions | Analytics 7.1 screens at 1024, 7.7 at 390; organised by sections, not questions | Exports to Excel to find answers |
| 21 | University admin | Change a requirement safely | Proposals + history exist; no impact on currently matching prospective students | Changes made blind |
| 22 | University staff | Bulk work | Selection covers the current page only | Repeat per page or email |
| 23 | Hangyul ops | Judge partner agencies | No partner-quality view with cohort/n; readiness page not classified by launch category (credentials / agreement / legal / human review / infrastructure) | Agency quality by anecdote |
| 24 | Student | Visa next step | Visa page 5.3–5.7 phone screens (Bảo, Hnin, Lan); route money text arrives as English research fields (`financial.amount_en`) | Bureaucracy by scrolling; English leakage |
| 25 | Student | Discovery scan | Zero-count groups shown ("Needs your grades 0", "Not eligible yet 0"); scholarship and unlock hidden until expanded; early-student discovery still 7.1 phone screens | Noise; expand-to-find |
| 26 | Visitor | First impression | Hero = Eduan h6 banner + index-7 tiles; section anatomy (eyebrow pills, outline tickers, outline counters, CTA over footer) still Eduan's | Looks like a template site |
| 27 | Agency staff | Services queue | Opens on an empty "New · needs owner 0" tab while 2–3 cases wait elsewhere; providers list not operational (no agreement status, open/late cases) | Extra clicks; partner claims unclear |
| 28 | Everyone | Phone pages earn their length | 56 of the captured phone views have no primary action in the first viewport (many legitimately lists); marketing services/how/home 8.6–9.0 screens | Scrolling without a next step |
| 29 | All | Recovery from real-world failure | Some cases are tested piecemeal (document expiry and max age, wrong university in essays, connector `NotConfigured`, flight delay, cancellations); **no** test covers requirement change after an application, a staff member leaving (open work orphaned), payment callback delay, message-provider failure, housing provider cancellation, nationality or target-intake change mid-journey, or duplicate applications as one adversarial suite | Breakage when reality changes is found by users, not tests |
| 30 | Business | Run at real scale | No validation with 200 students per counselor or 1,000 applicants per university in the UI | Unknown cliff at launch size |

| "E2E 47/47 deterministic" | Not re-run before V9 (re-run in §63). |

# 56. V9 Global Study-Abroad Operating Benchmark

*Fresh research 2026-10-10 (80 sources: 51 read in full, 9 search excerpts, 16 vendor claims, 4 inaccessible) in `docs/research/v9-operating-model.md` + `v9-sources.json`; visa and arrival playbooks re-validated against current embassy, KVAC, visa-portal, HCCH and HiKorea sources in `docs/research/v9-visa-revalidation.md` and `v9-arrival-revalidation.md` (corrections applied in §62). V8 research is kept in `COMPETITOR_BENCHMARK.md`; the V9 section is new at its top. This section benchmarks **workflows**, not features.*

## 56.1 What changed in the world since V8

| Finding | Source (research doc) | Product consequence |
|---|---|---|
| MOJ draft package (2026-10-07): agency details **mandatory on the Certificate of Admission** (H2-2026 target), overseas **agency registration** with Korean missions (H2-2027), university **visa-refusal-rate assessment** feeding visa screening | §2 #1–2 [S1–S3] | Record the agency's legal identity, registration status and responsible counselor per case now; university-facing agency quality must include visa outcomes. Status: draft — shown as "announced", never as law. |
| Proof of funds splitting: TOPIK 4 / KIIP 4 exemption (H2-2026), deposit scheme for high-risk countries (H1-2027) | §2 #3 | The money plan must model **money to show** per route with effective dates; today's rule stays until a dated change is in force. |
| MOE standard university–agency agreement announced (Oct 2026), **text not public**; refund-after-visa-denial to the student's own account | §2 #5–6 | Refund terms belong on every payment line; refund case on visa refusal; agreement disclosures are a legal dependency (§64). |
| Fraud at scale (forged degrees, TOPIK proxy ring, forged leases, temporary deposits ruled unlawful) | §2 #7 | Flags with reasons + human decision; never auto-reject; tell families that funds must be genuinely held. |
| Tuition via money changers/proxies can freeze the student's virtual account | §2 #8 | Payment-route guard: pay the university directly, own name. |
| Rails (UWAY, JinhakApply, Gradnet, Study in Korea): still **no** public API, agency account, batch upload or status callback; KU requires personal application; Jinhak terms forbid third-party ID use | §6 | Connector truth unchanged: GUIDED_EXTERNAL everywhere; AUTHORIZED_AGENCY only with a recorded legal basis. Watch NIIED one-stop and FIMS. |
| Universities run on e-mail, post, Google Forms, per-fee virtual accounts, nine mailboxes; immigration visits campuses for residence cards | §2 #11–13, §5 | The university's value from Hangyul = structured requests and outcomes on one case; residence card timing depends on the university batch. |
| Agency CRMs (Agentcis, Meritto) sell pipelines/checklists, **not** assignment, SLA or ageing | §2 #15 | Hangyul's agency differentiation is operational: one queue, waiting-on, weighted capacity, SLA, ageing. |
| Parent visibility nearly absent (Crimson meeting summaries only) | §2 #18 | Consent-based sponsor view is a genuine gap, with no essay content. |
| UK / Australia / Canada measure agents (visa refusal, retention, LOA verification) | §2 #19 | Partner-agency quality must be process + outcome metrics with cohorts. |

## 56.2 How the work is done today vs. what Hangyul must beat

The stage-by-stage map (lead → graduation, 46 stages) is §3 of the research doc; each stage marks manual copying, re-upload, manual reminders, Excel, chat switching, website searching, missed deadlines and conflicting state. The blueprint (`docs/SERVICE_BLUEPRINT.md`, §57) answers each mark. The ones that shape V9:

| Job | Best current reference | Bar Hangyul must exceed |
|---|---|---|
| "Can I go?" without TOPIK | IDP FastLane (document-free, but "instant offer" without the non-binding label) | Honest routes (language program first / English track / direct) with counts from published requirements, labelled "not an offer" |
| Money | Wise fee display; university guides (payee, refund ladders) | One plan: payee, timing, refundable, basis; money to *show* separate; payment-route guard |
| Agency operations | Agentcis / Meritto pipelines; Excel + KakaoTalk/Zalo | One queue with reasons, seven-value waiting-on, weighted capacity, templates in the student's language, submissions queue |
| University review | Slate Reader (bins, queues, review-and-advance) | Requirement · evidence · status first; review-and-advance; safe bulk incl. select-all-matching |
| University value | Nobody connects admission → CoA → visa → arrival → retention | Partnership evidence with cohorts and denominators, including visa outcomes the MOJ will score |
| Parents | Crimson summaries | Read-only, revocable sponsor view without private content |

**Do not copy** (research §8): unexplained success rates (ApplyBoard 95 %), speed guarantees (Leverage one-day/one-week/one-month), "instant offer" without "not binding", hidden fees, language versions that disagree, AI-written statements, AI credibility scores.

# 57. V9 Service Blueprint

The full blueprint is `docs/SERVICE_BLUEPRINT.md`: five phases (discover & qualify · prepare · submit & decide · visa · arrival & settlement), one row per step with student / Hangyul / agency / university actions, automation, external system, data, error risk, SLA, escalation, next state and code status, followed by the manual-work → automation table.

**Where the blueprint shows a locally solvable gap (V9 scope):**

| Gap in the blueprint | V9 answer | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Quick check has no route when language blocks the degree | Routes | §58 S1 |
| Money: no payee/timing/refund; funds to show only at visa stage; no payment-route guard; no refund path on visa refusal | Money plan + refund case | §58 S2 |
| Parents switch to chat | Sponsor view | §58 S3 |
| Document privacy not answered at upload | "Who can see this?" | §58 S4 |
| "Us" hides who acts | Seven-value waiting-on | §59 A1 |
| Two parallel agency queues | One work queue | §59 A2 |
| Capacity by memory; staff leaving orphans work | Team + weighted load + reassignment | §59 A4 |
| Guided submissions not tracked as a queue | Submissions queue across methods | §59 A7 |
| Agency identity not on the case | Agency legal identity + registration status per case, visible to the university | §59 A12 |
| University decides before seeing evidence at 1024 | Evidence first; review-and-advance | §60 U2 |
| Rule changes made blind | Impact preview | §60 U6 |
| Partner agency quality by anecdote | Process + outcome quality with cohort/n | §61 H2 |

**Stays outside by design or dependency** (blueprint Status EXTERNAL/GUIDED): official submission on the rails, fees and tuition paid to the university, embassy actions, flight data, housing inventory, OCR, external message delivery, payments — each with a truthful state in the product and a dependency in §64.

# 58. V9 Student Experience

*Written before any V9 code change. Persona used throughout: Aarati's situation without her advantages — 19, Kathmandu, budget Android phone (360–390 px), limited English, **no TOPIK**, parents pay. "PRIMARY QUESTION" is written for every major page before it is touched; a page with two unrelated questions is split or recomposed.*

## 58.1 What a zero-knowledge student actually meets today (verified 2026-10-10)

| Moment | What the product does | Why it fails the job |
|---|---|---|
| Quick check: Nepal · Bachelor's · "Neither yet" | `POST /public/quick-eligibility` → **0 programs**, 31 "not yet", "21 more with TOPIK 3" | The honest answer to "Can I realistically study in Korea?" is **yes — through a Korean language program first** (10 language-institute programs in the catalogue accept her today; that is the route most students without TOPIK actually take) or an English-taught track with IELTS. The product answers "no" and stops. |
| Budget | First-year range, cash before arrival; insurance and visa fee "no reliable figure yet" | The researched visa fee, residence-card fee (KRW 35,000, official) and the **funds the family must show for the visa** (e.g. Myanmar KRW 20,000,000 for Seoul, 6-month history, certificate ≤ 30 days old — already in the visa route data) never reach the money screens. The parent's biggest money question — "how much must be in our account, for how long?" — has no answer before the visa stage. No line says who receives the money, when, or whether it is refundable. |
| Discovery "For you" | Tier tabs with counts including **zeros** ("Needs your grades 0", "Not eligible yet 0") | Zero tabs are noise; rows don't show the scholarship or "what would unlock this" until expanded. |
| Documents | Requirement-centric dossier, reuse per application | Nothing tells the student **who can see a passport or bank certificate, which university received it, how long it is kept, or how to withdraw sharing** — the privacy questions the brief lists. The data exists (`applications[].sent`, consent records). |
| Parents | No sponsor surface (V8 decided "not built") | Families fund and decide; today the student screenshots the app or forwards KakaoTalk messages. |
| Language | `vi/ne/my` student 100 %, but V5 namespaces (dossier 87–91 %, success 62 %, writing 24 %, concierge 67 %, visaroute 90 %); 38 locales have **no** student namespace; ja 71 %, ru 57 %, zh-Hant 66 %; th, id, hi, bn, ur 0 % | A Burmese or Nepali student meets English on the writing, concierge and success screens; a Thai, Indonesian, Hindi, Bengali or Urdu student gets an English app with a notice. |

## 58.2 V9 student changes (each removes a step, a decision, a tool switch or an uncertainty)

| # | Change | Removes | Primary question it answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | **Routes, not a dead end.** When language blocks the chosen degree, the quick check, Discovery and the early home show the realistic routes from the catalogue: (a) *Korean language program first* — N programs accept you now, typical length, cost of that year, what changes for the visa (D-4-1 → D-2), then which degree programs open at TOPIK 3; (b) *English-taught* — N programs, the IELTS/TOEFL level they need; (c) the smallest test step that opens the most. Counts come from the matching engine; no probability. | "No" answers for the most common real student; Google + agency consultation | Can I realistically study in Korea? |
| S2 | **One money plan.** One server model (`services/money.py`) used by Budget, program page, offers and visa: every line has payer → **payee**, **when** (application / offer / before visa / on arrival / monthly), **refundable** (yes / no / per university rule / unknown), **basis** (Official · Estimate · Sample · Unknown with source + date), plus a separate **"Money you must show (not pay)"** block from the student's visa route (amount, holding period, whose name, certificate age). Researched official figures (visa fee by route, residence card) replace "no reliable figure yet" where a source exists. | Parent arithmetic; "which number is real"; surprise at the visa stage | How much will everything cost, who do we pay, and when? |
| S3 | **Sponsor view (permission-based).** The student creates a read-only, expiring, revocable link for a parent/sponsor and chooses what it shows (money plan, family documents needed, key dates, admission and visa progress, arrival plan). It **never** shows messages, essays, counselor notes or document files. The sponsor reads it in their own language without an account. Every view is audited; the student sees when it was last opened and can revoke. | Screenshots and chat forwarding to parents | What does my family need to know and do? |
| S4 | **"Who can see this?" on every document**: you · your counselor (agency name, by your consent of date) · Hangyul reviewers · universities it was sent to (with application and date) · how long it is kept · what you can withdraw (sharing with an agency; not a file already submitted to a university). Plain words, no jargon. | Trust anxiety before uploading a passport | Is my passport safe here? |
| S5 | Discovery: zero-count groups collapse; each row answers *can I apply · why · missing · first-year cost · deadline · language · scholarship · what unlocks it* without expanding (unlock line on the row when one step away). | Expand-to-find | Where can I apply? |
| S6 | Visa page ≤ 3 phone screens: route · ready · needed now · who provides · where the official action happens · next; the rest folds. | Scrolling bureaucracy | What do I do for my visa now? |
| S8 | **Refund path**: a visa refusal opens a refund case with the university's refund rule (or "your counselor confirms"), the own-account rule and elapsed days; every payment line has a payment-route guard (pay the university directly, in the student's name — never via money changers). | What happens to my money if it goes wrong? |
| S7 | **Localization finished** for the core journey (§58.4). | English mid-journey | — |

**Primary questions (student):** Home — *What is the one thing I should do now, and where am I?* · Discovery — *Where can I apply?* · Program — *Can I apply here, what will it cost, by when?* · Compare — *Which of these differs in a way that matters to me?* · Budget — *How much, to whom, when?* · Applications — *Where does each application stand and what is next?* · Application — *What is left before submission, and who is doing it?* · Documents — *Which documents are ready, which need me, and who sees them?* · Writing — *What does my reviewer want me to change?* · Visa — *What do I need now for my visa?* · Housing — *Where will I live and what is confirmed?* · Arrival — *What happens when I land?* · Messages — *What did my team say and what do I answer?* · Sponsor — *What does the family need to pay, show and know?*

## 58.3 Not built (feature theatre test)

AI chatbot, acceptance score, "chance" meter, gamified readiness, a separate onboarding wizard (progressive profile already explains what each answer unlocks — verified, kept).

## 58.4 Localization target

A locale counts as **complete for students** only when (1) every key of the student-journey manifest (keys reachable from student web screens, server-sent codes included) is translated, (2) the leak scan finds no unexplained English on the core screens for that locale, (3) a synthetic review scored ≥ 4/5 on every dimension for the four reader profiles (18–20 student, 23–29 graduate, 35–49 parent, 50–65 parent). Locales that do not meet it are not offered as a student-app language; they are offered on the public site only, and the picker says so. Priority locales first: ko, en, vi, ne, my, uz, mn, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ja, th, id, hi, bn, ur, ar, ru — plus kk, ky, fil (visa-priority countries).

# 59. V9 Agency Operating System

*Persona: a counselor with 200 students starting at 9 AM; a manager who must answer six questions in 60 seconds.*

## 59.1 Verified gaps

| Area | Today (2026-10-10) | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Waiting on | Server values `us / student / university / external` (none) | "Us" hides **who**: the named counselor, the agency team (unassigned review), or Hangyul (assignment, payment, ops). The brief's model is Student · Counselor · Agency · Hangyul · University · External · No one, with one meaning everywhere. |
| Work queue | Today = case ranking with reasons (`/agency/today/queue`) **plus** eight category counts (`/agency/today`) | Two ways to see the same work; no filter by work type on the ranked list. |
| Team | `/agency/team`: name, role, title, languages, active | No countries, university or degree/major expertise per person, no personal capacity, no availability (leave), no weighted workload or review load; capacity is one agency-wide number (60) split evenly. |
| Templates | 12 templates, all ORG scope, en/ko only, kinds without payment/arrival/housing | A Vietnamese agency has no Vietnamese template; no personal/team scope in practice; no permission rule for editing organisation templates. |
| Providers / Services | V5 queue and providers list | Not operational: no per-provider open cases, SLA, last issue, agreement status as the first fact. |
| Submissions | V6 "Ready to submit" for authorised fixture | Not a queue across all methods: Ready · Needs final review · Authorized · Submitted · Confirmation missing · University received · Issue. |
| Consultations | Tasks view "Meetings" | A meeting's notes, decisions, follow-up tasks and next appointment are not one record in the student workspace. |
| Manager | `/agency/ops`: backlog, ageing, load, SLA, deadlines, stages | "Oldest blocked case" and "unassigned paid case" not first-class; load ignores reviews, visa and service cases. |
| Quality | Outcome metrics (V5) on Performance | Not organised as process quality (correction loops, revision loops, completeness at submission, university and visa extra-document rates, turnaround, student response time, arrival issues) with cohort and n. |
| Messages | Channel model; in-app only | No per-message delivery state shown; messages cannot be tied to an application or task from the thread. |

## 59.2 V9 agency changes

| # | Change | Primary question |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | **One "waiting on" model** (`services/waiting.py`): STUDENT · COUNSELOR · AGENCY · HANGYUL · UNIVERSITY · EXTERNAL · NONE with one reason; legacy `us` accepted as an alias in filters. Used by caseload rows, views, Today, workspace header, applications, university "waiting for applicant" and student "who is doing what". STATE_MAP updated. | Why is this case not moving, and who has to act? |
| A2 | **One work queue**: the ranked list absorbs the category counts as type filters (Documents · Writing · Applications · Messages · University requests · Visa · Services · Deadlines · Tasks); each row = reason + next action + deadline + owner. | Who needs me now? |
| A3 | Workspace header: *Why it is not moving · Next action · Waiting on · Deadline · Owner* before any tab. | Same |
| A4 | **Team rebuilt around operations**: per member languages, countries, university expertise, degree/major expertise, availability (on leave until …), personal capacity; **weighted load** with a visible, editable weight table (active applications, deadlines ≤ 14 days, document reviews, writing reviews, visa cases, service cases, conversations waiting) → load vs capacity and SLA risk; reassignment when someone leaves (open items listed and moved with a reason). | Who can take more, and who needs help? |
| A5 | **Templates**: kinds incl. payment, arrival, housing, visa; scopes personal · team · organisation; edit permission by scope (organisation = owner/manager); language variants of one template; inserting picks the student's language. | What do I say, in the student's language, without retyping? |
| A6 | **Providers & services**: per provider — agreement status first (no agreement recorded → never called a partner), service types, open cases, late cases, last issue, contact; services queue unchanged in logic. | Which arrival services are at risk and with whom? |
| A7 | **Submissions queue** across every method with the seven states above, derived from submission records and evidence; "Confirmation missing" and "Issue" first. | Which applications are stuck between ready and received? |
| A8 | **Meetings in the workspace**: one meeting record = notes + decisions + follow-up tasks + next appointment, shown on the student's timeline; Tasks keeps the "Meetings" view. | What did we decide and what happens next? |
| A9 | **Manager in 60 s**: oldest blocked case, overloaded counselor (weighted), SLA breaches, deadlines at risk, slowest stage, **unassigned paid case** — each one click to the exact records. | Where is my operation failing today? |
| A10 | **Process quality** (manager): correction loops, revision loops, completeness at submission, university extra-document rate, missed deadlines, review turnaround, student response time, visa extra-document rate, arrival issues — cohort + n, n < 5 withheld, no causal claims. | Where does our process create rework? |
| A12 | **Agency identity on every case**: legal entity, registration status ("not recorded" until real), responsible counselor and any sub-agent — shown on the case and to the university, ready for the announced CoA field. | Who is responsible for this applicant? |
| A11 | **Messages**: delivery state per message (sent · read · failed); thread can be linked to an application; "make task" keeps the link; external channels still "Not connected" (nothing simulated). | Did the student get it, and what is it about? |

## 62.1 Research and data (no UI)

- **Operating-model research** (`docs/research/v9-operating-model.md`, 80 sources): 46-stage map of how agencies/universities work today, agency and university operations, submission-rail reality re-checked, parent/sponsor practice, dark patterns, 20 concrete removals for Hangyul. - **Visa/arrival revalidation** (`v9-visa-revalidation.md`, `v9-arrival-revalidation.md`): 218 visa rows re-checked (149 same, 25 changed, 38 newly confirmed, 26 still unconfirmed), 31 arrival facts (17 same, 3 changed, 2 newly confirmed, 9 unconfirmed). **46 + 10 corrections applied** by `server/scripts/v9_visa_research_apply.py` from untouched baselines (`docs/research/archive/*.v8-2026-09-29.json`), loaded as new route versions (history kept) by `scripts/v9_visa_data.py`. ## 63.3 Localisation

The V9 gate: a locale is offered in the **student app** only when every key of the student-journey manifest is translated **and** a recorded leak scan found 0 English leaks on ~166 page views (390 + 1440, 10 personas). Namespace-level coverage in `npm run i18n:check` stays below 100 % for these locales by design — it counts staff-only subtrees (agency items, reviewer workspace, concierge staff) that the student app never renders and the manifest excludes.

| Locale | Student manifest | Leak scan (≈166 page views × 390/1440) | Synthetic review (min of 20 scores) |
|---|---|---|---|
| en | source language | — | — |
| ko · vi · ne · my · uz · mn · ja · zh-Hans · zh-Hant · ar · ru · kk · ky · tr · th · id · hi · bn · ur · fil (**20**) | **100 %** | **0 leaks** | **4 / 5** |

All 20 pass. Live status: `packages/i18n/locales/_student_status.json` (the picker and the in-app notice read it; a locale that is complete for the student journey no longer shows a "partial translation" banner — it used to measure raw namespace coverage, which counts staff-only subtrees). The leak scanner itself was corrected twice during this pass: it now waits for `<html lang>` to be the locale under test (a slow first load had been reported as English on `/login`), and it treats scholarship programme names and Hangyul's own programme names as catalogue/brand text, the way it already treated university and program names.

**No locale is HUMAN_REVIEWED.** Each `docs/qa/v9/l10n/<loc>.md` carries the line "synthetic review by an AI model — not a human review" and a residual-risk list. The other 35 locales keep the marketing site and are **not** offered as a student-app language; the picker says so.

Terminology fixed across locales during the pass: `verdict.COMPETITIVE`/`REACH` were swapped or odds-worded in nine locales; English `common:tier` itself still said "Competitive match"/"Reach"; Korean "Possible match" had become "there is a chance". All now follow STATE_MAP.

## 63.5 What was *not* measured (and is therefore not claimed)

Re-measured in this pass and reported above: axe, visual QA, production LCP, the full Playwright suite, the 442-view capture, scale timings and the per-locale leak scans. Still **not** measured, so nothing is claimed about them:

- **Real people.** No student, parent, counselor, manager or admissions officer has used V9. Every task figure is a scripted walkthrough.
- **Human translation review.** 20 locales pass the automated gate and an AI review; none has been read by a human. No locale is HUMAN_REVIEWED.
- **The human blind visual test.** V8's synthetic round was inconclusive; the human round has not run (protocol §8 of `docs/research/v9-validation-protocols.md`).
- **Native apps.** The Android smoke test was not re-run in V9 (V8 ran all three apps on an emulator); the agency app still shows the pre-V9 waiting values and no V9 queue. **iOS: NOT VERIFIED** — no macOS environment exists here, and nothing about iOS is inferred.
- **RTL at V9 screens.** ar/ur/fa/he were not re-captured as a set; ar and ur pass the leak scan, which renders every core screen at 390 and 1440 in RTL.
- **Anything behind a credential, agreement or legal approval** (§64): payments, storage, AV, OCR, flight data, housing inventory, external messaging, and any rail integration.

## 63.6 Scorecard

`docs/qa/v9/SCORECARD.md`: V9 rubric, baseline (V8 state) **65/100** → V9 **87.5/100**, every category re-measured. The brief's target was ≥ 95; V9 does not reach it. The missing points are almost entirely the things that need people and partners — user research, human translation review, a human visual test, real prices, verified catalogue data, provider and university agreements — and inventing them would be the dishonesty the brief forbids. The score is an engineering/product proxy. It is not a claim that the service is "100/100": user, legal, integration and human-language validation are all outstanding (§64).

## 63.7 Final hostile review — why a competitor would still tell you not to use Hangyul

*Written as a rival's product review, after V9 was built. Each point is either fixed, answered, or classified honestly as external. Nothing here is softened.*

### To a student
1. **"Nothing in it has been used by a student like you."** True. Zero real students, parents, counselors or admissions officers have used V9; every figure is a scripted walkthrough or a machine measurement. *External: user research (§64).*
2. **"The catalogue is sample data."** True for tuition, fees, deadlines and dorm costs: they carry `verification_status=DEMO`, labelled in the UI, with the dated source shown where one exists. A student planning on these numbers would be planning on demo figures. *Business dependency.*
3. **"Your language is a machine translation."** True. 20 locales have a complete, leak-scanned student journey, but **no locale has been reviewed by a human**; the app says so and offers English. *Human review (§64).*
4. **"Hangyul cannot actually submit your application."** True by design and by law: every real university requires the applicant to submit personally, so Hangyul prepares everything and hands off, then records the evidence. A competitor claiming "we submit for you" in Korea is either an authorised rail user or overstating.
5. **"You still leave for the embassy, the bank and the portal."** True; those are official acts. Hangyul removes the search and the paperwork around them, not the acts.
6. **"No one can tell you your chances."** By choice: no acceptance-rate claim, no score, no probability. A competitor advertising "95 % success" is making a claim it cannot support.

### To an agency
7. **"Your counselors would run two systems."** Partly answered: V9 has one work queue, waiting-on, templates in the student's language, submissions and meetings — but **external channels (KakaoTalk, WhatsApp, Zalo, SMS, email) are not connected**, so student conversations that live there still live there. *External: provider agreements.*
8. **"Your mobile app is behind the web."** True: the agency native app does not show the V9 queue or the seven-party waiting values; only the keys were added. *Engineering backlog.*
9. **"We only tested it at 200 students."** True: one counselor with 200 students and 1,011 applicants, p95 under 1 s on 13 endpoints. Beyond that is unmeasured.
10. **"Commission and payouts aren't there."** True: commission tracking, agency payout and sub-agent accounting are modelled only as identity and contract data. *Business/engineering.*

### To a university
11. **"It is one more inbox."** Answered where it counts (requests and decisions live on the applicant record, outcomes come back), but there is **no SIS, no SSO beyond OIDC, no scheduled export**, and no rail integration — so email and Excel do not disappear for everything. *External/infrastructure.*
12. **"Your numbers come from a handful of applicants."** True in the demo: most rates are withheld at n < 5, and that is the honest behaviour, but it also means a university sees little until real volume exists.
13. **"Agencies will be regulated and you are not ready."** Partly: V9 records agency legal identity, registration status ("Not recorded" until real) and the responsible counselor per case, ready for the announced Certificate-of-Admission field — but the MOJ package is a **draft** and the MOE standard agreement text is not public. *Legal, tracked.*

### To a parent
14. **"You cannot verify who Hangyul is."** True: no company proof, reviews, partners or outcomes exist to publish, and the product refuses to invent them. Trust today rests on transparency (sources, dates, honest states) alone.
15. **"Your money is not protected by anything in the app."** Fair: the product tells you who receives each payment, when, and whether it is refundable, warns against paying through changers or agents, and opens a refund case on a visa refusal — but refund terms, prices and the payment provider are all still external.
16. **"The sponsor page shows what the student chooses."** By design: scopes are the student's, messages/essays/notes/files are never shown. A parent wanting full visibility will not get it.

### Where the review changed the product (this pass)
The hostile pass was run against the build, not against the plan. It produced the budget-summary contradiction fix (§62.8), the match-tier vocabulary corrections, the "46 languages" and "Korean is reviewed" claims, the seeded English provider name, and the i18n load bug that could show raw keys. Everything else above is either a stated boundary or a dependency in §64.

# 64. V9 Launch Readiness & Remaining Dependencies

*Every remaining item is classified by what it needs. "CODE-COMPLETE" means the product behaves correctly and truthfully today and needs nothing from engineering; everything else names the outside thing it waits for. The same classification is generated from real settings and records on `/hq/readiness` (seven categories), so operations sees the same list. Legal detail: `docs/LEGAL_DEPENDENCIES.md`. Research protocols: `docs/research/v9-validation-protocols.md`.*

## 64.1 By category

### CODE-COMPLETE (works now; no external dependency)
One profile and dossier with reuse and per-application applicability · language routes · one money plan (payee, timing, refundability, basis) and money-to-show · sponsor view · document visibility · strategy, portfolio and writing review with the quality gate · guided submission with evidence and the seven-state submissions pipeline · visa route resolution for 14 countries from researched playbooks · arrival/housing/pickup/settlement service cases · one waiting-on model across the three consoles and the student app · agency one work queue, team weights and leave/reassignment, templates with language variants, process quality · university evidence-first review, review-and-advance, safe bulk with select-all-matching, questions-first analytics with drill-down, rule impact preview, partnership value · HQ failure list, partner quality, readiness page · adversarial recovery for 18 scenarios · the localisation gate and 20 locales' student journey.

### NEEDS CREDENTIALS (an account or key, no negotiation)
| Item | Today | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| Email (SMTP) | Not connected; in-app only | `HG_SMTP_*` |
| SMS | Not connected | `HG_SMS_*` |
| Push (Expo) | Off by default | `HG_PUSH_PROVIDER=expo`, receipts tested |

| Flight data | Manual entry, labelled "not live" | a flight data provider |
| AI provider (writing checks) | Rule-based only, nothing AI shown | `HG_AI_PROVIDER` + key (no-fabrication rules stay) |

### NEEDS PROVIDER AGREEMENT (a contract, not just a key)
WhatsApp / KakaoTalk / Zalo business messaging · payment providers (Stripe/Toss merchant account; the V9 payment callback endpoint exists and is idempotent but returns 503 until a provider is configured) · housing inventory (no listing is invented) · airport transfer providers · SIM/eSIM, insurance and relocation partners · **submission rails**: UWAY, JinhakApply, Gradnet and Study in Korea have no public API, agency account, batch upload or status callback (re-checked 2026-10-10) — watch NIIED's announced one-stop application and the MOJ's FIMS plans.

### NEEDS BUSINESS DATA
Real service prices (demo prices are flagged) · verified catalogue figures (tuition, fees, deadlines, dorm costs are sample data with `verification_status=DEMO`) · real partner contracts (no university or agency agreement is recorded; "partner" is never shown without one) · university refund rules (the refund case says "your counselor confirms") · university visa-certification tiers (unknown everywhere, so no e-visa is ever offered) · Hangyul's own photography (licensed CC0/CC BY images are used, and the Eduan template photographs have no licence recorded in the package).

### NEEDS LEGAL APPROVAL
Terms, privacy notice and consent wording · retention schedule (the product says "policy pending approval") · cross-border transfer mechanism · recruitment-fee and refund terms · agency submission authority · sponsor-access basis · MOE standard university–agency agreement (announced 2026-09-08, text not public) · MOJ draft rules (agency details on the Certificate of Admission, overseas agency registration, university visa-refusal scoring — drafts with target dates, shown nowhere as current law). Full table: `docs/LEGAL_DEPENDENCIES.md` (L1–L13).

### NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW
**No locale is HUMAN_REVIEWED** — every record says "synthetic review by an AI model — not a human review". Human translation review per locale (protocol §7) · the residual-risk lists in each `docs/qa/v9/l10n/<loc>.md` (certification tier names, Korean administrative terms, parent-facing money and visa sentences) · 14 visa fields and 9 arrival facts that need a call or email to a post (listed in `VISA_ROUTES.md` / `ARRIVAL_SERVICES.md`) · the blind visual test's human round.

### NEEDS HUMAN VALIDATION (users)
No real student, parent, counselor, manager or admissions officer has used V9. Protocols and recruitment criteria are written for 5–8 students, 3–5 parents, 5 counselors, 3 managers, 5 university admissions staff and 3 university managers (`docs/research/v9-validation-protocols.md`). **Every V9 task number is a scripted walkthrough, not an observed user.**

### NEEDS INFRASTRUCTURE
Production deployment (none exists) · TLS/HSTS/CSP · rate limiting and lockout · MFA for staff · scheduled-jobs worker (daily job runs manually; scheduled exports are shown disabled) · backups and retention jobs · penetration test · iOS build machine (iOS has never been run).

## 64.2 Launch blockers, shortest list

| Kind | Blocker |
|---|---|
| **CODE** | None known for the journeys V9 covers. Open engineering items are improvements, not blockers: the Kyrgyzstan 2027-01-01 document/language changes need the loader re-run on/after that date; JPEG/WEBP truncation is undetected; a housing case returned to the team after a provider cancellation is not listed on the Providers page; the university list's eligibility summary judges submitted applicants against the current published minimum; ~35 locales have no student journey; agency mobile does not yet show the V9 queue. |
| **BUSINESS** | Real prices, verified catalogue data, partner agreements (universities, agencies, providers), refund rules, certification tiers, own photography. |
| **EXTERNAL** | Payment, storage, AV, email/SMS/push, messaging channels, OCR, flight data, housing inventory, and any rail integration (none is available today). |
| **LEGAL** | Terms/privacy/consent/retention, recruitment fees, submission authority, cross-border transfer, sponsor access, MOE standard agreement; MOJ drafts to track. |
| **HUMAN VALIDATION** | All usability rounds, human translation review, the human blind test, and the visa/arrival fields that need confirmation from a post. |

## 64.3 What must not happen before those are closed

Do not enable `AUTHORIZED_AGENCY` for a real university, do not label a provider or university a "partner", do not take real money, do not promise a retention period, do not mark a locale HUMAN_REVIEWED, and do not describe any V9 measurement as user-validated.

# 65. V10 Koreanasha Template Audit

*2026-10-16, before any V10 code change. Method: `template-koreanasha/` inspected recursively (1 HTML page, 19 CSS,
27 JS, 46 SCSS partials, 147 images, 36 font files); the page served locally and captured at 1440×900 / 1024×768 /
768×1024 / 430×932 / 390×844 (`docs/qa/v10/koreanasha-original/`), then captured again with scroll-reveal forced
visible because AOS leaves every section at `opacity: 0` until a CDN answers. The deployed reference
<https://univ.talkhangyul.com/> was captured at the same five widths (`docs/qa/v10/koreanasha-live/`). Full
element-by-element table with SOURCE / COMPONENT / PURPOSE / CONTENT / HANGYUL USE / DECISION:
`docs/TEMPLATE_KOREANASHA_INVENTORY.md`.*

## 65.1 The finding that reframes the whole pass

**`univ.talkhangyul.com` and `template-koreanasha/` are the same build** — identical page heights at all five widths,
identical title, identical markup. One reference, verified, not two.

**And Koreanasha is itself a customised Eduan build.** `assets/css/main.css` line 5 reads
`Template Name: Eduan - School University & Online Education Template`; the class vocabulary (`h2_blog-item`,
`h6_footer-area`, `h4_faq-content`, `section-area-6`, `theme-btn`, `brand-active`) is Eduan's, and
`assets/js/main.js` is Eduan's file unmodified — it still boots ~25 Swiper instances for demo pages that do not
exist on this site.

This changes what "stop using Eduan, use Koreanasha" means in practice. The thing the user prefers is not a
different template; it is a **~500-line customisation layer** that Koreanasha prepended to Eduan's compiled CSS:

| The Koreanasha layer | Why it beats our V9 Eduan build |
|---|---|
| Floating white **pill header** — `position: fixed; top: 40px; left/right: 30px; border-radius: 60px; border: 1px solid #E5E5E5` (`main.css:293`) | The page *opens as a photograph*. V9 opens with a dark chrome band across the top. |
| **Full-viewport hero** — `.single-banner { height: 100dvh }` with a background image (`main.css:3926`) | Photography at full scale, not a 900 px band with a form card on it. |
| **Three hand-made crops**, one per breakpoint — `banner_c.webp` 4032×2250 ≥1200 px, `banner_t_c.webp` 1560×919 at 575–1199, `banner_m_c.webp` **900×1200 portrait** ≤575 (`main.css:23363, 23457`) | Exactly the "intentional focal-position/crop configuration" the brief demands, instead of one `object-fit: cover` focal point at every width. |
| Band alternation **white / `#E8EFFD`** at `pt-100 pb-90` | Every section is a distinct movement. V9 is one continuous white scroll. |
| Centred **eyebrow → two-tone headline → lead** | One typographic idea repeated; the second headline line carries the brand colour. |
| White cards, **radius 20, padding 50/45**, no border; photography at **radius 15, full column width** | Content sits on the band; photography is a first-class element. |
| Three-row **logo marquee**, alternating direction | Institutional credibility without making a claim. |

Because Koreanasha and Eduan are the same family, `packages/eduan-ui` and a new `packages/koreanasha-ui` cannot
visually disagree. The brief's "must look like ONE website" is satisfied by construction.

## 65.2 Technology

One static `index.html` (122 KB). The page **loads** ≈1.5 MB of CSS+JS — Font Awesome Pro CSS 505 KB (for four
glyphs: `angle-right`, `bars`, `star`, `times`), `main.css` 425 KB, Bootstrap 195 KB, jQuery + Swiper + 8 plugins —
and ships a further ≈750 KB that is never referenced (`jquery-ui-slider-range.js` 558 KB, select2, datepicker,
bxslider, and a second copy of Swiper as `swipper-bundle.min.js`). Translations are a 109 KB `lang.js` injected
through `innerHTML` for two languages (ko, ru). AOS and SweetAlert2 come from CDNs.

## 67.3 Scope decision for V10 — and how it changed

*Written before the console pass:* the console work would be defect repair plus the shared brand fix, not another

parts of the product that score highest.

*What actually happened:* that stood for the **operating models**, which were re-examined screen by screen
against the brief's own questions and held up (§69.10). It did **not** stand for the detail layer. Extending the
design sweep to the three consoles — which the first pass had not done — found a set of defects that no

link and button in all three consoles. Those are fixed in §69.10, and §72 no longer lists the console sweep as
outstanding.

# 68. V10 Product & Design Strategy

## 68.1 The one-line strategy

**Koreanasha's opening, V-Education's concreteness, Hangyul's substance and honesty.** Koreanasha wins the first two
seconds. V-Education wins the next thirty — it says exactly what you get, for what money, in what order, from which
humans. Hangyul wins everything after that and is the only honest one of the three, but today a student must get
past a dark photograph and a form card to discover it.

## 68.2 Design system after V10

| Surface | Foundation | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Marketing, public university discovery, public service pages | **Koreanasha layer + Hangyul brand** (`packages/koreanasha-ui`) | new in V10 |
| Student Platform | Hangyul tangerine system, sharing the Koreanasha chrome vocabulary at the login seam | kept, retuned |
| Agency / University / Hangyul Operations | **YNEX + Hangyul professional (cobalt) system** | unchanged, by design |
| Eduan | supporting component and asset source only | demoted |

Re-theming map, Koreanasha → Hangyul: primary `#1C49FF` → `#CC4E00` (white on it 4.51:1, AA) · accent text
`#145CE6` → `#B84600` (5.2:1 on white) · band tint `#E8EFFD` → `#FFF4EC` (tangerine-50) · headline ink `#1E1E1E` →
`#181A1F` · gradient headline **dropped** (no reliable fallback, fails at small sizes) · Roboto → Pretendard
Variable · card radius 20 kept, hairline border added (cards on a tinted band need an edge) · photo radius 15 → 16
· header geometry kept exactly, shadow softened from `0 0 4px rgba(0,0,0,.25)` to `0 2px 18px rgba(24,26,31,.14)` ·
section rhythm `pt-100 pb-90` → `--kn-band` 100 / 72 / 56 px (Koreanasha has no phone step-down; ours does).

## 68.3 Home composition

Each movement names the customer question it answers. Target ≤ 8 phone screens, ≤ 7 at 1440.

| # | Movement | Question answered | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Hero** — full-viewport Korean campus at golden hour, three hand-made crops, floating pill header, one promise, two actions (*Explore universities* · *Login*) | "Do I want this?" | Koreanasha DIRECT; photograph replaced |
| 2 | **Where could I study** — real programme cards: deadline, language level, first-year cost | "Where?" / "Can I?" | Hangyul V9, kept |
| 3 | **Quick check** — three questions, after the hero, never dominating it | "Can I, specifically?" | V9, moved down |
| 4 | **What Hangyul does** — four product moments from real UI states | "What complexity disappears?" | V9, restyled |
| 5 | **Real student services** — alternating image/text rows, named as nouns | "Housing? Pickup? Visa? Documents?" | Koreanasha PORT + V-Ed lesson |
| 6 | **My study journey** — numbered steps to the first week in Korea | "What happens after I apply?" | V9 + V-Ed lesson |
| 7 | **Questions students actually ask** — FAQ | "TOPIK? Without Korean? Costs? Age?" | Koreanasha PORT |
| 8 | **Trust** — sourced numbers with check dates, responsibility statements | "Can I believe this?" | V9, kept |
| 9 | **Continue** — closing band: *Explore universities* · *Login* | — | restyled |

Removed from the public site's narrative: the hero form card · "Apply now / 신청하기" in every form · *Partners*
in the primary navigation · *For universities* / *For agencies* from the footer's main columns · *Create a free
account* as the primary action.

## 68.4 Navigation

Public primary navigation, student-only, four items plus account:

`대학 찾기 / Universities` · `한국 유학 / How it works` · `서비스 / Services` · `가이드 / Guides` — then language, then
the account action.

Account action: **`로그인 / Login`** when anonymous; **`내 유학 준비 / Continue my journey`** when a student session
exists. University and agency consoles keep their own login URLs, reachable from one discreet `Partner sign-in`
line at the foot of the footer — never in the primary navigation and never in the home narrative.

## 68.5 Authentication behaviour (not just the button)

1. The marketing site asks the API, with credentials, whether a **student** session exists — a new non-rotating
   `GET /auth/session-hint` that reads the existing `hg_rt_student` cookie, checks it is unexpired and unrevoked,
   and answers `{authenticated, name}`. It issues no access token and rotates nothing, so it cannot trip the
   refresh-token reuse detector.
2. Anonymous + a personalised action (save a university, compare, start an application, see my match, upload a
   document) → `studentUrl('/login?next=<path>')`.
3. `LoginScreen` already honours `?next=`; after sign-in the student lands on the action they asked for.
4. Authenticated → the header reads *Continue my journey* and personalised actions deep-link straight into the
   Student Platform with no login stop.
5. Registration stays reachable from the authentication screens. The home page never looks like a form.

## 68.6 Honesty constraints carried into V10

No success rate, no student count, no years-in-business, no partner logos, no testimonials, no university crests,
no invented discount or "BEST" badge, no fabricated employee, no fabricated social accounts, no company
registration number until Hangyul supplies a real one. Every V9 dependency in §64 stays open and is restated in
§72. Nothing in V10 may describe a measurement as user-validated: no human has used this product.

# 69. V10 Implementation Log

*§65–68 were written before any V10 code change. This section records what was actually built. Evidence lives in
`docs/qa/v10/`: `koreanasha-original/` and `koreanasha-live/` (the reference, five widths each), `benchmark/`
(V-Education), `before/` and `after/` (our own routes, five widths), `COMPETITIVE_UI_AUDIT.md`. Measured results
are §70; what is still open is §72.*

## 69.1 A new adapter package: `packages/koreanasha-ui`

Because Koreanasha is a customised Eduan build (§65.1), the package carries **only Koreanasha's own layer** —
about 500 lines that existed solely as compiled CSS and are now maintainable SCSS for the first time — and
layers it over the shared chassis. `main.tsx` imports it last, so it wins wherever the two overlap.

| Export | Replaces | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `kn-header` (markup in `SiteLayout`) | Koreanasha `main.css:293` | The floating pill, kept at its exact geometry (`inset: 40px 30px auto`, `border-radius: 60px`, hairline border); the original's `0 0 4px rgba(0,0,0,.25)` shadow reads as a hard edge, so it is softened. It tightens to the top edge once the hero scrolls away — Koreanasha has no such state because it has only one page. |
| `<Hero sources>` | `.single-banner` + two background-image media queries | A `<picture>` with **one hand-made crop per breakpoint** and a WebP source per crop, so the crops can be preloaded and width-selected. `100dvh` → `100svh` with a floor: on iOS `100dvh` grows when the URL bar retracts, which pushed Koreanasha's bottom-anchored copy under the fold mid-scroll. |
| `<Band>`, `<SectionHead>` | `pt-100 pb-90` + `.bg-gray` + `section-area` | Band alternation and the centred eyebrow → two-tone headline → lead. `--kn-band` steps 100 / 72 / 56 px; Koreanasha has no phone step-down. |
| `<Card>`, `<Cards>` | `.h2_blog-content` | Radius 20, padding 50/45 kept; `height: 100%` added (equal card heights) and a hairline border, because a shadowless white card on a tinted band has no edge. |
| `<MediaRow>` | `.about-img` + `.about-content` | The alternating photo/text row, Koreanasha's strongest composition. |
| `<Marquee>` | the three logo tracks | Koreanasha animates them with a `requestAnimationFrame` loop that never stops, ignores `prefers-reduced-motion` and keeps running off-screen. Ours is a CSS animation on a duplicated track: GPU-composited, paused on hover and focus, and switched off entirely under reduced motion, where the row becomes a static wrapped list. A short list is repeated until it is wider than any viewport, so the loop never shows a gap. |
| `<Faq>` | Bootstrap collapse | Native `<details>/<summary>`: keyboard- and screen-reader-correct with no JavaScript. |
| `<Reveal>` | AOS from a CDN | AOS sets `opacity: 0` at parse time, so a CDN failure blanks the page. Ours starts **visible** and only arms the animation once `IntersectionObserver` is known to exist and motion is allowed. |
| `Offcanvas`, `useStickyHeader` | MeanMenu, the scroll handler | Re-exported from `@hangyul/eduan-ui` rather than written twice. |

Re-theming is §68.2. What was deliberately **not** ported: the gradient-clipped headline (`.text-gradation` — no
fallback, fails contrast at small sizes), the offset text-shadow (`2px 2px 4px` smears Korean glyphs; a centred
soft shadow does the same contrast job), the 40 px button height (below the 44 px touch target), and the
duplicate mobile CTA (Koreanasha hides the real button with `visibility: hidden` and renders a second one — two
tab stops, one invisible).

## 69.2 The home page, rebuilt

`pages/home/v10.tsx` + `pages/Home.tsx`. Nine movements, each answering one question (§68.3). Sections kept from
V8/V9 — the four product moments, the journey, the trust band — were **re-seated in the Koreanasha rhythm**
(`v10.css`): same band measure, centred heads at the same scale, the two-tone accent, and the alternation fixed
so two tinted bands never touch.

New: the hero, the university band, the four service rows, the FAQ. Moved: the quick check, from *being* the
hero (V9) to one movement below it. Gone: the hero form card, the sticky sign-up nudge, two programme cards
(eight → six: at 1024 the last two cost a whole screen for two more cards, and the catalogue is one click away).

## 69.3 Brand: the lockup is now the brand asset

V1–V9 drew `brandAssets.symbol` plus the CSS string `Hangyul<em>Univ</em>`, while the real BI-kit lockup
(`logo-combined.png`, 456 × 96) sat in `packages/icons` exported and unused — the brief forbids exactly this.
`<Logo>` now renders the asset with an `@2x` source. A **light-ink variant** was derived for dark surfaces by
repainting only the near-neutral `#282828` wordmark pixels white, alpha preserved; the tangerine symbol is
untouched (`tone="light"`; method in `docs/MARKETING_ASSETS.md` §5). The collapsed console rail shows
`symbol.webp` through `.hg-logo__mark`. Stale `.hg-logo__word` selectors were removed from the YNEX skin, the
console stylesheet and the student app. One lockup now appears on every header, both console logins, the student
auth screens and the footer, in all four apps.

## 69.4 Photography

`s1_c.webp` (a Korean university campus from the air, autumn, golden hour) replaces the V9 night-river hero, in
**three hand-made crops** — desktop 2400 × 1100, tablet 1600 × 1000, phone a bottom-anchored 1200 × 1600 portrait
that drops 230 px of empty sky and lands the main hall where the phone's copy sits. WebP with a JPEG fallback,
and a 1600 step added so a 1440 px viewport stops jumping to 2400. `s2_c.webp` (a Korean Air aircraft) joins the
arrival service row. Both are registered as **owner-supplied** in `credits.json`; `/credits` renders those
without licence or source links, because no third-party licence exists and an empty `href` would be a false
claim. Full map, alt text, crop behaviour and the not-used list: `docs/MARKETING_ASSETS.md`.

Kim Yechan: `p1*` (the only image his name is bound to, through the `.text-overlay` caption at `lang.js:27`) is
not carried over, and the person-centric row is **removed rather than restaffed** — no invented employee. `p2*`
and `p3*` name two other real Koreanasha consultants and are not used either. No facial recognition was used:
every association came from repository metadata.

## 69.5 Student-only public site

- Primary navigation is four student destinations. The `Partners ∨` dropdown (For universities / For agencies)
  is gone from the header, and the footer's Partners column is replaced by **one** `Partner sign-in` line under
  the copyright. The `/agencies` and `/universities-partners` routes still resolve — links from outside must not
  break — but nothing in a student's reading path leads to them.
- No public application form, and no "Apply now / 신청하기" anywhere. A scripted check
  (`scripts/qa/v10-authflow.mjs`) asserts both, plus the absence of B2B links in the primary navigation.
- Every remaining "Create a free account" call to action on the public site became **Login** (the closing band,
  How it works, the university decision box). Registration stays one click away, on the login screen itself.

## 69.6 Authentication behaviour, not just the button

| Piece | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /auth/session-hint` (new) | Answers `{authenticated, name}` for a client from the existing refresh cookie. **Non-rotating**: it issues no access token and revokes nothing, so a marketing page load can never consume a session or trip `/auth/refresh`'s reuse detector. 5 pytest cases cover anonymous, signed-in-without-rotation, per-client isolation, revoked, expired and forged cookies. |
| `lib/session.ts` (marketing) | `useStudentSession()` reads the hint; `studentAction(path, authenticated, locale)` returns either the destination or `/login?next=<destination>`. |
| Header | **Sign in** when anonymous, **Continue my journey** when a student session exists. (The Korean renders 로그인, which is the brief's wording; English stays "Sign in" so the public site and the student login screen do not disagree mid-flow.) |
| `safeNext()` (new, `@hangyul/ui`) | `next` arrives from a URL, so only an in-app absolute path is accepted — `https://…`, `//evil` and the backslash form fall back to the app's landing route. |
| `carryQuery()` (new) + Register | The login's "Create an account" link forwards its whole query (minus the dev `demo` param), and Register honours `?next=`. A visitor who clicks a personalised action, has no account, and signs up still lands on the action they clicked — with the quick-check prefill intact. |

End-to-end, verified by script: anonymous → service action → `/login?next=%2Fdocuments` → sign in → `/documents`;
back on the public site the header reads *Continue my journey*; `?next=https://example.com` lands on `/`.

## 69.7 Mobile, made intentional rather than stacked

Four full-width photo rows stacked on a phone cost 3.9 screens. Below 992 px — every phone and every tablet,
exactly where a media row is single-column anyway — the set becomes **one horizontal swipe** with snap points:
same photographs, same words, 0.8 screens. It is focusable, so keyboard users can scroll it (axe
`scrollable-region-focusable`), and it is a plain stack again from 992 px. The account action was also pulled out
of the burger menu and onto the pill at every width down to 320 px; below 576 px the language switcher moves
into the menu instead, where three controls would crowd the pill.

## 69.9 Corrected from the pre-code audit

§67.2 #3 claimed that development-fixture text ("Authorised-submission fixture (development only)") leaking into
Agency Today was a defect. On inspection it is not: `server/app/seed/extra_60_submission_v6.py` returns early
when `HG_ENV=production`, the programme is `is_active=False` and never listed, and an E2E spec depends on the
name. It is dev-only data behaving as designed, and renaming it would break that spec for no user benefit. It is
left alone and recorded here rather than quietly dropped.

Chasing that claim is, however, what uncovered a **real** leak of the same fixture on the public site:
`/universities/{slug}` loaded programmes with no `is_active` filter, so the inactive fixture was served to
anonymous visitors and — sorting first alphabetically — became the default programme and the `<h1>` of a public
university page. That one is a genuine defect, fixed with a regression test (§69.8, §71 #11). The audit note was
wrong about where to look, not about there being something to look for.

## 69.10 Console pass (brief Parts 11–16)

*Done after §69.1–69.9, when the marketing rebuild was finished and measured.*

**The operating models were re-examined against the brief's own questions and kept.** Agency Today answers "who
needs me now?" as one ranked list with a stated reason, owner, deadline and a single action per row, filtered by
nine work types. Agency Students is the table the brief asks for: dense rows, seven operational saved views, a
view-saver, search, intake/stage/deadline filters, column configuration, CSV export, bulk selection, and
waiting-on / next-action / deadline / owner as columns. University Overview opens on "Needs your decision" and
only then on intake progress. University Analytics is four question-titled tabs where every figure is a link to
the exact filtered records, states its population and denominator, and withholds rates below five records.
Hangyul Operations is one severity-ordered "Where is the ecosystem failing?" list with counts, the oldest case
and an exact drill-down, followed by an "all clear" line naming the checks that found nothing. None of that
needed rebuilding, and rebuilding it would have been change for its own sake.

**The detail layer did need work.** Extending `scripts/qa/v10-design-errors.mjs` to the authenticated consoles —
which the marketing-only first pass had not done — surfaced defects that neither screenshots nor axe had caught:

| Where | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **All three consoles** | `a, button { outline: 0 !important }` — verbatim YNEX CSS (`ynex/custom/_custom.scss:31`) that **removed the keyboard focus indicator from every link and button**, with an `!important` no later rule could beat. WCAG 2.4.7; axe's automated rules do not test for a missing focus ring, so four clean axe runs had passed over it | The reset is scoped to `:not(:focus-visible)` — kept for pointer interaction, which is what it was for, withdrawn for keyboard focus. Documented in place, as the repo's template-edit convention requires |
| **All console tables** | Sticky headers were declared (`.hg-table th { position: sticky }`) but **did not work**: `.hg-table-wrap { overflow-x: auto }` makes a scroll container on *both* axes (a non-visible value on one axis forces the other away from `visible`; `clip` likewise computes to `hidden` when paired with `auto`), trapping the header in a box that never scrolls vertically. The agency panel's `overflow: hidden` trapped it a second time. And `top: 0` would have put it behind the fixed app header anyway | From 992 px up the wrapper needs no horizontal container at all — V8/V9's column priority already gives 0 sideways tables — so it is dropped there; the agency panel uses `overflow: clip`, which clips identically without creating a scroll container; and `--hg-table-sticky-top` holds the header at the app header's 4.75 rem. Verified: header holds at 76 px on agency students, agency applications and university applicants |
| **Agency Messages** | The composer's audience toggle is a `role="radiogroup"` whose buttons carry **`aria-checked`**, but the CSS styled **`aria-pressed`** — so the selected state never rendered and "Message" and "Internal note" looked identical. A counselor could not see whether they were about to write to the student or to the team | Both attributes styled, plus a focus ring. The sibling implementation in the writing editor (`.wr-mode`) was checked and is correct |
| **Agency Essays @≈992** | `table-layout: fixed` crushed the Essay column to a few pixels (header "Es", content spilling into Deadline) because the columns declared `size` but no `meta.minWidth`, so the DataTable's folding estimate assumed 140 px each and folded the wrong ones | Every column declares its real `minWidth` and a `priority` ordered for a reviewer's job: 1 student · 2 university/programme and the SLA clock · 3 deadline and next action · 4 type and reviewer |
| Agency Essays | "Escalated to <long name>" overflowed its fixed table cell by 28 px into the next column | Shrinks and truncates with an ellipsis; the full text stays in the cell's `title` |
| Agency Performance @390 | The stage-duration funnel table scrolled sideways — the only such view in the capture, and present in the baseline too | Step labels wrap and the side padding tightens below 576 px; nothing is hidden |
| Hangyul Operations | The launch-category badge overflowed its fixed 9.5 rem column, in both the readiness rows and the legend | The pill wraps inside its own column |
| Hangyul Operations | Assignment override's section headings were h3 directly under the page h1 | h2, appearance unchanged |
| Student Discovery / Compare | h1 → h3 outline jumps: the For-you group headings and the "Same for all" card had no h2 above them | The open group's label and the results count became the region's h2; "Same for all" became h2 |

**Not a defect, after checking:** the consoles are cobalt while the student-facing surfaces are tangerine. That
is the documented V6 decision (`design-tokens/src/console.ts`: "tangerine stays the consumer journey's colour")
and the brief's own Part 18 assigns YNEX to the consoles. Left alone.

Three of my own checker's findings were false positives and the checker was corrected rather than the product:
a skip link that is indicated by sliding into view (not by an outline), `-webkit-line-clamp` truncation (which
renders its own ellipsis), and `hg-sr-only` text (which exists to be clipped). A fourth — Recharts' legend
sitting 4 px outside the plot area with `overflow: visible` — set the overflow threshold to 8 px.
