## 69.12 Dead code and CSS removed

V10 replaced the chrome and the home page but, at first, only *added*: `v10.css` and the Koreanasha layer went on
top of `styles.css`, `v6.css` and `v9.css`, and the superseded components stayed in the tree. That is how a
design system rots, and the brief asked for it not to happen, so the superseded layer was found and deleted
rather than left to be inherited by whoever works here next.

**What `prune-css.mjs` could not see.** The V8 tool asks "is this class name a substring of any source file?",
which keeps every rule that a superseded-but-still-present component mentions. `.ed-hero`, `.ed-tiles` and
`.hg9-hero` all passed that test while being unreachable, because `home/v7.tsx` and `home/v9.tsx` still named
them and nothing rendered either file. **The dead CSS was hidden behind dead TSX**, so the components had to go
first:

| Removed | Why it was unreachable |
|---|---|
| `pages/home/v9.tsx` + `src/v9.css` (entire files) | `HeroCheck` was V9's hero; nothing has imported it since the V10 home landed. Every one of the ten `hg9-*` classes in `v9.css` was referenced by that one file — and `v9.css` was still imported by `pages/Home.tsx`, so it shipped on every home page load |
| `home/v7.tsx`: `Hero`, `QuickCheck`, `Programs`, `SignUpNudge` (138 of 280 lines) | Superseded by `KoreaHero`, `QuickCheckBand`, `ProgramsBand` and the Koreanasha header. `Cost`, `Trust` and `rich()` are still used, by `HowItWorks` and the V10 home, so the file stays |
| `_hangyul-glue.scss`: **252 selectors**, 60.0 → 39.1 KB | Koreanasha's header, offcanvas nav, hero, CTA band and footer replaced Eduan's, so the glue for `ed-header`, `ed-mnav`, `ed-hero`, `ed-tiles`, `ed-cta`, `ed-footer`, the index-7 typewriter and the V7/V8 sections (`ed-why`, `ed-life`, `ed-guides`, `ed-options`, `ed-programs`) could no longer match anything |
| `agency-web/src/styles.css`: 25 selectors | The `ag-attn__*` attention list and `ag-spec` definition grid, replaced during V9's console work and never deleted |
| `koreanasha.scss`: `.kn-page-top` | Written for pages that open without a hero, then superseded by `.kn[data-page='inner'] .ed-crumbband`, which does the same job |
| `ui/styles/layout.css`: `.app-sidebar.sidebar-mini` | A YNEX template class that nothing in this repository ever adds — the consoles collapse their sidebar with `data-collapsed` |

**280 selectors in total** (200 distinct selector strings). Shipped CSS: marketing **273.7 → 255.2 KB** raw
(56.3 → 53.0 KB gzip, on every page of the site), agency 301.8 → 299.9 KB (59.8 → 59.5 gzip). A second pass over
all ten stylesheets reports **0 dead selectors**, so this is a fixed point, not a dent.

### The mistake this pass made, and how it was caught

The first run of the prune deleted a rule it should have kept:

```scss
.ed :is(.h6_banner-content-title, .h6_banner-content-title span,
        .h7_counter-info-title, .h7_apply-item-number span) { text-transform: none; }
```

Three of those four alternatives died with the V7 hero. The fourth, `.h7_counter-info-title`, renders on **every
home page** — it is the Trust counters. `prune-css.mjs` treats a selector as dead when *any* class in it is
dead, which is right for a compound selector (`.a .b` needs both) and wrong for the arguments of `:is()`, which
are alternatives. Deleting the rule handed Eduan's `text-transform: capitalize` back to the counter headings —
the exact i18n defect the rule was written to prevent, and one that would have shown up first in German or
Turkish, not in the English screenshots. `deadSelector` now splits functional pseudo-class lists and treats
them as the disjunction they are; the rule is back, with its three dead alternatives kept so the file is
exactly what the tool produces.

**Two notes on verifying a deletion, because the obvious methods both failed.**

1. *Comparing capture phases does not work here.* Re-capturing all 170 views and diffing against `after/`
   reported 62 changed views. Re-capturing a **third** time, with no code change at all between the two runs,
   reported 37 — the same console pages, at the same magnitudes (`university/cohorts-1024` 15.2 %,
   `agency/messages-1024` 12.1 %). The cause took three attempts to find and is not what it looked like:
   loading one of those pages eight times and reading the heading's `x` from the DOM gives **220 every time**,
   while the PNG of that same page puts it at 206 or 221 run to run. Chromium's full-page rasterisation jitters
   horizontally; the page does not. Two waits were written to "fix" it — geometry stability, then stylesheet
   readiness — and both were taken out again when they changed nothing, rather than left in to look like
   diligence. The recorded measurements are unaffected, and provably so: two runs write byte-identical
   `metrics.json` across all 85 console views.
2. *Injecting the removed CSS back and diffing screenshots does not work either.* Injected last, those rules
   outrank the cascade position they held, and any rule lifted out of a `@media` block applies unconditionally,
   so the method reported 16 differences that the removal had not caused.

What does work is asking the DOM whether a selector can match at all. `scripts/qa/v10-removed-css-probe.mjs`
takes the before/after pair of each stylesheet, computes the removed selectors and tests every one of them
against 19 routes at two widths with the mobile menu open: **200 removed selectors, 0 still match an element.**
That probe is what found the `:is()` mistake, on its first run, as the single exception in a list of 201.

Run again over the *compiled* stylesheets — what the browser actually receives, after PurgeCSS and RTL
mirroring — it reports 237 removed selectors and one that still matches. That one is not a defect, and the
probe now says so itself: a selector can be **rewritten** rather than deleted, and then the same declarations
arrive under a different name. PurgeCSS trims dead alternatives out of an `:is()` list exactly as the fixed
`prune-css.mjs` now does, so the shipped CSS carries `.ed :is(.h7_counter-info-title){text-transform:none}`
where it used to carry the four-alternative form. The probe therefore compares the computed value on the
matched element against what the removed rule declared, and reports **effect lost** or **effect still
delivered**; only the first is a defect, and there are none.

A check that cannot be re-run is half a check, and this repository has no version control to recover a baseline
from. The pre-prune stylesheets were recovered from the last production build that predates the removal and are
kept as evidence in `docs/qa/v10/css-baseline/` with the command to repeat the probe. They are compiled output
rather than source, which is the better thing to test anyway: it is what the browser receives, after PurgeCSS
and RTL mirroring.

**Three tools, and what each is for.**

- `prune-css.mjs` gained SCSS support. postcss cannot parse `//` comments or `@use`, so an SCSS file is parsed
  from a copy with those blanked out *line for line* — every rule keeps its real line number — and the edits are
  then applied to the original by line range. That is what lets a 60 KB commented file be pruned without losing
  a single comment. It also still honours the `base--` rule, which matters: `ed-section--ink`, `hg-btn--lg` and
  `mk-qs--result` are composed at runtime from a `tone`/`variant`/`size` prop and appear in no source file
  literally. A hand-rolled grep over class names flagged all five as dead; they are not. One trap worth knowing:
  `used()` greps the source roots and the script lives inside one of them, so a class name written in a comment
  in that file marks the class live everywhere — which happened, and silently spared six selectors until the
  numbers were re-derived.
- `scripts/qa/css-conflicts.mjs` (new) finds a property declared twice for one selector under the same at-rule
  condition in one file, where the first value can never apply. 23 hits across the four apps. **Twenty-two are
  sound CSS** — a later generation's deliberate re-tuning block (the V8/V9 density passes) overriding its own
  earlier values, which is why the tool reports rather than rewrites. One was a real mistake:
  `.ag-task__title` was declared on two adjacent lines with `font-weight: 600` then `500`, the first dead on
  arrival. Collapsed into one rule.
- `scripts/qa/v10-dead-css.mjs` (new) asks the DOM which selectors in a stylesheet match nothing. It is kept
  for inspection but **not used as the instrument**, and the report should say why: it called 677 of 1,073
  selectors dead, because an unvisited route, a hover state and an error state all look identical to dead from
  the outside. It is a hypothesis generator; the probe above is the test.

# 70. V10 Visual & Functional Validation

*Method: the same script, routes, personas and widths before and after — `scripts/qa/v10-capture.mjs`, 170 views
(17 routes × 5 widths: 1440×900, 1024×768, 768×1024, 430×932, 390×844), captured into `docs/qa/v10/before/` on
2026-10-16 **before any V10 change** and into `docs/qa/v10/after/` when it was finished. Side-by-side pairs:
`docs/qa/v10/comparisons/`. **No human being has used V10.** Every figure below is a measurement or a scripted
walkthrough, exactly as in V9 — and a design pass is the kind of work proxies measure worst, so this section is
careful to say what each number is.*

*Artifact note: `before/metrics.json` was overwritten by a partial re-run of the capture script during the pass.
The screenshots were not, and a full-page PNG is exactly as tall as the page was, so
`scripts/qa/v10-metrics-from-shots.py before` recovers every baseline height from the preserved evidence into
`before/heights.json`; the recovered numbers match what was recorded at capture time.*

*Determinism note, found late and chased to the bottom because the first two explanations were wrong. The
capture's **screenshots** are not pixel-stable on the console surfaces: two runs with no code change between
them (`docs/qa/v10/after2/` and `after3/`, kept as the control) differ on 37 of 340 images, up to 15 % of a
page. Its **measurements are**: those same runs write byte-identical `metrics.json` across all 85 console
views — height, overflow, h1 count, sideways tables and console errors agree exactly. Every figure in §70.2
and §70.6 is one of those measurements, read from the DOM, so none of them is affected.*

*The cause is not timing. Loading one console page eight times and reading `h1.getBoundingClientRect().x`
gives 220 every single time, while the full-page PNG of that page puts the heading at 206 or 221 depending on
the run: Chromium's full-page rasterisation jitters horizontally, the page does not. Two waits were built to
fix it — geometry stability, then stylesheet readiness — and both were removed again when measurement showed
they changed nothing. `--hide-scrollbars` reduces the jitter to one run in eight but alters the layout width,
so it is not used. The conclusion is a limit on one technique: **pixel-diffing full-page console screenshots
between runs does not work here**, which is why the dead-CSS removal was verified by asking the DOM which
selectors still match (§69.12) and not by comparing images.*

## 70.0 The V10 QA tooling

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/qa/v10-shots.mjs` | Any URL at the five V10 review widths. Used for the Koreanasha reference (local + live) and the V-Education benchmark. |
| `scripts/qa/v10-capture.mjs` | The brief's critical screen set — 17 routes × 5 widths as the right persona — with per-view metrics (screens, overflow, sideways tables, h1 count, errors). |
| `scripts/qa/v10-metrics-from-shots.py` | Recovers page heights from captured full-page PNGs, which is how the overwritten `before/metrics.json` was reconstructed from evidence. |
| `scripts/qa/v10-design-errors.mjs` | The Part 17 sweep, by measurement rather than by eye: uneven card heights, button-scale drift, overflow, clipped text, small targets, heading-order jumps, images without intrinsic size, content under fixed chrome, **controls clipped out of reach**, and missing focus indication. All five surfaces. |
| `scripts/qa/prune-css.mjs` (V8, extended) · `scripts/qa/css-conflicts.mjs` · `scripts/qa/v10-dead-css.mjs` | Dead and conflicting CSS — §69.12, including why the DOM-based one is not the instrument. |
| `scripts/qa/v10-removed-css-probe.mjs` | Proves a prune was safe: every selector a stylesheet lost is tested against the live DOM across 19 routes. This is what caught the one real mistake the cleanup made. |
| `scripts/qa/v10-pixdiff.py` | Pixel comparison of two capture phases — and the measurement that showed the capture is not deterministic at that resolution (§69.12). |
| `scripts/qa/v10-authflow.mjs` | The Part 5 acceptance check: Login as the account action, no public application CTA, no B2B in the nav, return path through login and through sign-up, and the open-redirect guard. |
| `scripts/qa/v10-locale-check.mjs` | Renders the home in every locale and checks raw keys, overflow, `lang` and `dir`. |
| `scripts/qa/v10-heights.mjs` | Per-section height breakdown, which is how the mobile reductions were targeted. |
| `scripts/qa/v10-comparisons.py` | Before/after pairs into `docs/qa/v10/comparisons/`. |

Two of these found things the established gates did not: the design sweep found the missing console focus
indicator that four clean axe runs had passed over, and the locale check confirmed the long-language expansion
the brief asks about.

**The sweep's tenth check was added after it missed something.** Every check in it was written against a defect
it had already found, which is the honest way to build one and also its weakness: it cannot see a defect of a
shape nobody has met yet. The burger rendering outside the pill at 320 px (§69.8) is that case. The overflow
check skips any parent whose `overflow-x` is not `visible` — precisely the pill, which clips to its own radius —
and the target-size check only looks at elements under 24 px tall, while the burger was a full 42 px, simply
positioned outside its container. The page did not overflow, so nothing registered. The new check asks the
question the old ones could not: *is this control inside the box that clips it, and if not, can anything be
scrolled to reach it?* Reachability is evaluated per axis and ends at the first ancestor that scrolls on that
axis — the first draft lacked that and called every tab in an `overflow-x: auto` strip unreachable, 68 false
positives across the agency and university consoles. A scrollable strip inside a clipping card is not a defect;
a clip with no scroll anywhere beneath it is.

LCP **improved** on a page with a larger, warmer hero photograph, because the hero is served as WebP with a
1600 px ladder step (so a 1440 viewport stops jumping to 2400) and `fetchPriority="high"`. Marketing's initial
JS grew 2.6 KB for the new sections and the session hook; the other three apps grew 0.2 KB for the lockup.

**On preloading the hero:** measured, the LCP element is *text* — `.kn-hero__lede` on phone, the title's `<em>`
on desktop — so the image is already painted by then and a `<link rel="preload">` would not move LCP, while
costing ~160 KB on the 14 marketing routes that do not use it. Not added, and the reason is a measurement
rather than a guess (§72.3).

# 71. V10 Final Hostile Review

*Written against the built product, as each reader, after V10 was finished. The V9 hostile review (§63.7) is not
repeated — every point in it that V10 did not touch still stands. This section asks only: **why would I still not
use Hangyul?** Each answer is fixed, answered, or classified honestly as external. Nothing is softened, and no
V9 dependency is quietly retired.*

## As an international student

1. **"It's beautiful now, but it is still a catalogue of sample data."** True and unchanged. Tuition, fees,
   deadlines and dorm costs carry `verification_status=DEMO`; the FAQ answer on cost says so in the student's own
   words rather than hiding it in a footnote. A student planning on these numbers would be planning on sample
   figures. *Business dependency (§72).*
2. **"Nobody like me has used this."** True. Zero students, parents, counselors or admissions officers have used
   V10, exactly as for V9. Every number in §70 is a measurement or a scripted walkthrough.
3. **"Your language is a machine translation."** Still true, and unchanged by V10's effort: the new copy now
   exists in all 21 locales that pass the student gate, renders with 0 raw keys and 0 overflow, and mirrors
   correctly in Arabic and Urdu — but **no locale has been read by a human**. Volume is not review. The 24
   marketing-only locales still show the English fallback behind the notice.
4. **"You show me a beautiful campus that isn't any university I can apply to."** Fair. The hero is a Korean
   campus from Hangyul's own photo library, used as what it is — an image of studying in Korea. It is never
   captioned as a partner, and a named campus photograph appears only on that university's own page.
5. **"There are no students in your photographs."** True. Every licensed image in the library is `people: none`
   or `people: distant`, and Hangyul has no commissioned photography and no student releases. Both competitors
   lead with faces; we lead with a place. Inventing or buying faces was not an option this pass. *Business
   dependency.*
6. **"You still can't submit my application."** True by design and by law, unchanged from V9.
7. **"Why should I log in before I can save anything?"** Because nothing is stored without an account, which is
   the honest trade. The check itself needs no account and saves nothing, and that is said on the card.

## As a parent or sponsor

8. **"I cannot verify who Hangyul is."** Still true, and V10 makes it slightly more visible: the footer now has
   the Korean trust-signal shape (identity under the copyright), with nothing in it, because Hangyul's
   registration number, address and phone have not been supplied. V-Education publishes all three. The space is
   built and empty rather than filled with something invented. *Business dependency.*
9. **"There are no reviews and no success rate."** By choice. V-Education publishes "98 % 합격" and "1,000명 이상"
   with no source; Hangyul publishes neither, and §70 records that refusal as a deliberate result.

## As an agency counselor

10. **"Nothing in V10 was for me."** Less true than it was. The operating model is V9's and was kept
    deliberately (§69.10), but the console pass fixed things your counselors would actually have hit: keyboard
    focus was invisible everywhere in your console, table headers scrolled away on long lists, and the message
    composer gave no visual sign whether you were writing to the student or to your team. Still unchanged:
    everything §63.7 said — external channels, the native app lagging, commission and payouts.

## As a university admissions officer

11. **"Your public page was advertising a development fixture."** It was — and that is the most serious defect
    this pass found. `/universities/{slug}` loaded programmes without an `is_active` filter, so the inactive
    submission fixture was served to anonymous visitors and, sorting first alphabetically, became the default
    programme and the `<h1>` of a public university page carrying *our* university's name. Fixed, with a
    regression test that asserts the public payload contains no unlisted programme and no "development only"
    string anywhere.
12. **"Everything else you showed me is still a handful of applicants."** True, unchanged.

## As a professional product designer

13. **"The home page doubled in length."** True: 7.4 → 11.9 phone screens, 6.7 → 12.0 at 1440. It is also a
    different page — it gained a university band, four photographed services and eight answered questions that
    V9 did not have, and it is still well under Koreanasha's 15.2 and V-Education's 24.9. The honest framing is
    that V10 traded brevity for the desire and concreteness the brief asked for, and spent real effort keeping
    the trade small: the services carousel alone saved 3.1 phone screens, and six programme cards instead of
    eight saved another at 1024.
14. **"You are running two template families in one codebase."** Only in name. Koreanasha *is* a customised
    Eduan build (§65.1), which is why `packages/koreanasha-ui` layers over `packages/eduan-ui` instead of
    competing with it. A reader cannot tell which section came from which: the inherited V8/V9 sections were
    re-seated in the Koreanasha rhythm, and the sweep in §70 finds no mixed radii, button scales or card heights.
15. **"Your consoles are blue and your website is orange."** Deliberate and documented since V6
    (`design-tokens/src/console.ts`: "tangerine stays the consumer journey's colour"), and the brief's own Part 18
    assigns YNEX to the consoles and Koreanasha + Hangyul to the student-facing surfaces. The seam a student
    actually crosses — marketing → login → Student Platform — is one tangerine system with one lockup.
16. **"A hero photograph is not a brand."** Correct, and this pass did not invent one. What V10 added is the
    first consistent use of the **real BI lockup** across all four products, replacing nine versions of a
    CSS-typeset wordmark.
17. **"Your own audit got something wrong."** Yes: §67.2 #3 called the development-fixture text on Agency Today
    a defect; it is dev-only data behaving as designed (§69.9). The correction is recorded rather than deleted —
    and chasing it is what uncovered the real leak in #11.

## What this review changed

The public-catalogue leak (#11) and its regression test; the correction in #17. The second pass — prompted by
asking whether the console scope decision was really defensible — added §69.10 and §69.11: the missing focus
indicator across three consoles, the broken sticky headers, the invisible composer mode, the crushed Essays
column, the caseload's non-deterministic university, and the translation of the new copy into all 21 gated
locales. Everything else above is either a stated boundary or a dependency in §72.

**A note on method.** Four separate axe runs reported zero violations over consoles in which no link or button
had a visible keyboard focus indicator. A measurement passing is not the same as the thing being right, and a
clean gate is only as good as what the gate looks at.

that picture, and (b) what V10 itself added to the list. `/hq/readiness` generates the same classification from
real settings, so operations sees it too.*

| Kind | Item | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW** | **The 69 new marketing strings, like every other string in the product** | They were translated into all 21 locales that pass the V9 student gate (§69.11) through the validating pipeline, and render with 0 raw keys and 0 overflow. But **no locale is HUMAN_REVIEWED** — that was true before V10 and is still true. The 24 locales that have the namespace without a student journey remain at 93 % and show the English fallback behind the existing notice; closing those is one `v9-merge` chunk each, and they are marketing-only machine drafts regardless. |
| **NEEDS BUSINESS DATA** | **Hangyul's own photography** | All 17 licensed images are `people: none`/`people: distant`; the two owner-supplied Koreanasha photographs are a campus and an aircraft. Both competitors lead with human faces. Needs commissioned photography and student releases — not something to buy stock for. |
| **NEEDS BUSINESS DATA** | **Company identity for the footer** | Registration number, registered address, contact phone. V-Education publishes all three and Korean buyers check them. The block is built and empty. |
| **NEEDS HUMAN VALIDATION** | **Nobody has seen the new home page** | Unchanged in kind from §64, restated because V10 is a *design* pass and design is the thing proxies measure worst. Every figure in §70 is a measurement or a scripted walkthrough. The blind visual test's human round (`docs/research/v9-validation-protocols.md` §8) has still not run, and the V8 synthetic round was inconclusive. |

## 72.3 Engineering backlog V10 leaves behind

- **Hero preload.** The hero `<img>` carries `fetchPriority="high"` but is React-rendered, so the browser
  discovers it only after the entry chunk parses. A `<link rel="preload" imagesrcset … media>` in `index.html`
  would start it earlier, but the shell is shared by all 15 marketing routes, so it would also fetch ~160 KB on
  the 14 that do not use it. Worth doing with per-route HTML (or SSR), not before.
- **The home page is longer than V9's** — 11.9 phone screens against 7.4, for substantially more content
  (§70). Further reduction is possible (the journey band is 1.8 screens on a phone, Trust 1.3) but each cut
  removes something the brief asked for.
- **`/agencies` and `/universities-partners` still exist as routes.** They are out of every student path, but
  they are now unowned pages in a student-only site — either give them to the B2B surface or retire them.
- **The console operating models are V9's, by decision not omission.** They were re-examined screen by screen
  against the brief's questions and kept (§69.10); the detail layer was repaired. Everything §63.7 said about
  those models — external channels, the agency native app lagging, commission and payouts, no SIS or rail
  integration — still stands.
- ~~`scripts/qa/v10-design-errors.mjs` is marketing-only.~~ **Done** — it now covers all five surfaces, and the
  prediction was right: the console run found more than the marketing one, including the missing focus
  indicator across all three consoles (§69.10).
- **E2E, axe and the capture all run against the development stack.** The isolated-stack runner
  (`scripts/qa/e2e-run.mjs`) remains the production-build gate.
- **`scripts/qa/` holds 45 throwaway probe scripts** (`_shot.mjs`, `_ovf2.mjs`, `_offender.mjs`, …) accumulated
  from V6 onward. They are dead code by any reasonable reading, and V10 deleted its own two. The other 45 were
  **left deliberately**: ten of them are cited by name in `docs/qa/v9/` and `docs/qa/v8/` as the method behind a
  published measurement, and this repository has no version control, so deleting them would destroy the only
  record of how those numbers were taken. The fix is to promote the cited ones into named tools and delete the
  rest — a documentation job, not a cleanup job, and not one to do silently.

## 72.4 What must not happen before those are closed

Unchanged from §64.3, plus: do not describe the new marketing copy as translated beyond English and Korean, do
not present catalogue costs as verified, and do not fill the footer identity block with anything that has not
been supplied by Hangyul.

# 73. V11 Radical Complexity Audit

*2026-10-17, before any V11 code change. Method: every route table, every `AppLayout` navigation array and every
home-screen composition read in source; counts are of shipped destinations, not of files.*

## 73.1 The user's verdict, taken literally

V10's gates were green — 0 overflow at nine widths, 0 axe violations, 0 raw keys, every test passing — and the
product still reads as **too complicated, too AI-generated, too feature-heavy**. That is not a contradiction. Our
gates measure whether a screen is *broken*. None of them measures whether a screen should *exist*. V10 added nine
home sections, 14 public routes and 49 console destinations, and every one of them passed.

So this pass does not add a gate that measures breakage better. It removes things, and then measures the removal
(`docs/qa/v11/complexity.json`).

## 73.2 Measured complexity, V10

| Surface | Count | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Public marketing routes | **14** | `/`, `/universities`, `/universities/:slug`, `/how-it-works`, `/students`, `/agencies`, `/universities-partners`, `/guides`, `/guides/:slug`, `/guides/country/:code`, `/credits`, `/trust`, `/privacy`, `/terms` |
| Homepage sections | **9** | hero, universities, programs, quick check, Hangyul-at-work, services, journey, questions, trust |
| Student top-level nav | **16** | explore, compare, applications, documents, essays, tasks, scholarships, budget, family, visa, housing, arrival, support/help, profile, services, settings |
| Agency top-level nav | **20** | today, students, pipeline, tasks, messages, applications, submissions, services, documents, essays, performance, universities, 5 × `/hq/*`, team, vendors, settings |
| University top-level nav | **13** | overview, applicants, offers, documents, messages, analytics, cohorts, agencies, programs, partnership, scholarships, exports, settings |
| **Total destinations** | **72** | |

## 73.3 Where the "AI made this" feeling actually comes from

Not from any single screen. From five repeatable habits, each found by name in the V10 source:

1. **A page per domain object.** `Documents`, `Essays`, `Tasks`, `Scholarships`, `Budget`, `Family`, `Visa`,
   `Housing`, `Arrival` are nine student destinations that exist because nine tables exist. A student has one
   question — *what should I do now?* — and must guess which of nine nouns holds the answer.
2. **The same job reachable twice.** Student `/tasks` and the home next-action answer the same question.
   Agency `/tasks`, `/deadlines` and `/pipeline` are three views of "what is late". University `/offers` and
   `/applicants` both end in a decision.
3. **Marketing that demonstrates the backend.** The V10 home's fifth movement, `HangyulAtWork`, shows four
   product UI states to a visitor who has not yet decided they want to study in Korea. "Source freshness",
   "submission connectors" and "dossier reuse" are engineering achievements, not reasons to emigrate.
4. **A metric wherever a number exists.** The home ends on a Trust band of sourced figures; three consoles open
   on KPI rows. Numbers answer questions nobody asked at that moment.
5. **Explanatory copy standing in for design.** `/how-it-works`, `/students`, `/trust` and `/guides` are four
   routes that each explain the service in prose. A visitor reads none of them.

## 73.4 The rule this pass applies

For every section, card, metric, button, menu item, tab, filter, chart, badge and paragraph: name the user's
question it answers, and the decision it enables. No question, or a question a neighbouring element already
answers → it is removed, not restyled. Capability is never removed; only its claim on a menu slot.

# 74. V11 Koreanasha Copy & Visual Fidelity Audit

## 74.1 Where the canonical copy actually lives

`template-koreanasha/index.html` renders the Korean homepage from **empty** elements — `<h1 id="banner_title">`
carries no text. Every visible string is injected by `assets/js/lang.js`, an i18next bundle of **301 Korean
keys**. That file, not the HTML, is the authoritative source, and §65.1 already established that the local
template and the deployed <https://univ.talkhangyul.com/> are the same build — so there is no local-vs-live
divergence to reconcile.

`scripts/i18n/v11-extract-koreanasha.mjs` parses it and writes `docs/qa/v11/koreanasha-copy.json`:
**43 canonical strings** reused, **8 groups excluded**. `scripts/qa/v11-copy-fidelity.mjs` compares the manifest
against `locales/ko/marketing.json` on every run and fails on any character that differs.

## 74.2 The only permitted edits

| Class | Strings | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | 35 | Nothing. Byte-identical, `<br>` and `<span class="text-blue">` markup included. |
| `brand` | 7 | `Koreanasha` → `한귤`. Korean particles agree with the noun's final sound: Koreanasha ends in a vowel (는/가/와), 한귤 ends in ㄹ (은/이/과). Carrying the old particle across would ship the ungrammatical "한귤는". Swapping it is part of replacing the name; the surrounding words are untouched. |
| `count` | 1 | Koreanasha's marquee heading reads **"50+개 이상의 한국 대학교"**. Hangyul's catalogue holds **10**. Shipping "50+" would be a false statement about our own coverage — the same rule that forbids "95 % acceptance" (brief Part 21). The figure alone becomes `{{count}}`, bound to the live catalogue; the sentence is otherwise verbatim. |

## 74.3 What is deliberately not reused, and why

The owner authorises the content, but four groups cannot become Hangyul's voice without stating something untrue:

| Group | Reason |
|---|---|
| `about_us_section1–3_*` | Names three real Koreanasha employees — 김예찬 (with an 800k-follower credential), 체보타레바 알리나, 사이라노바 알렉산드라 — and their degrees. Re-badged as Hangyul staff this is a false claim about who works here. The V11 home ships **no** team section, which is also what Part 6's target structure asks for. |
| `reviews_*` | Four signed student testimonials naming the Koreanasha consultants who helped them. Re-attributed to Hangyul they would be fabricated social proof. |
| `pricing_plans_*` (≈180 keys) | Another company's prices and service guarantees — `$40` add-ons, a 3-hour reply guarantee, 주 7일 멘토 coverage. Hangyul's plans are Hangyul's own, and no pricing section exists on the V11 home. |
| `modal_*` | The 상담 신청 consultation form. Brief Part 7 forbids a public application form outright. |

`footer_description` (대표 김예찬 · koreanasha333@gmail.com · 사업자등록번호 139-74-00672) is replaced by Hangyul's
own identity block, which remains **empty** pending owner-supplied data, exactly as §72.1 recorded.

## 74.4 One claim the owner should confirm

`why_koreanasha_section3_description` ends **"성공적인 유학생활을 보장합니다"** — *we guarantee a successful study
abroad experience*. It is shipped verbatim, as instructed. Two notes for the record: the footer's standing
disclaimer says Hangyul does **not** guarantee admission (a different claim, so not a literal contradiction), and
a guarantee of outcome is the kind of sentence consumer-advertising rules treat differently from ordinary
puffery. This is flagged, not edited — §82 carries it as an owner decision.

## 74.5 The university crests

`assets/img/university/` holds 32 SVGs already grouped `u-1-*` (10), `u-2-*` (12), `u-3-*` (10) — the three
marquee rows, in the source. Each file carries its university's Korean name in the root `<g id>` as numeric
character entities; decoding the entity bytes identifies **24** of the 32:

> 서울대학교 · 연세대학교 · 고려대학교 · 카이스트 · 포항공과대학교 · 성균관대학교 · 서강대학교 · 유니스트 ·
> 이화여자대학교 · 서울시립대학교 · 중앙대학교 · 경희대학교 · 한국외국어대학교 · 동국대학교 · 홍익대학교 ·
> 부산대학교 · 국민대학교 · 세종대학교 · 아주대학교 · 단국대학교 · 가톨릭대학교 · 가천대학교 · 한국항공대학교

V11 ships **those 24 only**, eight per row. The remaining 8 carry no name metadata, so no accurate `alt` text
could be written for them, and a crest nobody can name is decoration with an accessibility cost.

V10 refused crests outright (§65.4) on the grounds that a university mark implies a partnership. The owner has
now authorised the asset set and asked for the original design back, so V11 ships it with the implication closed
in copy instead of by omission: the section keeps Koreanasha's own heading — *Korean universities are waiting for
your admission*, a statement about Korean universities, not about Hangyul's contracts — the word "partner" appears
nowhere, and a visible line states that the marks belong to their institutions and do not indicate a
relationship with Hangyul. Trademark permission is an owner-level question and is recorded in §82.

## 74.6 Header geometry — the actual defect

Koreanasha's header is **one rule**, `main.css:293`:

```css
.header { position: fixed; top: 40px; left: 30px; right: 30px; z-index: 8;
          background: #fff; border-radius: 60px; border: 1px solid #E5E5E5;
          box-shadow: 0 0 4px rgba(0,0,0,.25); }
```

There is no scrolled state, at any breakpoint. The pill is fixed from the first paint and never changes. The
`.header-sticky.sticky` rules elsewhere in that file belong to Eduan's *other* demo headers (`h2_`, `h3_`, `h6_`)
and never apply to this page.

V10 invented the morph. `packages/koreanasha-ui/src/scss/koreanasha.scss:63`:

```scss
.kn-header.is-stuck { inset: 0 0 auto; border-radius: 0; border-inline-color: transparent; }
```

driven by `useStickyHeader(96)` in `SiteLayout.tsx:57`. Side insets to zero, radius to zero — precisely the
full-width rectangular bar the brief forbids. It is **one** rule and **one** hook call, in one place, so there is
no competing source of header state to untangle.

## 75.1 Public site: 14 routes → 6

| Route | Decision | Where it goes |

| `/` | **keep** | rebuilt, 9 sections → 6 |
| `/universities`, `/universities/:slug` | **keep** | the catalogue is the one thing worth browsing before an account |
| `/privacy`, `/terms` | **keep** | legally required |
| `/credits` | **keep, footer only** | 13 of 19 home photographs are CC BY 2.0/3.0/4.0, which *require* attribution. This page is a licence obligation, not a content choice. It absorbs `/trust`'s sourced-figure table and is renamed *Sources & credits*. |
| `/how-it-works` | **remove** | → `/#services` |

Nothing 404s: each removed path becomes a redirect to the section that answers the same question, and no redirect
targets another redirect.

## 75.2 Guides — decision B, removed from the public product

The brief demands a decision and forbids a mediocre middle state. The screenshot's defects are not styling:
**the guide bodies exist only in English.** `server/app/seed/content_data.py` carries long-form prose with no
`body_ko` field at all, which is why a Korean visitor gets Korean chrome around English text. Fixing that
properly means translating substantive visa, apostille and funding guidance into 58 locales — content where a
machine draft is a liability, not a nicety.

So the public guide routes go. The research behind them is not thrown away: it already powers the visa-route
engine, the document-requirement rules and the per-country apostille dates *inside* the platform, where every
field is localised and every figure carries its source and check date. The ten questions a visitor actually asks
are answered on the homepage, in Koreanasha's own words, in Korean.

| 6 Continue | Hangyul | *How do I start?* |

Cut, with the reason: **programs band** (the catalogue is one click away and that is where deadlines belong),
**quick check** (a form on a page that must not carry a form), **Hangyul at work** (backend demonstration —
brief Part 6), **journey** (the services section already covers arrival and settlement, which is Koreanasha's own
section 2), **student questions** (replaced by Koreanasha's FAQ), **trust band** (moved to `/credits`).

Not *Documents · Essays · Visa · Housing · Arrival · Tasks · Services · Support · Notifications · Scholarships ·

# 79. V11 Implementation Log

*Order follows the brief: header first, then the crest band, then copy, then the reductions.*

## 79.1 Part 1 — the header

One rule deleted and one hook call removed; nothing added.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/koreanasha-ui/src/scss/koreanasha.scss` | `.kn-header.is-stuck { inset: 0 0 auto; border-radius: 0; … }` **deleted**. `.kn-header` keeps `position: fixed; inset: var(--kn-header-top) var(--kn-header-inset) auto; border-radius: 999px` and nothing else; the `transition` on `inset` went with it, since there is no longer a second state to animate to. |
| `apps/marketing-web/src/components/SiteLayout.tsx` | `useStickyHeader(96)` and the `stuck && 'is-stuck'` class **removed**. |

There is now **no header state at all**, which is the strongest possible form of "one source of header state": nothing
can disagree with anything. That is also what the original does — `main.css:293` has no scrolled variant at any
breakpoint, and the `.header-sticky.sticky` rules in that file belong to Eduan's other demo headers.

Measured geometry (`scripts/qa/v11-header-scroll.mjs`, nine widths × four scroll positions, captured to
`docs/qa/v11/header/`):

| Width | inset L/R | top | width / viewport | radius | identical at 0 / 25 / 50 / 75 % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 320 / 360 / 390 / 430 | 12 / 12 | 12 | 296/320 … 406/430 | pill | yes |
| 768 / 1024 | 20 / 20 | 20 | 728/768, 984/1024 | pill | yes |
| 1280 / 1440 / 1728 | 30 / 30 | 28 | 1220/1280 … 1668/1728 | pill | yes |

Desktop lands inside the brief's `top: 24–28px`, `left/right: 24–32px`. The pill does not even move closer to
the top on scroll, which the brief permits but the original does not do.

## 79.2 Part 2 / Part 20 — the three-row crest marquee

`UniversityCrests` in `apps/marketing-web/src/pages/home/v11.tsx`, built on the existing `Marquee` primitive.

* **Three rows, left / right / left.** That is the original's own behaviour: its loop sets
  `isReverse = index % 2 === 1`, so rows 1 and 3 run forward and row 2 reverses.
* **Real crest images**, `object-fit: contain` against a fixed height (100 px ≥1200, down to 52 px at 320), with
  the intrinsic ratio on every `<img>` so a row cannot reflow while decoding. No chips, no cards, no borders.
* **Different speed and phase per row** — 68 s / 76 s / 72 s, offset 0 / 0.33 / 0.66 of a loop through a new
  `offset` prop that emits a negative `animation-delay`. Without it three rows start on the same column.
* **No seam**: the track renders two identical halves and translates by exactly `-50%`, so the loop closes on
  itself. The 23 crests are repeated to a minimum of 18 items per half, which covers 1728 px, and because the
  list repeats as a block no two adjacent logos are the same.
* **Reduced motion**: the shared rule drops the animation and wraps each row into a centred static grid — three
  rows of logos, which is what the brief asks for.
* Pauses on `:hover` and `:focus-within`.
* Crests whose university is in our catalogue are links to that university's page.

Two defects were found and fixed during this work, both mine:

1. **A zero-scale matrix.** The crest optimiser rounded all long decimals to two places. Figma writes pattern
   transforms in `objectBoundingBox` units — `matrix(0.000280449 0 0 0.000289352 -0.000741186 0)` — and rounding
   those produced `matrix(0 0 0 0 0 0)`, so the Yonsei and Ewha marks rendered as **nothing**, leaving a hole in
   the row. The rule now only shortens numbers at or above 1.
2. **Lazy loading inside a moving track.** With `loading="lazy"`, a crest only begins loading as it slides into
   view, so it pops in mid-loop. The crests load normally now, at `fetchpriority="low"` behind the hero.

Weight: the 23 files were **2,111 KB → 826 KB** (337 KB gzipped) by re-encoding two embedded photographs — a
626 KB JPEG and a 541 KB PNG, both rendering into a 100 px box — as WebP at 240 px
(`scripts/qa/v11_optimize_crests.py`).

## 79.3 Parts 19 / 20 — the copy pipeline

Three scripts, so fidelity is mechanical rather than a promise:

| Script | Does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/i18n/v11-extract-koreanasha.mjs` | parses `lang.js` (301 ko keys) → `docs/qa/v11/koreanasha-copy.json`: 43 reused strings with their substitution class, 8 excluded groups with reasons |
| `scripts/i18n/v11-install-copy.mjs` | writes the Korean strings **from the manifest**, so the ko bundle cannot drift from the source by construction; English is a translation of that Korean |
| `scripts/qa/v11-copy-fidelity.mjs` | fails on any character that differs, on a surviving `Koreanasha`, and on any excluded name (김예찬, 체보타레바, 사이라노바, the old registration number) reappearing |

Result: `43/43 strings match the owner-supplied source exactly`.

`lib/koreanasha-copy.tsx` renders the template's own markup — exactly four tags occur (`<br>`, two
`<span class="text-…">`, one `<h2>` wrapper) — through a whitelist that produces React elements. No
`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`: an unexpected tag renders as visible text rather than executing.

## 79.4 Parts 4 / 5 / 6 — the public site

Routes 14 → 6; homepage 9 sections → 6. `routes.tsx` carries a `REDIRECTS` map so every removed path lands on
the section that answers the same question, with no redirect pointing at another redirect.

Deleted outright: `pages/{Trust,Guides,GuideArticle,CountryGuide,HowItWorks,Students,Agencies,UniversityPartners}.tsx`,
`pages/home/{v7,v8,v10}.tsx`, `components/{QuickSentence,LegalizationWidget,Illustrations,UniCard,sections}.tsx`,
`lib/quick.ts`. The footer went from fourteen links in three columns to four in two.

`/credits` absorbed `/trust` and became *Sources & credits*. It is kept for a licence reason, not a content one:
13 of 19 photographs are CC BY. Its sourced-figure table lost the status filter row, the search box, the status
badges and the review-interval column — a console UI on a public page.

## 79.5 Parts 10–13 — the consoles

| Product | Change |
|---|---|
| Student | `lib/nav.ts`: `NAV_SLOTS` is no longer `Record<NavStage, …>` but a constant four. The V8 rail rotated with the journey, so one tab position meant Compare, then Documents, then Visa. The menu dropped Tasks (the home screen *is* the task list) and Compare (a mode of Universities), and gates visa/housing/arrival on the stage. `Improve` lost its own section and became the tail of Applications — "what should I do now" was answered twice on one screen. |
| Agency | Fifteen rail items → seven. New `pages/Review.tsx` makes Documents and Writing two **modes** of one area, chosen from a segmented control in the page header — not nested tabs, because the writing queue already has its own view tabs. New `pages/Manage.tsx` collects Team, Providers, Services, Templates, Catalog, Settings, Payments and Audit. `/documents` and `/essays` now redirect into `/review`. |
| University | Thirteen → six. New `pages/Manage.tsx` for rules, scholarships, partnership, exports and settings. Offers and Documents are linked from the Applicants header; Cohorts and Partner agencies from the Analytics header. |

No route was deleted in any console, so every deep link, every in-product link and the mobile apps still resolve.

One defect introduced and fixed: the new agency Review page was first given the class `ag-review`, which already
exists in `styles.css:172` as the two-column grid of the document *detail* pane. The page became a grid and threw
its own header into the second column. Renamed `ag-revhub-`. This is exactly the accidental-inheritance problem
§73 set out to remove, met head-on while adding to it.

## 79.6 Tests

`e2e/v11-marketing.spec.ts` replaces `e2e/v3-marketing.spec.ts` with the brief's ten assertions plus one more,
and it is the shape of them that matters rather than the count:

* the header test **scrolls** and measures real geometry, because the V10 defect passed every first-viewport
  check that existed;
* the crest test asserts three rows of `<img>`, zero `.kn-chip`, `object-fit: contain`, and that **no crest
  failed to decode** — a broken SVG renders at zero width and is otherwise invisible to a screenshot diff;
* the eleventh renders the page under `prefers-reduced-motion` and asserts each crest appears **exactly once**,
  which is the only way the duplicate-logo defect in §81.2 could have been caught.

`apps/student-web/src/lib/nav.test.ts` now asserts the rail is stage-independent — the V8 test asserted the
opposite (five slots per stage), so it had to be rewritten rather than extended.

## 79.7 Second pass — the four items §82 had listed as not done

The first pass stopped with four pieces of the brief unbuilt and said so. They are built now.

### Agency student workspace: 10 tabs → 4 (brief Part 12)

It was ten, not the nine §77.3 estimated: *overview · applications · portfolio · documents · essays · visa ·
services · tasks · messages · history*. Now **Overview · Application · Communication · More**.

The ten did not disappear — each is a **section** inside one of the four, stacked with a heading and an anchor
rather than hidden behind a second row of tabs. Application holds applications → documents → writing → visa, in
the order the work happens; Communication holds the thread and the history behind it; More holds tasks, the
dossier and paid services.

Two details that make the merge safe rather than cosmetic:

* **Every old link still works.** `?tab=documents` resolves to Application *and scrolls to the documents
  section*, because `SECTION_TAB` maps each V10 tab name to its new home. All nine legacy values were tested.
* **The visa section is conditional** — it renders once there is a visa case or an offer, since before that it
  is a heading over nothing. The exception is an explicit `?tab=visa` link, which renders it anyway so the
  person who followed that link gets the panel explaining there is no case yet, rather than a page that
  silently ignores where they asked to go.

`More` carries no badge. It would have read "20" from the open-task count — the largest number on the screen,
beside the least urgent tab — and Overview already lists those tasks under "What happens next".

### The chart audit (brief Part 15)

The question/decision test, applied to every chart the design system ships:

| Chart type | Rendered anywhere? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `ColumnChart` | 4 call sites (agency backlog by week; university cohort mix, progression rate, intake trend) | **Keep** — each answers "is this going up or down, and where" |
| `TrendChart` | **0** | Removed |
| `BarList` | **0** | Removed |
| `DonutChart` | **0** | Removed — and a donut is on the brief's own list of charts not to use |

Three of the four chart types had no call site in any app. We had written a chart library for ourselves. Deleting
them also drops Recharts' `Pie`, `PieChart`, `Cell`, `Line`, `LineChart`, `Area` and `AreaChart` from the
bundle: the chart chunk fell **429.45 KB → 380.12 KB** (122.07 → 110.58 KB gzipped) in both consoles.

What the audit did **not** find was a decorative chart on a screen. The manager visuals V8/V9 built already pass:
`/hq` and `/performance` print the question on the card itself (`<p className="ag8-q">`), counsellor workload is
a horizontal `ProgressRow` bar per person against capacity, and case ageing by stage is the same. The brief's
preferred visuals were already the ones in use — the failure was a library of unused ones behind them.

### Hangyul HQ: 5 destinations → 3 (brief Part 14)

`/hq` already answered exactly the question Part 14 asks — *where is the ecosystem failing?* — as one
severity-ordered incident list where every row opens its exact records. What it did not have was configuration
kept away from it. **Operations · Agencies · Tools**: the source registry, launch readiness and the assignment
override moved to `/hq/manage`. Source freshness was already an incident row on `/hq` linking to its queue, so
the registry is the detail behind an incident rather than a place to visit.

### Russian is a second canonical locale, not a translation

The strongest finding of the second pass. `lang.js` ships **two** owner-written locales — ko (301 keys) and
**ru (301 keys)** — and Koreanasha's audience is Russian-speaking, so its Russian is the company's own words
rather than a translation of its Korean. Russian is therefore treated exactly like Korean: extracted from the
template, installed from the manifest, and gated character-for-character. The fidelity check now reports
**86/86 strings across ko + ru**.

The gate immediately earned its keep. `koreanasha_services_section3_description` was classed `none` because the
Korean names no company in it — but the Russian does, and the check failed on a surviving "Koreanasha". The
substitution class belongs to the *string set*, not to one locale's text.

Per-locale substitutions: Korean takes 한귤 with the particle corrected; Russian takes the Latin `Hangyul`, as
`locales/ru/common.json` already writes it. The count phrase differs too — "50+개 이상의" and "Более 50" — so each
locale has its own replacement, and the extractor throws if the phrase it expects is not there.

### Mobile

`agency-mobile` already had Today · Students · Review · Messages · **Tasks**. Tasks went, for the same reason it
went from the web rail: Today *is* the list of what needs this counsellor. `href: null` keeps the route
reachable. `university-mobile` keeps Pipeline and Cohorts — on a phone those are two read-only views, not the
desktop tables the brief warns against, so they stay deliberately.

### One stale sentence

`/universities` still told visitors to "check where you qualify **from the home page**" — the quick-eligibility
form Part 7 removed. Rewritten in en and ko to describe what the page actually does.

## 79.8 Two more defects, found by widening the gates rather than by changing code

Merging the workspace's ten tabs into four put **History** beside Messages on the Communication tab — and
because that tab is a new route, it went into the axe list. It immediately failed, seven nodes at both widths:

1. **`.ag-rowbtn[data-past='true'] { opacity: .7 }`.** A past appointment was dimmed with a blanket opacity,
   which composites *every* label inside it. `--hg-text-tertiary` (#5F6B80) became #8F97A6 — **2.93:1** against
   white, where 12 px text needs 4.5. Its status badge measured 3.25:1. "Past" is now a background tint
   instead, so the row still reads as behind us and every word in it stays legible.
2. **`.hg-chip .hg-subtle`.** Tertiary text on a chip's tinted background measured **4.15:1** at 12 px. Inside
   a chip the secondary token is used instead.

Neither was caused by this pass: both rules predate V11, on a tab that existed in V10. They had never been
measured because `?tab=history` was not in the a11y route list — only the workspace's default tab was. The fix
is as much the route list as the CSS: the new tabs, `/hq/manage` and both `/review` modes are in it now.

That is the same lesson as §81.2, from the other direction. The first three defects were invisible because no
gate rendered that *state*; these two were invisible because no gate visited that *route*.

## 79.9 The CSS generations (brief Part 16)

"The UI should not be the sum of ten redesigns." Every app loads a stack of generation-named stylesheets —
student `v2 · v4 · v7 · v9`, agency `v8 · v8-ops · v8-hq · v8-secondary · v9`, university `v8 · v9`. The
question is not whether those files exist; it is whether any rule in them still reaches the screen by accident.

**Two independent methods, and only their intersection is deleted.** `scripts/qa/v11-dead-css.mjs` (the V10
detector, generalised to log into the consoles) asks the *browser* "did this selector match anything, on any
route, at any width?". `scripts/qa/v11-dead-css-confirm.mjs` then asks the *source* "does any class in it still
appear in a component?". Method one alone is not enough — a selector can be real and only match in a state the
sweep never reached (a modal, an error, an empty list). Method two is what rules that out: if no component can
produce the class, no state can.

| Console | Selectors checked | Matched nothing | **Confirmed dead by both** | Removed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Student (`v2`, `v4`, `v7`, `v9`) | 635 | 212 | **22** | 32 selectors / 25 rules; `v2.css` 469 → 442 |
| Agency (`v8*`, `v9`) | 283 | 91 | **12** | 18 selectors / 16 rules; `v8.css` 81 → 64, `v8-ops.css` 42 → 35 |
| University (`v8`, `v9`) | 176 | 57 | **4** | 6 selectors / 6 rules |

What was actually dead: a budget-table style set (`.bd-lines` and its ten descendants), a privacy note
(`.sd-privacy`), a V8 "who needs me now" row (`.ag8-now__*`), a jump bar (`.ag8-jump`), and four single rules.
All superseded components whose markup was replaced in V9/V10 while their CSS stayed.

The gap between the columns is the point: **860 of 1,094 selectors are live**, and of the 360 the DOM sweep
could not reach, only 38 were genuinely dead. The consoles are not the sum of ten redesigns — they are layered
by generation in the filename only, and the layering is almost entirely load-bearing. Reporting that honestly
matters more than inflating the deletion count.

Two refinements were needed before anything was removed, each caught by a wrong answer:

* The confirmation script first scanned only the app's own `src`, so four live locale-conditional rules
  (`:lang(my) .hg-tabbar …`) looked dead — `hg-tabbar` is a `packages/ui` component. It scans every source root
  that can render on those routes now.
* "Dead if *every* class is dead" kept `.bd-schol .bd-num` and `.bd-lines td:last-child .hg-status`, which each
  name one live class and can still never match. Every class in a chain must be present for a selector to
  match, so one dead class is enough: the rule is "dead if *any* required class is dead", ignoring `:not()`.

Marketing was done in the first pass: `v10.css` deleted outright (every rule targeted a section V11 no longer
renders) and `v6.css` cut 136 → 68 lines.

# 80. V11 Visual Validation

*Captures in `docs/qa/v11/`. Automated gates were run, and then the screens were looked at — §79.2 and §79.5
each record a defect that every gate passed.*

## 80.1 The header, after scroll — the capture that matters

`scripts/qa/v11-header-scroll.mjs` loads the home at nine widths, scrolls to 0 / 25 / 50 / 75 % of the real page
height, measures the header and screenshots it: **36 captures** in `docs/qa/v11/header/`.

| Assertion | Result |
|---|---|
| `position: fixed` at every stop | 9/9 widths |
| Left and right inset > 8 px at every stop | 9/9 |
| Width < viewport width at every stop | 9/9 |
| `border-radius` ≥ half the pill's height at every stop | 9/9 (999 px throughout) |
| Geometry **identical** at 0 % and at 25 / 50 / 75 % | 9/9 |

V10's `is-stuck` would have failed four of those five at the 25 % stop.

## 80.2 Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `typecheck` | 7 workspaces clean |
| Vitest | **204 passed** (marketing 47, student 73, agency 68, university 16 + 22 live-smoke skipped) |
| pytest | **350 passed** |
| ruff | clean |
| Playwright desktop | **47 passed, 3 skipped** (the three need fresh seed data, as in V9/V10) |
| Playwright mobile | 3 passed |
| axe-core, WCAG 2.1 A/AA | **0 violations** — marketing, student, agency, university, at 1280 and 390 |
| i18n | en 100 % across every namespace; ko unchanged at 97–100 % (the gaps are `_one` plural forms, which Korean does not have); ru marketing 99 % |
| Copy fidelity | **86/86** strings (ko + ru) byte-identical to the owner's template |
| Visual QA sweep | marketing 35 views, student 72, agency 78, university 57 — **0 issues** |

Three defects were found by these gates and fixed:

* **axe** — the services row becomes a horizontal scroller below 992 px and had no way in from the keyboard
  (`scrollable-region-focusable`). It is `tabIndex={0}` with a group label now.
* **Visual QA** — the new university `/manage` rendered **nothing** at all three widths, caught as `h1=0`. The
  university router's `page()` helper returns the loader itself (`lazy: page(…)`), where the agency's returns an
  object to spread (`...page(…)`). Written the agency's way, the spread produced `{}`, so the route matched and
  had no component. `routes` is untyped in that file, so `tsc` had nothing to object to — the only gate that
  could see it was the one that opens the page and looks for a heading.
* **By eye** — the student menu rendered "Going to Korea" as a heading over nothing, because V11 gates that
  group on the journey stage. Empty groups are not rendered now.
* **E2E** — the agency upload test began failing after the workspace merge. The cause was the new
  scroll-to-section: `behavior: 'smooth'` was still animating when the first click landed, so the button moved
  out from under it. It is an instant jump now, which is also the better behaviour — arriving on a URL should
  put you where you asked to be rather than glide you there while the page settles.

One apparent defect was **not** real: a full-page capture of the writing queue at 768 px showed a row overlapping
the table's sticky header. Measured live at a real scroll position, `top` resolves to 76 px and the header never
goes behind the app chrome — Playwright's full-page screenshots reposition sticky elements. Worth recording so it
is not "fixed" later.

## 80.3 Page weight

| | V10 | V11 |
|---|---|---|
| Marketing CSS (one bundle) | 249 KB | **210 KB** |
| Home page height @1440 | 9 sections | 6 sections, 7.0 screens |
| Home page height @390 | — | 7.3 screens |
| University crests | n/a (text chips) | 23 SVG, 826 KB raw / **337 KB gzipped**, loaded at `fetchpriority="low"` |
| Console chart chunk | 429.45 KB (122.07 gz) | **380.12 KB** (110.58 gz) — three unrendered chart types deleted |
| Dead CSS removed | — | 38 selectors / 35 rules across the three consoles, plus `v10.css` deleted and `v6.css` halved in marketing (§79.9) |
| Home LCP, throttled phone (4× CPU, ~9 Mbps) | 2.23 s (V7 baseline) | **1.97 s** (2.38 s with the VM under load from a parallel suite — the range, not a single reading) |
| Home LCP, desktop | — | **0.98 s** |
| Home transfer, phone / desktop | — | 996 KB / 856 KB |

7.0 and 7.3 screens are inside the brief's "avoid a 12-screen homepage".

## 80.4 Locale check

The homepage's 53 `v11.*` strings exist in **two canonical locales** — ko and ru, both taken from the owner's
template and both gated character-for-character — plus **en**, an AI translation of the Korean. The other 52
locales have none and fall back to English, verified by loading the page in Vietnamese, Russian and Arabic:
**0 raw keys** reach the screen (Russian now renders its own canonical copy, not the fallback). This is still a
coverage regression against V10 and is recorded as one, per locale, in `docs/qa/v11/translation-status.json`
and in §82. No locale is marked `HUMAN_REVIEWED`.

The gate also refuses any tag outside the four the renderer handles (`<br>`, the two `text-*` spans, the `<h2>`
wrapper), so a future copy change cannot silently render markup as visible text.

# 81. V11 Final Hostile Review

*Written as a senior product designer who does not like this product and wants to find what is still wrong.*

## 81.1 "Why does this still feel AI-made?" — what I found, and fixed

| Finding | Done |
|---|---|
| The homepage's fifth movement showed four screenshots of our own product to someone who has not decided they want to study in Korea. | Removed. |
| Four public pages — `/how-it-works`, `/students`, `/trust`, `/guides` — each explained the service in prose. Nobody reads four. | Removed or merged. |
| Three ways to see "what is late" in the agency console (Today, Tasks, Deadlines) and two in the student app (Home, Tasks). | One each. |
| `/documents` and `/essays` were two top-level concepts for one job done by one person in one sitting. | One Review area, two modes. |
| Seven administrative pages in the agency rail, five in the university rail, competing with daily work. | One Manage area each. |
| The student rail changed its five slots three times on the way to Korea, so the same position meant Compare, then Documents, then Visa. | Four fixed destinations. |
| `/trust` was a filterable source registry — a console UI on a public page, with a status filter row, a search box, status badges and a review-interval column. | A flat list: what it is, where it is, when we last looked. |
| `v10.css` still shipped: every rule in it targeted a section V11 no longer renders. `v6.css` still carried the quick-check's styles. | `v10.css` deleted, `v6.css` 136 → 68 lines. |

## 81.2 Three defects the gates could not see

All three passed typecheck, every unit test, axe and the overflow sweep. All three were found by looking.

1. **Two crests rendered as nothing**, leaving a hole in a moving row, because my own optimiser rounded a
   normalised pattern matrix to zeros.
2. **Crests popped in mid-loop** — `loading="lazy"` inside a track that is wider than the viewport.
3. **Reduced motion repeated every logo four times.** The static fallback is supposed to show each crest once;
   an inline `display: contents` on the duplicated half outranked the rule that hides duplicates. Only a
   reduced-motion render shows this, so there is now a test that does exactly that.

Two more followed the same shape:

4. **The university `/manage` page rendered nothing** — a route helper copied from the agency app, where it has
   a different signature. `tsc` could not see it because that router's `routes` is untyped; the visual sweep
   caught it as a missing `<h1>`.
5. **An empty menu heading.** Gating the student menu's Korea group on the journey stage left "Going to Korea"
   as a title over nothing for every student who is not going yet.

The pattern is worth stating: this pass began because green gates and a bad product are not a contradiction, and
it ended by finding five more defects the same way — three of them introduced by this pass's own changes.

Listed plainly rather than quietly left out.

|---|---|---|
| 1 | **"The agency student workspace still has nine equal tabs."** It had **ten**. Now four, with the old tabs as addressable sections and every `?tab=` link still resolving. | **Done** (§79.7) |
| 2 | **"You wrote a chart standard and audited no charts."** Audited. Three of the four chart types the design system shipped had no call site anywhere — removed, chart chunk 429 → 380 KB. The rendered ones pass the test and already print their question on the card. | **Done** (§79.7) |
| 3 | **"HQ is untouched."** Five destinations → three; the three tools moved off the incident view. | **Done** (§79.7) |

The rest still fall back to English with no raw keys. | Improved; recorded, §82 |
| 5 | **"Eight filter chips on the agency Today screen."** True, and I kept them deliberately. They are counts of real work by kind and let a counsellor batch similar cases, which is a real working habit; removing a used control to lower a number would be the brief's own "do not optimize for an arbitrary number if it harms real work". Judged, not overlooked. | Kept |
| 6 | **"The university Applicants header now carries breadcrumbs and two buttons on one line."** Fair — it is busier than it was, the cost of removing two rail items. | Accepted |

| 8 | **"Marketing CSS is still 210 KB."** Down from 249 KB, but the Eduan layer still loads for the inner pages. | Partly |

## 81.4 The question the homepage now has to answer

Does it make someone want to study in Korea? It opens on a full-viewport Korean campus in autumn with four words
of Korean over it, moves to twenty-three real university crests in three rows, and then says — in the owner's own
sentences, not ours — what the service does and what it costs you to find out. It asks for a login, never an
application. There is no metric on it, no product screenshot, no card grid of features, and no icon before any
heading.

What it is not yet: translated into anything but Korean and English.
