# 83. V12 Production-Likeness Audit

*2026-10-17, before any V12 code change. Method: every customer-visible string in `packages/i18n/locales/{en,ko}`
read by a script that walks the JSON and matches the brief's vocabulary against the **values**, not the keys;
then every rendered route opened in a browser and looked at. Counts are of what reaches a screen.*

## 83.1 The distinction the audit had to make first

The brief lists words to search for — DEV, Demo, Sample, Fixture, Draft, Readiness, 개발, 초안, 준비 중 — and it
also says "maintain an explicit allow-list". Those two instructions are the whole audit, because four of those
words are ordinary product vocabulary in this domain and three are not:

| Word | Ordinary meaning here | Development signal |
|---|---|---|
| `draft` / `초안` | an essay or application **is** a draft; "Open your draft" is the student's own work | "Draft — not final, not legal advice" over a policy page |
| `준비 중` | 서류 준비 중, 비자 준비 중 — real journey stages | `states.comingSoon`, `exports.notYet` — the "coming soon" sense |
| `sample` | "the sample is too small to rate" — a statistical statement on a console metric | "Sample data", "Sample University, Seoul" |
| `readiness` | share of the document checklist complete at submission — a metric agencies and universities use | `v8.nav.readiness` = "Production readiness", an engineering dashboard |

A scan that bans the word fails on the first column; a scan that excludes the word misses the second. So the
audit worked by **key**, not by word, and the leak gate built from it (§90.6) does the same.

## 83.2 What was actually there, by surface

Fifty-one key paths matched. Of those, **18 still had a render site**; the other 33 were strings left behind by
V11's route removals — dead weight in the bundle, invisible to a customer. The 18 that mattered:

| Surface | What a customer saw |
|---|---|
| `/privacy`, `/terms` | "Draft" eyebrow over the title, a warning callout "Draft — not final, not legal advice", and *"Final wording to be provided by legal counsel."* under all nine sections. The SEO title was literally "Privacy policy (draft)". |
| `/credits` | A source row named **"Hangyul Univ development sample data"**, linking to `github.com/hangyul/hangyul-univ#demo-data`, with the summary "Placeholder values for development. Not verified facts." |
| all four apps | A floating **DEV** chip, bottom-right, on every screen. |
| three native apps | The same chip once signed in, plus "Development build · API http://…" under the login form. |
| every console login | An inline "Demo access" persona picker on the sign-in screen. |
| agency Today, agency deadlines, student submission | A programme named **"Authorised-submission fixture (development only)"** — the V6 fixture, reaching the UI through *stored task titles*. |
| agency Messages | "Email · WhatsApp · KakaoTalk · Zalo · SMS — Not connected — needs provider credentials", on the composer, plus a page note repeating it in prose. |
| agency document review | "Not scanned (development)" / "검사 안 함 (개발 환경)" on every document. |
| agency Students | Every row carried the student's email: `student01@demo.hangyul.kr`. |
| agency HQ | "Production readiness" as a navigation item; `DEVELOPMENT_ONLY` statuses; "Demo payment"; `hq.kind.DEMO` = "Synthetic". |
| student services | "Demo payment — no real charge", "Confirm demo payment". |
| university console header | A **"Hangyul partner"** badge, driven by `University.is_partner`, which the seed sets from `PartnerContract` rows with `is_demo=True`. |

## 83.3 The pattern

Three of these are worth separating out, because they are not carelessness and fixing them naively makes the
product worse:

1. **The DEV chip was correctly gated.** `import.meta.env.DEV || VITE_DEMO_LOGINS` — it could never ship. The
   defect was never that it leaked to production; it was that *every screenshot anyone takes of this product,
   in any review, in any deck*, has a badge in the corner saying the product is a development build. Capability
   was not the problem. Its permanent claim on ordinary chrome was.
2. **"Not scanned (development)" and "Not connected" were honest.** Development does run a no-op malware
   scanner; no message provider is connected. Relabelling either one would be a lie. The answer is not better
   wording — it is that a working screen is the wrong place to report infrastructure state.
3. **The "Sample data" labels were the right instinct, applied to the wrong surface.** Labelling an unverified
   figure beats publishing it bare. But the brief's rule is sharper and correct: on a public surface, a value
   we cannot verify should **not be rendered at all**. The label was V10's way of keeping a page that should
   not have existed.

## 83.4 Where the fixture leak actually lived

Worth recording separately, because it defeated every gate V11 had and would defeat a careless V12 gate too.

`extra_60_submission_v6.py` seeds an inactive programme called "Authorised-submission fixture (development
only)" to exercise the authorised-agency submission path, which no real Korean university permits. `is_active=False`
keeps it out of the catalogue, matching and the public site — so the seed's own precautions were sound.

It reached the screen anyway, through **task titles**: the task engine writes "Submit your {program} application
to {university}" into `tasks.title` and `tasks.title_params` at seed time. Those are stored rows. No front-end
change, no i18n audit and no scan of the public site could have found it; only opening the agency Today screen
and reading it could, which is how it was found.

# 84. V12 Legal & Customer Trust Audit

## 84.1 The page, as shipped by V11

The screenshot the brief supplies is accurate, and the cause of each defect is in one 33-line file
(`pages/Legal.tsx`):

| Defect | Cause |
|---|---|
| Full-bleed photograph of Seoul traffic at night, ~390px tall, above the title | `<PageHero photo=…>` — the same hero component the marketing pages use |
| "Draft" eyebrow over the title | `eyebrow={t('legalPages.draftBadge')}` |
| A warning callout under the hero | `<Callout tone="warning">` with `legalPages.draftTitle` |
| "Final wording to be provided by legal counsel." under every section | `<p className="mk-legal__placeholder">` rendered unconditionally for all nine sections |
| Table of contents and every heading flush at x = 0 | `mk-container--narrow` had no rules; the container never applied a gutter or a width |
| "Start studying in Korea now." marketing band at the foot | `SiteLayout` renders its default closing CTA for every page that does not override it, and `null` means *default*, not *none* |
| Footer disclaimers and "Partner sign-in: University console / Agency console" | the shared footer |

Nine sections, each one `<h2>` + one sentence + one placeholder. The whole document was 1,100 words of structure
and no content.

## 84.2 What the product actually processes

The privacy policy had to be derived from the code, so the code was read: `users`, `student_profiles`,
`student_educations`, `student_languages`, `documents` + `document_versions` (24 `DocumentCategory` kinds),
`messages`, `essays` + `essay_versions` + `essay_comments`, `appointments`, `application_status_history`,
`tasks`, `orders`, `payments`, `service_cases`, `login_events`, `audit_logs`, `analytics_events`. The audit is
`docs/qa/v12/PRIVACY_DATA_MAP.md`, generated from the same module the page renders from.

Four findings changed what the policy can say:

1. **No card data exists anywhere.** `Payment` holds provider, provider reference, status, amount, currency and
   a sanitised payload. Checkout is provider-hosted. The policy can therefore state plainly that Hangyul does
   not store card numbers, expiry dates, security codes or billing addresses — and a Korean reader has every
   reason to doubt that sentence unless it is said explicitly.
2. **There is no third-party analytics, advertising or tracking of any kind.** A repository-wide scan for
   Google Analytics, GTM, Segment, Mixpanel, Hotjar, Meta, Sentry, PostHog, Amplitude and Clarity returns
   nothing. Client storage is one httpOnly refresh cookie per app, scoped to `/api/v1/auth`, plus `localStorage`
   interface preferences (`hg.locale`, sidebar, theme, compare list, currency) that never leave the browser.
   **There is no consent-requiring cookie, so there is no cookie banner** — which is what brief Part 9
   anticipated and what the audit confirms rather than assumes.
3. **No processor is configured in production.** File storage is the local filesystem; the malware scanner is a
   no-op recording `SKIPPED`; no email, SMS or chat provider is connected; the payment provider is the
   development stub. §§4–5 of the policy say exactly that, and say it from a list (`PROCESSORS`) that is empty,
   so both sections become false the moment a vendor is contracted — which is the only safe way to write them.
4. **No retention schedule exists.** `LEGAL_DEPENDENCIES.md` L8 has carried it as `OPEN` since V9, there is no
   retention job, and the student-facing text said "legal retention policy pending approval". The four Korean
   statutory commerce periods are publishable; the periods for documents, accounts and logs are not. §2
   publishes the rule Hangyul does follow and the four statutory records, and no invented number.

## 84.3 The company does not exist in this repository

Searched for: registered legal name, corporate form, business registration number, e-commerce registration
number, address, representative, privacy officer, department, contact email, phone, governing law, jurisdiction,
announcement date, effective date. **None of them has a value anywhere** — not in `app/core/config.py`, not in
the i18n bundles, not in the footer. §74.3 recorded the footer identity block as "empty pending owner-supplied
data" and nothing has filled it since.

The brief's Part 25 is therefore the load-bearing instruction for this pass, and it has a consequence worth
stating plainly: **the privacy policy and the terms of service cannot be production-ready in this pass, and no
amount of engineering changes that.** What engineering can do is make the absence honest instead of decorative —
render nothing where a required field is missing, and record the field as a blocker.

One more edit the audit forced. The brief's own Korean baseline opens *"주식회사 한귤(이하 '한귤')은"*. 한귤 is the
verified brand (confirmed against `/root/hangyul-web/messages/ko.json`, §V8); **주식회사 한귤** asserts a corporate
registration nobody has recorded. The published copy says 한귤, and the registered legal name is §92's first row.

## 84.4 The disclaimers

A copy search for the repeated legalistic sentences found **50 distinct keys** across nine namespaces. Only
**seven** still had a render site — the rest died with V11's route removals. The seven:

| Where | Sentence |
|---|---|
| `/credits`, student sign-in, student Compare | "Universities make all admission decisions. Hangyul does not guarantee admission unless…" |
| student Services | "Support helps you prepare strong, complete applications. Universities make every admission decision, and visas are issued by…" |
| student Start (eligibility result) | "This is an eligibility check against published requirements, not an admission prediction. Universities make every decision." |
| student Visa | **"Hangyul does not issue visas."** + "Visas are issued by the Korean government (embassy, consulate or immigration office)." |
| student Sponsor | "…모든 결정은 대학과 대사관이 합니다." |
| mobile quick check | "This is an eligibility check, not an admission guarantee." |
| marketing footer (every page) | "Hangyul does not issue visas. Visa decisions are made by the Korean immigration authorities." |

The visa one is the clearest case the brief makes. A student on the visa screen has an admission letter and is
assembling a financial statement. Telling them a government issues visas is not information; it is the product
apologising for itself in the one place the student needed a list of documents.

What must *not* be lost with it is the official action context, and that already exists and is better: the visa
route names the actual submission post (`주{{city}} 대한민국 대사관`), the method (방문 신청 / 대행기관 접수 / CCVI),
the fee with "한귤이 아닌 대사관에 내는 비용", the embassy's own English wording, a source link and a
verification date. That is authority shown naturally, which is what Part 5 asks for in place of a box.

# 85. V12 Korean University Directory Strategy

## 85.1 What the public catalogue was

Ten universities. Every number on them — tuition, fees, living cost, dorm cost, seats, GPA minimums — seeded
with `verification_status=DEMO` (`server/app/seed/catalog_data.py`, line 2 of its own docstring says so).
Programme names "representative samples, not a verified list of each university's offerings". Three of the ten
carried fictional `PartnerContract` rows.

On that data, `/universities` was built as a **programme search engine**: a filter sidebar (degree, region,
language, "Hangyul partners only"), a sort control (relevance / deadline / tuition / name), 66 results across
six pages, and a card wall where the largest element on each card was a first-year total — ₩18.8M, ₩19M,
₩26.7M, ₩13.2M, ₩20.6M — above a TOPIK level and an application deadline. Because there is one photograph per
university and six programmes each, the same Kyung Hee campus picture appeared six times down the first column.

Every one of those figures was sample data, and the page led with them.

## 85.2 The question the public page should answer

*What kinds of universities can I study at in Korea?* — not *which intake row from our database should you apply
to?* The second question needs the visitor's nationality, education, GPA, language scores, budget and intake,
none of which a public page has, and all of which the authenticated Student Platform already holds.

## 85.3 The sources, and why in that order

| Tier | Source | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical registry | **대학알리미 / AcademyInfo** (`academyinfo.go.kr`) | whether an institution exists, its official Korean name, its division, its establishment, its region, its campus role. Nothing else. |
| International enrichment | **Study in Korea** (`studyinkorea.go.kr`) | IEQAS certification (교육국제화역량 인증제) — degree programmes, Korean-language programmes, and the "outstanding" subset |
| Reference | **Wikidata** | English name, official website, coordinates |

The registry is reached through the endpoint its own school picker uses,
`POST /main/main0790/selectList.do`, which returns the full public-disclosure dataset for a survey year. The
2025 dataset is **1,578 rows**. The payload repeats its own row count on every row, so a truncated response is
detectable, and the importer fails on a mismatch rather than silently publishing a short list.

Of those 1,578 rows, **1,126 are 대학원** — the graduate *school* of a university that is already in the list.
A graduate school is a faculty, not an institution; including them would have tripled the directory with
duplicates of their own parents. Excluding them leaves **452 institution rows**, of which **425 are 본교** (main
campuses). The other 27 are 분교 and 제2/3/4캠퍼스, recorded against their main campus so a branch is never
presented as a separate university.

Study in Korea is enrichment and not the registry for exactly the reason the brief gives — its own search is not
exhaustive. What it uniquely provides is worth having: IEQAS certification is reviewed annually by the Ministry
of Justice and the Ministry of Education and **relaxes visa criteria for applicants**, which is a fact with a
consequence a prospective student can act on, unlike a ranking.

## 85.4 What the dataset contains

`server/app/data/korean_institutions.json`, built by `scripts/catalog/import_korean_universities.py`:

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Active institutions | **425** |
| — 대학 (university) | 218 |
| — 전문대학 (junior college) | 163 |
| — 대학원대학 (graduate institution) | 44 |
| With an English name | 302 |
| With an official website | 281 |
| IEQAS certified (degree programmes) | 173 |
| IEQAS outstanding | 43 |
| IEQAS certified Korean-language programme | 118 |
| Withdrawn (retained, never shown as available) | 0 |

The three IEQAS lists parse against the page's **own declared totals** — 184 / 126 / 43 across 일반대학,
전문대학 and 대학원대학 — and the importer fails if any group's parsed count differs from the count the page
prints next to it. Two of the 353 listed names do not match an institution and both are correctly outside the
directory: `국립창원대학교 남해캠퍼스` (a branch campus) and `한국학중앙연구원 한국학대학원` (the graduate school of a
research institute, which is not in the registry's institution divisions).

National universities were renamed with a 국립 prefix between 2023 and 2025 (공주대학교 → 국립공주대학교) and Wikidata
mostly carries the older label, so the match key drops that prefix **for matching only** — the published name is
always the registry's.

## 85.5 What is deliberately absent

Dormitory availability, English-taught course availability and scholarship availability are all named in the
brief as possible enrichment, and all three are **absent from every card and every detail page**, because no
source consulted publishes them per institution in a form that could be verified. A field with no source is not
rendered. That is why two universities' pages are different lengths, and why there is no grid of grey dashes.

The one near-miss worth recording: Wikidata returns a `located in the administrative territorial entity` value,
but for Seoul institutions it is a district (관악구) and elsewhere a city, so it is inconsistent as a "city"
field. The directory publishes **region**, which comes from the registry and is authoritative, and publishes no
city at all.

# 86. V12 Public Experience Reduction

## 86.1 `/universities` — what was removed

| Removed | Why |
|---|---|
| Programme cards (66 across 6 pages) | a programme is an application decision, and that happens signed in |
| First-year totals (₩13.2M–₩26.7M) on browsing cards | sample data, and cost does not belong in front of desire (Part 10) |
| Application deadlines per programme | changes by intake; belongs beside the application |
| TOPIK / IELTS requirements per card | means nothing without the visitor's own scores |
| Degree / language / sort controls | filters for a search that is no longer happening |
| "Hangyul partners only" checkbox | a partnership filter over three fictional contracts |
| Repeated campus photography | one picture per university × six programmes = the same photo six times |
| Keyword search in a photographic hero | the page is browsed by place now |

## 86.2 What it is instead

A question, a map, and the institutions that are there. The first viewport is *한국에서 어디에서 공부하고 싶나요?*
and one line of copy; below it, the Korea map on the left and the selected region's institutions on the right.
Each entry gives the university's name in both scripts, its region, its kind, who runs it, and — only when the
published list names it — its IEQAS certifications. No price, no date, no score, no partnership.

## 86.3 Cost, and where it went

Public discovery now renders **no monetary figure at all**. The three components that could produce one —
`components/EdCards.tsx`, `components/catalog.tsx`, `components/AButton.tsx` — had already been orphaned by the
page rewrite (0 importers) and were deleted, so a `formatMoney` call cannot return to a public surface by
accident. A grep for `formatMoney|KRW|₩` across `apps/marketing-web/src` now matches one comment and nothing else.

Cost did not get quieter; it got moved to where a student is deciding rather than dreaming. Signed in, the
Student Platform still shows tuition, the application fee, housing, living costs, the Hangyul fee, scholarships
and pre-arrival cash — with payee, timing and refundability per line (`services/money.py`, V9). The rule the
brief states is the rule as built: **do not hide cost when deciding; do not lead with cost while dreaming.**

## 86.4 The homepage count

Koreanasha's marquee heading reads "50+개 이상의 한국 대학교가 여러분의 입학을 기다리고 있습니다". V11 bound the figure
to `useUniversities` — the ten institutions Hangyul holds admission data for — so a sentence about Korea rendered
as a sentence about our own coverage: *10곳의 한국 대학교*.

V12 binds it to the directory's **university** count: **218**. Not all 425 rows, because the sentence says
대학교 and junior colleges and graduate-only institutions are not what that word means. The threshold the brief
sets for the "50+" claim is met more than four times over, and it describes the directory, not a contract count.

## 86.5 No partnership is implied anywhere

The directory card carries a `has_catalog` boolean — whether Hangyul holds verified admission data — and it is
**never rendered as a label**. It only decides which call to action a signed-in visitor gets. The word "partner"
appears nowhere in the public directory, on any card or on any detail page.

# 87. V12 Student UX Re-Audit

## 87.1 What V11 left, and whether it holds

V11 cut the student rail from 16 destinations to 5 and rebuilt the home screen around three questions. Opened
and read at 1440 and 390, it holds:

* **Where am I** — a six-step journey band (Discover ✓ · **Prepare** · Apply · Admission · Visa · Arrival) with
  "You are here" and one sentence of what this stage is.
* **What should I do** — one next step, named concretely: *"Fix your academic transcript for Pusan National
  University · Business Administration (BBA)"*, with *"Your application can't be submitted until this is fixed"*
  and one primary button.
* **When** — "Due Oct 28, 2026 · 12 days left".
* Then applications, then what else can be done today, then the counsellor. No metric row.

The brief's Part 13 asks for simplification *inside* the pages and explicitly warns against reducing for a
number. Measured against the work a student does, the student app did not need another reduction, and it did not
get one.

## 87.2 The one thing that was broken

The public directory's call to action — *이 대학 유학 준비하기* — pointed at the Student Platform's
`/universities/:slug`, which reads the **application catalogue**. The catalogue holds 10 of the directory's 425
institutions, so the primary action on the public site led to a 404 for **415 universities**.

This is brief Part 22, and the honest answer is not to hide the action or to fabricate programme data for the
other 415. A university Hangyul has no verified admission data for is the ordinary case, not an error, and the
product has something real to offer in it: a counsellor who can go and check. §90.5 has the build.

# 88. V12 Agency UX Re-Audit

## 88.1 Seven destinations, measured against the work

Part 14 asks whether even seven are necessary and says to measure work, not to reduce for a target. Opening
Today as a counsellor:

| Slot | Is it where work happens? |
|---|---|
| **Today** | yes — the prioritised queue, 10 rows, each with student, reason, deadline, waiting-on and one action |
| **Students** | yes — the caseload, filterable, the same rows from a different angle |
| **Review** | yes — documents and writing, two modes of one surface |
| **Messages** | yes |
| Applications | supporting — reached from a student more often than from the rail |
| Performance | management context, not daily work |
| Manage | administration, one slot for six former destinations |

Four primary, three supporting — which is exactly the model the brief describes, already built. Removing
Applications or Performance would move real work behind an extra hop to make a number smaller; the brief forbids
that in the same breath as it asks the question.

## 88.2 Today, as built

No KPI cards. The first heading is **"Who needs you today"** with a count, then eight filter chips by kind of
work, then the ranked queue with "How is this ordered?" beside it. Right column: **Waiting on** by party
(Counselor 5 · Agency team 1 · Student 4 · University 1) and **Next 14 days**. That is Part 14's specification,
and V11 built it.

## 88.3 What the audit found wrong

Not the structure — the content:

1. A programme named "Authorised-submission fixture (development only)" in two queue rows and two timeline
   entries (§83.4).
2. Every caseload row printed the student's email, which was `student01@demo.hangyul.kr`. The email is also not
   what a counsellor reads a queue by: the row already carries name, country, university, stage, reason, action
   and deadline.
3. The message composer offered Email, WhatsApp, KakaoTalk, Zalo and SMS as disabled options beside "Not
   connected — needs provider credentials", with the same statement repeated in prose above the thread and
   again in Settings.
4. Document review printed "Not scanned (development)" on every document.

## 88.4 Visualisations retained

Unchanged from V11's audit, which was done properly: workload by counsellor (horizontal bars — who is
overloaded) and cases by stage with ageing (where work accumulates). V11 also found that three of the four chart
types the design system shipped had **no call site anywhere** and deleted them. No chart was added in V12 and
none was removed.

# 89. V12 University UX Re-Audit

## 89.1 Six destinations, and the Overview

Overview opens on **"Needs your decision — 5 decisions waiting on your team"** with a link to all of them, then
**"This intake's progress"** (the eight-step funnel from submitted to enrolled, with the largest drop marked and
rates withheld below five records), then two summaries under "ALSO TODAY": **Waiting on applicants** and
**Coming up**. That is Part 15's specification almost exactly.

## 89.2 What the audit found wrong

1. **A half-empty card.** The two "Also today" summaries sit in a Bootstrap row, which stretches its columns.
   *Waiting on applicants* has two rows and *Coming up* has six, so the shorter card grew to the taller one's
   height — **162px of content in a 510px card**, about 320px of empty box under two lines of text. An empty
   card reads as a product that expected data it does not have.
2. **A partnership badge on fictional data.** The console header showed **"Hangyul partner"** beside Pusan
   National University, driven by `University.is_partner`, which the seed sets from `PartnerContract` rows with
   `is_demo=True`. V6 established that a partner label needs a verified, non-synthetic agreement before it may
   appear on a public page; a badge nobody can produce the paperwork for is a partnership claim wherever it is
   rendered.

## 89.3 Analytics retained

The four V11 kept answer the four questions Part 15 names: the admissions funnel (where applicants drop),
country → enrolment (which countries convert), programme demand, and the post-admission lifecycle
(admission → visa → arrival → enrolment). Nothing decorative was found and nothing was added.


# 90. V12 Implementation Log

*Order follows the dependency chain, not the brief: the data had to exist before the directory could be built,
and the directory had to exist before the homepage could count it.*

## 90.1 The data pipeline

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/catalog/sources.py` | the three sources, the 17 `zn_cd` → region-key mappings, the division and establishment mappings. One place where 대학알리미 and the product's own region taxonomy are joined. |
| `scripts/catalog/import_korean_universities.py` | fetch → merge → write. `--offline` re-merges from the cached raw payloads, `--check` fails if the committed file is not what a fresh merge produces. |
| `server/app/data/raw/` | the raw payloads, committed: the registry JSON, the IEQAS page, the Wikidata result, the KOSTAT boundaries. A dataset nobody can re-derive is not a dataset. |
| `server/app/data/korean_institutions.json` | 348 KB, 425 active institutions, every field carrying the source that produced it. |

Design decisions worth recording:

* **Every published field names its source, and a field with no source is absent.** There is no default, no
  inferred value and no placeholder anywhere in the merge. This is the whole reason the directory can be shown
  without labels on it.
* **Merger and closure handling.** The registry is the arbiter of existence. The importer reads the previous
  committed file before writing, and anything the current registry no longer lists is retained with
  `status: "WITHDRAWN"` and a `withdrawn_at` date — never deleted, and never served by the API, which filters on
  `status == 'ACTIVE'`. The first run of a new disclosure year therefore reports exactly what changed. Today:
  0 withdrawn.
* **`academyinfo_id` is the identity**, not the name. A renamed institution is recognised as a rename rather
  than as one closing and another opening, which matters because 국립 prefixes were added across the national
  universities between 2023 and 2025.
* **Self-validating parses.** The registry payload repeats its own row count on every row; the IEQAS page prints
  a total beside each group. The importer fails on a mismatch in either, so a silently truncated response
  cannot become a short directory.

## 90.2 The directory, as data

| Layer | File |
|---|---|
| Model | `server/app/models/institution.py` — `institutions`, 26 columns, deliberately **not** `universities` |
| Migration | `alembic/versions/v12_institutions.py` (`v12inst0001`, down from `v9a1agencyops`) |
| Loader | `server/app/seed/institutions.py` — idempotent upsert keyed on `academyinfo_id` |
| Live refresh | `server/scripts/v12_load_institutions.py` — the directory only, for a populated database |
| API | `server/app/api/v1/directory.py` — `/directory/regions`, `/directory/institutions`, `/directory/institutions/{slug}` |

Part 21's architectural separation is the point of the model file, and its docstring carries it: `Institution`
exists because the institution exists; `University` exists because Hangyul holds enough verified admission data
to prepare a real application against it. `catalog_university_id` is the one link and it is nullable **because a
university in the directory with no catalogue entry is the normal case** — 415 of 425 today — and not an error.

The API module carries the same rule as an invariant: there is no price, no deadline, no requirement, no match
and no partnership in it, and a reviewer can confirm that by reading one 165-line file.

## 90.3 The map

`scripts/catalog/build_korea_map.py` turns KOSTAT's census administrative boundaries (센서스용 행정구역경계, 2013
simplified province set, redistributed by `github.com/southkorea/southkorea-maps`) into
`apps/marketing-web/src/media/korea-regions.ts` — 17 paths, 48 KB, `viewBox 0 0 820 869`.

**Licence, checked before use.** That repository states its KOSTAT material is "free to share or remix" and its
**GADM** material is non-commercial with redistribution not allowed. Only the `kostat/` path is used; nothing
touches `gadm/`. The attribution is on `/credits` with everything else published under licence.

Projection is equirectangular with longitude scaled by cos(mid-latitude) — over Korea's five degrees of latitude
visually indistinguishable from a conic projection, and two multiplications that anyone can check. The label
anchor is the centroid of each region's **largest** landmass, because Jeollanam-do has 63 rings and the mean of
all of them is in the Yellow Sea.

`components/KoreaMap.tsx` renders it as a `radiogroup` of `radio`s, which is what a one-at-a-time region
selector actually is. Arrow keys move, Space/Enter picks, a roving tabindex keeps the whole map one tab stop,
and each region's accessible name is "{region} · {n} institutions". Hover state lives in React rather than in
`:hover` because the readout has to be driven from it and because a touch device must not get stuck in a hover
it cannot leave.

Two deliberate design choices:

* **No permanent labels.** Seventeen of them collide in the capital region — Seoul, Incheon and Gyeonggi overlap
  at this scale, and Sejong, Daejeon and Chungnam do too. One live readout under the map does not collide and
  says more (region + count).
* **Dots on the eight metropolitan regions.** Seoul is a few pixels across at 420px wide. The dot is not
  decoration; it is the part of the control you can hit with a mouse or a fingertip.

The map is **never the only way in** (Part 23): `RegionSelector` renders the same 18 choices as ordinary
buttons, and on a phone that list *is* the control — the map is `aria-hidden` there rather than shrunk to an
unusable 320px.

## 90.4 The public directory and university pages

`/universities` — question, map, region chips, institution list, source line. URL state is
`?region=seoul` (lower-case, so it reads like a place), parsed case-insensitively back to the registry's key,
written with a real history entry so the back button undoes a region choice. Selecting a region on a phone
scrolls to the list with `behavior: 'auto'` — V11 recorded why a smooth scroll driven by a URL change swallows
the next tap (§80.2), and that lesson is applied rather than relearned.

The list is an **editorial list, not a card wall**: a rule between entries, no box, no shadow, no photograph.
That is partly taste and partly arithmetic — one photograph per university across 425 of them would be either
425 unlicensed images or the same picture repeated, which is what V11's grid actually did.

`/universities/:slug` — a university introduction. Name in both scripts, region, kind, establishment, one
primary action, the official site. Then: the verified facts, the IEQAS certifications **with what they mean for
a visa**, and an "Official information" section listing every source with the date it was checked. A section
with nothing verified to put in it does not render, which is why two universities' pages are different lengths.

## 90.5 Part 22 — the call to action that used to 404

The public action pointed at the Student Platform's `/universities/:slug`, which reads the application
catalogue, so it 404'd for 415 of 425 universities. `apps/student-web/src/pages/University.tsx` now treats a
404 from the catalogue as a state rather than a failure and renders `DirectoryOnlyUniversity`: the institution's
verified facts and the one thing genuinely on offer — **"Ask your counsellor"**, which opens Messages — plus the
university's own site and a way back to browsing. No programme, no deadline, no fee and no eligibility verdict
is invented for it.

## 90.6 The development-tool boundary

| Change | Where |
|---|---|
| DEV chip removed from the public site | `SiteLayout.tsx` |
| DEV chip removed from both web shells | `packages/ui/src/shells.tsx` (`ConsoleShell`, `StudentShell`) |
| DEV chip removed from the console shell | `packages/ynex-ui/src/components/Shell.tsx` |
| Inline persona picker removed from every console sign-in | `packages/ui/src/app.tsx` |
| Floating chip and "Development build · API …" removed from the native apps | `packages/mobile-ui/src/bootstrap/LoginScreen.tsx`; `DevAccessChip` and `DevIndicator` deleted |
| `/__dev` route in all four web apps | `packages/ui/src/devtools.tsx` + one page per app |
| Hidden gesture on native | five taps on the login heading, development builds only |

The now-inert `demo` / `showDemo` / `demoAccounts` props were removed from the shell and login signatures rather
than left defaulting to `true` — a prop nothing reads is a prop somebody will wire up again.

`/__dev` is gated **at the route table** (`...(import.meta.env.DEV ? [...] : [])`) and again inside the
component, so a production build contains neither the route nor the persona list it imports. On native there is
no route table, so the equivalent is a five-tap gesture on the sign-in heading; nothing on screen advertises it,
and in production there is no sheet to open.

## 90.7 The legal documents

`components/LegalLayout.tsx` — the standard floating pill, then a restrained header (eyebrow, title, one-line
summary, effective date **only if configured**), then a single column capped at an 820px measure. Sticky section
navigation beside the column at ≥1200px, where there is room for it without stealing from the measure; a
disclosure above the text at every narrower width. No hero image, no card, and `useNoClosingCta()` suppresses
the marketing band outright — `null` meant *default* in the old context, so an explicit "no band here" state had
to exist.

Body is 17px/1.85 with `word-break: keep-all` on the Korean, which is the difference between 회원 및 계정 and
회원 및 / 계 / 정 in a narrow table cell. Tables are ruled rows with no zebra and no card, and below 768px each
row becomes its own block with the column name above each cell — a four-column processing table cannot be read
at 390px and must not be solved by letting it clip.

`/privacy` ships **10 sections**, `/terms` **14**, both from the structured inventory in
`src/lib/legal/data-map.ts`, which `scripts/qa/v12-privacy-data-map.mjs` also generates the engineering audit
from. One source, so the published policy and the audit cannot drift.

`src/lib/legal/entity.ts` holds the company identity. Every field is `null`, `REQUIRED_FOR_LAUNCH` names the ten
that a Korean privacy policy and terms of service cannot be complete without, and the pages render a section
**only when its required fields exist**. §10 of the privacy policy (개인정보 보호책임자) and §15 of the terms
(준거법 및 관할) therefore do not appear at all today — which is a different and more honest state than a page
that looks finished and says `[회사명]`.

## 90.8 Copy

`scripts/i18n/v12-copy.mjs` installs 212 keys in ko and 212 in en. Korean is the brief's baseline with three
classes of edit, each argued in the script's own docstring: the corporate form (§84.3), the retention periods
(§84.2), and the processor/overseas-transfer sections written from the configured list rather than as prose.
English is a translation of the Korean written in the same pass. It is not human-reviewed and is not marked so.

## 90.9 The seven standing disclaimers, removed

Removed from: `/credits`, the student sign-in screen, student Compare, student Services, the student eligibility
result, the student Visa screen, the mobile quick check, the sponsor footer and the marketing footer of every
page. The limitation they expressed is stated **once**, in the terms, article 6:

> 대학의 합격, 장학금 및 출입국 관련 최종 결정은 각 대학 또는 관계 기관의 기준과 심사에 따릅니다.

What replaced them on the visa screen is nothing, because the official action context was already there and is
better: the submission post by name, the method, the fee marked as the embassy's and not Hangyul's, the
embassy's own wording, a source link and a verification date.

## 90.10 The four defects the audit found in the running consoles

| Defect | Fix |
|---|---|
| "Authorised-submission fixture (development only)" in the agency queue and timeline, via stored task titles | the fixture is an ordinary programme name now (`International Business (English track)` / `국제경영학과 (영어트랙)`), still `is_active=False`. `server/scripts/v12_clean_dev_labels.py` repairs a pre-V12 database; the seed produces clean data. |
| `student01@demo.hangyul.kr` on every caseload row | the email is not what a counsellor reads a queue by — removed from the row, kept on the student's own page |
| Five unconnected channels + "Not connected — needs provider credentials", three times over | the picker lists only channels that can send, and renders nothing when there is one; the page note and the settings hint are gone |
| "Not scanned (development)" on every document | `SKIPPED` renders no row. Relabelling it would have claimed a scan that did not happen. |
| 320px of empty card under "Waiting on applicants" | `align-items: start` on the row — a Bootstrap column stretches by default |
| "Hangyul partner" badge driven by `is_demo=True` contracts | `real_partner()` requires an ACTIVE, non-demo `PartnerContract`. None exists, so the badge is gone. |

## 90.11 Two defects of my own, found by the gates I built

Recorded because they are the useful part:

1. **`/credits` was leaking.** The first run of the leak scan failed on a source row named *"Hangyul Univ
   development sample data"*. The public `/sources` endpoint served the provenance record for the seeded sample
   data. It now excludes `source_type == DEMO` unless a caller passes `include_internal=true`, which only the HQ
   registry does. The brief's rule decided the shape of the fix: a public surface does not get the row at all,
   rather than getting it with the label filed off.
2. **The privacy data map named three tables that do not exist.** `document_shares`, `consultations` and
   `order_items` were written from memory. The generator checks every table name against the live SQLAlchemy
   metadata and printed `**missing**` next to all three; they are `application_documents` +
   `document_reviews`, `appointments`, and `service_cases`. A data map nobody checks against the schema is a
   legal template with table names in it.

## 90.12 One test, fixed properly

Renaming the fixture programme broke
`test_v9_student::test_quick_check_nepal_no_test_shows_language_route` on a count of 20 where it expected 21 —
but only in the full suite, never in isolation.

The cause was not the rename. `tests/conftest.py` seeds the database **once per session** and shares it, and
`test_v3_university::test_rule_changes_are_proposed_then_published` raises a programme's TOPIK minimum from 3 to
4 and leaves it raised. It had been passing because it took `programs[0]`, and the university programme endpoint
orders by `(degree_level, name_en)` and includes inactive rows — so `[0]` was the **inactive fixture**, whose
requirement nothing counts. Renaming it to "International Business…" moved an *active* programme into that slot.

The fix is the test, not the assertion: it now selects its programme by name rather than by position, and
restores the original value when it is done. A test that mutates shared session state and leaves it mutated is a
trap for whoever writes the next one, and this one had already sprung.

## 91.2 The defects the gates caught, and what they prove

Three of the gates built in this pass failed on their first run, and all three failures were real:

* the leak scan on `/credits` (§90.11.1) and then again, after it learned to sign in, on **four authenticated
  console routes** that the signed-out version could not see;
* the privacy data map on three invented table names (§90.11.2);
* the visual sweep on a **1,677px horizontal overflow** at 320–768px, where the region-chip scroller sat in a
  grid column whose default `min-width: auto` refused to shrink below its content. `min-width: 0` on the two
  columns fixes it, and it is the classic CSS-grid trap: the scroller was containing its own content correctly
  and the *column* was the thing overflowing.

The leak scan's authenticated sweep is the one worth keeping in mind. The only genuine development-vocabulary
leak this product had reached the screen through **stored task titles** on a signed-in queue. A scan of the
public site would have passed it forever.

## 91.3 Looked at, not only measured

| Route | What was wrong, and fixed |
|---|---|
| `/universities` | the `<h1>` rendered **underneath the fixed header pill** — the page does not use `PageHero`, which is what used to carry the clearance. A shared `--mk-headclear` on the three new page types. |
| `/universities` | the fact row produced a stranded middot on wrap — `· Private` opening a line with `::before`, a dangling `·` closing one with `::after`. Separators removed; the gap does the work and nothing is read out that is not content. |
| `/universities` | the first map was `#EDEAE4` on white and read as a ghost; land, hover and dots were all darkened, and selection is the brand tangerine and the only colour on the map. |
| `/universities` | the directory list was ordered by Korean name in every locale, so an English reader saw Kaya, Gachon, Catholic Kwandong, Kangnam… The API takes `order=ko\|en` and the page asks for the script its reader is reading. |
| `/universities/:slug` | the body sat **210px right of its own heading**: `max-width` was on the element that was *also* `.kn-container`, so the container's auto margins centred the 780px box. The cap moved to the content. |
| `/universities/:slug` | then it sat **32px left** of the heading: `padding: … 0 …` on a `.kn-container` wiped the container's inline gutter. `padding-block`. Verified aligned at 1440 / 1024 / 390. |
| `/universities/:slug` | every source link wrapped its external-link icon onto its own line. |
| `/privacy`, `/terms` | the header was centred independently of the content grid, putting the title and the body on **two different left edges ~140px apart** at 1440px. The header moved inside the content column. |
| `/privacy` (ko) | the first table column broke mid-word — 회원 및 / 계 / 정. `word-break: keep-all` on the Korean, which this codebase already does for headings, plus a floor on the row-heading column. |
| university Overview | 320px of empty card (§89.2). |
| footer | three customer groups, no partner line, no standing disclaimers. |

## 91.4 Responsive and locale

`/privacy` at 390 linearises correctly: single column, the section list becomes a disclosure (이 페이지의 내용),
and every table row becomes a labelled block — 구분 / 처리하는 정보 / 이용 목적 above each value, no clipping and
no horizontal scroll. The directory at 390 drops the map from the accessibility tree and gives the chip scroller
the full bleed. Korean renders the owner's canonical copy throughout.

## 91.5 What is measured and what is not

Everything in §91.1 was re-run after the last change in this pass. Two things were **not** done and should not
be read as passing:

* **The Android smoke test.** The native apps were changed (the DEV chip and the API line removed from the login
  screen, the floating indicator deleted, two disclaimers removed from the student app's visa and explore
  screens) and were verified only by `tsc`. No build ran on a device or an emulator.
* **A dead-CSS sweep.** V11 shipped tooling for it (`scripts/qa/v11-dead-css.mjs`). V12 deleted the `.hg-devchip`
  rules by hand because the component was gone, and did not re-run the sweep over everything else it removed.

# 92. V12 Remaining Launch Dependencies

*§§64, 72 and 82 are **not** superseded. Everything in them is still open unless named here.*

## 92.1 Launch blockers this pass created the gate for, and could not close

**The company does not exist in this repository.** Ten fields are required before `/privacy` and `/terms` can be
called production-ready, and none of them has a value:

| Field | Needed for |
|---|---|
| `legalNameKo` — the registered Korean name **including its corporate form** | both documents; the brief's own baseline said 주식회사 한귤 and nothing records it |
| `representative` (대표자) | 통신판매업 disclosure |
| `businessRegistrationNumber` (사업자등록번호) | both |
| `addressKo` | both |
| `privacyOfficerName`, `privacyOfficerEmail` | PIPA Art. 30 — the privacy policy's §10 does not render without them |
| `policyAnnouncedOn`, `policyEffectiveOn` (공고일 / 시행일) | both |
| `governingLaw`, `jurisdiction` | terms art. 15, which does not render without them |

`node scripts/qa/v12-legal-gate.mjs` prints the list and fails on any rendered placeholder. The pages are honest
without the values; they are not complete without them.

**No retention schedule is approved.** `LEGAL_DEPENDENCIES.md` L8, open since V9. The policy publishes the rule
(purpose achieved → destroyed without delay) and the four Korean statutory commerce periods. It publishes no
period for applicant documents, accounts or audit logs, and no retention job exists to enforce one. A business
decision, not an engineering one.

**No refund matrix is approved.** L5/L10. Terms art. 9 publishes only what the product implements: the
cancellation route, the visa-refusal case, and that tuition is paid by the student directly to the university
and refunded by the university to the student's own account. Hangyul's own fee refund ladder is absent rather
than invented.

**No prices are approved.** L5. Terms art. 8 says how price is shown and where it is confirmed, and quotes no
figure. `service_prices` still holds demo values.

## 92.2 One claim in the privacy policy that production does not yet support

§8 states that uploads are checked for type and size and **scanned for malware** before they can be reviewed.
The pipeline does that; production does not, because the configured scanner is a no-op that records `SKIPPED`
(`docs/SECURITY.md`, "Before production"). The sentence is true of the product's design and not yet of its
deployment. It belongs with the storage, encryption and scanning dependencies in §64 and should be made true
before launch rather than softened.

## 92.3 Carried forward, unchanged by V12

* **University trademark permission** for the 23 crests on the homepage (§82.1). Unchanged.
* **The guarantee sentence** — `why_koreanasha_section3_description` ends "성공적인 유학생활을 보장합니다" and the
  Russian says "гарантируем поступление". Shipped verbatim as instructed; still the owner's call with counsel
  (§82.1).
* **Homepage copy in 52 locales.** Korean and Russian are canonical and gated; English is an AI translation.
  The other 52 render English. V12 added 212 ko + 212 en keys for the directory and the legal documents, and
  **did not** translate them further — so the directory and both policies are now in the same state: two
  locales, 52 falling back. Translators, not code.
* **No locale is `HUMAN_REVIEWED`** and none may be labelled so without a named reviewer and a date.
* Agency submission, real payments, published partnerships, MFA, CSP, rate limiting, S3 + encryption,
  penetration test — all unchanged from §64.

## 92.4 Added by V12 — directory maintenance

* **The disclosure year is a constant.** `SURVEY_YEAR = "2025"` in the importer. When the next year publishes,
  that string moves, the importer runs, and anything the registry has stopped listing becomes `WITHDRAWN`
  automatically. Nobody has to notice a closure for it to be handled — but somebody does have to run it.
* **IEQAS is dated 2026-03-03** on Study in Korea and is re-read on every import. The certification is shown
  with that date, not with today's.
* **123 institutions have no English name and 144 no website**, because no consulted source publishes one. They
  appear in the directory under their Korean name and a slug derived from their registry id. This is a coverage
  gap, not an error, and it is visible rather than papered over.
* **Dormitory, English-taught and scholarship availability are absent** for every institution. No source
  consulted publishes them per institution in verifiable form. They are named in the brief as *possible*
  enrichment and are the obvious next addition if a source is found.

reason is given rather than the number being made to move.*
