Two of these deserve a sentence rather than a row.

**The homepage and the student app did not get simpler, and should not have.** V11 did that work properly, and
the brief is explicit that reducing a count that is already right is a cost, not a gain. What V12 changed on the
homepage is one number inside one sentence — the university count now describes Korea instead of describing our
own data coverage.

**`/privacy` got three times longer.** It went from 1,100 words of structure and placeholders to a document with
ten substantive sections. That is the right direction for this one page: the complaint about the old one was
never that it was long.

# 94. V12 Final Hostile Review

*Brief Part 33. Written as five people who each want to find something wrong, after the gates were green.*

## 94.1 Prospective student — "does this make Korea feel attractive?"

Opening the homepage cold: a full-viewport Korean campus in autumn, four words of Korean over it, two buttons.
Then twenty-three real university crests moving in three rows under *218곳의 한국 대학교가 여러분의 입학을
기다리고 있습니다*. Then why, what, and ten questions — in the owner's own sentences.

**Do I see a university before I see bureaucracy?** Yes. The first thing after the hero is a wall of university
marks, and the first click goes to a map of Korea.

**Does it make me curious instead of showing me ₩20M?** The number is gone. There is no monetary figure on any
public page, and `formatMoney` no longer exists in the marketing app at all.

**Does it feel like a real company?** Two things still say no, and both are in §92 rather than in the code: the
footer has no company identity block, and the privacy policy has no named privacy officer. A Korean consumer
looks for 사업자등록번호 in a footer. Until the owner supplies it, the most finished-looking thing about this
product is also the one a careful Korean reader will notice is missing.

**What I would still attack.** The directory is *plain*. 425 institutions and not one photograph. That was a
deliberate trade — one licensed image per institution does not exist, and V11's alternative was the same Kyung
Hee photograph six times — but "elegant restraint" and "we had no pictures" look identical from the outside, and
a competitor with campus photography will feel richer. The honest fix is licensed photography for the fifty or
so institutions most applicants actually consider, not a stock-photo wall.

## 94.2 Active student — "do I know what to do next?"

Yes, and it is the one screen in the product I would change least. *Your next step · Due Oct 28, 2026 · 12 days
left* over *"Fix your academic transcript for Pusan National University · Business Administration (BBA)"*, with
*"Your application can't be submitted until this is fixed"* and one button. The journey band above says which of
six stages this is.

**What I would attack.** *"We found 11 details in your documents — please check them"*, at the foot of "What you
can do today". Eleven of what? It is the document-analysis findings count, and the sentence makes it sound like
a problem without saying what kind. It survived this pass's copy audit because it is not a disclaimer and not
development vocabulary — it is just vague, which is a different fault and one V12 did not systematically hunt.

## 94.3 Agency counsellor — "do I know who needs me?"

Yes. *Who needs you today · 10*, ranked, with the reason for the ranking on each row and one action per row, and
"How is this ordered?" next to the heading for anyone who doubts it. *Waiting on* splits by party, so "the
student has not replied for 47 days" and "a document is waiting on us" are not in the same bucket.

**What I would attack.** Eight filter chips. V11 judged and kept them, and I agree with the judgement — they are
counts of real work by kind and they let someone batch similar cases. But a counsellor with 200 students will
have eight chips whose counts are all double digits, and at that point they stop being a filter and become a
second KPI row by another name. Worth re-measuring at scale rather than at seed size.

## 94.4 University officer — "do I know who I need to review?"

Yes. *Needs your decision — 5 decisions waiting on your team*, then the intake funnel with the largest drop
marked and rates withheld below five records, then two summaries.

**What I would attack.** The four decision tiles are the one place in the product where I cannot cleanly defend
the design against the brief's own "no KPI gallery". They are queues with counts and they link to filtered
lists, which is what saves them — but with five applications in total, four tiles reading 2 / 1 / 1 / 1 look
like a dashboard pretending to have data. At real volume they will read correctly. That is an argument from
future data, which is exactly the argument this report has spent three passes distrusting, so it is recorded as
a judgement rather than as a finding.

## 94.5 Designer — "does anything still look AI-generated?"

The tells this pass removed were real ones: a page per domain object was already gone in V11; what was left was
a *card for every fact whether or not the fact existed*. The legal pages are the clearest case — nine sections
each with one sentence and one italic apology is what a language model produces when asked for a privacy policy
and given nothing to write it from.

The fix was not better prose. It was reading the schema and finding that there were, in fact, six categories, 24
document kinds, three disclosure triggers, zero processors and zero tracking cookies — and then writing those
down. A section that renders only when it has something verified to say cannot be padded.

**What I found and then fixed while writing this.** The directory list and the legal pages are both ruled rows
with no colour, and they sit in the same product as a tangerine marketing site. Somebody will call that two
design languages. It is two, deliberately — a document and an index are not a landing page — but the seam
between them was at `/credits`, which still used the V11 `PageHero` and looked like neither: the same night-
traffic photograph above the title, every line of the body flush at x = 0 from the same missing container, and
every source link wrapping its icon onto its own line. It is a licence obligation, so it is a document: it uses
`LegalLayout` now, with the registry, IEQAS, Wikidata and KOSTAT sources listed as a section of its own. Three
documents, one layout, and the seam is gone.

**What I would still attack.** Nothing in the design system. The remaining design risk is volume: every screen
in this product has been judged at seed size, and three of the judgements in this section (the agency's eight
chips, the university's four decision tiles, the directory's 18-chip region row) are judgements about how
something will read when it holds ten times more.

## 94.6 Executive — "does anything still look like a development build?"

Not on a rendered route: **72 routes across four apps and HQ, signed in, in Korean and English, zero leaks.** No
DEV chip anywhere, no demo banner, no sample-data label, no fixture name, no demo password, no provider-debug
status, and the persona picker exists only at `/__dev` in a development build.

**What I would attack, and it is the most useful finding in this section.** Every gate V11 shipped was green
while a programme called *"Authorised-submission fixture (development only)"* sat in the agency's daily queue,
because it arrived through **stored task titles** rather than through a component or a translation file. The
leak scan only found it because it signs in. There will be another one of those — a seeded string written into
a row by a service, surfacing somewhere nobody screenshots — and the scan's route list is the only thing
standing between it and a customer. That list is 72 routes out of considerably more than 72.

## 94.7 The three things I was wrong about during this pass

Recorded because the pattern matters more than the fixes.

1. **I hid the map on phones.** The brief says "Do not force a tiny unusable map. Show: compact map + horizontal
   region selector." I read the first clause and dropped the map below 992px — removing the one element that
   makes the page feel like Korea, on the devices most of this product's audience will use. It is a 260px map
   above the chips now.
2. **I shipped the directory with no way to find a named university.** Part 6 says remove the *programme*
   search, and I removed search. With 425 institutions, somebody who knows they want 성균관대학교 had to know it
   was in Seoul and page through 85 entries. A name lookup is now the one control on the page.
3. **I wrote three table names into the privacy data map from memory**, and all three were wrong. The generator
   checks them against the live schema and said so. The lesson is not about table names: a legal document
   derived from the code is only as good as the check that it was.

# 95. V13 Visual Hierarchy Audit

*Brief Parts 1, 5, 21–23. Written before implementation, against the running product, and revised once —
where it was revised, the revision is kept visible rather than tidied away.*

## 95.1 The hero, measured rather than described

The brief's example is the homepage hero, and the first useful thing was to stop reading the stylesheet and
measure the page. The authored CSS and the rendered page did not agree:

| | authored | **rendered @1440** |
|---|---|---|
| headline → description | `var(--hg-space-5)` = 20px | **15px** |
| description → buttons | `var(--hg-space-8)` = 32px | **0px** |
| primary (tangerine) action | — | **대학 둘러보기** |
| the other action | — | **로그인** (white pill) |
| header's tangerine action | — | **로그인** |

The buttons were not *nearly* touching the description. They were touching it. And the user's complaint about
hierarchy was, if anything, understated: the hero advertised the directory in the brand colour while the
header advertised the account in the same brand colour, so whichever a visitor read first was contradicted by
the other.

## 95.2 Why the spacing was wrong, which was not a spacing problem

`rtlcss` runs over the Eduan template in this project's Vite config and rewrites its directional element rules
into `[dir] p { margin-bottom: 0 }` and `[dir] :where(.ed) :is(h1,…,h6) { margin-bottom: 15px }`. An attribute
selector plus a type selector is specificity **(0,1,1)**; a single class such as `.kn-hero__lede` is
**(0,1,0)**. Every margin this design system set on a heading or a paragraph was therefore discarded.

Swept across the public site, **8 of 13 composition rules were dead**:

| class | intended | rendered |
|---|---|---|
| `.kn-hero__title` | 20px below | 15px |
| `.kn-hero__lede` | 32px below | **0** |
| `.kn-head__eyebrow` | 12px below | 0 |
| `.kn-head__title` | 0 | **15px** |
| `.kn-head__lede` | 16px above | 0 |
| `.kn-card__title` | 12px below | 15px |
| `.kn-mediarow__title` | 16px below | 15px |
| `.kn-cta__title` | 12px below | 15px |

Every heading on the public site was exactly 15px from whatever followed it, and every paragraph meant to
have space below it had none — which is precisely the "placed by default flex-gap values" the brief
describes. It was not a judgement failure. It was a silent one, and **no gate this repository had could see
it**: nothing overflowed, no console error fired, axe was clean, and the V12 visual sweep reported 0 issues
across 240 views. A bad design does fit perfectly inside the viewport.

## 95.3 Hierarchy errors found on the other screens

Audited with the brief's own list. Only what was actually found is listed; the absence of the rest is not a
claim that they cannot exist.

| Screen | Error | Class of error |
|---|---|---|
| homepage hero | directory = primary, account = secondary | wrong primary button |
| homepage hero | `width: 100%` applied to *every* button below 420px | two equal full-width buttons |
| closing CTA band | explore was a solid white pill on a near-black band, optically heavier than the tangerine primary beside it | secondary styled as primary |
| university Overview | *Applicants* rendered as a filled primary in the page header, duplicating the left rail two rows above | navigation competing with the page action |
| university Overview | *Analytics* reachable three ways on one screen (rail, header button, section link) | duplicate navigation |
| agency Today | *Operations* — same destination **and the same label** as the rail item — was the only button on the screen | navigation competing with the page action |
| university Overview | four equal decision tiles reading 2 / 1 / 1 / 1 | multiple equal cards |
| agency Today | eight work-type chips, predicted by V12 to become a second KPI row at scale | too many visible filters |
| student Home | *"We found 11 details in your documents"* | a count with no noun |

## 95.4 For each screen: question, primary, secondary, remove

| Screen | User question | Primary | Secondary | Removed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Homepage | *Should I study in Korea, and can this help?* | 내 유학 준비 | 대학 둘러보기 | — (V11 already cut it to six sections) |
| `/universities` | *Which universities are there, and where?* | the map itself | region chips, name lookup | — |
| Student Home | *What do I do next?* | the one next step | active applications | the bare-count nudge |
| Agency Today | *Who needs me now?* | the row's own action | state chips | the *Operations* header button; four chips |
| Agency review | *Can this be submitted?* | approve / request changes | the evidence | — |
| University Overview | *What needs a decision?* | Open all awaiting decision | the ranked queue rows | both header buttons; four stat cards |
| University Applicants | *Which applicant, and what about them?* | open the applicant | filters | — |

## 95.5 What V13 did not audit

The student application page, the agency student workspace's four tabs, the essay editor, HQ, and all three
native apps were **not** put through this audit. They were looked at; they were not measured. Recorded here
so that "V13 audited the product" is not read as more than it is.

# 96. V13 Global Competitive Benchmark

Full document: **`docs/qa/v13/GLOBAL_BENCHMARK.md`** (IDP FastLane, ApplyBoard, Enroly Apply, Enroly CAS
Shield, Cialfo / Direct Apply, Leverage Edu, Studyportals, plus Adventus.io and the Korean regulator's own
2026 material). Researched 2026-10-17 from current public product and help-centre pages; `COMPETITOR_BENCHMARK.md`
is a V9 document and is superseded for these seven products.

**None of these platforms was used as a logged-in customer**, because every operator surface among them is
behind a contract. That makes the benchmark strong evidence about what task each product thinks it is doing
and weak evidence about how well it does it, and it is written that way throughout.

The three lessons that changed code:

1. **ApplyBoard** — requirement-centric upload with per-requirement state is right, and Hangyul already does
   it. What its published model does *not* appear to do is check one document against another. That is the
   more common cause of a Korean university returning a file, and §97 is the response.
2. **Enroly CAS Shield** — the most attractive bad idea in the benchmark. It publishes an **"enrolment
   confidence score"**: a single number predicting whether a person will enrol, from features that correlate
   with nationality and region. It looks like intelligence and it is a correlation with a passport. Named
   explicitly as a thing not to copy.
3. **IDP FastLane** — early eligibility clarity from a thin profile is the right instinct, and Hangyul's
   `/start` already returns tiers with reasons. The failure was never the engine; it was that the homepage
   advertised *로그인* instead of that answer.

Deliberately not copied: in-principle offers (we have no authority to imply an admission decision),
multi-institution single-form lodgement (Korean practice requires the applicant to submit personally), a
parallel email inbox, and paywalled late-journey support.

# 97. V13 Admission-Success Strategy

*Brief Parts 6, 7, 11.*

## 97.1 What already existed, and the discipline of checking

The brief asks for an application quality system that reports blockers and risks rather than a score. That
system exists and has since V5: `strategy.application_strategy` returns named items with a severity, an
owner, a reason and an action, and `docs/ADMISSION_SUCCESS.md` opens with *"No score, no percentage, no
probability."* Most of the brief's Part 7 checklist was already implemented across three services —
eligibility, missing documents, validity, legalization, language, essays, deadlines, university requests,
interviews in `strategy.py`; document findings and extracted fields in `dossier.py`; word limits, prompt
coverage, factual consistency and other-university names in `writing.py`.

So V13's job here was not to build a quality system. It was to find out whether the one that exists is
actually connected — which the brief's own instruction demanded: *"Do not trust historical 'Done' statuses.
The running product is the truth."*

## 97.2 The finding: a hook that nothing had ever registered

`strategy.register_essay_hook` was built in V5 so the writing workstream could push its findings onto an
application's quality check. `ADMISSION_SUCCESS.md` has described it as the writing hook ever since.

**`_ESSAY_HOOKS` was empty.** Across eight passes, `grep -rn register_essay_hook server/app` returned exactly
one line: the definition.

The consequence is specific and expensive. A student looking at their application could be told *"Revise your
study plan"* and could not be told that **the study plan names a different university** — even though that
finding was already computed and stored by the `NAMES` gate. An essay addressed to the wrong university is
one of the cheapest rejections there is to prevent, and it was invisible on the one screen where the student
was deciding whether they were ready to submit.

The existing test (`test_essay_hook_adds_items`) had been green the whole time, because it clears the hook
list and registers its own. It proved the mechanism worked and never asked whether anything used it.

## 97.3 What V13 changed

`writing.application_quality_items` is registered as a real hook. Four quality-gate blockers now arrive as
named items on the application, each one linking to the draft:

| Gate | Item | Why it is a blocker |
|---|---|---|
| `NAMES` | `ESSAY_WRONG_NAME` | the essay names the wrong university |
| `WORD_LIMIT` | `ESSAY_OVER_LIMIT` | over the university's published limit |
| `PROMPT_ANSWERED` | `ESSAY_PROMPT_GAP` | part of the prompt is unanswered |
| `PROFILE_CONSISTENCY` | `ESSAY_CONTRADICTS_PROFILE` | the essay says something the documents do not |

`WAITING` gates ("not assessed yet") are deliberately silent: an application page that lists everything not
yet checked is a reviewer's to-do list, not an applicant's quality check.

And the registration is now **gated**, because an implicit, import-order-dependent registration is how it
stayed empty for eight passes. `test_v13_quality.py::test_a_real_essay_hook_is_registered_in_the_running_app`
imports `app.main` and asserts a real hook by name.

## 97.4 Risks, not scores — verified rather than asserted

`test_quality_check_never_reports_a_score` asserts that a strategy response contains no "probability",
"chance of admission", "acceptance_score" or "admission_score", and that its state is one of `BLOCKED` /
`IMPROVABLE` / `READY`. The existing V5 test already walked the portfolio response for `score` and `percent`
keys; this adds the application side.

## 97.5 Vague counts (brief Part 9)

V12's own hostile review named *"We found 11 details in your documents — please check them"* as the clearest
surviving example of a count with no noun, and could not fix it because it is not a disclaimer and not
development vocabulary — it is just vague.

Eleven **of what** turned out to be: eleven facts read out of the student's own documents, waiting for them
to confirm. A number with no noun made a routine confirmation look like a fault report. The nudge now carries
the field names, and the client turns the codes into words with labels it already had:

> **Confirm your name, date of birth and 9 more details read from your documents**

The list joiner is `Intl.ListFormat` with `type: 'unit'` when a *"and N more"* tail follows, because
"name and date of birth and 9 more" reads as a stutter.

## 97.6 What was *not* done

**Document-to-document identity consistency** — the brief's "name consistency / date-of-birth consistency /
school / GPA consistency" — is still **not** on the application's quality check. `ExtractedField` holds the
values per document and `DocumentFinding` holds staff-facing mismatches, so the data exists; nothing
aggregates them across documents into an application-level blocker. This is the largest remaining gap in Part
7 and it is named rather than glossed. Translation requirements, recommendation requirements and application
fee state are likewise unimplemented as quality items.

# 98. V13 Country-by-Country Student Simulations

Full documents: **`docs/qa/v13/country-simulations/`** — fourteen markets (Vietnam, Nepal, Myanmar,
Uzbekistan, Mongolia, China, India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Indonesia, Thailand, Philippines, Kazakhstan,
Kyrgyzstan), one file each, plus a README ranking the findings by how many markets they affect.

**These are synthetic simulations and every file says so in its own first lines.** No person from any of
these markets was interviewed, observed or surveyed. The personas are authored. What is *not* authored is the
factual half, and it is marked `measured`: the legalization route comes from the live `countries` table, the
visa route from `docs/research/visa-playbooks.json` (which covers exactly these fourteen countries), and the
language behaviour from a real sweep of the running product (`scripts/qa/v13-country-probe.mjs`).

## 98.1 The recurring findings

| # | Finding | Markets | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The public homepage renders in English | **11 of 14** (was 14) | Translation dependency |
| 2 | `uz`/`kk`/`ky` fell back to English although complete **owner-written Russian** exists | 3 | **Fixed** |
| 3 | The accession note was silenced after 365 days, and again by any explicit rule row | 2 reachable | **Fixed** |
| 4 | One planning constant (`LEGALIZE` = 14 days) is used for every country | 14 | Open |
| 5 | The sponsor model assumes a parent or self-funding, not a sibling remitting from a third country | 4 | Open |
| 6 | No locale is human-reviewed | 14 | Reviewers, not code |

## 98.2 The country-specific defects that only a per-market sweep could find

**Bangladesh — two scripts in one sentence.** The homepage rendered *২০০+ Korean universities are waiting for
your admission.* `Intl` localises digits and has no idea which language the surrounding sentence ended up in,
so a Bengali numeral landed inside the English fallback copy. Correct localisation of the number, incoherent
on the page, and invisible to every gate: the sentence was not missing, not overflowing and not untranslated
— it was merely written in two scripts. `copyLocale()` now formats a figure in the script of its own
sentence, following the same chain i18next resolves the words through. The count regression asserts `bn`
alongside `ko` and `en`.

**Central Asia — the owner's own words were available and unused.** Uzbek, Kazakh and Kyrgyz fell straight
through to English, while the Russian that would have been served is not a machine translation but the
company's own copy (Koreanasha's audience is Russian-speaking; its 301 Russian strings are gated by the
fidelity check exactly like the Korean). `FALLBACK_CHAIN` now resolves `uz|kk|ky|tg → ru → en`, **and
`loadNamespaces` fetches the whole chain** — without that second half the fallback is silent and looks
exactly like "no translation exists". Measured: 3 of 14 markets now read the owner's Russian; the English
fallback fell from 14 markets to 11, at no translation cost.

**Vietnam — a finding that was false, and the check that proved it.** The first draft recorded that the
product tells a Vietnamese student "apostille" without explaining that the rule changed five weeks ago.
Calling `readiness.legalization_for(db, 'VN', …)` returned `note_code=JOINED` with the date. V5 built that
and it works. It is kept in the file as a non-finding on purpose: a simulation that only reports problems is
a simulation that invents them.

**Bangladesh — what the same check did find.** The accession note fired for 365 days. Measured across all
fourteen markets, that window caught Vietnam (37 days) and nobody else, while Bangladesh (567), China (1,076)
and Pakistan (1,319) are all recent enough that informal advice reliably predates the change. 365 days is
roughly how long a consular-legalised *document* stays in circulation; the note is about what an older
sibling remembers, which has a much longer half-life. Now `3 × 365`. A second defect surfaced while checking
it: a country with an explicit `LegalizationRule` row never reached the accession branch at all. China has
one, and its own verified note already explains the 2023 accession in more detail — so the first fix, which
would have *replaced* that richer note with the generic one, was wrong and was corrected.

**Philippines — the only priority market with no student-app locale.** `isStudentAppLocale('tl')` is false,
so Mary Grace uses the app in English. For her that is fine; Philippine higher education is English-medium.
The finding is that the product cannot tell the difference between "we chose English because this market
reads English" and "we have not translated this yet" — and the next person to read the coverage table will
open a translation project this market does not need.

**Pakistan — RTL, measured not assumed.** At 390px with `lang=ur` the homepage renders `dir=rtl` with 0px
horizontal overflow, scrim mirrored. V13's new secondary button style and phone CTA stack were re-measured
there rather than assumed.

# 99. V13 Agency at Scale Simulation

Full document: **`docs/qa/v13/AGENCY_AT_SCALE.md`**. Isolated scale database (`hangyul_univ_scale`, seeded by
`server/scripts/v9_scale_seed.py`, which refuses any database whose name lacks "scale"), API on :8091,
console on :4702. None of it touches the development stack or appears in a development screenshot.

**V12's prediction was correct.** At 200 students for one counsellor the nine work types read
165 / 94 / 88 / 54 / 18 / 1 / 1 / 0 / 0 — seven chips would render and five are double digits. A row of those
numbers above a list is a dashboard, and the one reading 165 tells a counsellor nothing, because "documents"
is the largest category every single morning.

Today's default filter row is now four **operational states** — properties of a case, so they do not multiply
with caseload size: All 220 · Urgent 20 · Our work 198 · Waiting on student 22 (waiting-on-university is 0 and
is therefore not a chip). The nine work types moved into one `Filter` select and still narrow the same list
by the same rule. `urgent` is a severity cut *across* the party states rather than a fifth bucket, so the
counts do not sum and the UI never implies they do.

Measured at 1440px: **four chips, one line, a 47px filter block, 1.1 screens**. Every state's count equals the
rows it shows, verified through the API (`state=our_work → total 198`, and so on) and now asserted in
`e2e/v5-flow-g.spec.ts` for both controls.

**One defect found that seed size could not show.** The heading read **220** while its own button read **"Show
all 100"**, because the queue is fetched with a limit of 100 — two numbers for one list, one of them untrue.
It now reads "Show 100 of 220" and claims "all" only when the limit is not binding.

**One finding left open, with its caveat attached.** All ten top rows read *"First reply is N days late"* with
the same action, so the ranking produces a block a counsellor cannot triage within. The rule is working as
published. The seed creates an unusually uniform population of never-contacted students, so the monotony is
probably a fixture artefact — and both obvious fixes are worse than the problem: capping consecutive
same-reason rows makes the order stop meaning what the "How is this ordered?" popover says, and a bulk-reply
affordance is new product in a pass whose first instruction is not to add any.

# 100. V13 University at Scale Simulation

Full document: **`docs/qa/v13/UNIVERSITY_AT_SCALE.md`**. 1,011 submitted applications to Pusan National
University across programmes, intakes and four agencies.

**V12's doubt about the four decision tiles was right, and wrong about why.** It expected them to read
correctly at volume. At 1,011 applications there are no longer four things:

| Decision | Count |
|---|---|
| Awaiting review | **513** |
| Interviews | 84 |
| Tuition invoices to issue | 51 |
| Flagged | 46 |
| Waitlisted | 43 |
| Documents returned | 1 |

The four *core* tiles were a fixed set — review, documents returned, interviews, waitlisted. At this volume
that set would have given a full-width tile to **Documents returned: 1** while burying **Tuition invoices:
51** and **Flagged: 46** below the fold, because those were conditional tiles that render after the core four.
A composition chosen at five applications would have hidden two queues of fifty.

The ranked queue reads correctly at both ends, which is the test the tiles could not pass: four short rows at
seed size instead of four tiles of whitespace, six rows with 513 first at scale, every queue visible.

Also measured: the funnel publishes rates at volume and marks the largest drop (submitted 398 → reviewed 323,
81% → offered 86, **27%, largest drop**), where at seed size it correctly withheld nearly all of them. This is
the first pass in which anyone has seen `MIN_N` suppression work in both directions.

The Overview is **2.1 screens** at 1440, not the 1–1.5 the brief prefers. Recorded rather than forced: the
extra height is the queue having six real rows instead of four invented ones, and hiding a queue of fifty to
hit a height target is the change this pass exists to argue against.

**Not tested:** multiple intakes under load, per-agency cohorts against `MIN_N`, and analytics cross-filter
correctness. Gaps in the measurement, not findings of correctness.

strong, realistic application?"*

| Removed | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 4 `StatCard` decision tiles | university Overview | replaced by a ranked queue that works at 5 and at 1,011 |
| 2 page-header buttons | university Overview | both duplicated the left rail; one was a filled primary |
| 1 page-header button | agency Today | same destination *and label* as the rail item, and the only button on the screen |

| `DefaultCtaActions` | marketing `blocks.tsx` | zero call sites |
| `DevAccess` + `.hg-devchip` rule | `packages/ui`, `packages/ynex-ui` | zero call sites since V12; the CSS was still compiled into two production stylesheets |

**Moved rather than removed:** the nine work types (chips → one Filter control). Nothing lost; a narrowing
reached for occasionally stopped occupying the row a counsellor reads every morning.

**Deliberately not removed:** nothing on the student's five destinations, nothing on the homepage's six
sections, and no backend capability. V11 did that work properly and the brief is explicit that reducing a
count which is already right is a cost, not a gain.

# 102. V13 Implementation Log

## 102.1 Design system — composition spacing (brief Part 22)

`packages/design-tokens/src/index.ts` gains a `flow` scale, emitted to `tokens.css` as `--hg-flow-*`. These
are composition decisions rather than steps on a ruler, and each is fluid because the right optical gap at
320px is not the right one at 1728px:

```
--hg-flow-heading : clamp(24px, 2.1vw, 30px)   headline → its supporting copy
--hg-flow-copy    : clamp(28px, 3vw,   36px)   copy → the controls that act on it
--hg-flow-actions : clamp(12px, 1vw,   16px)   between sibling actions
--hg-flow-section : clamp(32px, 3.4vw, 48px)   section heading → its content
--hg-flow-group   : clamp(40px, 4.6vw, 64px)   content group → next group
```

`koreanasha.scss` loses fourteen per-component margin declarations and gains one **Composition spacing**
block at the end of the file, scoped `.kn .kn-*` — specificity (0,2,0), which beats the rtlcss-generated
(0,1,1) element rules cleanly and without `!important`. Having every vertical gap inside a content group in
one reviewable place is the point; defeating the template is the mechanism.

`scripts/qa/v13-composition.mjs` (`npm run qa:composition`) asserts **computed** values on real pages at six
widths — 66 assertions — because a stylesheet that merely *contains* the right declaration is exactly what
shipped for eight passes. It also asserts the *relationship*: copy→action must stay larger than
headline→copy, or the three parts collapse into one block however generous each gap is alone.

## 102.2 Button system (brief Part 23)

Four levels, documented in the stylesheet: PRIMARY (filled tangerine), SECONDARY (restrained, never a brand
fill), TERTIARY (text weight), DESTRUCTIVE.

New: `.kn-btn--quiet-onphoto`, the secondary treatment for a photograph or a dark band. The dark translucent
fill is not decoration — it guarantees the label's contrast over whatever part of the image lands behind it,
so the hierarchy does not depend on the photo. `.kn-btn--onphoto` (solid white) is kept, with a comment
recording why it is *not* the secondary: on a dark ground solid white outweighs a tangerine fill, which is
how both the hero and the closing band came to advertise the wrong button.

## 102.3 Hero (brief Part 1)

`v11.tsx` — the actions swap order and style. The conversion action is first and filled; the directory is
second and quiet. The label is the goal, not the mechanism: signed out it reads 내 유학 준비 /
*Start my preparation* (new key `v13.cta.prepare`) and goes to sign-in, which is where a preparation starts.
Nobody's goal is to log in.

`SiteLayout.tsx` — `AccountAction` uses the same label, so the header, the hero and the closing band agree.
There is no separate "Log in" control: that button is already the way in, and a second door beside it is one
more thing competing for the same decision.

Phones: the rule that gave `width: 100%` to *every* button in the hero group is replaced by a primary at full
measure and a secondary at text weight beneath it. Two equal full-width pills is two primaries. The hero's
bottom padding grows to 68px below 576px because the secondary, now a text link, sat on the same optical line
as the photography credit — a licence obligation that cannot move.

Rendered @1440 after: headline→copy **30px**, copy→action **36px**, action gap **14px**, primary
`rgb(204,78,0)`, secondary not.

## 102.4 Marketing numbers (brief Parts 3, 24, 33)

`marketingScale()` in `@hangyul/utils` rounds **down** to one significant figure at or above 100, so the "+"
is always true however the register moves: 218 → 200, 1,480 → 1,000, 94 → 90, and `null` below 10 so a caller
can hold a sentence back rather than print a rounded figure that is really an exact one.

The sentence itself returns to the Koreanasha source's own scale wording. V12 had replaced *"50+개 이상의"*
with a bare *"{{count}}곳의"*, which the manifest's `count` substitution policy ("surrounding sentence
unchanged") did not permit; V13 restores *"{{count}}+개 이상의"* and substitutes only the numeral — strictly
*more* faithful than V12 was. Russian keeps *"Более {{count}}"*, which is the source's own phrasing and
carries the scale without a "+". The fidelity gate passes 86/86 across ko + ru.

`copyLocale()` formats that figure in the script of its own sentence (§98.2).

## 102.5 Agency Today (brief Part 10)

Server: `priority.STATES`, `PARTY_STATE` and `state_of()` fold the existing seven-party waiting model
(`services/waiting.py`) to the three parties a counsellor can act on the difference between, plus `urgent` =
tier 1 as a cut across them. `ranked()` takes `state`, returns `by_state`, and evaluates parties in one
grouped query — the same evaluation the "Waiting on" panel uses, so the two can never disagree about a
student. Their totals differ on purpose and the code says so: this queue holds students with an open reason,
that panel counts the whole caseload.

Client: four state chips plus one `Filter` select holding the nine work types. Both narrow the same list by
the same rule; both counts equal their rows; both are asserted in `e2e/v5-flow-g.spec.ts`.

## 102.6 University Overview (brief Part 13)

`NeedsDecision` is a ranked queue (largest first, ties by severity, zero-count kinds omitted) built from the
`uv7-listrow` idiom the Overview already used for "Waiting on" — so the screen gained a component's worth of
information and no new vocabulary. Tones and icons went with the tiles: colour here now means status.

## 102.7 Application quality (brief Part 7)

`writing.application_quality_items` registered as a `strategy` essay hook (§97.2), with
`test_v13_quality.py` asserting a real registration in the imported app — not merely that the mechanism
works.

## 102.8 Country work (brief Part 17)

`FALLBACK_CHAIN` + `localeChain()` in `packages/i18n`, with `loadNamespaces` fetching the whole chain.
`APOSTILLE_NOTE_DAYS = 3 × 365` and `_accession_note()` factored out of `legalization_for` so an explicit
rule row no longer suppresses it — while keeping a verified rule's own note as the primary one.

## 102.9 Release gate (brief Part 26)

`npm run release:check` → `scripts/qa/v13-release-check.mjs`, reading `hq_ops.launch_items` through
`server/scripts/v13_launch_json.py`, the ten company fields, and a catalogue of requirements that are policy
rather than configuration. Exit 0 when the requested level passes (`--require=preview|beta|production`,
default `preview`); `--json` for CI.

## 102.10 Scripts added

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run release:check` | three launch levels, PASS/FAIL, exact blockers and who can clear each |
| `npm run qa:composition` | 66 computed-spacing assertions at six widths |
| `npm run qa:countries` | what each of the 14 priority markets actually sees |
| `npm run qa:v13` | the two above |
| `scripts/qa/v13-capture.mjs` | before/after capture, 11 screens × 5 widths, viewport + full page |
| `scripts/qa/v13-scale-qa.mjs` | the consoles against the isolated 200-student / 1,011-application database |
| `scripts/qa/v13-country-sims.py` | regenerates the fourteen simulation documents from measured data |

## 102.11 Two fixes that were wrong first

Recorded because the pattern matters more than the fixes, and both were caught by checking rather than by
review.

1. **The accession note.** The first version appended the generic note to a rule's own note. The client
   renders the translated `note_code` *instead of* `note`, so that would have **replaced** China's richer
   verified sentence with a generic one. Corrected to attach a code only where a rule has nothing of its own
   to say.
2. **The Vietnam simulation.** The first draft reported that the product never explains a recent apostille
   change. Calling the function showed it does. The false finding is kept in the file, labelled, because a
   simulation that only reports problems is a simulation that invents them.

## 102.12 One pre-existing defect found in the test suite

`test_v9_adversarial.py` set `TODAY = date.today()` — the *machine's local* date — and asserted against
services that compute "today" in UTC. On this project's reference machine (KST, UTC+9) the two disagree for
nine hours of every twenty-four, between local midnight and 09:00. Two tests had been failing that whole
window and passing the rest of the day; they failed at 00:22 KST on 2026-10-18 having passed all the previous
afternoon. `TODAY = utcnow().date()`. Not a product defect and not a V13 regression — a flake that had
roughly a 37% chance of being invisible to any given run.

# 103. V13 Launch Readiness

*Brief Part 26. Run it yourself: `npm run release:check` (add `--require=beta|production`, or `--json`).*

**Nothing here says "ready to launch because the tests passed."** Every gate in §104.6 is green and all three
levels fail, which is the correct answer: green tests mean the code does what it was written to do. They do
not mean a company exists, a refund policy is approved, uploads are scanned in production, or anyone has
agreed a price.

```
MARKETING PREVIEW        FAIL   (4/6 requirements met)
CLOSED BETA              FAIL   (4/14)
COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION    FAIL   (4/29)
```

## 103.1 MARKETING PREVIEW — FAIL, 2 blockers

| Blocker | Owner | State |
|---|---|---|
| The company exists in the product | **the owner** | 10 of 10 fields unconfigured: `legalNameKo`, `representative`, `businessRegistrationNumber`, `addressKo`, `privacyOfficerName`, `privacyOfficerEmail`, `policyAnnouncedOn`, `policyEffectiveOn`, `governingLaw`, `jurisdiction` |
| Nothing published publicly is sample data | engineering + the owner | 0 of 66 active programmes verified against an official source |

These are the two things standing between this product and a public marketing site. The first is ten strings
in `apps/marketing-web/src/lib/legal/entity.ts`; the pages render honestly without them (sections with
missing required fields are omitted rather than placeheld) but a Korean consumer looks for 사업자등록번호 in a
footer, and it is not there.

The second is the one blocker on this list that nobody has named before, and `release:check` found it by
asking a question no previous gate asked: the **directory** (425 institutions) is real, imported and
reproducible, but the **application catalogue** (66 active programmes) is seeded and not one programme
carries a verification against an official source. The public site does not publish programme data — V12
removed all of it — so nothing untrue is on screen today. It becomes a marketing-preview blocker the moment
anything from the catalogue reaches a public page.

Four gates must also be green at release and are not re-run by this command: `qa:legal`, `qa:leak`,
`qa:data-map`, `e2e/v13-hierarchy.spec.ts`. All four are green as of this pass (§104.6).

## 103.2 CLOSED BETA — FAIL, 10 blockers

Everything above, plus eight. Real people put real documents in at this level and nobody has paid yet.

| Blocker | Owner |
|---|---|
| Documents on production object storage with encryption at rest | engineering |
| Uploads scanned for malware before anyone can open them | engineering |
| Production secrets from a secret manager, not defaults | engineering |
| Demo sign-in refused by the deployed environment | engineering |
| Cross-border transfer consent approved under PIPA | **the owner + counsel** |
| An approved retention period for documents, accounts and audit logs | **the owner + counsel** |
| A named incident contact and a breach-notification process | **the owner** |
| A job runner in production for scans, reminders and exports | engineering |

The malware one deserves its own sentence, because the product currently says something about itself that its
deployment does not support: privacy policy §8 states that uploads are scanned before they can be reviewed.
The pipeline does that; the configured scanner in this build is a no-op that records `SKIPPED`. The sentence
is true of the design and not yet of the deployment, and it should be made true rather than softened.

## 103.3 COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION — FAIL, 25 blockers

Everything above, plus fifteen: approved prices, an approved refund matrix, a live payment provider, counsel
review of both legal documents, the MOE standard agreement once its text is published, signed provider
agreements, human-reviewed priority locales, rate limiting, CSP, MFA, an independent penetration test,
production monitoring, tested backups, a real support process with a published response time, and usability
sessions with real participants.

By owner: **engineering 11, the owner (business) 6, legal 4, providers 2, named human reviewers 2.** Fifteen
of twenty-five cannot be cleared by code at all.

## 103.4 What V13 added to this list, and what it closed

**Added one blocker** — `verified_catalogue` was always in `launch_items`; no gate had ever mapped it to a
launch level, so nobody had to look at it.

**Closed none.** V13 changed no launch dependency, and says so rather than finding a way to present a smaller
number.

## 103.5 One decision this pass made that the owner should confirm

**Russian as the second language for Central Asia.** `FALLBACK_CHAIN` now serves the owner's own Russian copy
to `uz`, `kk`, `ky` and `tg` before falling through to English (§98.2). The argument for it: the alternative
is an AI translation into English, the Russian is the company's own writing, and Koreanasha's audience is
Russian-speaking — so this is aligned with the owner's existing commercial posture rather than a new bet.

The argument against it, stated because it is real: Russian literacy among 18-year-olds in these markets is
declining, and a Kazakh speaker who reads English better than Russian is now served worse. This is a product
decision about an audience, not an engineering one. It is one line in `packages/i18n/src/index.ts` to
reverse, and `npm run qa:countries` measures the effect either way.

## 103.6 Carried forward unchanged

§§64, 72, 82 and 92 are **not** superseded. Everything in them is still open unless it appears above. In
particular: the university trademark permission for the 23 crests, the guarantee sentence in
`why_koreanasha_section3_description` ("성공적인 유학생활을 보장합니다" / "гарантируем поступление"), homepage
copy in 52 locales, agency submission, real payments, published partnerships, S3 + encryption, and the
penetration test.

Two V12 items are now partly addressed and should not be read as closed: homepage copy still falls back for
**11** of the 14 priority markets rather than 14, and no locale is `HUMAN_REVIEWED`.

# 104. V13 Final Hostile Audit

*Brief Part 35. Written after the gates were green, pretending the redesign was made by a junior team, and
attacking it. The two findings that changed code are first, because they are the ones that matter.*

## 104.1 "Your spacing fix is a workaround, not a fix"

Correct, and it is worth saying plainly. `.kn .kn-hero__lede` beats `[dir] :where(.ed) p` because (0,2,0)
beats (0,1,1) — it does not remove the conflict, it wins it. A future template rule written as
`[dir] .kn p` would be (0,2,1) and would beat this block in exactly the same silent way.

The real fix is upstream: stop `rtlcss` rewriting bare element selectors, or scope the Eduan element rules
under the template's own class. That is a build-pipeline change this pass did not attempt.

What makes the workaround defensible is the gate rather than the specificity. `npm run qa:composition` reads
**computed** values off real pages, so the next rule that outranks this block fails a check instead of
flattening a page. Verified by reintroducing the exact defect: the gate exits 1 and names
`.kn-hero__lede marginBottom = 0px, expected 28–36px`, and `e2e/v13-hierarchy.spec.ts` fails its grouping
test. Restored, both pass. **A gate nobody has watched fail is not a gate**, so both were watched.

I also checked whether the same class of defect exists in the three consoles — it does not, and the reason is
structural rather than lucky: `packages/config/vite.ts` runs `rtlcss` over the Eduan stylesheet only. Swept
across seven authenticated routes, zero single-class heading or paragraph rules compute to a margin they did
not declare.

## 104.2 "Your new primary button still opens a password field"

**The worst finding in this audit, and it is against V13's own work.**

The pass began by criticising a hero whose actions were *대학 둘러보기* and *로그인*, and whose second button
was named after the mechanism a visitor must pass through rather than the thing they came to do. V13 relabelled
it *내 유학 준비* / *Start my preparation* and left it pointing at `studentAction('/')` — which, for a
stranger, resolves to `/login?next=/`.

So the button said "start my preparation" and opened a password field. The original defect, moved one layer
down, where a label change could not reveal it and where the new regression test — which checked the label,
the style, the order and the spacing — did not look.

It is worse than an oversight, because this pass's own benchmark had already written down the answer.
`GLOBAL_BENCHMARK.md` §1 identifies IDP FastLane's best idea as *early eligibility clarity from a thin
profile, with no documents and no account*, and asks the brief's question: "how quickly can a new student get
a useful answer before completing a huge profile?" The answer was sitting at `/start` — a **public**
three-question check that compares the visitor against every registered programme's published requirements
and returns tiers with named reasons. Verified cold: `/start` returns 200 signed out, renders *"질문 세
가지면 충분합니다. 계정 없이 바로 확인하세요."* and contains **no password field**.

`prepareAction()` now sends a stranger there and a signed-in student to the platform, from the hero, the
header and the closing band alike. The regression test asserts the **destination**, not only the label:
`/start`, and explicitly not `/login`.

This also settles a smaller worry from §95.4. V13 removed the header's separate "Log in" control on the
grounds that one primary action is better than two doors — which was a real cost for a returning user.
`/start` carries its own sign-in link, so the returning student's path is one click from the primary CTA
instead of being absent.

## 104.3 "Two of your products disagree about what time it is"

At 00:22 the student app said *"Good evening, Lan"* while the agency console said *"Good morning, Hoa"* —
the same minute, two products, two answers. Both read local time; the thresholds simply differed, because
each had written its own. The boundary is a judgement rather than a fact, which is exactly why it belongs in
one place: `dayPart()` in `@hangyul/utils`, used by both, treating 00:00–04:59 as the end of the reader's
evening.

Small, and it is the kind of seam that tells a user they are looking at two products rather than one.

## 104.4 "Your consoles still ship a development class name"

They did. `.hg-devchip { z-index: 120 }` was compiled into the agency and university production stylesheets,
for a component (`DevAccess`) whose last call site V12 deleted. No markup, so the leak scan — which reads the
DOM — correctly found nothing, and V12's §91.5 had already admitted it removed the chip by hand and did not
re-run the dead-CSS sweep. Both the component and the rule are gone; `DemoAccessDrawer` and
`useDemoParamLogin` stay, because `/__dev` uses them in development builds. Rebuilt and confirmed: **0**
occurrences in any bundle.

## 104.5 What I attacked and could not fault

* **The ranked decision queue.** Doubted as a cosmetic change until it was measured at 1,011 applications,
  where the four fixed tiles would have given a full-width tile to *Documents returned: 1* and buried
  *Tuition invoices: 51* and *Flagged: 46*. It is better at both ends, not just at volume.
* **The four state chips.** Doubted as a reduction for its own sake. Measured: at 200 students the nine work
  types read 165 / 94 / 88 / 54 / 18 and seven chips render. Every state's count still equals its rows, and
  that is now asserted for both controls.
* **Contrast on the new secondary button.** White on the hero base measures 17.41:1; the tangerine primary
  measures 4.51:1, which passes AA with very little room — pre-existing, and worth knowing before anyone
  lightens that orange.
* **RTL.** Urdu at 390px: `dir=rtl`, 0px overflow, scrim mirrored, with the new secondary style and phone CTA
  stack in place.
* **The "200+" copy.** It returns to the Koreanasha source's own *"50+개 이상의"* shape rather than departing
  from it as V12 did, and the fidelity gate passes 86/86 across both owner locales.

## 104.7 What I would attack next, and did not fix

Named rather than left for someone to discover.

1. **Document-to-document identity consistency is still missing** (§97.6). The brief's name / date-of-birth /
   school / GPA consistency checks are the largest unimplemented part of Part 7. The data exists in
   `ExtractedField` and `DocumentFinding`; nothing aggregates it to an application-level blocker.
2. **One planning constant for every country.** `DAYS_NEEDED['LEGALIZE'] = 14` is used for Nepal's four-step
   consular chain and for Mongolia's apostille alike. Every country simulation hits this and none of them
   fixed it.
3. **The agency queue can be monopolised by one reason type** (§99). Probably a seed artefact; both obvious
   fixes are worse than the problem; genuinely unresolved.
4. **Half the product was not put through the hierarchy audit** (§95.5): the student application page, the
   agency student workspace, the essay editor, HQ and all three native apps. "V13 audited the product" would
   be an overstatement and this report does not make it.
5. **The composition system covers the public site only.** The consoles were *checked* for the same defect and
   are clean, but they have no semantic composition tokens and no gate holding them to any rhythm.
6. **The native apps were not built or run.** Changed only by shared packages; verified only by `tsc`.

## 104.8 The three things I was wrong about during this pass

1. **I pointed the new primary CTA at a login page** (§104.2) — having spent the pass arguing that naming an
   action after its mechanism is the defect.
2. **I nearly replaced China's verified legalization note with a generic one** (§102.11). The client renders a
   translated note code *instead of* a rule's own text, so attaching a code to a rule that already had
   something better to say would have thrown it away.
3. **I wrote a finding about Vietnam that was false** (§98.2) and only discovered it by calling the function.
   It is kept in the simulation, labelled, because the alternative — quietly deleting it — would leave a
   document that looks more reliable than the process that produced it.

# 105. V14 Visual Continuity Audit

The owner's judgement of V13's homepage was that it reads as "separate coloured rectangles stacked together".
That is not a matter of taste; it is a structural property of how the page was built, and it is measurable.

## What V13 actually was

Six full-width bands, each with its own background colour and a hard horizontal boundary at every join:

| # | Section | Background | Edge above it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hero | photograph | — |
| 2 | University marquee | `#FFF4EC` (peach) | hard |
| 3 | 한귤과 함께라면 (value) | `#FFFFFF` | hard |
| 4 | Services | `#FFF4EC` | hard |
| 5 | FAQ | `#FFFFFF` | hard |
| 6 | Closing band + footer | `#FFFFFF` | hard |

Five hard colour boundaries in one page. A reader can point at each one and name the section it begins, which
is the brief's own test for the failure. The alternation also carried no meaning: peach did not signify
anything that white did not, so the page changed colour five times to say nothing.

## What V14 is

**The page is white.** `--kn-page: #FFFFFF`, and `.kn-band` is transparent. Nothing alternates and nothing
is tinted.

This is the *second* answer. V14's first pass replaced the alternation with one warm off-white surface
(#FDFAF7) and bridged any section that needed its own tone. That removed all five boundaries and the owner's
verdict on the result was still negative: a page-wide pale orange reads as "a weak tinted rectangle". The
criticism is correct and worth recording, because the lesson generalises — **a tint applied to everything is
not a design decision, it is a filter.** It cannot separate anything, because there is nothing it is not
applied to.

So orange went back to being an accent: buttons, emphasis, the triptych ordinals, interaction states. The
only warmth left on a surface is a single short bridge immediately below the hero.

| # | Section | Surface | Edge above it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hero | photograph | — (the one deliberate full-bleed contrast) |
| 2 | University marquee | `#FFFFFF`, entered through a 96–160 px warm bridge | atmospheric, not a line |
| 3 | Value triptych | `#FFFFFF` | none |
| 4 | Services | `#FFFFFF` | none |
| 5 | FAQ | `#FFFFFF` | none |
| 6 | Closing band (a dark card) + footer | `#FFFFFF` | none |

**One** hard boundary remains, where the photograph meets the page — which is where the brief reserves
full-bleed contrast.

### The bridge out of the hero

A full-bleed photograph meeting flat white at a hard line is the most visible edge on the page, because the
contrast is greatest. `.kn-band--afterhero` starts the first band below the hero at `--kn-warm` (#FFF8F3, 2 %
saturation) and reaches pure white within `--kn-bridge` (96–160 px).

At that strength it is not perceived as a colour. On screen it reads as light coming off the photograph above
rather than as a band of its own, which is the difference between atmosphere and a gradient component. It is
the only place on the page where a surface is not white, it is used exactly once, and
`scripts/qa/v14-surface.mjs` asserts both facts.

### White is harder, not easier

Removing the tint removed the only thing that was separating one section from the next, and three places
immediately looked empty rather than spacious. Each was fixed by composition, never by putting a tint back:

| Section | What went wrong on white | What was done |
|---|---|---|
| Services | the photograph was 568 px wide and the words beside it a 130 px block floating in a 568 px column — ~130 px of dead white above and below | image column given the larger share, text given a fixed 420 px measure so it wraps to 5–6 lines; 16:10 crop; inter-row gap 100 → 56–88 px |
| FAQ | ten white cards with hairline borders, on white — the same "a white box on white has no edge" defect that killed the old value cards | the cards are gone. Hairline-separated rows, one structure instead of ten, aligned to the heading above |
| Value triptych | the ordinals were tuned at 34 % against a warm band and read as faded on white | 45 % |

### The university section is white, and is still not a rectangle

Brief Part 5 asks for `#FFFFFF` behind the university marks. With the whole page white that is now the
default rather than an exception — but the rule stays explicit (`.kn-band--canvas { background-color: #fff }`)
and keeps its regression assertion, because a stated requirement that survives only as the *absence* of a rule
is one nobody can see, and the next person to tint a section would not know they had broken it.

The peach it replaced was competing with twenty-three sets of university colours.

## What else carried the "stacked" feeling

- **The footer** painted its own `--hg-bg` white. It is transparent now; the page surface runs to the bottom.
- **`.kn-card`** was a white box with a hairline, used for the value section. On a white band it had no edge
  at all, which is the "three pale rectangles" the owner described. The section no longer uses cards (§110).
- **Decorative eyebrows** gave every section a visible "here begins section N" marker. Removed (Part 12).

## A cost of the white page: the secondary button disappeared

Making the page white has a consequence the white itself does not announce. `.kn-btn--outline` — the
light-surface secondary, and the only treatment 대학 전체 보기 has ever had — was `transparent` on
`--hg-border-strong` (`#D5D7DB`). On V13's warm page that was quiet. On pure white it is **1.44:1**: a
hairline, and the owner's verdict was that the button "almost disappears".

The whole homepage was audited rather than just that one button — every `.kn-btn` at 390 / 768 / 1024 / 1440,
with each one's border and fill measured against whatever actually paints behind it:

| Button | Surface | Level | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 유학 준비 (header) | white pill | primary | filled tangerine, 4.51:1 — fine |
| 내 유학 준비 (hero) | photograph | primary | filled — fine |
| 대학 둘러보기 (hero) | photograph | secondary-dark | `--quiet-onphoto`, deliberately left alone |
| **대학 전체 보기** | **white** | **secondary-light** | **1.44:1 — the defect** |
| 내 유학 준비 (closing) | dark band | primary | 3.86:1 against the band — fine |
| 대학 둘러보기 (closing) | dark band | secondary-dark | 17.4:1 label — fine |

One button was wrong, and only on light surfaces — which is why the hero's secondary was not touched. A dark
translucent pill on a photograph and a bordered white pill on white are the same semantic level on two
different surfaces, and treating them the same would have broken the hero to fix the marquee.

A `--hg-border-control` token now carries the control outline: **`#8A9099`, 3.22:1** — the lightest grey that
still clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor for the boundary of a user-interface component. The brief suggested
`#C9CDD3`; that is 1.60:1, better than 1.44 and still under the standard, so it went darker. Hover takes the
edge, the label and the arrow to tangerine over a very light warm fill — the container never fills with the
brand colour, so the action's *level* is the same before and after the pointer arrives. Height is unchanged at
48 px. No new variant was created: the four levels are still primary, secondary (two surfaces), tertiary and
destructive.

**Secondary does not mean invisible.** `qa:polish` holds the 3:1 floor, the 44 px target and the absence of a
`pointer-events` gate; it reports 1.44:1 and exits 1 if the old border comes back.

## Measured

`npm run qa:composition` — 54 computed-spacing assertions across 320 / 390 / 768 / 1024 / 1440 / 1728 px. It
reads *computed* values on real pages rather than checking that a stylesheet contains a declaration, which is
the distinction that made V13's eight dead rules visible in the first place.

# 106. V14 Media / Licensing Audit

Full document: `docs/MEDIA_LICENSE_AUDIT.md`. Gate: `npm run qa:media`.

## The finding

The owner asked for no customer-visible photo attribution. **13 of the product's 19 photographs were licensed
CC BY**, whose single condition is attribution. Removing the captions would have put us in breach of thirteen
licences; keeping them would have ignored the owner. The brief resolves it explicitly — replace the asset —
and that is what was done.

| Class | Before | After | May ship |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| `HANGYUL_OWNED` | 2 | 2 | yes |
| `CC0_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` | 4 | 9 | yes |
| `ATTRIBUTION_REQUIRED` | 13 | 13 (**0 served**) | no |
| `UNKNOWN` | 0 | 0 | no |

The thirteen are not deleted. Their files moved to `docs/media/retired-attribution-required/` and their rows
stay in `credits.json` with licence, author and source intact — the record of what we used and under what
terms survives. What changed is that nothing serves them and no slot can name them.

## Sourcing

`scripts/media/fetch_cc0.py` downloads only what **Wikimedia Commons' own API** reports as CC0 or public
domain — not the page text, not a category, not the uploader's claim. Six assets were added this way. Two more
were downloaded, looked at, and rejected on quality rather than licence: a parked truck in the foreground of
one, an amateur snapshot of banners and a bank sign in the other. "Legally clear" is not "makes someone want
to be there", and the brief asks for the second.

## What it cost

Stated plainly because it is a real regression, not a rounding error:

- **Yonsei and Kyung Hee lost their campus photographs.** Both CC BY. Their pages fall through to the region
  or brand visual. Honest, and worse than having the photograph.
- **Busan has no attribution-free photograph.** Its `cityFallback` entry was removed rather than pointed at a
  Seoul image, because showing Seoul as Busan is the failure Part 36 names.
- **The CC0 pool for Korean campus photography is thin.** Nine usable assets came out of a full sweep;
  Hangyul holds exactly **one** licensed Korean campus photograph. The durable fix is commissioned or licensed
  stock — `COMMERCIAL_NO_ATTRIBUTION`, the one allowed class Hangyul has none of. Recorded as a launch
  dependency in §115.

## Removed

`.kn-hero__credit` (the rule, not just the caption), the `credit` prop on `Hero`, the `/credits` route, page
and footer link (`/credits` → `/`), and `v6.credits.*` / `v11.credits.*` from all 55 locale bundles. Internal
rights metadata is unchanged and still enforced per class.

## The three service photographs, rechosen

The licence work left the service column *compliant* and bad. It ran a car park at a campus gate, an empty
subway platform and a canal walk: accurate, attribution-free, and an advertisement for nothing. Every slug in
the attribution-free set was rendered at both crop ratios and looked at, not sorted by filename.

| | Slug | What it is | Focal |
|---|---|---|--:|
| 1 · study | `snu-law-library` | A stone law building — pediment relief, columns, lit windows. Unmistakably a university. | `50% 42%` |
| 2 · arrival | `seoul-songpa-sunset` | Seoul from the air at sunset, the sun bursting between towers, lake and park below. | `62% 45%` |
| 3 · life | `seoul-namsan-tower` | A dancheong-painted pavilion lit at night, people under the eaves, the tower behind. | `50% 92%` |

Three times of day, three palettes (grey stone · gold · night) and three scales (facade · aerial · detail),
so the column reads as a sequence. Two candidates were rejected for concrete reasons rather than taste:
`korean-air-apron` because the brief warns against reaching for an aeroplane and it is a crop of a fuselage,
and `seoul-jamsil-lotte-tower-night` — the most beautiful frame in the set — because it is the same landmark
and the same district as image 2, which would have made two of three the same picture.

**The focal points are per image and were chosen by looking at the crop, not by centring.** Namsan is the one
that needed it: the source is 3:4 portrait and the row is 16:10, so no crop holds the tower whole. At `72%`
the tower's top was cut *and* the pavilion lost — a frame of a green shaft and a roof ridge. At `92%` the lit
pavilion is unambiguously the subject, the tower reads as background, and the people and the N sign come into
frame — which is what makes it a picture of a place people go. Verified at 390, 768 and 1440.

### A bug this pass introduced and caught

The three slugs were re-encoded to AVIF and WebP (`scripts/media/encode_modern.py`), roughly 2.5× smaller
than the JPEG at 2400 px, served through a `<picture>` and opt-in per asset via a `formats` field — a slug
without it still ships plain JPEG. That `<picture>` then matched an existing rule,

```css
@media (max-width: 699px) and (orientation: portrait) { .mk-picture img { object-position: … !important; } }
```

written for the *portrait art-direction* wrapper, and silently reset all three focal points to `50% 50%` on
phones. Found by measuring computed `object-position` at 390 after the swap, not by looking at the page. The
rule is now scoped to `.mk-picture--art`, the class only the art-direction branch renders.

### Alt text

The three alt strings described the photographs from **two** sets ago — Ewha's ECC, Incheon T1, a Hongdae
ramyeon shop — in all 31 locales. Already wrong before this pass, and swapping the images would have made
them wrong in a new way. All 93 were rewritten to describe what now ships. They carry the same synthetic,
unreviewed caveat as the rest of the non-Korean copy (§115); nothing here is relabelled as reviewed.

# 107. V14 32-Market Localization Audit

Full document: `docs/qa/v14/LOCALE_MATRIX.md`. Gate: `node scripts/qa/v14-locales.mjs`.

## It is 31 markets, not 32

`apps/flags` holds **31** flag assets. `apps/flags/index.ts` wires 30 of them; `RS.svg` (Serbia) ships in the
folder and is not exported, and no `sr` locale existed anywhere in the product. V14 added the locale rather
than dropping the flag.

Nothing was invented to reach 32. **If a 32nd market was intended, its asset was not delivered**, and only the
owner can say which country it is. That is an open question in §115, not a defect this pass could resolve.

Three of the owner's filenames do not name the country they depict — the French tricolour is `GP.svg`, the
Polish flag is `ID2.svg`, Korea's is `KO.svg` (a language tag). The files are **not renamed**; `markets.ts`
maps each to its real ISO code and `scripts/media/sync-flags.mjs` publishes `GP.svg` as `FR.svg`. `ID.svg` and
`ID2.svg` are near-mirror images, so getting this wrong shows a Polish reader the Indonesian flag — the locale
gate asserts the flag matches the market.

### Two market lists, deliberately different

`apps/flags` defines which markets the product **presents** itself to. It is not the only market list the
product holds, and the second one is not wrong for being different. Both are now in
`packages/i18n/src/markets.ts`, and `marketGap()` computes the difference:

| | Defined by | Answers | Count |
|---|---|---|--:|
| `MARKETS` | `apps/flags` | which markets we **present** to | 31 |
| `RESEARCH_MARKETS` | visa playbooks, country simulations, student personas | which markets we **know how to serve** | 14 |

In both: **11**. Researched but not presented: **3** — Nepal (`ne`), Myanmar (`my`), Pakistan (`ur`).
Presented but not yet researched: **19** (Korea excluded; it is the destination).

`npm run qa:locales` prints this on every run, which is the actual fix. The failure this pass found by
accident was three researched markets reading the site in English with nobody noticing — possible only
because no single place held both lists.

Three things were deliberately **not** done: no flag was invented, no locale was dropped, and the lists were
not merged. They measure different things, and collapsing them would destroy the only signal that says which
markets are ready and which are aspirational. Whether to commission flags for the three, research for some of
the nineteen, or neither, is the owner's call. `docs/qa/v14/LOCALE_MATRIX.md` carries the standing table.


## The gap V14 closed

The homepage existed in Korean, English and Russian. **28 of the 31 markets read the owner's marketing copy in
English.**

| | Before | After |
|---|--:|--:|
| Markets with a fully translated homepage (49 keys) | 3 | **31** |
| Markets with translated site chrome (header, footer, legal labels, language search) | 2 | **31** |
| Markets with a translated university directory (225 keys) | 2 | 2 (+3 nav/footer labels elsewhere) |

All 49 homepage strings were translated **from the Korean source**, which is canonical (Part 41); English was
a second reading to check meaning, never the source.

## What the pipeline refuses

`scripts/i18n/v14-merge.mjs` rejects a value that drops or invents an interpolation, uses markup the renderer
cannot handle, is byte-identical to the English source, or contains characters from a writing system the
locale does not use.

The last check earned its place immediately. The first batch, written by hand, contained **a Chinese sentence
ending in the Russian word "материалы" and a Japanese one containing the Korean "설계"** — both invisible to a
coverage count, both obvious to a native reader. A genuine cognate needs a named entry in
`scripts/i18n/v14-cognates.json` with a reason, so "equals the English" is always a decision or a failure.

## What the visual gate found that coverage could not

1. **The primary CTA rendered in Russian on the Uzbek homepage.** V13's `FALLBACK_CHAIN` (`uz → ru → en`) is
   sound for a long-tail key and wrong for the product's one conversion action. An Uzbek reader saw "Начать
   подготовку" on the button the whole site funnels to. Fixed by translating the chrome for all 31 markets.
2. **The Portuguese header label broke the pill at 390 px.** 내 유학 준비 is 7 characters; "Começar a minha
   preparação" is 26. Truncation was tried and rejected — an unreadable primary action is not an action — and
   the header now uses a short label (`v14.cta.prepareShort`, one or two words per market) while the hero and
   closing band keep the full phrase.
3. **A long Dutch compound pushed the closing band's heading past the viewport at 320 px**, and the band's
   32 px padding left 224 px for a button that needed more. Headings now break; full-width buttons wrap.
4. **Japanese headings would not break at all** — `word-break: keep-all`, correct for Korean, applied to
   everything.

## Status, stated honestly

**No locale is `HUMAN_REVIEWED`,** and none is claimed to be. What V14 added is `SYNTHETIC_REVIEWED` at best.
Privacy and terms are **deliberately excluded** from translation: a privacy policy is a legal instrument, and
a machine-drafted one in 29 languages would be worse than a correct English one. `sr` is new in this pass and is the
least complete of the 31: the homepage and the chrome, with `common` at 2 % (ten keys of 587).

# 108. V14 Language URL Architecture

Gate: `npm run qa:locale-url`.

Before V14 the current language was a `localStorage` key. Two consequences a user feels: a link you send opens
in the recipient's language, not yours; and crossing from the public site to the student app lost the choice
entirely, because they are different origins with different storage.

`?lang=<code>` is now the authority.

```
1. explicit ?lang= in the URL     ← always wins, including over an account preference
2. the authenticated account's preference
3. the saved device preference
4. the browser's language
5. the default
```

The account preference moved **above** the saved device preference (it was below). That is safe precisely
because the selector now navigates: any explicit in-session choice is in the URL and has already won at step 1.

**One selector, everywhere.** `LocaleSelector` replaces V8's `LanguageSwitcher` on every surface the brief
names: the marketing header pill, the mobile menu, the marketing footer, the student app's top bar, both
console shells, the public quick check, the sponsor view, and all three settings pages. The old component is
**deleted**, not deprecated — leaving a second, older language UI in the package is how a product ends up
with two of them again. It had no flags, searched three fields instead of six, offered an unordered 55-item
list and wrote only to `localStorage`.

The one caller that needs more than a URL change is the account settings page, which also persists the choice
to the server. It passes `onChange`; the selector still navigates, so there is one behaviour and one
appearance rather than a header control and a settings control that differ.

**The sync is one-way.** The selector navigates; `useLocaleFromUrl` reacts. A two-way sync is how a language
picker ends up fighting the back button, because every correction it makes is a history entry the previous one
undoes. Back and forward move between languages for free.

**Changing the language changes only the language.** `withLang` / `localeHref` rebuild the URL preserving
path, every other query parameter and the hash: `/universities?region=seoul&lang=ko#list` → `…&lang=vi#list`
with the region and the scroll target intact.

Verified end to end: direct loads for `vi`, `ne`, `ar` (with `dir="rtl"`), `zh-Hans` (script subtag preserved)
and `my`; an unknown tag resolving rather than breaking; internal navigation; **a homepage university crest
clicked at `?lang=vi` landing on `/universities/seoul-national-university?lang=vi`**; the auth hand-off to the
Student Platform carrying `lang=ne`; and back/forward.

# 109. V14 University Photography & Discovery

## The model

`apps/marketing-web/src/media/university-media.ts` — `UniversityMedia` with `asset`, `university_id`, `kind`
(`HERO` · `CAMPUS` · `LIBRARY` · `STUDENT_LIFE` · `DORMITORY` · `CITY` · `REGION_FALLBACK`), `source_type`,
`rights_status`, `focal_x/y`, `alt_key`, `width`, `height`. One resolver, `resolveVisual()`, implements the
brief's priority order so every surface answers "what does this university look like" identically.

**The rule that shapes it: a city photograph is never presented as a campus.** When the picture is the city,
the component says so in the reader's language, in a caption that is part of the image — and the `alt` text
says it too, so a screen-reader user is not told they are looking at a campus either.

## The detail page

V13's public university page was entirely text: a breadcrumb, a name, a facts table and a list of sources. It
answered *what is this institution* and nothing about *could I be there*.

It now has two forms, and which one a university gets depends on whether there is anything true to show:

- **With a photograph** — an immersive first viewport (24:9 at desktop, 4:3 on a phone) under the floating
  header, then the name, the region, one action. Then 캠퍼스 둘러보기 when **two or more** verified images of
  *this* university exist: an editorial grid on desktop (one lead image, the rest beside it), a scroll-snapped
  row on a phone where one image fills 88 % of the viewport — which is right here, because the task is visual
  browsing, and wrong for the service section, where the task is reading.
- **Without one** — the typographic header, now with the section's soft warmth and a 44 rem measure instead of
  floating in a 1,200 px void.

A first draft gave the no-photograph case a brand-led hero: an initial on the brand gradient. At hero scale it
was a 500 px peach band with a giant letter in it — **demonstrably worse than the text header it replaced**,
and exactly the "bolted on" look the brief's optical review asks about. It was removed. A brand-led fallback
only works at a size where a mark reads as a mark.

## The directory thumbnail that was built and then removed

Part 53 asks for a 16:10 visual per directory row. It was built, and it is not shipped.

Hangyul holds **one** licensed Korean campus photograph for 425 institutions, so 424 rows drew the same brand
placeholder: a wall of identical peach squares with mostly the same character in them, because the registry is
alphabetical. It was less informative than the text list and read as something that had failed to load.
`UniversityVisual` and `UNIVERSITY_MEDIA` are in place and the thumbnail returns the day there is photography
for it. What is missing is licensed imagery, not code.

The same pass did fix a real directory defect: the three-column grid at ≥1400 px gave each row ~350 px, and
"가톨릭관동대학교 / Catholic Kwandong University" wrapped across five lines. Two columns now.

## Coverage, measured

| | |
|---|--:|
| Institutions in the directory | 425 |
| With a verified campus photograph | **1** |
| With a region photograph (labelled as the region) | 85 (Seoul) |
| With neither | 339 |

That number is the finding of this section, not a footnote to it.
