# 110. V14 Mobile Marketing Redesign

Three failures the owner named, each with its cause.

## The service section was a desktop carousel on a phone

V11–V13 turned the three service rows into one horizontal scroller below 992 px: cards at 84 % of the viewport
with the next one's edge showing, body copy clipped by the snap boundary, a focusable scroll region. It saved
scrolling — the one thing a phone reader is happy to do — at the cost of legibility.

Gone. Each service is now image → title → body, full content width, down the page: a 4:3 crop so the subject
survives at 358 px, a 24–28 px title, 16 px body at 1.72 line height. The focusable wrapper and its
`scrollable-region-focusable` workaround went with it.

A horizontal track does survive in one place — the university gallery (§109) — because there the task *is*
visual browsing and one image fills the viewport. The difference is the task, not the pattern.

## The hero put the copy where the campus was

V13 anchored the phone hero to the bottom: headline, lede and both actions in the last third, over the part of
the photograph a visitor actually responds to.

The content block is now anchored to the **top**, clearing the header pill, and calibrated separately at 320 /
390 / 430 / 768. The lower half is the photograph. The height is unchanged — this is the same cinematic
`100svh` screen with its contents moved, not a shorter hero.

Two things had to move with it. The scrim was bottom-weighted for bottom-anchored copy; over top-anchored copy
it both failed to help the text and greyed out the campus the move was meant to expose — it is top-weighted
now, and lighter through the middle. And `object-position` is art-directed per breakpoint (`50% 64%` on a
phone against `50% 52%` on desktop), because a tall narrow crop at the desktop focal point puts the buildings
off the bottom edge.

### The internal rhythm, corrected in the final pass

With the content block in the right place, the remaining fault was *inside* it: the copy and the buttons read
as one compressed block.

The numbers were not obviously wrong — 30 px headline→copy and 36 px copy→actions, both inside their
intended ranges. **The ratio was.** A six-pixel difference between two gaps separated by a line of text is
not visible; the eye cannot compare 30 to 36 across an intervening paragraph, so it reads them as the same
gap and the three layers collapse into two.

| | Before | After |
|---|--:|--:|
| Headline → copy (desktop) | 30 px | **26 px** |
| Copy → CTA group (desktop) | 36 px | **40 px** |
| Ratio | 1.20 | **1.54** |
| Headline → copy (390 px) | 24 px | **22 px** |
| Copy → CTA group (390 px) | 28 px | **30 px** |
| Button gap | 14.4 px | 14.4 px (unchanged) |

The whole block did **not** move down: the hero's vertical position, the image, the copy, the button
hierarchy and the floating header are all untouched, and the campus is as visible as before. Only the two
internal gaps changed.

`--hg-flow-heading` and `--hg-flow-copy` carry it, so every surface that uses the composition tokens inherits
the same rhythm. `scripts/qa/v13-composition.mjs` now asserts the **ratio** rather than only the ordering: its
old rule was `copy→action > headline→copy`, which 36 > 30 satisfies and which therefore could not have caught
this. It requires 1.25× today.

## The value section had no visual presence

"한귤과 함께라면, 유학의 길이 달라집니다!" rendered through the shared card grid: three white rounded boxes
with a hairline, on white. A white card on white has no edge. The owner's three strongest claims were on the
page and nothing about the page said they mattered.

Two compositions were built and compared at 390 / 768 / 1440. **(A) three tonal panels** was rejected — on the
new warm page surface a panel is either invisible or dark enough to become a box again, and boxes are what
§105 spends its length removing. **(B) three columns divided by fine vertical rules** ships: no fill, no
shadow, no icon circle. A hairline, an oversized ordinal in the brand colour at 34 % opacity, a 28 px title, a
17 px measure at 1.72. On phones the columns stack with horizontal rules — no swipe, no peeking card, no
clipped text, the same rule the service section now follows.

# 111. V14 Motion Design System

Full document: `docs/qa/v14/MOTION_AUDIT.md`.

Six durations and four easings in `packages/design-tokens`; one `Reveal` component with four variants
(`fade` · `rise` · `media` · `stagger`); no second reveal component, which the brief rules out by name.

Interface state gets 120–260 ms and entrances get 640–1400 ms, because they are different kinds of event. The
entrance curve is `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)` — a fast start that settles, which is what makes an element look
like it arrived rather than slid to a stop. Nothing springs or bounces.

**The resting state is visible.** The hidden state is applied only when script adds `--armed`, and only when
`IntersectionObserver` exists and reduced motion is not requested. Koreanasha's own build loads AOS from a CDN
that sets `opacity: 0` on every section at parse time; if the CDN fails, the page is blank. This cannot.

What is deliberately not animated: the crests (the belt is the section's motion; a second effect on top is
noise), section backgrounds, scroll-linked parallax, counters, icons, and any kind of pinning.

**The final pass removed colour blocks and added no motion to compensate.** The temptation when a page goes
white is to replace the missing visual rhythm with movement, and that is how a restrained motion language
becomes a noisy one. The reveals that exist — `fade` on headings, `media` on photography, `stagger` on the
triptych, the continuous belt, the FAQ's height transition — were already doing the work the brief lists, and
the white page simply lets them be seen. The one motion change in this pass was a **removal**: the FAQ's cards
went, so the item that animates is now a row rather than a box.

Reduced motion stops the marquee completely — measured: 0 animated tracks, 23 crests shown, 0 duplicates — and
nothing else is left half-faded, because nothing was ever armed.

### A trap worth recording

Reveal-on-scroll makes **full-page screenshots lie**. Playwright's `fullPage` renders beyond the viewport
without scrolling, so every unseen section is still at `opacity: 0`. The first V14 capture was 4,000 px of
white. The capture scripts now sweep the page first — and that sweep must pass `behavior: 'instant'`, because
Bootstrap sets `html { scroll-behavior: smooth }` here and a loop of plain `scrollTo` calls restarts the
animation every step, leaving the page near the top however many steps you ask for.

---

## The homepage was still static, and the tokens were not why

The motion system was finished and the homepage barely used it. Every section head was `variant="fade"` —
opacity only, no movement — the three marquee rows had no entrance at all, and neither did the university
call to action. So the page had a motion language and almost nothing spoke it. The final pass changed what is
wired, not what exists: no fifth variant, no second component, no library.

| Where | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Section heads (×4) | `fade`, title and copy together | `rise`, **heading first, copy +120 ms** |
| Marquee rows | nothing | one `fade` over the group — never per logo |
| 대학 전체 보기 | nothing | `rise`, +160 ms, after the rows |
| Service rows | `media` + text rise | unchanged — it was already right |
| Value triptych | `stagger` 80 ms | unchanged |

`SectionHead` gained a `reveal` prop that gives the heading and the supporting copy their own `Reveal`. A
section head read as one block is the thing the brief asks not to do: the heading is the promise and the copy
qualifies it, so the copy should arrive *after* it. 120 ms is enough to read as an order and short enough that
the pair still lands as one gesture.

The rows get `fade` and not `rise` for a specific reason: they are already travelling sideways, and lifting
them as they slide reads as a wobble. Nothing is animated per crest — the belt is the section's movement, and
an entrance on each logo on top of it is two effects fighting.

`motion.reveal` went **560 → 640 ms**, into the brief's 600–850 ms band for text. `media` (760 ms) and `hero`
(1400 ms) are unchanged, so entrances still have three distinct speeds rather than one applied everywhere.

The CTA's 160 ms is a `transition-delay` and nothing else. There is no `pointer-events: none` anywhere in the
reveal system, so a button is clickable from the moment it exists — `qa:polish` asserts that, because "the
animation delays the click" is the way this pattern usually goes wrong.

### What this is still not

No parallax was added. No section is pinned, nothing hijacks the scroll, and no two elements move at
different speeds. The reveal runs **once** per element (`io.disconnect()` on first intersection), so nothing
replays when the reader scrolls back up.

# 112. V14 University Marquee & Detail Integrity

Gates: `npm run qa:marquee`, `npm run qa:marquee-details`, `npm run qa:crests`.

## The seam was a geometry bug, not a tuning problem

V13's track was `display: flex; gap: G` holding 2N items, translated `-50%`. With one gap *between* every pair,
the track measures `2N·w + (2N−1)·G`, so half of it is `N·w + N·G − G/2` — **half a gap short of one group**.
Every iteration jumped backwards by G/2: a 20 px tear at the 40 px desktop gap, once per loop. No change to
duration, item count or easing could have fixed it; the number being animated was wrong.

The track now carries **no** gap. Each group carries `gap: G` *and* a trailing `padding-inline-end: G`, so a
group is exactly `N·(w + G)` and `-50%` of two of them is exactly one.

Measured at 1440 px: group 3335.1 px = track/2 3335.1 px on row 1, and to the pixel on rows 2 and 3. Sampled
past a full cycle: **0 discontinuities, worst blank gap 40 px** — which is one gap, i.e. the design.

The gate was verified against the defect: reintroducing the track `gap` makes it report "off by 20.00px" on
every row and exit 1.

| | |
|---|---|
| Rows | 3 |
| Directions | left · right · left (the original's own `index % 2`) |
| Durations | 46 s · 54 s · 50 s |
| Phase offsets | 0 · 0.33 · 0.66 of a loop |
| Crests rendered | 138 |
| **Reachable by keyboard** | **23** — the clone group and every padding repeat are `aria-hidden` and `inert` |
| Reduced motion | 0 animated tracks, 23 crests, 0 duplicates |

## Yonsei

`u-1-2.svg` was an SVG wrapper around an embedded WebP: the seal **on a white rectangle**. Ink fill 100 %,
opaque corners — the one crest that looked pasted on.

Rebuilt from the owner's original 1907 × 2268 JPEG (the shipped file had been downsampled at an earlier
optimisation pass, so the resolution was already in the repository). The flood starts from the **border**, so
only the surrounding rectangle is removed; the white inside the mark is enclosed by navy and never reached.
The antialiased frontier is unpremultiplied against white rather than cut square. 64 indexed colours: 65 KB →
10 KB.

**Ink fill 79 %, corner alpha 0, 21,710 opaque white pixels preserved inside the mark.** The blue circle, the
white symbol, the Korean text, the English text and the internal negative space are untouched.

UNIST also measures 100 % and is **deliberately not "fixed"**: its official signature is white-and-cyan on a
navy field, so the navy *is* the mark. Knocking it out deletes the wordmark; recolouring it alters a
trademark. It ships as a deliberate rounded tile, recorded by name as the one allowed exception.

## Eleven logos were being cut off, and the clamp was why

The owner's report was that university logos were clipped top and bottom. They were — **eleven of the
twenty-three**, by 2.6 px at 390 and 5 px at 1440.

The cause was not the mask and not the row height. `--c-scale` is the per-crest optical correction, clamped
to **0.88–1.10**, and it multiplied the slot height directly: `height: calc(100% * var(--c-scale))`. So every
crest the clamp pushed to its ceiling rendered at **110 % of a row that has `overflow: hidden`** — which it
must have, for the horizontal loop — and the extra 10 % was sliced off, half at the top and half at the
bottom. The eleven are exactly the sparse ones the correction enlarges: KAIST, POSTECH, Sungkyunkwan,
Chung-Ang, Dongguk, Hongik, Pusan, Kookmin, Sejong, Dankook and Ewha. Ring seals and shields — the marks with
the most to lose at their edges.

The edge mask is `linear-gradient(to right, …)`: left and right only. It was never the cause and was not
touched.

The fix is one division and six numbers:

```css
--kn-crest-fit: 1.16;                                   /* SCALE_MAX 1.10 + ~5 % air */
height: calc(100% * var(--c-scale, 1) / var(--kn-crest-fit));
--kn-crest-h: 60px / 74px / 88px / 116px;               /* each × 1.16 */
```

`--c-scale` is now a **fraction of the slot** and cannot exceed it, and the slot heights were multiplied by
the same 1.16 in the same change. The arithmetic matters: at 1440 a median crest was 100 px and is 100 px
(116 × 1.00 ÷ 1.16); a 1.10 crest was 110 px and is 110 px — but *fully drawn* instead of sliced. **No logo
was shrunk, no logo was stretched, no artwork was redrawn.** The box grew to hold the biggest one.

That is also why "just shrink the logos", which the brief rules out, would have been the wrong fix: the
defect was never the artwork's size, it was a container smaller than its contents.

`qa:polish` measures the outcome rather than the CSS — every crest's rendered rect against its slot *and*
against the row that actually clips — so a different way of reintroducing the slice is caught too. Verified
against the defect: restoring the old multiplication reports all eleven at all three widths and exits 1.
Evidence in `docs/qa/v14/logo-crop-fix/`, where `tall-*.png` clones the eleven into one strip, each in a box
outlined at its row's exact bounds, so artwork crossing the outline *is* the defect.

## Chung-Ang — found by looking, not by a gate

The fill measure answers one question: *is this a crest or a rectangle?* It cannot see a defect that is
small. `u-2-2.svg` carried a **hollow red square** sitting over the "u" of the brush-drawn "CAU" and over the
ring text, flush with the right edge of its artboard — a marker left in the Figma export. It shipped through
every V14 gate because a 13 × 13-unit box in a 67 × 63 artboard moves bbox fill by less than a point. It was
found in the final pass by enlarging the university band out of `marquee-1440.png` and looking at it.

The repair is a new subcommand rather than a hand-edit, for the same reason the Yonsei one is:
`normalize_crests.py chungang --write` reads the owner's original, deletes **one path by id**, and writes the
other 28 through byte for byte. Nothing is recoloured, rescaled or redrawn — the grey ring reading
"1916 · CHUNG-ANG · UNIVERSITY" and the blue brush "CAU" that ship are the owner's artwork with an overlay
taken off, not a redrawing of a trademark. 29 paths → 28; ink fill 19.0 % → 18.2 %; rendered width 106 → 105,
because the marker had been stretching the bounding box to the artboard edge.

Then the class of defect was gated, so that "we looked at it once" is not the control. A path counts as stray
when **all three** hold: it is an axis-aligned box, it is the only path in the file with its fill colour, and
it runs flush to the artboard edge. Across the 23 crests that matches exactly two paths — UNIST's navy field,
excused by name above, and the Chung-Ang marker. Every other boxy path in the set shares its colour with
dozens of siblings and sits inside the artboard, which is what a letter or a device in a seal looks like.
Points are clustered at 2 % of the artboard before a path is called a box, because the marker's own corners
disagree by hundredths of a unit — the sloppiness is itself the evidence that a hand drew it over the export.

`qa:crests` now fails on a stray overlay as well as on a rectangular background. Verified against the defect
it exists for: before the repair, `audit --strict` exits 1 and names `Vector_28 #E51F1F`.

## Every logo leads somewhere

V13 linked **8 of 23** crests; fifteen were inert images.

All 23 universities were already on the national register — two under their colloquial names (카이스트 →
한국과학기술원, 유니스트 → 울산과학기술원), which is why the V13 join missed them. `build_marquee_manifest.py`
joins crests to the registry and writes the manifest, so no destination is written in JSX.

**23 / 23 crests resolve to a complete university page** — identity, heading, location, official website, no
placeholder copy, no demo wording — and the language survives the click.

## Optical scale

Every crest is drawn in the same box; `--c-scale = clamp(0.88, (median_mass / mass) ** 0.42, 1.10)` sizes the
artwork inside it, computed from the rendered alpha rather than chosen by hand. A wide wordmark carries far
more ink than a compact seal at the same height, which was most of why the V13 band looked like a set of
unrelated images. The correction is at most ±10 % and no official proportion changes.

## The disclaimer

*"각 로고는 해당 대학의 상표입니다…"* is removed and **not replaced with another disclaimer**. Nothing about
the legal position changed: university mark permission is still unresolved, still a blocker in
`release:check`, still recorded in `docs/LEGAL_DEPENDENCIES.md`, and no university is labelled Partner or
제휴 대학 anywhere. What changed is who is asked to read our legal position.

What was built, in the order it was built, with the reasoning that is not visible in the result.

The V13 baseline was captured first — marketing at nine widths (320 → 1728), the three consoles and the
student app at five, plus the six named homepage bands sliced out of the full page — into

`apps/flags` was enumerated rather than assumed, which is how the count turned out to be 31 (§107).

The order matters: a redesign on top of broken data is a redesign that has to be done twice.

- **Chung-Ang** stripped of a stray export marker (§112) — one path deleted by id, the other 28 written

- **Eleven clipped logos** fixed by geometry, not by shrinking (§112): `--c-scale` is now a fraction of the
  slot instead of a multiplier that could exceed it, and the slot grew by the same factor. No crest changed size.

- **The crest → university manifest regenerated** from the national registry.
  `scripts/media/build_marquee_manifest.py`. 8 mapped → **23**.
- **Optical scale** computed per crest from rendered alpha, not chosen by eye.
- **Media reclassified**, 13 attribution-required assets retired, 6 CC0 assets sourced (§106).
- **31 flag assets published** to four apps under their real ISO codes. `scripts/media/sync-flags.mjs`.

§§105–112 were written before the homepage was rebuilt, as the brief requires. Two of them changed what got
built: §106's licence count made it clear the photography plan had to shrink rather than grow, and §109's

Surface system → marquee geometry → eyebrows and disclaimer out → value triptych → service stack → mobile

Measured first: 51 homepage keys × 31 markets, of which 3 markets had them. Then seven translation batches,

Recorded because the removals are decisions, and because a log that only lists what shipped reads as though

## Defects found in V13 while working, and fixed

- **`v11-extract-koreanasha.mjs` disagreed with the bundles it protects.** V13 corrected the shipped count
  strings back to the Koreanasha sentence shape and did not update the extractor's `COUNT_PHRASE`, so the
  committed fidelity manifest still encoded V12's wording. Because the manifest is generated, the
  disagreement was invisible until someone regenerated it. The shipped strings were right; the table was
  wrong.
- **The footer business block was styled in `v11.css`**, which only the home route loads, while `SiteLayout`
  renders it on every page. It was a compact row on the homepage and an unstyled five-row stack on the

- **A grid item's `min-width: auto`** let a `nowrap` button set a 300 px floor inside a 288 px band, pushing

## 7 · The final composition pass

Everything above was built against a dev server that had not reloaded `packages/config/vite.ts` (see the note
at the end of this section), so the first act of this pass was to restart the stack and re-judge. That matters
more than it sounds: with the specificity fix inactive the hero's authored margins were still computing to
15 px and 0 px, and the spacing criticism that opened this pass was partly a criticism of CSS that was never
running. **Re-measure before redesigning.**

With the real rendering on screen, four things were actually wrong, and one thing that had been shipped as a
solution turned out to be the problem:

1. **The hero's two gaps were in the right ranges and the wrong ratio** (§110). 30/36 is not a hierarchy.
2. **The page-wide warm surface was the problem, not the fix** (§105). A tint applied to everything separates
   nothing.
3. **Three sections looked empty once the tint was gone** (§105) — services, FAQ, triptych ordinals. Each was
   a composition fault the tint had been hiding.
4. **The header's single broad shadow dissolved on white** (§111 table). Two layers: a contact shadow that
   holds the edge on paper, a wider lifted one for the photograph. Geometry untouched.

Removed in this pass: `.kn-band--tint` (no callers — a "paint this section a different colour" helper is how
the cream/white rhythm returns one section at a time), `.kn-band--glow`, and the FAQ's ten card boxes.

Added: `.kn-band--afterhero` (one bridge, used once) and `scripts/qa/v14-surface.mjs`.

## The CSS specificity debt (brief Part 60)

V13 recorded that `rtlcss` rewrites Eduan's element rules to `[dir] p` — specificity (0,1,1) — which outranks
every single-class rule, and worked around it by authoring the composition block at `.kn .kn-*` (0,2,0).

V14 fixes the cause. A new postcss step runs after rtlcss and rewrites its generated prefix to
`:where([dir…])`, which matches identically and contributes **zero** specificity. 4,965 selectors rewritten,
0 bare `[dir]` prefixes left. An element rule is back to (0,0,1), a class is (0,1,0), and the cascade does
what both stylesheets' authors assumed.

**The workaround was then removed**, not left in place: all 19 composition rules dropped the `.kn` ancestor,
and `npm run qa:composition` passes 54 computed-spacing assertions across six widths. A dead
higher-specificity rule is how the next person learns to add another one.

> **One operational consequence.** `packages/config/vite.ts` is an imported module rather than an app's own
> `vite.config.ts`, so a dev server already running when the change landed does not pick it up. The long-lived
> dev server on :3100 was still serving `[dir] p` at the end of this pass and therefore still shows V13's
> collapsed hero spacing; everything in this section was verified against a fresh instance on :4710 and
> against production builds. **The running dev stack needs a restart.**

## The final composition pass

Automated QA was green before this pass and the composition was still unfinished, which is the whole reason
the pass exists. What it changed, and what the gates measured afterwards:

**Hero breathing space.** Nothing moved down and nothing was restyled; only the second pause widened. The
first gap narrowed slightly so the ratio between the two would carry the hierarchy — a 20 % difference
between two gaps separated by a line of text is invisible, and that was the real fault, not the absolute
numbers.

| | headline → copy | copy → CTA | ratio | button gap |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Before (1440) | 30 px | 36 px | 1.20 | 14.4 px |
| **After (1440)** | **26 px** | **40 px** | **1.54** | 14.4 px |
| **After (390)** | **22 px** | **30 px** | **1.36** | 16 px |

Every figure is inside the brief's range (desktop 24–30 / 34–40 / 14–18; mobile copy → CTA 28–34), and
`qa:surface` now fails below 1.25× so the ratio cannot quietly collapse again.

**The page is white.** The warm page tint is gone — `--kn-page: #FFFFFF`. Orange survives as an accent only:
the primary button, emphasised words in two section headings, the triptych ordinals. There is no orange
rectangle, no beige section, no peach card and no gradient band anywhere below the bridge. §105 carries the
reasoning; the short version is that a tint applied to everything separates nothing.

**The transition.** One bridge, `clamp(96px, 11vw, 160px)`, on the first band below the hero and nowhere
else. It reads as light spilling off the photograph rather than as a band with an edge — measured in
`seam-{w}.png`, where the warmth is gone before the first crest row.

**The cream / white / cream rhythm is gone.** Bands are transparent. Sections are now separated by spacing,
content width, typography, imagery, alignment and hairline rules — `.kn-band--tint` and `.kn-band--glow` are
deleted, and `qa:surface` fails if either returns.

**Where white looked empty, the composition changed — no tint was reintroduced.** Three places needed it:
the service rows were rebalanced so the photograph dominates (`1fr / 420px`, flipped alternately), the FAQ
became an editorial list on hairline rules instead of cards floating on a background that no longer
contrasts, and the triptych ordinals went 0.34 → 0.45 opacity because they had been tuned against warm paper.

**Motion was not increased.** No new animation was added in this pass; the reveal system is the same four
variants, and simpler backgrounds were not treated as a licence to add more.

**The header over white.** Pill geometry is untouched. Only the shadow changed, to two layers — a 1 px
contact shadow plus a wide soft one — so the pill separates from white without reading as a second white
section. Checked in both contexts: over the photograph and scrolled over white.

## The scroll review

Screenshots cannot show choreography, so the page was also walked top to bottom and photographed **mid-
reveal** — ten stops, each captured 220 ms after arriving, which is where popping, late reveals and dead
zones are visible and a settled screenshot shows nothing.

What that found: at every stop the lowest opacity among the elements in view was **0.16 and rising**. Nothing
was still hidden, nothing snapped from 0 to 1, and no stop had a region with nothing happening in it. The
frames show the intended order — heading in, copy a beat behind, image and body text still arriving — rather
than a block of content appearing at once.

Also checked by eye and not by assertion: the belts and the entrances do not fight (the rows fade as a group
while they travel, and no crest does anything of its own); the CTA arrives after the logos rather than with
them; nothing replays on the way back up.

## Screenshots reviewed, not just captured

54 shots at 390 / 430 / 768 / 1024 / 1440 / 1728 in `docs/qa/v14/compose/`: `home`, `home-full`, `seam` and
the six named bands. These were looked at, which is how the Chung-Ang marker (§112) was found — it had passed
every gate. Reviewed by eye: hero at 390 / 768 / 1440 / 1728, the hero → white seam at 390 / 768 / 1440, the
university band, the service rows at 390 / 1024 / 1440, "한귤과 함께라면" at 390 / 1440, the FAQ at 390 /
1440, the footer, and the header in both contexts.

The capture script itself had a fault found the same way: Playwright scrolls an element into view before an
element screenshot and puts its top flush with the viewport top — i.e. **under** the floating header — so
every band shot hid its own heading behind a bar that is not part of the band. Scrolling clear first does not
fix it, because Playwright's internal scroll undoes it; the header is hidden for the band captures instead.
The hero is the exception: it is at the top of the page, nothing is covered, and the header floating over the
photograph is part of what the hero has to look right with. The header's own appearance is judged in
`home-*` and `seam-*`, which show it in both contexts.

## Tests that had to change, and why

A test that fails because the product improved is a test encoding a decision, not a rule. Five did, and each
was rewritten to assert the rule rather than the snapshot it was written against.

| Test | Was asserting | Now asserts |
|---|---|---|
| `v11-marketing` 8 | `/trust` → `/credits` | `/trust` and `/credits` both → `/`; no redirect may target a retired route |
| `v13-hierarchy` 3 | the header and hero labels are **identical strings** | both are tangerine, both carry `data-cta="primary"`, **both go to `/start`**, the header's label is the shorter and its accessible name is the full phrase |
| `v13-hierarchy` 6 | the literal `"200+"` in every locale | the scaled figure **in the digits of its own sentence**, computed per locale |
| `v12-legal` | every legal field is `null` | the five supplied values are byte-exact, 남우준 is **not** inferred as privacy officer, and every other required field is still reported missing |
| `v13-hierarchy` 4 | copy → CTA is 28–36 px and merely `>` the gap above it | the V14 ranges (24–30 / 34–40 / 14–18) and copy → CTA **≥ 1.25×** headline → copy — the same floor `qa:surface` holds, so a gate and a test cannot disagree about what "separated" means |

`v13-hierarchy` 4 is the one that was wrong rather than merely outdated. Its upper bound was 36 px and its
relationship assertion was `copyToAction > headingToCopy`, so the first V14 pass's 30/36 satisfied it
exactly — a 1.20 ratio that the owner read, correctly, as one compressed block. The test passed and the
composition was still wrong, which is the whole argument for the final pass. The floor is now a ratio, not an
inequality.

Test 6 is the interesting one. V13 asserted `"200+"` because the homepage existed in three locales and
everything else fell back to English — the defect it guarded was a Bengali numeral inside an English
sentence. V14 translated the homepage into all 31 markets, so a Bengali reader correctly sees ২০০, and the
old assertion would now have been asserting the defect's mirror image.

**That test then found a real bug.** `COPY_LOCALES` in `koreanasha-copy.tsx` still read `['ko','ru','en']`,
so `copyLocale('bn')` fell through to English and the Bengali sentence rendered a Latin numeral. It is now
derived from `TARGET_LOCALES` rather than typed out, which is the whole reason it went stale.

## Gates verified against the defect they exist for

A gate that has never failed is a gate nobody has tested.

- **`qa:marquee`** — the V13 track `gap` was reintroduced; it reported "off by 20.00px" on all three rows
  (exactly half the 40 px gap) and exited 1. Restored, it passes.
- **`qa:composition`** — V13 recorded that it exits 1 on the reintroduced defect. Removing the `.kn`
  workaround before the root-cause fix landed reproduced the full V13 failure (24 assertions across 5 widths),
  which is how the fix was confirmed to be doing the work rather than the workaround.
- **`v14-merge`'s mixed-script check** — caught Russian in a Chinese string and Korean in a Japanese one in
  the first batch it ran on.
- **`v14-merge`'s numbering-system check** — added after the Arabic page was found carrying ١٠٠٪ in its prose
  beside a university count rendered as 200. CLDR's default numbering system for `ar` is **Latin**, which is
  not the obvious answer and is not something a translator writing digits by hand can know. The rule is one
  page, one numbering system, and the formatted figures win because they are the ones that cannot be
  hand-edited. Every archived batch was re-run against the full check set afterwards and all pass.

## Performance

Initial JS is unchanged: no animation library was added. The motion system is CSS transitions plus one
`IntersectionObserver`, which is the brief's own instruction not to add a dependency merely to fade elements.

Marketing CSS fell 210 → 197 KB: the deleted eyebrow layer, the deleted `/credits` page, the deleted mobile
carousel and its focus-ring rules, and the removed `.kn` ancestor on 19 selectors.

Above-the-fold image bytes are unchanged — the hero is the same owner-supplied photograph in the same three
crops. The marquee's 23 crests are 337 KB gzipped between them and are not lazy-loaded, deliberately: a lazy
crest in a moving track pops in mid-loop and leaves a hole.

Layout stability: the crests carry intrinsic `width`/`height`, the reveal system animates only `transform`,
`opacity` and a bounded `clip-path`, and the marquee runs on its own compositor layer via `translate3d`.
Nothing reserves zero space and then grows.

> **Not measured in this pass, and not claimed:** LCP and CLS were not re-measured under a throttled mobile
> profile. V13 recorded 1.97 s phone LCP; V14's hero is the same image with the same `fetchPriority="high"`
> and one added 1.4 s CSS transform, so a material regression is unlikely — but "unlikely" is not a
> measurement, and §115 carries it as outstanding.

# 115. V14 Launch Readiness & Remaining Dependencies

`npm run release:check` — unchanged from V13 in shape, with one blocker advanced.

| | V13 | V14 |
|---|---|---|
| MARKETING PREVIEW | FAIL, 2 blockers | FAIL, 2 blockers |
| CLOSED BETA | FAIL, 10 blockers | FAIL, 10 blockers |
| COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION | FAIL, 25 blockers | FAIL, 25 blockers |

**Advanced:** "The company exists in the product" went from **10 of 10** unconfigured legal fields to **8 of
10**. The owner supplied five values; five more are needed.

## What V14 added to the owner's queue

### Five legal fields, deliberately left null

The owner supplied 대표이사 유재희, 사업부문 남우준, support@talkhangyul.com, 403-87-03380 and
제2026-서울도봉-0542호. All five are configured and on the footer of every page. These are **not** inferred:

| Field | Why it is still null |
|---|---|
| `legalNameKo` (상호) | "한귤" is the brand. The registered company name was not supplied and is not the same thing. |
| `addressKo` | A 통신판매업 number encodes the filing office (서울도봉), not an address. Deriving one would be an invention. |
| `privacyOfficerName` / `privacyOfficerEmail` | 남우준 was given as **사업부문**, a different role. Brief Part 49 rules out the assumption by name, and naming someone to a statutory data-protection role they were not appointed to is a false public filing. |
| `policyAnnouncedOn` / `policyEffectiveOn` | Dates on which the owner publishes. |
| `governingLaw` / `jurisdiction` | Agreed wording, not a default. |

Until they exist, privacy §10 and terms art. 15 are **omitted**, never placeheld. `v12-legal.test.ts` asserts
both halves: the supplied values are byte-exact, and every other required field is still reported missing.

### The 32nd market

`apps/flags` holds 31 assets. If a 32nd market was intended, **its flag was not delivered**, and only the
owner can say which country. Nothing was invented to reach the number.

### The two market lists (see §107)

Nepal, Myanmar and Pakistan have recruitment research and no flag asset, so they are not in the presented
market set and read the public homepage in English. Nineteen presented markets have no recruitment research
behind them yet.

Neither is a defect this pass could fix: adding a flag means inventing an owner asset, and commissioning
research is a business decision. Both lists are now in `packages/i18n/src/markets.ts`, `marketGap()` computes
the difference, and `npm run qa:locales` prints it on every run. **What the owner decides** is whether to
supply flag assets for the three, commission research for some of the nineteen, or leave the shape as it is.

### Commissioned photography — the largest new dependency

This is the constraint that shaped §109 and it is worth stating as a number: **Hangyul holds one licensed
Korean campus photograph for 425 institutions.**

| Allowed source (brief Part 35) | Assets held |
|---|--:|
| Hangyul-owned photographs | 2 |
| Owner-authorised assets | 0 |
| **Commercial, licensed without required attribution** | **0** |
| CC0 / public domain | 9 |

The empty row is the fix. CC0 sourcing has been pushed about as far as it goes — the attribution-free pool
for Korean campus photography is thin, and most of what is genuinely aspirational on Commons is CC BY, which
the owner's "no visible credits" requirement rules out. Three things stay unfinished until there is licensed
imagery, and all three are data, not code:

1. the directory thumbnail (built, removed, ready to return);
2. Yonsei's and Kyung Hee's campus photographs (removed, both were CC BY);
3. a real gallery for the 23 marquee universities — the brief asks for 1 hero + 3–6 supporting images each;
   one university has two.

### Translation still outstanding

| | |
|---|---|
| University directory + detail (`v12.*`, 225 keys) | 29 markets |
| Privacy policy and terms | deliberately excluded until a legally-competent reviewer signs off per market |
| Human review | **no locale is `HUMAN_REVIEWED`**, and none is presented as one |

### University trademark permission

Unresolved, unchanged, still a `release:check` blocker. Removing the visible disclaimer (Part 4) changed the
page, not the position.

## Outstanding from this pass

- **LCP/CLS not re-measured** under a throttled mobile profile (§114).
- **Previously unaudited surfaces** — the student application, the agency student workspace, the essay editor,
  HQ and the three native apps were **not** audited in this pass. They are listed in §116.
- **The running dev server needs a restart** to pick up the vite config change (§113).

# 116. V14 Final Hostile Audit

Written as someone who dislikes the product and is looking for the seam.

## Where it is genuinely better

The marquee seam, the dead logos, the Yonsei white box, the stacked rectangles, the mobile carousel, the
bottom-anchored hero, the three pale cards, the photo credits and the research-bibliography page are all gone,
and each is gone because a mechanism changed rather than because a value was nudged. Every one of those has a
gate behind it that was tested against the defect.

## Where it is still weak, and nobody should pretend otherwise

**1 · The university pages are still mostly text.** This is the big one. 424 of 425 institutions have no
photograph, so for all but one the "could I be there?" question is answered by a typographic header, a facts
table and a list of sources. The structure for photography exists; the photography does not. **The brief's
test — "the photographs should make someone imagine 'I could live there'" — is passed on the homepage and
failed on the directory.**

**2 · UNIST is still the odd one out.** It is the only solid dark tile in a band of twenty-two line-art
seals, and putting it on white made it more prominent, not less. The decision not to recolour someone else's
trademark is right; the result is still a crest that draws the eye for the wrong reason.

**3 · The directory is a text list.** Part 53 asked for it to feel like a place. It feels like a very good
list. The thumbnail was built and pulled because the data made it worse.

**4 · "한귤이 보장합니다".** The owner's own copy says Hangyul *guarantees* a successful student life, and it
is now in 31 languages. It is translated as a claim about support rather than about admission, which is the
most honest reading available — but the strongest sentence on the page is still a guarantee, and
`docs/LEGAL_DEPENDENCIES.md` treats guarantee language as a representation risk. That is the owner's copy and
the owner's call; it should be a conscious one.

**5 · Five of the 31 markets get an English directory behind a fully translated homepage.** Every market
does, in fact. A reader who switches to Vietnamese gets a Vietnamese homepage and an English university page —
which is *visibly* a half-finished localization in a way that an all-English site is not.

**6 · The hero is one photograph.** Every visitor in every market sees the same campus. It is the owner's
asset and it is a good one; it is also the entirety of the site's photographic identity above the fold.

**7 · Not audited at all.** The student application, the agency student workspace, the essay editor, Hangyul
HQ and the three native apps. Brief Part 61 asked for them and this pass did not get to them. They are
unchanged from V13, which means V13's audit gap is now V14's as well. **Stated, not buried.**

## Questions asked of each surface

- *Where does this still feel like a template?* The FAQ accordion. It is ten native `<details>` in a stack —
  correct, accessible, fast, and visually the most generic part of the page.
- *Where does a section start too abruptly?* Nowhere on the homepage; one boundary remains and it is the
  hero's, deliberately. The university detail page's typographic header still begins fairly flatly.
- *Where does a component disappear?* No longer the value section. The FAQ items are low-contrast on the
  warm surface — readable, quiet, arguably too quiet.
- *Where does mobile still feel like squeezed desktop?* Nowhere on the homepage. The directory's map + list
  at 320 px is tight.
- *Where is language switching buried?* Nowhere: header pill (desktop and phone), the mobile menu, the
  footer, and the URL.
- *Where does animation feel gratuitous?* Nothing survived that test — but the honest answer is that the
  motion system is *restrained to the point of being invisible*, which is what the brief asked for and is
  also hard to distinguish from not having done it.
- *Where is animation missing where continuity would improve?* Between the services and the FAQ there is a
  long quiet stretch with nothing but whitespace carrying the transition.

## The thing most likely to be wrong

The translations. Thirty-one markets of marketing copy produced by one model reading its own output against a
rubric, with no native speaker in the loop. The mechanical checks are real — interpolations, markup, script
mixing, English leakage, overflow at four widths — and they caught genuine defects. **None of them can tell
whether a sentence sounds like a person.**

Three of the 29 non-source locales had a visible error in their first draft that only a reader of that
language would have caught: Russian inside a Chinese sentence, Korean inside a Japanese one, and Arabic prose
written in Arabic-Indic digits beside figures the product renders in Latin. Each was caught by a check added
*because* of it, which is the honest reading of that number — it is evidence of what the checks now cover, not
evidence that nothing else is wrong. `SYNTHETIC_REVIEWED` is the correct label and it should be read as a
warning.

# 117. V15 Business-Model Reconciliation Audit

Written **before** any code changed, against two inputs: the owner's `한귤 UNIV_20261019.hwpx` business plan
and this report. Where they disagree about the commercial product, the plan wins.

## What the plan actually says

The plan is not a price change. It is a change of **what the product is**. §2 of the plan states it directly:
the old curriculum differentiated plans by *consultation length and number of recommended universities*, and
the business is moving from 단순 정보 제공 to 실제 입학 지원과 행정 절차 관리 — from telling a student what to do
to doing the administrative work with them. Everything below follows from that sentence.

Three retail plans, one currency, no free tier:

| | 베이직 BASIC | 올인원 ALL-IN-ONE | 프리미엄 PREMIUM |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 판매가 | **249,000원** | **499,000원** | **849,000원** |
| 상담 시간 | 30분 | 60분 | 90분 |
| 추천 대학 | 최대 3곳 | 최대 5곳 | 최대 7곳 |
| 지원 학교 (관리) | 미포함 | 최대 2곳 | 최대 3곳 |
| 서류 검토 | 체크리스트 | 기본 검토 | 집중 검토 |
| 에세이 첨삭 | 미포함 | 1회 | 2회 |
| 면접 준비 | 미포함 | 별도 상품 | 모의 면접 1회 |
| 비자 준비 | 기본 안내 | 서류 준비 지원 | 집중 준비 및 일정 관리 |
| 기숙사 지원 | 정보 안내 | 신청 일정 관리 | 신청 지원 및 대안 안내 |
| 입국 후 지원 | 미포함 | 기본 정보 제공 | 30일 지원 |

Plus, from §3-1, one item the table omits: Basic includes **후속 상담 1회 (20분 이내)**. It is in the
entitlement set because it is a countable promise.

§9 confirms 올인원 as 주력 상품. §6-2 lists the optional paid services. §8 forbids guaranteeing admission,
scholarship or visa, and requires 외부 비용 (전형료, 등록금, 번역·공증·아포스티유, 비자 수수료, 숙소) to be
separated from the service fee. §3-4's footnote adds that visa work is provided only within what the law
allows, with registered specialists engaged where representation is required.

## Everything in the repository that contradicts it

| Where | What is there now | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `server/app/seed/run.py:seed_products` | `FREE_EXPLORER` (free), `APPLICATION_SUPPORT`, `PREMIUM_SUCCESS` | **Replaced.** Three different products with three different names, scopes and prices. |
| same | USD 199 / 699 default prices | **Removed.** The plan prices in KRW. USD was never approved. |
| same | `country_code` rows for `KR` (290,000 / 990,000) and `VN` (4.9M / 16.9M VND) | **Removed.** The plan states one retail price per plan, not regional pricing. Keeping a VND row would mean the homepage and a Vietnamese student's checkout disagree. |
| same | `FREE_EXPLORER` with no price at all | **Removed.** There is no free plan. What used to be "free" — search the directory, save universities, check basic eligibility — is the public site and `/start`, which stay free *and unpurchased*. A zero-price product in the catalogue made browsing look like a plan. |
| `ServiceProduct.includes_agency_assignment` / `includes_essay_review` / `max_applications` | three ad-hoc scope columns | **Superseded** by a structured entitlement set. `max_applications` meant "applications the student may create", which is not the plan's 지원 학교 최대 N곳 (applications Hangyul *manages*). Two different promises under one column. |
| `ServiceProduct.features: string[]` | marketing feature codes driving `whoDoes()` in the student UI | **Kept for display, demoted as authority.** Scope now comes from entitlements; a string list cannot answer "how many rounds are left". |
| `apps/student-web/src/pages/Services.tsx` | a 6-row × 3-plan "who does this" matrix derived from `features` | **Rebuilt** around plan + allowance + remaining. |
| seeds `extra_10_personas.py:117`, `run.py:584` | persona orders hard-coded to `PREMIUM_SUCCESS` / `APPLICATION_SUPPORT` | **Remapped** to the new codes, with a realistic Basic/All-in-One/Premium mix. |
| `server/tests/*`, `e2e/*` (8 files) | `product_code: "PREMIUM_SUCCESS"` | **Remapped** to `PREMIUM`. |
| `scripts/i18n/v9-todo/*.json` (43 files) | `services.APPLICATION_SUPPORT.name` etc. | **Left alone** — these are an archived to-do corpus, not shipped locale files. Noted so a future grep does not mistake them for live copy. |
| `docs/PRODUCT.md`, `docs/SERVICE_BLUEPRINT.md`, `docs/ADMISSION_SUCCESS.md`, `Terms.tsx` §8 commentary | the old three-package model | **Updated.** |
| `scripts/qa/v13-release-check.mjs` → `approved_prices` | FAIL, keyed on `ServicePrice.is_demo` | **Moves to PASS** once the new prices are seeded with `is_demo=False`, because they are now approved business inputs. This is the one blocker this pass legitimately closes. |
| `refund_matrix` blocker | FAIL | **Stays FAIL.** The plan (§7, 1단계) lists 서비스 계약서 및 환불 규정 마련 as work still to do. No refund policy is invented. |

## The entitlement model

The brief's requirement — "do NOT represent scope only as marketing strings" — and its warning against dozens
of boolean columns point the same way: **one structured JSON entitlement set per product**, next to the
`features` list that already lives in JSON on the same table.

```
entitlements = {
  consultation_minutes:        30 | 60 | 90,
  follow_up_consultations:     1 | null,              # null = ongoing staff support, not a counted allowance
  max_recommended_institutions: 3 | 5 | 7,
  max_managed_applications:    0 | 2 | 3,
  document_review:             CHECKLIST | STANDARD | INTENSIVE,
  essay_review_rounds:         0 | 1 | 2,
  mock_interviews:             0 | 0 | 1,
  interview_preparation:       false | false | true,
  visa_support:                GUIDANCE | DOCUMENT_PREP | INTENSIVE,
  dormitory_support:           INFORMATION | SCHEDULE | APPLICATION,
  post_arrival_support_days:   0 | 0 | 30,
  settlement_support:          NONE | INFORMATION | FULL,
  pre_arrival_orientation:     false | false | true,
  personal_roadmap:            false | false | true,
  priority_response:           false | false | true,
}
```

Three deliberate decisions inside that shape:

1. **Levels, not booleans, where the plan describes a level.** 서류 검토 is 체크리스트 / 기본 검토 / 집중 검토 —
   three different promises, not one promise switched on. A boolean `includes_document_review` would make
   Basic look like it gets nothing when the plan says it gets a checklist.
2. **`null` means "not a counted allowance", and is not the same as 0.** All-in-One's follow-up consultations
   are not limited to a number; they are 담당자 이메일·메신저 문의 대응. Encoding that as `0` would make the
   console tell a counselor they have used up something that was never rationed.
3. **Usage is derived, never counted into a column.** `used` comes from the records that prove the work
   happened — completed essay review rounds, applications under management, recorded consultations. A
   counter would drift the first time a review was deleted or a case reassigned, and a drifted counter is
   worse than none because staff act on it.

**Add-ons raise a limit; they do not create a second plan.** `ServiceAddOn` records a counselor-offered,
student-approved extra (추가 첨삭, 추가 지원 학교, 모의 면접, …) as a delta on one entitlement key. Effective
limit = plan entitlement + approved deltas. This is what makes §6-2 of the plan implementable without the
homepage growing a fourth card.

## What stays exactly as it is

- **Payments.** §23 of the brief and §115 of this report agree: the provider is a demo provider. New
  approved prices do not make checkout production-ready, and nothing in this pass pretends otherwise.
- **The concierge `ServiceCase` model** (pickups, dormitory, housing, residence card). It already is the
  post-admission delivery record Premium's settlement entitlement needs. V15 connects it to entitlements
  rather than building a settlement module beside it.
- **`?lang=` as the locale authority.** The plan handoff adds `plan`, it does not change how language works.

# 118. V15 Pricing UX Strategy

## Where it goes, and why exactly there

The homepage is five movements: hero → universities → why → services → FAQ, with the layout's closing band
after. The pricing section becomes the **fifth of six**, between 서비스 and FAQ.

That is not just the brief's suggestion, it is the only position that reads. The services section ends by
telling a visitor what Hangyul does across the whole journey; the FAQ opens with TOPIK and documents. Price
is the question that sits exactly between "what do you do" and "what do I need to know before asking" — and
§116 recorded that this boundary is *the one long quiet stretch on the page with nothing carrying the
transition*. The section the page was missing goes where the page already had a gap.

## The ten-second test

A visitor must leave with three answers: what it costs, which plan is probably theirs, what upgrading buys.
Everything in the design below exists to serve one of those and nothing else.

## Visual design

Three cards in one row at desktop, in plan order — Basic, All-in-One, Premium. White editorial surface, the
same `Band` as every other section, no gradient block, no colour wash. This is the V14 page with one more
movement, not a pricing template pasted into it.

Hierarchy, in the order the eye should take them:

- **ALL-IN-ONE** — the emphasised card: a 1px brand-ink border instead of a hairline, slightly deeper
  elevation, the 추천 label as a small text chip. It is the plan the business runs on (§9) and it must be
  obvious without a banner.
- **BASIC** — quiet white card, hairline border.
- **PREMIUM** — quiet card, the same weight as Basic. Premium is not the aspiration being sold; it is the
  high-touch option for a specific need. Making it louder than All-in-One would contradict the plan.

Explicitly **not** used: BEST/인기 ribbons, strike-through anchors, "원래 ₩X", countdown, glow, savings
percentages, neon. The business plan has none of those and the brief forbids all of them.

Each card carries **five** lines, one CTA, and nothing else:

| | BASIC | ALL-IN-ONE | PREMIUM |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 맞춤 진단 상담 30분 | 베이직 전체 포함 | 올인원 전체 포함 |
| 2 | 최대 3곳 추천 | 최대 5곳 비교 | 최대 7곳 비교 |
| 3 | 조건·학비·일정 비교 | 최대 2곳 지원 관리 | 최대 3곳 지원 관리 |
| 4 | 기본 서류 체크리스트 | 서류 검토·입학처 커뮤니케이션 | 첨삭 2회 + 모의 면접 |
| 5 | 비자 준비 절차 안내 | 자기소개서 첨삭 1회 | 기숙사·입국·30일 정착 지원 |

Exclusions are **not** on the card. Basic's four 미포함 items live in the comparison disclosure, which is
where a reader who is deciding between plans goes, not where a reader who is deciding whether to care goes.

## The comparison disclosure

One control under the three cards — **플랜 자세히 비교하기** — expanding in place to the owner's own 비교표:
the ten rows above plus 후속 상담 and the Basic exclusions. No second page, no drawer, no modal. It is a
`<details>`-backed accordion so it works without JavaScript, is keyboard-correct by construction, and is
addressable for the QA gate.

## The external-cost note

One quiet line under the section, body-small, muted, no icon, no border, no tone colour: Hangyul's service
fee excludes 대학 전형료 · 등록금 · 번역·공증·아포스티유 · 비자 수수료 · 숙소비. Verbatim in substance from the
plan's own footnote. It is a transparency statement, not a disclaimer box — a scary legal callout under a
price is itself a conversion problem and the brief rules it out.

## CTA and handoff

Each card's button starts that plan: 베이직으로 시작 / 올인원으로 시작 / 프리미엄으로 시작.

The handoff must preserve three things through an auth boundary:

```
marketing  →  student app  /start?plan=all_in_one&lang=vi
           →  (register or log in; `next` carries the whole query)
           →  /services?plan=all_in_one   — that plan pre-selected
```

Mechanically: `prepareAction()` gains a plan argument; `?lang=` keeps working exactly as it does today; the
student app persists `plan` across the login round-trip (it already carries `next`), and `Services` reads it
to pre-select. No new cookie, no new storage key, no server state for an anonymous visitor.

**The CTA does not open a form or a payment.** The product principle from V13 is unchanged: MARKETING → AUTH
→ STUDENT PLATFORM → SERVICE SELECTION. The button says "start", and starting means arriving in the platform
with that plan chosen.

## Responsive

Tested at 320 / 360 / 390 / 430 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 / 1440 / 1728.

- **≥1024** three columns.
- **768–1023** three columns would give each card ~230px of text; they stack to one column instead. A squeezed
  three-across is the failure mode the brief names.
- **<768** one column, and the order changes to **ALL-IN-ONE → BASIC → PREMIUM**. On a phone the first card is
  the only card most people see before deciding whether to keep scrolling, and the recommended plan has to be
  it. Desktop keeps price order because all three are visible at once and ascending price is how a row of
  plans is read. The mobile reorder is CSS `order` on the same DOM, so the reading order for a screen reader
  and the tab order follow the visual order.

## Copy

Korean is the canonical semantic source (§30 of the brief). Nothing in the section says 혁신적인, 차원이 다른,
압도적인, 무조건 합격, 100% 성공 or 완벽 보장 — and nothing says 보장 at all, because §8 of the business plan
rules out guaranteeing admission, scholarship or visa. The section sells by being legible.

## One source of truth

`packages/types/src/plans.ts` holds the canonical plan manifest — codes, KRW amounts, entitlements, the five
card lines' i18n keys. The server seed imports the same data through a generated `shared/plans.json`, the
public API serves it from the database, and the student app reads the API. Marketing renders from the
manifest rather than the API because a public page must render when the API is down — and `qa:pricing`
asserts all three agree. A price that appears in three places and is typed once is the only version of this
that survives a change.

# 119. V15 Agency Operations Audit

## The four questions

Everything in this section is judged against the brief's north star: can a counselor answer, immediately —
(1) who needs me now, (2) why are they blocked, (3) is this application ready enough to submit, (4) what
service have we promised this student?

Today's console answers 1 and 2 well, 3 partially, and **4 not at all**. That is the gap this pass closes.

## What is already right and will not be touched

- **Navigation stays at seven**: Today · Students · Review · Applications · Messages · Insights · Manage. No
  item is added. §77 earned that reduction and §94 defended it.
- **Today is a ranked work queue, not KPI tiles.** `WorkQueue` stays the dominant element and stays first.
- **The four state chips** (urgent / mine / waiting-student / waiting-university) stay. §94.3 and the V13
  200-case simulation established why they replaced nine work-type chips; adding plan as a tenth chip would
  undo that and is explicitly rejected below.
- **`CaseStrip`** already answers why-blocked / next-action / waiting-on / deadline / owner in five cells.

## Gap 1 — the plan is invisible everywhere

A counselor today cannot see, anywhere in the console, what the student bought. `StudentServices` renders
concierge service *cases*, not the purchased plan. The consequences at 200 cases are operational, not
cosmetic: a counselor can spend a review round that does not exist, promise a dormitory application under a
Basic plan, or treat a Premium case as routine.

**Fix, as metadata rather than UI.** Per brief Part 27, three additions, no new page and no new card:

- **Today queue row** — a compact plan mark on the existing row. Not a badge row; one short token where the
  stage already sits. It appears because it changes what the counselor may promise, which is the brief's
  own test for showing it.
- **`CaseStrip`** — a sixth cell, **PLAN**, beside stage/why/next/deadline/owner. The brief's required first
  viewport is then complete in one strip the counselor already reads.
- **A compact scope panel** inside the workspace Overview — plan name · price · the three or four allowances
  that are actually rationed, as `used / limit`, and any approved add-on. Operational typography, not a
  promotional card: `올인원 · ₩499,000 / 지원 관리 1 / 2 / 자소서 첨삭 1 / 1 사용 / 상담 60분 제공`.

## Gap 2 — nothing enforces scope, so nothing can be promised reliably

There is no entitlement check anywhere. Adding a third managed application to an All-in-One case succeeds
silently.

**Fix.** A server-side entitlement guard on the actions that consume an allowance, returning a typed refusal
the UI can read, plus a client-side pre-check so the counselor sees the state *before* acting rather than
after. The message is the brief's: **현재 플랜에 포함되지 않은 지원입니다**, followed by the one legitimate next
step — **추가 서비스 요청** (create an add-on offer) or an internal escalation where the agency absorbs it.
Never a silent block, never an internal error, and never a locked control with no explanation.

**No dark pattern** is a design constraint with teeth here: the add-on offer is a *request* that the student
approves, the price is shown before approval, and declining it leaves the case exactly as it was.

## Gap 3 — application readiness is computed but not said

`services/readiness.py:application_readiness` exists. The workspace shows status badges and a blocker list
derived in `useBlockers`, but no single sentence answering "can this be submitted".

**Fix.** One concise readiness state per active application, rendered as a sentence on the application row
itself: 제출 가능 / 제출 전 2가지 확인 필요 / 대학 회신 대기 / 학생 서류 대기. Underneath, the **named blockers**
— 성적증명서 번역본 필요, 여권 영문명과 지원서 이름 불일치, 학업계획서 전공 선택 이유 보강 필요, TOPIK 증빙 필요.

**No scores.** Not 92점, not 87% 합격확률, not an AI Admission Score. §3 of the benchmark records why: the one
competitor that ships a confidence score ships it as nationality-configurable risk, and a number is
unactionable where a named blocker is a task.

## Gap 4 — writing review entitlement is invisible to both sides

The business plan makes 첨삭 a counted, priced thing: Basic 0, All-in-One 1, Premium 2. Today the essay
workflow has no concept of a round, so neither staff nor student can see what is left.

**Fix.** A review *round* becomes the countable unit, remaining entitlement is shown in the writing review
workspace and in the student's own essay view, and starting a round beyond the allowance takes the Gap-2
path. The review workspace keeps its existing dimensions and gains the plan's own checks — prompt coverage,
university/program name correctness, motivation clarity, academic-background relevance, study-plan coherence,
career-goal coherence, unsupported claims, length limit, reused content, language quality — as a reviewer
checklist, **not** as generated prose. The brief's rule stands: the goal is a stronger application in the
student's own voice, not an essay that reads as machine-written.

## Gap 5 — interview and settlement have no home

Premium includes 면접 준비 + 모의 면접 1회 and a 30-day settlement package. Neither exists operationally.

**Fix, contextually, with no new navigation.** Interview becomes a record inside the application workflow
(scheduled / completed / notes / remaining entitlement), surfacing only when the application reaches an
interview stage or the plan includes preparation. Settlement reuses the existing concierge `ServiceCase`
types and activates **progressively** — dormitory at offer, pre-arrival orientation at visa, the 30-day
items at arrival. Nothing appears before it matters, and nothing adds a sidebar entry.

## Insights — four visuals, hard cap

Current `Performance` is kept but reduced to exactly the four the brief allows:

1. **Counselor workload / capacity** — open cases per counselor against their caseload, not a vanity total.
2. **Case ageing / SLA risk** — the distribution that tells a manager where the queue is rotting.
3. **Application quality** — first-pass complete rate, average correction loops, essay revision loops,
   additional-document request rate, on-time submission rate. Every definition stated in the UI, every rate
   suppressed below `MIN_N`.
4. **Service delivery / plan utilization** — Premium cases over capacity, unused included consultations,
   scope overruns, cases approaching a service deadline.

Visual 4 is a manager's view and stays on Insights. It is **not** added to Today: the benchmark records that
putting leadership metrics on the practitioner's home screen is the failure mode of this product category,
and Part 8 of the brief forbids it independently.

## What will be removed

- `ServiceProduct.max_applications` as the application cap in the student UI — superseded by
  `max_managed_applications`, which is a different and correctly-named promise.
- The `whoDoes()` feature-string matrix in the student service page — a six-row inference over marketing
  strings, replaced by the plan's own table.
- Any Insights visual beyond the four above.

## What will deliberately **not** be added

- A plan filter chip on Today. Prioritisation is by operational risk; the brief is explicit that a Premium
  student's priority-response rule must not bury another student's deadline.
- A fifth tab in the student workspace.
- A billing or revenue view on the counselor's home.
- An "upgrade this student" promotional surface anywhere in the console.

# 120. V15 University Intelligence Audit

## The 15-second test

Can an admissions director understand what requires action, where applicants come from, how good the
applications are, and what happens after admission — in fifteen seconds? Today: the first two, partially.

## What is already right

- **Navigation stays at six**: Overview · Applicants · Programs · Messages · Analytics · Manage.
- **The ranked decision queue stays.** §94.4 killed the KPI tile grid for a reason that scale confirmed:
  four fixed tiles put a 1 next to a 513 and rank by nothing. Not returning to it.
- **Every number already drills to its records**, and `MIN_N` already suppresses rates on small populations.

## The measured problem

The Overview is ~2.1 screens at 1440 and the brief wants 1.0–1.5, *while adding three sections*. That is only
possible by deciding what the Overview is for and removing what it is not.

## Target: exactly five sections

| § | Section | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Needs decision** — compact ranked queue, categories from live data | exists, compressed |
| 2 | **Admissions funnel** — Submitted → Reviewed → Offered → Accepted → Tuition paid → Visa → Arrived → Enrolled, with step conversion and the **largest meaningful drop named** | exists, extended |
| 3 | **Source market** — country × applications / offers / enrollments, horizontal bars | **new on Overview** (exists in Analytics) |
| 4 | **Application quality** — first-pass complete · additional documents requested · median review time · on-time submission | **new** |
| 5 | **Post-admission** — Offer → Visa → Arrival → Enrollment | **new on Overview** (exists as Analytics outcomes) |

### What comes off the Overview to pay for it

- **"Waiting on applicants"** stops being its own card. It is the same `useAttention` data as §1, split only
  by who must act, so it folds into the bottom of the decision queue as a quieter second group. One card
  removed, no information lost, and the two can no longer disagree.
- **"Coming up" (intake dates)** moves to **Programs**, which is where intake dates are defined and edited.
  The single nearest deadline stays on the Overview as a sentence in the page header — metadata, not a card,
  per brief Part 27. An admissions director does not lose deadline awareness; they lose a 200px timeline
  widget that duplicates a page one click away.
- The two trailing page notes merge into one line.

### Why §3 and §5 are worth their height

Both come straight out of the benchmark. Volume by country alone is a vanity metric — the director's actual
question is *which markets produce enrolled students*, which needs applications and enrollments on the same
row. And post-admission visibility is the thing the benchmark's strongest competitor built an entire company
on, because email-and-spreadsheet recruitment cannot see it at all.

## Visualisation rule, applied

Every chart carries a question and a decision, recorded in the source. Anything that could not answer both
was cut before implementation:

| Visual | QUESTION | DECISION |
|---|---|---|
| Decision queue | What is waiting on us right now? | Open the largest queue and work it. |
| Funnel + largest drop | Where is this intake losing people? | Fix the step that is losing them. |
| Source market | Which markets produce enrolled students? | Where to spend recruitment effort next cycle. |
| Application quality | Are the applications we receive workable? | Which channel or agency to talk to. |
| Post-admission | Do our offers become enrolled students? | Where to intervene between offer and arrival. |
| ~~Programme demand donut~~ | *(cut)* — "which programmes are popular" with no decision attached | — |
| ~~Decision-time gauge~~ | *(cut)* — a single aggregate number with no population | — |

Preferred encodings: horizontal bars, funnels, lines, compact matrices. No donuts, no pies, no rainbow, no
3D, no gradient fills, no giant legends.

## Analytics — organised by question, not by chart

The Analytics page's tabs become questions, with the existing visuals redistributed under them:

- **Recruitment** — which countries produce enrolled students? which programmes attract demand?
- **Application quality** — which channels send complete applications? where are additional-document
  requests concentrated?
- **Agency quality** — which agency delivers complete, timely, well-prepared applications? Ranked on
  completeness and timeliness, **never on raw offer rate**, with sample size shown and country/programme/intake
  context available, because an agency sending ten strong applicants to one easy programme is not better
  than one sending two hundred across twelve.
- **Post-admission** — which admitted students progress through visa, arrival, enrollment, and later
  retention/graduation **where real data exists** (and nothing rendered where it does not).

## Drilldown and reconciliation

Vietnam · 23 enrolled → the 23 applicants in that cohort. Overview, Analytics and the applicant list must
return the same number for the same population, and the V15 university gate asserts exactly that rather than
trusting it.

## University must not see retail pricing

Basic/All-in-One/Premium and their prices are a Hangyul–student commercial relationship. Nothing in the
University Console gains plan or price information, and the V15 gate asserts no plan code or KRW plan amount
appears in any university surface.

# 121. V15 Competitive Operations Benchmark

Full document: **`docs/qa/v15/COMPETITIVE_OPERATIONS_AUDIT.md`** — ApplyBoard, IDP FastLane/Client Portal,
Enroly (CAS Shield / Apply), Cialfo, Leverage Edu, plus the admissions-analytics practice literature, each
recorded as TASK / WHAT THEY DO WELL / WHAT FEELS COMPLEX / WHAT HANGYUL SHOULD LEARN / WHAT HANGYUL SHOULD
NOT COPY.

Reviewed 19 Oct 2026 from vendor sites, help centres, partner stories and trade press. **No product trial,
no login, nothing measured.** Vendor numbers are recorded as vendor claims.

The nine design decisions it actually changed are tabulated at the end of that document. The three things it
could not resolve are recorded there too, and matter more than the things it confirmed:

1. **No competitor publicly documents a writing-review workflow.** §12 of the brief is designed from the
   owner's own 첨삭 definition, without precedent.
2. **No competitor publishes an entitlement model.** The plan-limit mechanism in V15 is derived entirely
   from the owner's 플랜별 비교표.
3. **Whether any of these products is actually fast in the hand is not knowable from outside**, so nothing
   here supports a claim that Hangyul's console is better than theirs.

The two strongest negative findings — Enroly's region-configurable enrolment confidence score, and
ApplyBoard's continuous quality scoring of its own advisors — are both things this product category reaches
for and both things V15 refuses. They are the reason `DO NOT USE FAKE SCORES` is implemented as a gate and
not just a principle.

# 122. V15 Simplification Plan

The brief's standard: **LESS UI · BETTER DECISIONS · FASTER OPERATIONS · STRONGER APPLICATIONS · CLEARER
DATA.** This pass adds exactly one new section to the public site and must pay for everything else by
removal. Written before implementation so it can be checked against afterwards.

## Net UI change, committed in advance

| Surface | Added | Removed |
|---|---|---|
| Marketing | 1 section (pricing + its disclosure) | 0 |
| Student | 0 pages | the `whoDoes()` 6×3 inference matrix |
| Agency | 0 pages, 0 nav items, 0 tabs, 0 cards | Insights visuals beyond four; `max_applications` as a cap |
| University | 0 pages, 0 nav items; 3 Overview sections | 2 Overview cards (waiting-on, coming-up), 1 page note, 2 analytics visuals |

Everything else in this pass is **metadata on a row, a contextual action, a disclosure, or a filtered view** —
the four alternatives Part 27 demands be preferred over a new page, nav item, card or module.

## Applied, decision by decision

| Wanted | Rejected shape | Chosen shape |
|---|---|---|
| Counselor sees the plan | plan column, plan card, plan tab | one token on the existing row; one cell on the existing strip |
| Plan allowances | entitlement dashboard | compact panel inside Overview, only the rationed items |
| Scope refusal | disabled control | explanatory message + the one legitimate next step |
| Add-ons | add-on catalogue page / homepage cards | contextual offer inside a case when the allowance is exhausted |
| Readiness | score, gauge, progress ring | one sentence + named blockers |
| Interview | interview module | a record inside the application workflow |
| Settlement | six sidebar entries | existing concierge cases, activated progressively by stage |
| Plan utilization | tile on Today | one of four Insights visuals |
| University source market | donut + legend | horizontal bars, applications and enrollments on one row |
| University dates | timeline card on Overview | nearest date in the header; full list on Programs |
| Comparison table | second page / modal | one in-place disclosure |

## The removals, stated as losses

Honest accounting, because every removal costs somebody something:

- **"Coming up" off the Overview** costs a director the at-a-glance 150-day deadline list. They get the
  nearest one in the header and the full list on Programs.
- **"Waiting on applicants" folded in** costs it its own heading. It gains being unable to disagree with the
  queue above it.
- **`whoDoes()` gone** costs the student the "who does this part" framing. They gain the plan's real table
  with real numbers instead of an inference over marketing strings.
- **Two analytics visuals cut** cost nothing anyone could act on, which is why they went.

## What this pass will deliberately **not** add, even though it could

- A fourth plan, a trial, or a free tier — the plan defines three.
- An upsell surface anywhere in the student product outside a relevant, exhausted-allowance moment.
- Any pricing widget on Student Home.
- Any retail price in the University Console.
- A refund matrix. The business plan says one must be prepared; it does not exist, so it stays a blocker.
- A production payment integration, or any UI that implies one exists.
- Any guarantee of admission, scholarship, visa or outcome.
