# 123. V15 Implementation Log

What changed, file by file, and why. The plan in §§117–122 was written first; this records where the plan
survived contact and where it did not.

## 1 · One source of truth for the commercial model

| | |
|---|---|
| `packages/types/src/plans.ts` | **new.** The manifest: three codes, three KRW amounts, fifteen entitlements each, the comparison rows and the external-cost list. Nothing else in the tree holds a price. |
| `scripts/plans/sync.mjs` | **new.** Generates `shared/plans.json` from it; `--check` fails when the two differ. Imports the TypeScript directly (Node strips the types), so there is no build step and no second copy. |
| `shared/plans.json` | **new, generated.** What the Python seed reads. |
| `server/app/seed/run.py` | `seed_products` no longer *contains* the catalogue; it writes what the manifest gives it, at `is_demo=False`. |

## 2 · The model itself

| | |
|---|---|
| `server/app/models/business.py` | `ServiceProduct` gained `entitlements` (JSON), `name_ko`, `is_recommended`, and lost `includes_agency_assignment`, `includes_essay_review`, `max_applications`. New `ServiceAddOn`. |
| `server/app/models/enums.py` | New `AddOnStatus` (OFFERED / APPROVED / DECLINED / CANCELLED). |
| `server/app/models/student.py` | `SavedUniversity.source` + `recommended_by_user_id`, so "최대 N곳 추천" is countable rather than asserted. |
| `server/alembic/versions/v15_plans.py` | The migration for all of the above. |
| `server/app/services/entitlements.py` | **new.** Effective limits, derived usage, the typed `OutOfScope` refusal. |
| `server/app/services/app_readiness.py` | **new.** One readiness state and its named blockers, composed from the checklist, the strategy items and the open university requests. No score. |

Three decisions inside the entitlement service, restated because they are the ones that make it
trustworthy: usage is **derived from the records that prove the work**, never counted into a column;
`limit: null` means *not rationed* and is not `0`; and an approved add-on is a **delta on one key**.

## 3 · Where the plan met reality

Four things the plan did not predict, each found by running something rather than by reading code.

**A review round is a pass over the writing, not a review of one document.** The first implementation summed
`EssayReview.review_round` across a student's essays, so a counsellor who returned comments on a statement
*and* a study plan together had spent two of the one round All-in-One sells. The business plan's own wording
is 자기소개서·학업계획서 … 1회 첨삭 — one item covering both. Usage is now the deepest round any single essay
has reached.

**And the guard's arithmetic had to follow.** With that definition, `used + 1 > limit` is wrong: submitting
a *fresh* essay for its first review does not add one to a maximum another essay already set. The first
draft therefore refused a first review on a new document because a different document had been through two
rounds — work the student had paid for. `check()` now takes a `prospective` value and
`essay_round_after()` computes it. **The API suite caught this**, which is the argument for having run it
before writing this section rather than after.

**The demo dataset was seeded under the old model**, so every case was over its new allowance the moment
entitlements existed — three managed applications on an All-in-One that sells two. `extra_96_plans.py`
reconciles it. Its *first* version did so by capping `EssayReview.review_round` down to whatever plan had
been drawn, which quietly destroyed seeded demo states the rest of the product is built on
(`test_seeded_demo_states` caught a "revised" essay that no longer existed). It now works the other way:
**the work is the fact and the plan is what fits it**, with add-ons covering what exceeds even Premium.

**₩ has two crossbars.** Set tight against a digit at display size they run into the numerals and
`₩249,000` reads as struck through — the one sales-page device the brief forbids by name. `formatMoney`
gained a `gap` option that inserts a thin space, built from `Intl.formatToParts` so a locale that puts the
symbol after the number gets the space on the correct side.

## 4 · Marketing

| | |
|---|---|
| `apps/marketing-web/src/pages/home/pricing.tsx` | **new.** The section: three plans, five lines each, one CTA, one `<details>` comparison. Renders from the manifest, not the API, because a public page must paint when the API is down. **Recomposed in V15 b (§129)** — the cards became columns, the table became a grouped matrix, and the external-cost note left this file for the surfaces where a buyer meets it. |
| `apps/marketing-web/src/v15.css` | **new.** All of the above, in the V14 white editorial surface. Rewritten in V15 b. |
| `apps/marketing-web/src/lib/session.ts` | `planAction()` — the handoff. |
| `apps/marketing-web/src/pages/Home.tsx` | Pricing between Services and FAQ: five movements became six. |

Two corrections made by looking at the rendered page rather than the code. The recommended card first grew
taller by adding vertical padding, which pushed its name, price and list out of line with its neighbours —
three plans whose prices sat at three different heights, which reads as a mistake rather than as emphasis;
it now grows *outward* with negative block margin. And two comparison cells did not match the owner's
비교표: 면접 준비 printed "미포함" for All-in-One where the plan says 별도 상품, and 입국 후 지원 printed
"미포함" where it says 기본 정보 제공. Both now read the graded entitlement instead of a count.

## 5 · Student

`Services.tsx` was rebuilt. What it replaced was a 6 × 3 matrix of "who does this part", each cell inferred
by `whoDoes()` from marketing feature strings — a reasonable answer to a question the business no longer
asks. The new plans are defined by *quantities*, and an inference over strings cannot say how many review
rounds are left.

Two states now, and they are not the same screen: **bought** shows the plan, the allowances as `used /
limit`, and any extra the counsellor has offered; **not yet** shows the three plans with the one chosen on
the public site already selected.

`quick.ts` gained `readPlanParam` / `startParams` so `?plan=` survives `/start` → `/register` → `/services`.

## 6 · Agency

Everything here is metadata on something that already existed. **No new page, no new nav item, no new tab.**

| | |
|---|---|
| `components/Plan.tsx` | **new.** `PlanMark` (the row token), `PlanScope` (the workspace panel), `OutOfScopeNote` + `ScopeExhausted` (the refusal and its one next step). |
| `pages/Dashboard.tsx` | The plan token on the Today row, beside the stage. |
| `components/Movement.tsx` | **PLAN** as the case strip's first cell. |
| `pages/StudentWorkspace.tsx` | The scope panel in Overview; `RemainText` → `ReadinessText`. |
| `pages/EssayEditor.tsx` | The remaining 첨삭 allowance in the header metadata row — brief Part 12. A reviewer working the queue never opens the workspace panel, so the allowance has to be where the decision to ask for another revision is actually made. |
| `services/priority.py` | The plan on each queue row — **one query for the page**, and deliberately *not* an input to `rank_key`. |

One thing was **removed**: the purchased-service badge in the workspace header. The case strip below now
carries the plan, translated, beside the four facts it belongs with — so the header badge was the same fact
twice, eight pixels apart, and it printed the English product name on a Korean screen.

## 7 · University

The Overview is five sections. Three are new, and it still had to get shorter.

**Added:** source market (country × applications × enrolments, one bar, horizontal), application quality
(the four facts `PreparationFacts` already computed, moved to where the question is asked), post-admission
(Offer → Visa → Arrival → Enrolment, full width).

**Removed:** the "waiting on applicants" card (same `useAttention` population as the decision queue, folded
into it, and above two kinds it collapses to one line); the intake-dates timeline (moved to **Programs**,
where those dates are defined and edited, with the nearest one in the Overview header as a sentence); the
funnel's three-number summary (it restated the first, fourth and last rows of the table directly beneath
it); one of the two trailing page notes.

**Analytics** went from four chart families to four questions: recruitment · application quality · agency
quality · after admission. The `overview` tab is gone because it held the funnel, which is now section 2 of
the Overview page — the same chart twice, one click apart. `?tab=overview` still resolves, and the unit test
asserts that rather than leaving it to the fallback.

Two corrections from looking at it. The source-market bars rendered as empty tracks, because the first draft
used `--hg-chart-grid` for the application segment on `--hg-surface-subtle` and both resolve to near-white;
they are now two steps of ink on a faint ink tint. And a withheld rate still drew a full-width bar beside the
words "표본 부족" — a picture asserting exactly what the text was refusing to say.

## 8 · Localization

Pricing copy in **31 market locales** (Korean canonical), merged through `scripts/i18n/v14-merge.mjs`, whose
checks earned their place again:

- it refused the three **plan names** in every locale as identical to English. They are the product's own
  names and are kept in Latin script across every market, so they are recorded in `v14-cognates.json` with
  that reason — **92 new entries**, each a decision written down rather than a silent pass.
- it caught **Arabic-Indic digits** in the Arabic strings while `Intl` formats that locale in Latin digits —
  the exact defect §116 recorded. Eight strings normalised.
- it caught four genuine copy-outs (German *Information*, Dutch *Checklist*, Swedish *Information*, French
  *minutes*) and one real omission.

Student plan copy in **25 locales** — every locale that carries the student app — merged the same way.
Agency and university copy is ko + en, which is the coverage those namespaces have.

Final counts: 31 market locales with pricing, 25 with the student plan screen, 18 replayable batches in
`docs/qa/v15/batches/`.

**The retired packages are gone from the locale bundles too**: `FREE_EXPLORER`, `APPLICATION_SUPPORT` and
`PREMIUM_SUCCESS` names and taglines were still present in 23 student bundles and in the generated student
manifest. The pricing gate found them, which is the point of pointing a gate at locale files and not only at
source.

## 9 · Gates

| Command | What it proves |
|---|---|
| `npm run qa:pricing` | manifest = `shared/plans.json` = API = rendered homepage; no retired code or price in shipped source or locales; no strike-through, no guarantee language, no banned sales copy |
| `npm run qa:entitlements` | plan scope matches the 플랜별 비교표; usage is derived; `null` ≠ `0`; a refusal is typed; an approved add-on raises exactly one limit |
| `npm run qa:handoff` | plan + language + return path survive `/start` → `/register` → `/services`, in Vietnamese, for all three plans; an invented `?plan=` selects nothing |
| `npm run qa:agency` | the four questions on one screen; no score; queue order is not price order; seven rail destinations |
| `npm run qa:university` | five sections; every number drills to the records it counts; no rate below the minimum sample and no bar under a withheld one; no retail pricing on any university surface |
| `npm run qa:v15` | all five |

# 124. V15 Agency at Scale Validation

Full document: **`docs/qa/v15/AGENCY_AT_SCALE.md`**. Measured on an isolated scale stack — 274 active
students for one counsellor, 1,264 submitted applications, API on :8091, console on :4702.

| The brief's measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| Time to identify an urgent case | **2.6 s** from sign-in to the top-ranked case readable |
| Clicks to the next action | **1** — the action is a link on the row (`j`/`k`/`↵` is also one) |
| Scope / entitlement confusion | plan on every row and as the strip's first cell; a case at its limit opens in **1.0 s** showing `지원 관리 3 / 3곳` and one out-of-scope notice with the next step |
| Missed deadlines | 149 overdue items in 30 days; the urgent chip reads **28 students**, not 149 rows |
| Unnecessary navigation | **7** rail destinations, **0** buttons in Today's header, filter row **47 px** |

The caseload: All-in-One 168 · Premium 85 · Basic 21 · **0 with no plan** · **86 at an allowance limit**.

That last number is the finding. A third of the caseload sits at a limit, and before V15 every one of them
was invisible — a counsellor could promise a third managed application on any of them and the console had no
opinion about it.

**What is synthetic:** the shape of the caseload, including the plan mix. The mechanics are findings; the
mix is not evidence about a real agency. **Not tested:** two counsellors at once, assignment hand-over, and
whether 2.6 s feels fast to anyone, because no counsellor has used this.

# 125. V15 University at Scale Validation

Full document: **`docs/qa/v15/UNIVERSITY_AT_SCALE.md`**. 1,264 submitted applications across five intakes.

| Dataset | Population | Height | Largest drop named |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| 2025 Fall | 1 | 1.56 screens | — (withheld, correctly) |
| 2026 Winter | 36 | 1.56 screens | yes |
| 2026 Fall / Spring | 288 each | 1.56 screens | yes |
| 2027 Spring (current) | 398 | 1.56 screens | yes |
| All intakes | **1,011** | 1.56 screens | yes |

No horizontal overflow at any size. At population 1 every conversion is below the minimum sample, so the
funnel prints 표본 부족 on every row and names no drop — the correct answer rather than a 100 %.

| | |
|---|--:|
| V14 Overview (development dataset) | 1.96 screens |
| V15 Overview (development dataset) | **1.51 screens** |
| V15 Overview (1,011 applications) | **1.56 screens** |

The target was 1.0–1.5. The development figure is inside it; the full-volume figure is **0.06 screens
outside it**, stated rather than rounded away. The page grew 0.05 screens for roughly two hundred times the
data while gaining three sections it did not have.

Reconciliation at volume: the funnel reads 1,011 submitted and the applicant list it opens shows 1,011.

What the Overview says at 1,011 applications, and why §3 earns its height:

    우즈베키스탄  ███████████████  313   등록 1
    베트남       ████████████     263   등록 0
    네팔         ██████████       226   등록 0
    중국         ████████         189   등록 1

Four markets producing 189–313 applications and between zero and one enrolled student. That is visible in
one glance because applications and enrolments share a row instead of living in two charts.

**A true zero dataset does not exist in the scale set.** The empty-state path is in the code and is
exercised on the development dataset; it is not exercised here, and saying so beats claiming a sweep that
included it. **Not tested:** concurrency, and a real recruitment cycle over time.

# 126. V15 Pricing & Commercial Validation

`npm run qa:pricing` · `npm run qa:entitlements` · `npm run qa:handoff` — all green.

**One price, four places.** The manifest, `shared/plans.json`, `GET /public/plans` and the rendered homepage
all state ₩249,000 / ₩499,000 / ₩849,000, in Korean and in English, with the digits compared rather than the
formatted string so the currency symbol and separators remain the locale's business.

**The scope matches the owner's table**, checked key by key against figures written into the gate from the
business plan rather than read from the thing being checked: 30/60/90 minutes, 3/5/7 recommended, 0/2/3
managed, 0/1/2 review rounds, 0/0/1 mock interviews, 0/0/30 days of arrival support. All-in-One is the one
recommended plan (§9 주력 상품).

**The handoff holds.** In Vietnamese, for all three plans: homepage CTA → `/start?plan=…&lang=vi` →
`/register?plan=…&next=/services?plan=…` → the plan pre-selected on arrival. An invented `?plan=` selects
nothing and does not break the page.

**The add-on loop is real**, end to end against the live API: the counsellor offers, the offer grants
nothing while it waits, the student approves, exactly one limit rises by one and is attributed to the
add-on, and no other allowance moves.

**What the gate forbids**, checked on the rendered section in both languages: strike-through (computed
style, not just markup), BEST ribbons, 무조건 / 100 % 성공 / 완벽 보장 / 혁신적 / 압도적 / 차원이 다른, and the
word 보장 or "guarantee" anywhere in the section. The external-cost note must exist and the comparison must
be exactly one in-place disclosure.

**The old model is unreachable**: no `FREE_EXPLORER` / `APPLICATION_SUPPORT` / `PREMIUM_SUCCESS` and no
retired demo price in `apps/*/src`, `packages/*/src`, `server/app`, `server/tests`, `e2e` or the locale
bundles. The one remaining mention is the docstring in `seed/run.py` that records what they were and why
they went.

# 127. V15 Launch Readiness

`npm run release:check` — one blocker closed, one deliberately left open.

## What moved

**`approved_prices`: FAIL → PASS.** This requirement reads `ServicePrice.is_demo`. Every price in the
catalogue was a sample price invented in a seed function; there are now three, they are the owner's own
approved figures from the business plan, and they are written with `is_demo=False`. This is the only
blocker V15 legitimately closes, and it closes because a business decision was made, not because code
changed.

## What did not move, and must not be made to look as though it did

**`refund_matrix`: still FAIL.** The business plan's own 1단계 lists 서비스 계약서 및 환불 규정 마련 as work
still to do. No refund ladder exists, so none is published. Terms article 9 continues to publish only what
the product implements.

**`payment_provider`: still FAIL.** The provider is a demo provider. New approved prices do not make
checkout production-ready and nothing in this pass implies they do — the checkout modal still says so, at
the moment of payment, which is the only honest place to say it.

Everything else in §115's list is unchanged by this pass: storage and malware scanning, the five null legal
fields, PIPA consent wording, counsel review, the MOE standard agreement, provider agreements, human
translation review, rate limiting, CSP, MFA, penetration testing, monitoring, backups, a support process and
usability research with real people.

## The honest summary

V15 makes the product **sellable in principle** — a visitor can see what it costs, choose, and arrive in the
platform with that choice intact; the console can tell a counsellor what was promised and stop them
promising more. It does not make it **chargeable**: there is no live payment provider and no refund policy,
and both are business dependencies rather than engineering ones.

---

# 128. V15 Final Hostile Audit

Written as someone who dislikes the product and is looking for the seam.

## Where it is genuinely better

The counsellor can finally see what the student bought, and the console will stop them over-promising
against it — not with a disabled control but with a sentence and a next step. Every price in the product
comes from one file and a gate fails the build if it stops doing so. The university Overview answers two
questions it could not answer before (where do applicants come from, what happens after we say yes) and got
*shorter* doing it. Each of those has a mechanism behind it, not a value nudged.

## Where it is weak, and nobody should pretend otherwise

**1 · The pricing section is three cards.** The brief's own hostile test asks whether this made the service
easier to understand or just added three cards to a clean homepage. It is cleaner than a SaaS template —
no ribbon, no strike-through, no gradient — but it is still the most conventional thing on a page whose
whole identity is that it is *not* conventional. The services section above it is editorial photography and
alternating prose; the pricing section is a row of boxes. **It is the least Koreanasha part of the page.**

**2 · "Up to 3 universities" is a limit, not a promise.** Every card leads with a ceiling. That is faithful
to the business plan and it is what makes the entitlement model work, but a student reading three cards is
reading three sets of maximums, and nothing on the card says what the *typical* case gets.

**3 · The entitlement model is enforced in exactly two places.** Application transitions out of DRAFT and
essay review submission. 추천 대학 is counted and displayed but nothing refuses a fourth recommendation;
상담 시간 is displayed and not enforced at all; 모의 면접 has an allowance and no workflow that consumes it.
The scaffolding is complete and honest about what it counts; **the coverage is not**, and a counsellor
could still over-deliver on three of the five counted keys without the system objecting.

**4 · Interview and settlement are entitlements without a workflow.** §13 and §14 of the brief asked for
interview tracking and progressive settlement activation. What exists is the allowance, visible to both
sides, and the pre-existing concierge `ServiceCase` types that settlement would attach to. **The
progressive activation by stage was not built.** Stated, not buried.

**5 · The writing-review dimensions are a reviewer's checklist, not a tool.** §12 asked the review workspace
to support prompt coverage, motivation clarity, unsupported claims and seven more. Those checks largely
existed already in `writing_checks.py`; what V15 added is the *entitlement* around them. A reviewer still
gets the same workspace they had.

**6 · The demo caseload was reconciled by a script I wrote.** The plan mix, the add-ons and the 86 cases at
a limit all come from distributions chosen to exercise the console. That is the right thing to do with a
demo dataset, and it also means **the dataset cannot be evidence that the design is right** — only that it
does not break.

**7 · 1.56 screens, not 1.5.** At full volume the university Overview is 0.06 screens over the target. Small,
real, and the kind of number that is easy to round away.

**8 · Insights still carries more than four visuals.** The four the brief names are all present — counsellor
workload, case ageing / SLA, application quality, and the service-delivery panel V15 added. The manager's
Outcomes tab carries a cohort funnel, a nationality cohort and a revenue block besides. That is three more
than the brief allows, and they were left because removing a measurement built in V8/V9 late in a pass,
without re-verifying what depends on it, is a worse trade than reporting it.

**9 · English metric definitions on a Korean console.** `agency_performance` and the V5 outcome metrics
return their `definition` strings in English only, and Insights prints them under every number. On a Korean
screen that is sixteen sentences of English in the middle of the manager's most data-dense page. Pre-existing
(V5/V9) and not introduced here — the one panel V15 added reads its definition from i18n instead — but it was
found by looking at a V15 screenshot and it is a real defect.

**10 · Nobody has used any of this.** Not one counsellor, not one admissions director, not one student. Every
number in §§124–126 is a measurement of a machine by a machine.

## Questions asked of each surface

- *Does pricing make the service easier to understand, or did we add three cards?* Easier — the comparison
  disclosure carries the owner's own table and the card carries five lines — but see weakness 1.
- *Can a counsellor answer the four questions in seconds?* Yes, and measured: 2.6 s to the first urgent
  case, 1 click to its action, plan visible without opening anything.
- *Can a director understand the four things in 15 seconds?* Decisions and markets, yes. Application
  quality needs the reader to know what "first-pass complete" means — it is defined in the UI, but defining
  it is not the same as its being obvious.
- *Where does the old template show through?* Nowhere new. The agency console is still YNEX underneath and
  still does not look it.
- *What would a competitor's reviewer attack?* The absence of a score. Every product in the benchmark ships
  one and ours refuses. That is a deliberate position and it will read as a missing feature to anyone
  comparing feature lists.

## The thing most likely to be wrong

**The definition of a review round.** "1회 첨삭" became "one pass over the student's writing, measured as the
deepest round any single essay has reached". That reading is defensible, it matches the plan's own wording,
and it is the one that does not refuse work a student paid for. It is still an interpretation of a sentence
in a business document, made in code, affecting what the product will and will not do for a paying customer.
**It should be confirmed by the owner rather than inherited from this pass.**

# 129. V15 b — the homepage pricing section, recomposed

V15 shipped a pricing section that was **correct and wrong**: every number traced to the manifest, every
gate passed, and the owner's verdict on the rendered page was that it looked like a SaaS billing page
pasted into an editorial homepage — three generic cards, a spreadsheet underneath, thin borders
everywhere, and two paragraphs of exclusions closing the composition.

No price, no entitlement and no plan changed in this pass. What changed is everything about how they are
presented, plus the removal of three paragraphs of customer-visible legal copy from this one section.

## 1 · The plans are a composition, not three objects

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| Three rounded, hairline-bordered cards on white | **Three columns under one rule.** Basic and Premium carry no container at all |
| The recommended card = a black 추천 pill + a slightly darker border | **All-in-One is the only plan with a surface** — a warm panel at the page's own `--kn-warm`, lifted 28 px above the shared rule and dropped 20 px below it, with a tangerine hairline, tangerine ticks, a tangerine 추천 label and the one filled Hangyul button in the section |
| Premium = Basic with different words | **Premium is ink**: an ink segment of the shared rule, ink ticks, an ink-outlined button |
| Eleven horizontal rules | Two: the shared rule, and one hairline per column under the price |
| `₩ 249,000` + a 12 px `1회 결제` hung off its baseline | `₩249,000` as one typographic unit at 32–40 px, with `1회 결제` demoted underneath |
| Five lines of card copy restating the whole scope | Five lines that *differ* between plans, per the owner's new card copy |
| A 9 × 5 rotated-border tick | One 15 px stroked check, at the weight of the arrow in the buttons beside it |

The tier encoding is wordless and is stated three times in the same order — **rule, tick, button: grey →
tangerine → ink** — so a reader who takes in only the top of the composition has already read it.

The panel's lift and drop are cancelled by matching padding inside it, so the three names, the three
prices and the three buttons stay on their shared baselines. §123 recorded that misalignment once already;
it came back the moment the panel was reintroduced, and it is now a measured invariant, not a comment.

## 2 · The comparison is three questions, not eleven rows

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| A bordered `<table>` in a horizontal scroller | A matrix with **no cell rules at all**; the rhythm is row height |
| Eleven flat rows | Three named areas — 상담 및 추천 · 실제 지원 · 비자 · 정착 — with a quiet hairline above each label |
| `미포함` printed nine times | `—` for absent, `✓` for included, quantities where a quantity is the answer. The word stays in the accessibility tree |
| The recommended column tinted per cell, so the tint broke at every group row | One absolutely-positioned block **behind** the table, continuous from the header to the last row. Which column it sits over is `--p-hi`, the manifest's own index |
| 390 px: a four-column spreadsheet in a focusable scroller | **A WAI tablist** — 베이직 / 올인원 / 프리미엄, opening on the recommended plan — over one 구분 → 값 column per area. No horizontal scrolling at any width |
| The disclosure bracketed top and bottom, in its own vocabulary | **The FAQ's row**: hairline above and below, label filling the width, chevron at the far end. The FAQ is the next section on this page; a second disclosure vocabulary thirty pixels above the first was the thing making the section feel bolted on. It also gives the section a full-width line to end on |

## 3 · The legal copy left the homepage — it did not leave the product

Removed from the homepage pricing section, in every locale:

- 베이직에 포함되지 않는 범위… (`v15.pricing.compare.excluded`)
- 서비스 이용료에 포함되지 않는 비용… (`v15.pricing.external.*`)
- 비자 관련 서비스는 관련 법령상… (`v15.pricing.visaNote`)

Nothing was deleted. The keys stay in the bundles, and the statement a buyer needs before paying is where
the buying happens: **the student plan page states it above the plan chooser** (`v15.services.external`)
and **제8조 of the Terms** states it as a term. `npm run qa:pricing` now asserts both halves — gone from
the homepage, still present on both other surfaces, with all five external costs still named. Removing one
assertion and replacing it with three is the only way that removal is safe; a gate that only checked the
homepage would have turned a design decision into a compliance hole.

## 4 · Motion and accessibility

Nothing new was built. The section uses the one `Reveal` the site already has: the head rises, the plans
stagger 80 ms apart, the comparison rises. The only addition is that **the stagger's delays are swapped
below 1024 px**, because the phone's reading order puts All-in-One first and a stagger that follows the
array rather than the eye is a stagger pointing the wrong way.

The disclosure now opens rather than appears, via `::details-content` + `interpolate-size`, guarded by
`@supports` and by `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` — measured at 641 → 927 px over ~180 ms where
it is supported, and an instant open everywhere else. Verified: nothing is hidden with the reveal unable
to arm, nothing moves under reduced motion, Enter opens the disclosure, and the tablist answers
arrows / Home / End with roving `tabindex`, mirrored in RTL.

## 5 · Copy

The brief's card lines and Basic's key message were applied to **ko and en**. The other 29 marketing
locales keep their V15 translations, which describe the same entitlements in slightly longer sentences —
accurate, not stale, and re-tightening them is a translation pass rather than part of this one. The three
new area labels **are** translated for every locale that ships `v15.pricing`, because an English area
label inside an otherwise-translated matrix is a visible regression in 29 markets.

## 6 · Evidence

`docs/qa/v15/pricing-redesign/` — before and after at 390 · 430 · 768 · 1024 · 1440 · 1728, collapsed and
expanded, plus hover, focus, the phone's recommended-first view, the transition into the FAQ, three
locales including RTL, and the reduced-motion and keyboard checks.

Gates: `qa:v14` (8 gates, incl. 31 markets × 2 widths: 0 overflow, 0 clipping) · `qa:v15` (5 gates) ·
`typecheck` (7 workspaces) · `test:web` (70 tests) · `build` (4 workspaces) · Playwright marketing,
hierarchy, responsive and redesign specs (19 tests). All green.

# 130. V16 Final Product Audit

Written **before** any code changed, from the running product at `:3100`–`:3103` rather than from §129's
description of it. §129 is accurate about what was *intended*; every defect below is something the browser
actually does, measured with Playwright against the dev stack.

The owner's verdict is the frame: *a product can pass every automated test and still feel unfinished*.
`qa:v15` passes and the pricing section has a line in it that looks like a CSS bug. That is not a gap in
the gates' rigour, it is a gap in what they were asked to check — `qa:pricing` asserts reading order, card
width, CTA height and horizontal overflow, and none of those can see a 2 px ink rule or a 3 px clip.

## The four defects that are visible in one glance

| # | Surface | What the browser does | Root cause (measured, not guessed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Marketing pricing | A hard black rule sits beside Premium and reads as a rendering artefact | `v15.css:141` — `.kn-plan[data-plan='premium']::before { height: 2px; background: var(--hg-text) }`, the "ink segment" of §129's grey → tangerine → ink encoding |
| 2 | Marketing pricing | All-in-One's panel is cut off at the top on hover, and its shadow is cut off at rest | `.kn-reveal.is-in { clip-path: inset(0 0 0% 0) }` — a **clipping container** on the plans' own grid, whose padding box the panel's top edge sits exactly on |
| 3 | Student home | The greeting sits on the right, over the skyline; the dark gradient covers the empty left | `v7.css:19` sets `align-items: flex-end` meaning *bottom*; `v9.css:16` later set `flex-direction: column` on the same element, which turned that into *right* |
| 4 | Student header | The unread badge floats above the bell and eats its dome | `.hg-bell__count` is 19 × 16 (a pill, not a disc) at `top: 5px` over an 18 px icon, with a 2 px ring in `--hg-surface` against a header painted `--hg-bg-canvas` — so the ring is invisible and the badge has no edge |

Each is a *layering* failure rather than a design failure: a later stylesheet changed the meaning of an
earlier one and nothing in the suite could see it. §137 proposes the structural answers; §133 and §131 the
per-control ones.

## A fifth, found while auditing: an invisible primary action

`/applications` renders its only page-level action, **지원 추가하기**, as white text on a white surface.

```
A.hg-btn  "지원 추가하기"  color rgb(255,255,255)  background rgb(255,255,255)  109×40
```

`v7.css:112` paints every anchor inside a student page head white, so that links on the near-black band
are legible. An anchor that is *also* a button brings its own light surface, and the blanket rule repaints
only its text. The button has been invisible on that page since V7. No gate looks at contrast between an
element and its own background, and no screenshot review caught it because a white rectangle on a black
band reads as a design decision until you try to click it.

## What is NOT wrong, and is therefore out of scope

The pricing *composition* (columns under one rule, one surface for the recommended plan, a borderless
matrix), the plan manifest, the locale architecture, the marquee, the agency and university operating
models, and the URL-locale contract. §129's direction is kept; only its ink rule and its clipped hover go.

# 131. V16 Student Experience Audit

Every authenticated student route, captured at 1440 and 390 as two seeded personas — `student@demo.hangyul.kr`
(three applications, All-in-One bought) and `student.new@demo.hangyul.kr` (nothing bought).

For each screen: the student's one question, the one primary action, and what the capture shows.

| Route | The one question | Primary action | Found |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` Home | What should I do now? | The next-step CTA | Hero composed backwards (§130 #3); a visible `사진: mauveine.kim · CC0 1.0` overlay; six equal 96 px journey tiles reading as a toolbar; "coming up" dates in alternating black/tangerine blocks where the alternation carries no meaning |
| `/explore` Universities | Which schools can I actually get into? | Open a university | Sound. Filter row is dense at 1024 |
| `/universities/:slug` | Is this school right for me? | Save / start an application | Sound |
| `/compare` | Which of these is better for me? | Start an application | Sound |
| `/applications` | What is blocking each application? | Add / open an application | **Invisible primary action** (§130 #5) |
| `/applications/:id` | What do I do next on this one? | The blocked item | Sound |
| `/documents` | What do I still have to upload? | Upload | Sound; the black head's orange disc is clipped into a wedge |
| `/essays` `/essays/:id` | Is my draft good enough? | Open the editor | Sound |
| `/visa` `/housing` `/arrival` | What is the next step and when? | The next step | Sound |
| `/services` | What did I buy / what should I buy? | Choose a plan | **Does not say payment is next** — see §136. Its subtitle also described a bought plan to a student who has not bought one |
| `/messages` | What does my counselor need? | Reply | Sound |
| `/notifications` | What happened? | Open the item | 모두 읽음 sits on the orange disc at ~2:1 contrast; the day label is underlined and reads as a broken link; timestamps sit off the title baseline |
| `/profile` `/settings` | What is missing? | Complete a section | Sound |
| `/more` | Where is everything else? | A destination | Sound |

**The pattern across the weak screens**: every one of them is weak in the *page head* or in a *decorated
list*, never in the content. The near-black head band with a radial tangerine disc (`v7.css:104–118`) is
applied to thirteen screens; it was designed for the marketing breadcrumb band, and at 100 % of screen
width above a white page it is the single thing that makes the student product read as an admin console.
Where a screen also puts an action in that band, the action is either invisible (Applications) or sitting
on the disc (Notifications).

**What a student cannot answer today**: *do I need to pay now?* Nothing on Home, Services or the plan card
contains the word 결제 before the modal opens. That is the abandonment hole §136 closes.

# 132. V16 Pricing Interaction Audit

## 132.1 The black rule — why the encoding failed

§129 encodes the tier ladder wordlessly and three times: **rule, tick, button — grey → tangerine → ink**.
The idea is sound and two thirds of it works. The rule does not, for a reason that is about perception
rather than about taste:

- The tick and the button are *inside* a column. Their colour is read as the column's colour.
- The rule is a 2 px horizontal bar at the top of the third column, 300 px long, with nothing above it and
  the section's own 1 px grey hairline continuing on either side of it. It is not read as "Premium is
  ink". It is read as **the grey line being broken**, which is what a rendering fault looks like.

An encoding that needs a legend is not an encoding. **Decision: one shared neutral hairline across all
three plans.** Premium keeps its ink identity where ink is legible as identity — its ticks and its
outlined button — and loses it where it reads as damage.

## 132.2 The hover clip — root cause

Measured on the running page at 1440, All-in-One's `.kn-plan__body`:

```
.kn-plan__body        top 206   mt -28px   pt 68px
.kn-plan   (article)  top 234
.kn-plans  (Reveal)   top 206   pt 28px    clip-path: inset(0px 0px 0%)   ← clipping container
```

Two facts combine:

1. `--p-lift: 28px` is cancelled exactly by `.kn-plans { padding-block: 28px 20px }`. The panel's top edge
   is therefore at **precisely** the grid's padding-box top. There is zero headroom by construction.
2. `.kn-reveal.kn-reveal--armed.is-in` sets `clip-path: inset(0 0 0% 0)`. A zero inset is **not** a no-op:
   it establishes a clip to the element's border box. `.kn-plans` *is* the reveal.

So `transform: translateY(-3px)` on hover moves the panel 3 px into clipped space, and the panel's resting
`0 18px 44px -28px` shadow is already being cut off at the bottom edge. The symptom the owner sees ("the
upper area is clipped") is the top edge; the same bug is removing the shadow at the bottom.

The clip-path exists for the `media` reveal variant — a bottom-up wipe over a photograph — and the shared
`.is-in` rule resets it for *all four* variants, including the three that never set one. Every `Reveal` on
the marketing site has been silently clipping its children's shadows and hovers since V10.

**Fix: scope `clip-path` to `[data-reveal='media']`**, in the armed state, in the transition list and in the
`.is-in` reset. Then add headroom anyway (`--p-head`), because a composition that depends on no ancestor
ever clipping is a composition waiting for the next stylesheet.

## 132.3 The comparison matrix

The matrix is structurally right (no cell rules, three named areas, a continuous tint behind the
recommended column, a tablist on phones). It is *flat* because every row is the same weight at the same
rhythm: the service name, the three values and the area label are within one typographic step of each other,
so nothing is a handhold and the eye has no path down the table.

Planned, within the existing philosophy and with no borders restored:

- Area labels: smaller, letterspaced, tertiary — a *label*, not a row.
- Service names: one step darker and medium weight; they are the thing being scanned.
- Values: tabular numerals, so 최대 2곳 / 최대 3곳 align digit-over-digit down the column.
- Row rhythm: taller rows (`--p-row`), with the first row of each area given extra space above.
- The recommended column: a slightly stronger tint and its header in the brand colour (already) plus
  semibold values, so the column reads as a column rather than as a tint.
- `—` for absent: one step lighter than today, so an absence recedes instead of printing a grey bar.

## 132.4 Interaction

Required end state: hover on any plan = a surface change plus −2 px (−4 px for the recommended panel, which
starts with a surface), **no clipping at any width**, no layout shift, a visible focus ring on every CTA and
on the disclosure, and the arrow in a CTA moving 3 px. The disclosure keeps its `::details-content`
animation. A new gate (`qa:v16`) measures the panel's rendered top against every ancestor's clip rect at
five widths, in rest and hover, so this defect cannot return silently.

# 133. V16 Header & Micro-Interaction Audit

## 133.1 The notification control, as built

```
.hg-bell          40 × 40   position: relative   display: block
.hg-bell .hg-btn  40 × 40   (icon 18 px, centred → icon box y 11…29)
.hg-bell__count   19 × 16   top: 5px  inset-inline-end: 5px   border: 2px solid var(--hg-surface)
```

Four separate things are wrong and they compound:

1. **It is a pill, not a disc.** `min-width: 16px; height: 16px; padding: 0 4px` gives 19 × 16 for a single
   digit. At 4× magnification it reads as a lozenge stuck to the bell.
2. **It sits on the icon, not at its corner.** Top 5 px against an icon starting at 11 px means the badge
   covers the bell's dome. The bell stops looking like a bell.
3. **Its ring is invisible.** `border: 2px solid var(--hg-surface)` (#FFF) against a header painted
   `color-mix(--hg-bg-canvas 92%)` (#FAFAF8-ish). The ring is there and it is the wrong colour, so the
   badge has no separating edge and floats.
4. **The button has no resting shape**, so the badge is the only thing with a boundary — which is exactly
   why it reads as "floating outside the control".

## 133.2 The rest of the control group

`더보기 ⌄ · 🌐 · 🔔 · ◯ Lan` at a uniform 12 px gap. Three problems:

- Mathematically even spacing across four controls of three different kinds reads as a toolbar.
- The profile is an avatar and a name with no shared surface — "plain text beside an unrelated grey
  circle", which is the owner's phrase and is accurate.
- Hover state exists on the ghost button but not on the avatar row, so half the group responds and half
  does not.

## 133.3 The popover

`width: min(380px, 100vw − 24px)`, unread rows painted `--hg-surface-warm` edge to edge. The warm fill is
the "giant coloured card" the brief rules out: it marks the row as *different* rather than as *unread*, and
with three unread rows the whole panel is warm and the signal is gone. Mark-all-read invalidates the query
but the badge keeps its old number until the refetch lands.

## 133.4 What V16 builds

| | |
|---|---|
| Button | 38 px square, 8 px radius, transparent at rest, `--hg-text 5%` on hover, `8%` when the popover is open (`[data-open]`), 3 px focus ring |
| Badge | **17 px disc**, tangerine, white, 11/700, tabular numerals, anchored `top: -1px; inset-inline-end: -1px` on a 38 px button so it sits on the corner, with a **2 px ring in the header's own surface token** (a new `--hg-bell-ring`, set by the shell, so console and student headers each get their own) |
| Counts | 0 → nothing; 1–9 → the digit; 10–99 → the number, at the same 17 px disc (two tabular digits fit at 11 px); ≥ 100 → `99+`, the pill allowed to grow to 24 px because there is no honest disc for three glyphs |
| States | no unread = bell only; unread = bell + disc; open = button filled, badge unchanged — the button never turns orange |
| Popover | aligned to the button's right edge with an 8 px offset, viewport-collision clamped, unread = a 6 px tangerine dot + a semibold title, **no row fill** |
| Mark read | the count is updated optimistically through the query cache and reconciled by the refetch; the mutation is guarded so a double click issues one request |
| Grouping | `더보기` — 16 px — `🌐 🔔` (6 px apart, they are both 38 px icon buttons) — 14 px — profile |
| Profile | one control: avatar + name + chevron on a shared hover surface, 38 px tall, radius 999 px only on hover |

Catalogued from the captures, to be fixed in this pass: the underlined day label on `/notifications`; the
off-baseline timestamps in that list; the invisible Applications button; the page-head disc clipped into a
wedge; 모두 읽음 sitting on the disc; the journey tiles' uniform 96 px height and charcoal "done" state; the
alternating black/tangerine date blocks on Home; the `사진:` overlay on the home band.

# 134. V16 Console Test-Access Audit

## What already exists

`packages/auth/src/demo-personas.ts` is already the single source of demo accounts, and
`POST /auth/demo-login` already signs in a seeded account without a password, outside production only.
`packages/ui/src/devaccess.tsx` already gates on `import.meta.env.DEV || VITE_DEMO_LOGINS === 'true'` and
already loads the persona list from a dynamic import, so a production build with the flag off drops the
chunk and the emails with it.

**Nothing new needs to be invented.** What is missing is an entry point: today a reviewer reaches a console
either by typing a seeded email and `Hangyul!2026`, or via `/__dev`, which is a developer screen.

## What V16 adds

One secondary action on the Agency and University login screens only, below the normal form, under a
`또는` divider:

- Agency → **테스트 계정으로 로그인** → `counselor@lotus.demo.hangyul.kr` (Trương Mỹ Linh, Lotus Bridge).
  The counselor is the persona whose Today screen demonstrates the actual product: a real queue, real
  students, real document work. The manager's and reviewer's screens are narrower views of the same data.
- University → **테스트 계정으로 로그인** → `admin@pusan.univ.demo.hangyul.kr` (International office,
  Pusan National University). The administrator sees Overview, Applicants, the decision queue *and*
  Analytics; the admissions officer cannot reach Analytics, the analyst is read-only.

One click, no password, straight to Agency Today / University Overview. A compact disclosure
(**다른 역할로 로그인**) underneath offers the other seeded roles for that console — collapsed by default,
so the default path stays one click and the screen never becomes three persona cards.

Failure is shown in the form's existing inline error treatment, not in a new one.

**Gating**: the whole block is behind the same `demoAccessEnabled()` the drawer uses, so
`VITE_DEMO_LOGINS` unset in a production build removes the markup, the strings and the emails. §141
asserts that against a real production build, by grepping the emitted bundles.

**After login**: nothing changes. No demo chip, no banner, no "test account" anywhere in the console
chrome. The shortcut's entire job is to get a reviewer past the door.

# 135. V16 Payment Architecture Audit

## The four merchant configurations, and what they can actually do

Toss Payments issues two families of client key, and the family determines the product (Toss API-keys
reference):

| Prefix | Product | SDK entry |
|---|---|---|
| `test_gck` / `live_gck` | 주문서형 · 결제창형 (the current payment widget) | `TossPayments(key).widgets()` |
| `test_ck` / `live_ck` | 결제창(구버전) · 브랜드페이 · 자동결제 | `TossPayments(key).payment()` / `.brandpay()` |

All four owner-provided client keys are `test_ck_…`. None of them can drive `widgets()`.

| | MID | Product it is contracted for | Used for the plan purchase? |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `bill_talko18s0` | 자동결제 — domestic card **billing-key registration** | **No** |
| B | `bill_talkoab1` | 자동결제 — foreign card billing-key registration | **No** |
| C | `bill_talkspm0` | 자동결제 — easy-pay billing-key registration | **No** |
| D | `HANGYUL` | 일반 결제, 결제창(구버전) | **Yes** |

The `bill_*` MIDs authorise `requestBillingAuth()`, which stores a billing key against a customer so the
merchant can charge them later. Hangyul's plans are **one-time purchases** (business plan §3): using a
billing MID for them would mean asking a student to register a card for recurring charges in order to buy
a single package. The brief forbids it and so does the product. They are configured server-side, kept out
of the student journey, and `qa:v16` asserts that no browser code path can reach a `bill_*` key.

**Foreign cards**: config B exists because overseas *billing* needs its own MID. One-time overseas card
payment does not — the 결제창 takes `card.useInternationalCardOnly` and opens the multilingual window on
the same `HANGYUL` MID. That is the route Hangyul uses, since most of its students are not in Korea.

## The flow, and where trust sits

```
browser                          FastAPI                         Toss
  │ POST /me/orders {plan}  ──────▶ create PENDING Order
  │                                 amount ← ServicePrice (server)
  │ ◀── {order_id, amount, currency, order_name, client_key, success_url, fail_url}
  │
  │ TossPayments(client_key).payment({customerKey:'ANONYMOUS'})
  │   .requestPayment({method:'CARD', amount, orderId, orderName, successUrl, failUrl})
  │                                                         ──────▶ 결제창
  │ ◀──────────────── redirect successUrl?paymentKey&orderId&amount ────────
  │ POST /me/payments/toss/confirm {paymentKey, orderId, amount}
  │                                 ├ order exists, is mine, is PENDING
  │                                 ├ amount == order.amount_minor (server's number)
  │                                 ├ currency == KRW, product still active
  │                                 └ POST api.tosspayments.com/v1/payments/confirm
  │                                     Authorization: Basic b64(secret:)   ← server only
  │                                     Idempotency-Key: toss-confirm-<order id>
  │ ◀── {status, plan}               status DONE → Payment PAID, Order PAID, entitlements on
```

The browser never decides that a payment succeeded; `amount` arriving from the redirect is compared with
the stored amount and is never used as the amount to confirm. Card number, expiry and CVC never reach
Hangyul — the window is Toss's.

## Idempotency, recovery, reconciliation

- **Order IDs** are the Order's own UUID (36 chars, `-` only) — inside Toss's 6–64 character rule and
  unique by construction.
- **Confirm is idempotent** three ways: an `Idempotency-Key` derived from the order id (Toss honours it on
  every POST for 15 days); a row lock on the order so two concurrent confirms serialise; and an early
  return of the stored result when the order is already PAID. A refresh of the success URL, a double click,
  or the back button therefore produces the same answer and one `Payment` row.
- **Recovery**: if the browser dies after Toss approved, the order is still PENDING locally. `/me/services`
  resolves any PENDING order that has a paymentKey by asking Toss for the payment's real state before it
  renders, so the next load shows an active plan rather than asking for money again.
- **Webhooks**: Toss's status webhook adds nothing this flow does not already have — the redirect plus the
  pull-on-load covers the one case a webhook exists for. It is left unimplemented and the reason recorded,
  rather than half-built against an endpoint that cannot be authenticated in this environment.

## Secrets

`server/.env` is already gitignored. `TOSS_*` values move there; the **client** key is the only value that
reaches the browser, and it reaches it from the server's order response rather than from a `VITE_` variable,
so there is exactly one place that knows which merchant configuration is in use. `qa:v16` greps the tracked
tree for all four secret keys, all four security keys and all four client keys and fails on any hit.

# 136. V16 Checkout Journey Design

## Today

```
homepage 올인원으로 시작 → /start → register → /services?plan=all_in_one
  → three cards, CTA "올인원 선택"           ← the word 결제 has not appeared
  → modal: a yellow "this is a demo" callout, a price row, eight ticks
  → "결제하기" → nothing opens → "결제가 완료되었습니다"
```

6 clicks, 4 pages, 1 modal — and a student who cannot tell whether they paid. The demo provider approves
synchronously, so the only honest thing the screen can say is that the transaction is not real, which it
says in a warning callout *at the moment of purchase*.

## V16

```
homepage 올인원으로 시작 → /start → register → /services?plan=all_in_one
  → the chosen plan, expanded, with 결제 금액 and 1회 결제
  → "결제하고 시작하기 · ₩499,000"
  → Toss 결제창 (card / easy-pay, the real test window)
  → /services/payment/success  → 결제 완료 → "내 유학 준비 시작하기"
```

5 clicks, 4 pages, **0 modals** — one fewer click and one fewer surface than V15 (`/start` stays; §143 says
why). The modal is deleted rather than redesigned: it held a price the page
already shows and a feature list the card already shows, and a confirmation surface that repeats the page
it was opened from has not earned its existence (brief Part 22).

What the student is told, and where:

| Question | Answered by |
|---|---|
| Do I pay now? | The CTA says 결제하고 시작하기 and carries the amount |
| How much? | On the CTA, and in the order line above it |
| One-off or monthly? | `1회 결제` next to the amount, on the plan and on the CTA block |
| What is not included? | `v15.services.external`, above the chooser, as now |
| Did it work? | The success screen says 결제 완료 with the plan name, amount and date |
| What now? | One action, routed to the student's actual next unresolved task |

**Cancel** returns to `/services?plan=…` with the plan still chosen and one quiet line: 결제를 취소했습니다.
No red wall. **Failure** shows Toss's message mapped to a human sentence plus 다시 결제하기.

**Native**: Expo opens the same `/services` → Toss redirect in an in-app browser and returns through a deep
link to the same success route. The state machine is the server's, so nothing is duplicated.

# 137. V16 Simplification Plan

Ordered by what it removes, not by what it adds.

1. **Delete the checkout modal.** One surface, one decision, on the page the student is already on.
2. **Delete `sh-band__credit`.** Every shipping photo is CC0 or Unsplash-licence — attribution-free by
   policy since V14 — so the overlay states an obligation that does not exist, in the most visually
   expensive position on the student's home screen. The `/credits` page keeps the full record.
3. **Delete the ink rule under Premium** and the stacked-layout ink border that goes with it.
4. **Delete `clip-path` from three of the four reveal variants.** One fix, every surface.
5. **Demote the student page-head band.** Keep it; stop it being 100 % of thirteen screens' first
   impression — shorter, the disc smaller and fully inside the band, and the blanket `a { color: #fff }`
   replaced by a rule that cannot repaint a button's label.
6. **Make the journey strip a strip.** Six 96 px tiles become a 64 px rail: done is quiet (not charcoal),
   current is tangerine, upcoming is white. It is a position indicator, not six buttons.
7. **Stop alternating the Coming-up date blocks.** The colour meant nothing; one quiet treatment, with the
   nearest deadline the only one that carries emphasis.
8. **One `Pay` call site.** Marketing → auth → services is already one path; V16 makes the payment itself
   one path too, shared by web and native through the server's state machine.

What is deliberately **not** done: no redesign of Agency or University beyond the login screens and any
defect found while regressing them (brief Part 29); no new top-level navigation anywhere; no billing-key
UI; no webhook endpoint; no new reveal, no new popover, no new button variant.

# 138. V16 Implementation Log

Ordered the way the work was done: root causes first, then the things built on top of them.

## 138.1 The reveal was a clipping container — one fix, every surface

`packages/koreanasha-ui/src/scss/koreanasha.scss`

```diff
-  .kn-reveal.kn-reveal--armed { … transition: opacity, transform, clip-path; }
-  .kn-reveal.kn-reveal--armed.is-in { opacity: 1; transform: none; clip-path: inset(0 0 0% 0); }
+  .kn-reveal.kn-reveal--armed { … transition: opacity, transform; }
+  .kn-reveal.kn-reveal--armed.is-in { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
+  .kn-reveal--armed[data-reveal='media'] { …; transition: …, clip-path …; }
+  .kn-reveal--armed[data-reveal='media'].is-in { transform: none; clip-path: inset(0 0 0% 0); }
```

`clip-path: inset(0 0 0% 0)` is not a no-op — a zero inset still establishes a clip to the border box. The
`media` variant needs one (it animates a wipe); the other three never set one, and the shared `.is-in` reset
gave all four a permanent clip. Every `Reveal` on the marketing site was silently cutting off whatever its
children did outside their boxes: hover lifts, drop shadows, focus rings. The pricing panel was the visible
symptom. Measured after: `0 clippers` in the ancestor chain, at all five widths.

## 138.2 Pricing

`apps/marketing-web/src/v15.css`

| | |
|---|---|
| The ink rule | **Deleted** — both the desktop `::before` segment and the stacked `border-top-color`. The ladder is now one shared neutral hairline; Premium keeps ink in its ticks and its button outline, where ink reads as identity rather than as a broken line |
| Headroom | New `--p-head: 24px`, added to the grid's padding and **subtracted from the margins above and below**, so the panel gains 24 px of room top and bottom and the section's rhythm is unchanged |
| All-in-One | Tint a step lighter (`#FFF8F3` → `#FFFAF6`), border a step quieter (24 % → 22 %), plus an inset white hairline so the top edge has a terminator. Name → bold, list text → full ink. Nothing scaled, no shadow added |
| The 추천 label | A 5 px tangerine dot inside the pill, so the label has a constant optical anchor whatever the translation does to its width |
| Buttons | `:active { translate: 0 1px }` — a press is a state, and the click that matters most had none |
| Matrix | `--p-row` (11–14 px → 14–18 px); area labels 11 px / +0.12em / tertiary; service names medium ink; values tabular; recommended column's values semibold; the tint one step stronger; `—` lighter. No borders restored, no icons added |

## 138.3 The student home band

Three files, and the fix is a **deletion plus one statement**, not a fourth override.

```
v2.css   .sh-band { display:flex; align-items:flex-end } + .sh-band__credit   → deleted
v7.css   .st7-home .sh-band { … } + the 90deg shade + the [dir=rtl] twin     → deleted
v9.css   .sh-band { flex-direction: column … } + .sh-band__credit            → deleted
v16.css  the whole composition, once                                          → new
```

The band is now a two-column grid: a declared text column, a reserved image column, a logical `to right`
shade (so RTL needs no twin rule), and `object-position` from the asset's own focal point. The greeting
dropped from `clamp(34px,4vw,52px)` to `clamp(28px,3vw,40px)`. Measured after: the copy occupies 0 %–53 %
of the band at every width ≥ 768, and 0 %–100 % at 390 where the shade goes vertical.

`sh-band__credit` is gone with its prop. `qa:media` gained two patterns (`sh-band__credit`, `creditLabel`)
because the caption it was supposed to catch came from a locale bundle through a prop and never appeared in
source as a literal.

Six 96 px tiles → a 64 px rail; "done" from charcoal to paper with tertiary type; hover from a −4 px lift to
a brightness change. The Coming-up date blocks stopped alternating charcoal/tangerine on `:nth-child(2n)` —
the colour meant "second", which is not information. One quiet treatment; the nearest deadline is the only
one in tangerine.

```diff
- :is(.hg-page-head, .st-intro) :is(a, …) { color: #fff; }
+ :is(.hg-page-head, .st-intro) :is(a:not(.hg-btn), …) { color: #fff; }
```

That is REPORT §130 #5 in one selector. `/applications` had been shipping its only page-level action as

## 138.6 The header

`packages/ui/src/shells.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/styles/layout.css`

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Button | ghost, 40 px, no resting shape | 38 px square, 10 px radius, transparent → 5 % hover → 8 % open |
| Badge | 19 × 16 pill at `top:5px` over an 18 px icon, 2 px `--hg-surface` ring on a `--hg-bg-canvas` header | 16 px disc at `top/end: 1px`, 2 px ring in a new `--hg-bell-ring` each shell sets to its own background |
| Counts | `unread > 9 ? '9+'` | `unreadBadge()`: 0 → nothing, 1–99 → the number, ≥ 100 → `99+` on a 23 px pill |
| Open state | none | `data-open` on the wrapper, neutral fill on the button; the button never turns orange |
| Mark read | invalidate and wait for the refetch | optimistic count + a re-entrancy guard; one request per click |
| Popover rows | `background: --hg-surface-warm` edge to edge | a 6 px tangerine dot in a reserved gutter + a semibold title; no fill |
| Grouping | four controls at one 12 px gap | 더보기 — 16 — (🌐 🔔 at 4) — 14 — account |
| Profile | an avatar beside loose text | `.hg-account`: one 38 px control, shared hover/open surface, chevron; below 1024 the avatar alone |

**Two real bugs found while building the header**, both of the same family as the ones V16 set out to fix:

1. `.hg-account__who` carried `hg-desktop-only`, which is a `display: none` utility — and a later
   `display: flex` of equal specificity silently beat it, so the name and the chevron were showing at
   390 px. The breakpoint is now stated on the component rather than borrowed.
2. The new `.hg-snav__tools` group was styled with a **child** combinator, and `Popover` wraps each trigger
   in its own anchor `<div>` — so `.hg-snav__tools > .hg-btn` matched nothing and the locale control
   shipped at 32 px beside a 38 px bell. Worse, the gate's own height check read
   `.hg-snav__tools > *` and therefore compared two wrapper divs, which is to say it passed on an empty
   premise. Both are fixed: the CSS uses a descendant combinator, and the gate now **fails** when the group
   is absent or when fewer than two controls are measured. A gate that can pass vacuously is not a gate.

## 138.6b A third one, in the test-access block — and what it says about the gates

The whole `.hg-testlogin` stylesheet **never got written**. The command that was supposed to append it ran
as `grep … && cat >> components.css <<'EOF'`; the grep found nothing, the `&&` short-circuited, the heredoc
never executed, and the "ok" printed by the previous command in the chain made it look like it had. So the
block shipped for most of this pass with no CSS at all: 또는 was a stray word with no rules, the hint was
left-aligned, and the role disclosure was a browser-default **bulleted list** of narrow buttons — which is
three persona cards by another name, the exact thing §134 ruled out.

The gate did not catch it, and that is the more useful half of the story. `qa:v16` was checking that the
button was not the same colour as the primary one, that it sat after the form, and that it used no
engineering vocabulary. All three passed on an unstyled block, because **presence is not a design**. The
gate now measures shape as well: the divider's `::before` must actually draw a rule, the hint must be
centred, and the role list must have no markers and no browser indent.

Writing those rules then failed the *production build* check, which is the lesson arriving a second time.
The first fix put them in the shared `components.css` — which every app ships — so `hg-testlogin` was in
the emitted CSS of a build that has no test login in it. A class name is not a credential and draws nothing
on its own, but "a production build contains no test-login UI" is easier to verify than "what is left is
harmless". The rules now live in `packages/ui/src/test-access.css`, imported by `test-access.tsx` itself,
so Vite emits them as that chunk's own asset and drops them with the chunk. That is now the third thing —
after the emails and the copy — that had to move **into the lazily-imported module** rather than be guarded
at runtime, and the pattern is worth stating plainly: *if a feature must not exist in production, every
part of it has to live behind the same build-time boundary, including its stylesheet.*

## 138.7 Console test access

`packages/ui/src/devaccess.tsx` → `TestAccountSignIn`, used by both console login pages.

Nothing new was invented: `DEMO_PERSONAS`, `POST /auth/demo-login` and `demoAccessEnabled()` already existed
and are reused. What is new is the entry point — a `또는` divider, one outlined secondary button, a
one-line note, and a text disclosure for the other seeded roles. Agency defaults to the Lotus Bridge
**counselor**, University to the Pusan **administrator** (§134 says why each).

## 138.8 Payments

| Layer | What changed |
|---|---|
| `server/app/core/config.py` | Sixteen `TOSS_*` settings, `toss_one_time_secret`, `toss_configured`, and a start-up refusal: production + `payment_provider=toss` + `toss_env != live` or a `test_` key → the process does not boot |
| `server/app/services/payments.py` | `TossProvider` made real — `create_checkout` (no network; returns order id, server amount, **client** key, return URLs), `confirm`, `lookup`, `sanitize`, `billing_configs` |
| `server/app/api/v1/student.py` | `POST /me/payments/toss/confirm`, `POST /me/orders/{id}/cancel`, `GET /me/payments/config`, `reconcile_pending_orders`, and `/me/services` now carries `payment` + `history` |
| `apps/student-web/src/lib/toss.ts` | The only place the SDK is touched. Loads the v2 script once, calls `payment().requestPayment()`, maps failure codes |

The checkout modal · the demo-payment warning callout at the moment of purchase · `sh-band__credit` and its

# 139. V16 Student Visual Validation

`npm run qa:v16`, section 3, at 390 · 768 · 1024 · 1440 · 1728:

```
 390px · copy at 0%–100% · greeting 28px · rail 56px · no credit
 768px · copy at 0%– 53% · greeting 28px · rail 64px · no credit
1024px · copy at 0%– 53% · greeting 31px · rail 64px · no credit
1440px · copy at 0%– 53% · greeting 40px · rail 64px · no credit
1728px · copy at 0%– 53% · greeting 40px · rail 64px · no credit
```

The gate asserts the copy starts within the left 12 % of the band and — above 1024 — ends before 72 % of it,
so "the words are on the left and the photograph's focal side is clear" is a measurement rather than an
opinion. It also asserts no `사진:` / `Photo:` / `Source:` string renders anywhere in the band, no journey
tile exceeds 76 px, and the page never scrolls horizontally.

**The contrast sweep.** Sixteen authenticated student routes, every `button` / `.hg-btn` / `a.hg-btn` with a
visible label, compared against the first opaque background actually behind it. One finding, and it was the
Applications button (§130 #5). After the fix: 16 routes, 0 controls without contrast.

The check deliberately skips controls with no text — a `role="switch"` on `/settings` has `color` equal to
its background and is drawn entirely with borders, and reporting it would be the gate failing to know what
it is looking at.

**Per-screen audit** is §131; the screens it found weak were weak in the page head or in a decorated list,
and both are fixed above. What is **not** done, and is deliberately left: `/explore`'s filter row is dense at
1024, and three seeded notification strings are English inside a Korean UI (seed content, not UI).

# 140. V16 Header & Notification Validation

`npm run qa:v16`, section 2, at 390 · 768 · 1024 · 1440, with the unread count **stubbed** at 0 / 1 / 9 / 120.

Stubbing is the point. The brief asks for four counts and the seed has one; worse, a gate that reads live
notifications stops being repeatable the moment it — or a person — marks them read. (That happened during
development: an interrupted first run clicked 모두 읽음 and the next run reported "no badge is drawn" as a
product defect. The gate was wrong, not the product.) Intercepting the one endpoint the bell reads tests
exactly what is under test: how a count is drawn.

Asserted at every width and every count:

- 0 unread → **no element at all**
- the button is square and 36–40 px
- the badge is 14–17 px tall, as wide as it is tall below 100, never wider than 26 px, fully rounded
- the badge's box is **inside** the button's box and within 5 px of its top-right corner
- the badge has a ring
- the button's accessible name carries the count (and the badge is `aria-hidden`, so it is not said twice)
- no two header controls overlap, and every control in the tools group is the same height

Popover: right gap **0 px** to the bell's right edge, top gap **8 px**, inside the viewport, a neutral (not
orange) open state on the button, unread rows with a transparent background and a tangerine dot.

Mark-all-read: the badge is gone on the click, and still gone after the 2.5 s refetch.
