# 142. V16 Toss Test Payment Validation

## What is proven, and how

| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| The right merchant configuration is used | `/me/payments/config` → `one_time: { mid: "HANGYUL", product: "일반 결제 (결제창)", used_by_plan_purchase: true }`, three `bill_*` configurations all `used_by_plan_purchase: false` |
| The owner's **secret** key authenticates against the live Toss test API | A confirm against a non-existent payment answers **`NOT_FOUND_PAYMENT_SESSION`** — a *business* error. A wrong key answers `UNAUTHORIZED_KEY`. The difference is the check |
| The browser gets a client key and nothing else | `POST /me/orders` → `client_key: test_ck_…`, `amount.value: 499000`, `sdk: js.tosspayments.com/v2/standard`, `success_url`, `fail_url`. Asserted free of `_sk_` and of `bill_` |
| The real 결제창 opens on the real order | The student app loads `payment-gateway-sandbox.tosspayments.com/pc?clientKey=test_ck_…` in an overlay, showing **All-in-One**, **499,000원**, 간편결제 (토스페이 · 페이코), nine card issuers, and Toss's own **"실제 결제가 안되는 테스트입니다"** badge |
| The order is PENDING until the server says otherwise | `POST /me/orders` → `"status": "PENDING"`; opening the window grants nothing |
| A forged amount cannot pay | `confirm` with `amount: 1000` on a ₩499,000 order → **409**, and the provider is never called |

## What is **not** proven, and why

**A completed card authorisation.** Toss's test 결제창 is not a mock: selecting a card hands off to the
issuer's own 3-D Secure page (`vbv.shinhancard.com/xacsv2/…`) and selecting 토스페이 hands off to a real
Toss Pay account login at `pay.toss.im`. Both require credentials that do not exist in this environment, so
no `paymentKey` can be obtained here. A full round trip needs a person with a Korean test card (or Toss's
own test-card fixtures enabled on the merchant) clicking through once.

It is recorded as a **remaining dependency**, not papered over. What depends on a real `paymentKey` — and
only that — is the single call `POST /v1/payments/confirm` returning `status: "DONE"`. Everything either
side of it is covered: `server/tests/test_v16_payments.py` (12 tests) drives the confirm endpoint with a
stubbed provider and asserts ownership, state, amount equality, the amount actually sent to Toss,
idempotency, activation, recovery and sanitisation; the gate proves the credentials authenticate and the
window opens on the right order.

## Idempotency, as tested

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Confirm the same order twice | one provider call, one `Payment` row, one activation, `PAID` both times |
| Refresh the success URL | the same `PAID` order, no second charge |
| Someone else's order id | **404** (not 403 — a 403 would confirm the order exists), provider never called |
| Unknown order id | 404 |
| Provider refusal | 402 with the provider's code, order `FAILED`, nothing activated |
| Browser died after approval | the next `/me/services` asks Toss, finds `DONE`, activates — once |
| Provider total ≠ our price | **not** activated; an `order.amount_mismatch` audit row for a person |

## The billing MIDs

`bill_talko18s0` / `bill_talkoab1` / `bill_talkspm0` are **자동결제** (billing-key registration)
configurations. They are in `server/.env`, described by `billing_configs()`, and reachable from no code path
a student can take. Hangyul's plans are one-time purchases (business plan §3); using a billing MID for one
would mean asking a student to register a card for future charges in order to buy a single package. Both
`qa:v16` and `test_v16_payments.py` assert that none of them is marked as used by the plan purchase and that
no `bill_` string reaches a browser.

**Overseas cards do not need one.** The `HANGYUL` 결제창 takes `card.useInternationalCardOnly`, which opens
the multilingual window on the same MID. The foreign-card `bill_*` MID is for billing keys, not for one-time
overseas payment, and is not an alternative to this.

# 143. V16 End-to-End Journey Validation

`e2e/v16-journey.spec.ts` walks a brand-new student from the homepage to the payment window and asserts the
*words*, not only the state — because the owner's standard is that the student never has to ask.

```
homepage 올인원으로 시작 → /start (quick check) → /register → /services?plan=all_in_one → Toss 결제창
          click 1            clicks 2,3            click 4            click 5
```

**5 clicks · 4 pages · 0 modals.** Before V16 it was 6 clicks, 4 pages and 1 modal, and the modal's first
element was a warning that the payment was not real.

**What V16 did not remove, and why.** `/start` sits between the plan and the account, and that is V13's
decision rather than an oversight: it answers "would a Korean university take someone like me?" without an
account, and a CTA that says "start" and opens a password field has not started anything (`planAction`,
`apps/marketing-web/src/lib/session.ts`). Removing it would shorten this count by two and is exactly the
kind of change a pass like this one should **not** make to a documented decision it was not asked to
revisit. What V16 removed is the modal, and the click that opened it: the plan page went from
선택하기 → modal → 결제하기 to one 결제하고 시작하기.

Asserted on the way:

| Question | Where the test finds the answer |
|---|---|
| Is this one payment or a subscription? | `1회` on the homepage card, before anything is committed to |
| Do I pay now? | the order block's primary action contains 결제 |
| How much, for what? | `올인원` and `499,000` in the order block |
| Where am I about to go? | `토스` in the line under the button |
| Did opening the window buy anything? | `/me/services` → `owned: []`, `pending_order_id` set |
| I closed the window — did I lose my plan? | `?payment=cancelled` → an info notice, the plan still chosen, **zero** danger callouts |
| Can a forged return pay for me? | 404/409, `owned` still `[]` |

Two more: a student who already owns a plan sees no sales UI and finds the payment history inside the plan
screen (no new navigation item); a cancelled Premium selection comes back as Premium.

# 144. V16 Launch Readiness

## TEST payment readiness — **ready, with one human step**

Everything is wired and the credentials work. What has not happened is one card authorisation by a person
with a Korean test card. Until then the confirm endpoint has been exercised against a stub, and against the
live API for its error path.

## LIVE merchant readiness — **not ready, and deliberately so**

| | |
|---|---|
| Live keys | Not issued. `HG_TOSS_ENV=test` and the four `test_` configurations are all that exist |
| Start-up guard | In place: production + `toss` + (`toss_env != live` or a `test_` key) refuses to boot |
| Receipts / 현금영수증 | Not implemented. Toss returns a receipt URL and the success screen links it; a Korean business selling to consumers needs more than that |
| Refunds | **Not implemented.** The Order model has no cancellation path and `/v1/payments/cancel` is not called. Korean e-commerce law gives a buyer a withdrawal right; a service that can take ₩849,000 and cannot give it back is not launchable |
| Webhooks | Not implemented — see below |

## Why there is no webhook

Toss's payment-status webhook exists for the case where the redirect never arrives. That case is already
covered twice: the success URL confirms, and `/me/services` asks Toss about any pending order on the next
load. A webhook would add a third path into the same state machine, needing its own authentication and its
own idempotency, for no behaviour this product does not already have. If a future flow needs one (virtual
accounts, which settle hours later, are the obvious candidate) it should be built then, against a real
endpoint. Half-building it now is how a payment system acquires a path nobody tests.

## Remaining blockers

1. **Refunds and cancellation** — the real blocker. Legal requirement, not a feature.
2. **One live test-card authorisation**, to close §142's gap.
3. **Live merchant contract and keys**, and the 전자금융거래 / 통신판매업 registrations the footer will need.
4. **Translations**: the fifteen `v16.pay.*` strings ship in 12 locales (ko, en, vi, ne, my, uz, mn, ar,
   zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ja, ru — every locale whose student bundle is above 85 %). The remaining 40 fall back
   to English, as ~30 % of the student namespace already does. A payment screen in English for a market the
   product otherwise speaks is a conversion problem, and it is a translation task, not a code one.

# 145. V16 Final Hostile Audit

Assume it was built badly. Attack it again.

**"The pricing ink rule is gone but Premium's button outline is still ink — that is the same device."**
It is the same *colour*, not the same device. The complaint about the rule was never the colour: it was that
a 2 px black bar at the top of one column, with the section's grey hairline continuing either side of it,
reads as the hairline being broken. A button outline is a boundary around a thing; a rule is a line through
nothing. The gate now encodes exactly that difference — it flags a dark border-top only when there is no
bottom, left or right border, so an outlined control passes and a rule does not.

**"You added headroom and called it a fix. The real fix was the clip-path."**
Both, and in that order. The clip-path is the root cause and is fixed where it lives. The headroom exists
because the panel's top edge sat on its grid's padding box *by construction* — a composition with zero
tolerance that works only while no ancestor ever clips is a composition waiting for the next stylesheet.
The gate measures the rendered panel against every ancestor's clip rect, so if a clip returns it is caught
rather than absorbed.

**"The student hero is fixed at 1440. What about 1728 and 390?"** 0 %–53 % at both 1440 and 1728; at 390
the band is a single column and the shade turns vertical, because at that width there is no "right side" to
protect — what there is to protect is the lower third, where the skyline is in every crop.

**"The badge is 16 px. The brief said 14–17 px with a 2 px ring — did you check it at every count?"**
0, 1, 9 and 120 at four widths, with the count stubbed so the check is repeatable. 0 renders nothing; 120
renders `99+` on a 23 px pill, which is the one count with no honest disc.

**"Opening a menu collides with another."** The gate checks pairwise overlap of every direct child of the
header at every width and every count. The popover is clamped to the viewport and measured at 0 px from the
bell's right edge, 8 px below it.

**"Test login makes the console look like a test environment."** The gate signs in through it and then
scans the whole console shell for `demo` / `test account` / `development account` / `fixture` /
`sample user`. Zero. The shortcut exists on one screen and leaves no trace past it.

**"You put four Toss merchant configurations in and used the most convenient one."**
The opposite. All four client keys are `test_ck_…` — the API-개별-연동 family — and three of the four MIDs
are `자동결제`, which registers a billing key to charge someone *later*. Hangyul sells one-time packages.
The one-time MID is used, the three billing MIDs are configured and unreachable, and both the gate and the
pytest suite assert that no browser path can touch one.

**"The browser could just call the success URL with a made-up amount."** It can call it. The server compares
the amount with the figure it stored before the window opened, answers 409, writes an
`order.amount_mismatch` audit row, and never contacts Toss. Verified live: `409`, `owned: []`.

**"Two tabs, a refresh and a double click."** One provider call, one `Payment` row, one activation. Three
mechanisms, because one is not enough: an order-derived `Idempotency-Key` that Toss honours for 15 days, a
`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the order so concurrent confirms serialise, and an early return of the stored
result when the order is already `PAID`.

**"What if the student's phone dies between Toss approving and your page loading?"** The order is `PENDING`
here and `DONE` there. `/me/services` asks Toss about any pending order from the last day before it renders,
and activates it. Tested. If the provider's total disagrees with our price it does **not** activate — it
writes an audit row for a person, because a silent activation on a number we did not set is worse than a
delay.

**"You claim a real TEST transaction. Show the receipt."** There is no receipt, and §142 says so in the
section heading rather than in a footnote. Toss's test window hands off to the card issuer's own 3-D Secure
page and to a real Toss Pay login; neither can be driven here. What is demonstrated is: the secret
authenticates against the live API, the real 결제창 opens on the real order with the right name and amount
and Toss's own test badge, and every server leg either side of the authorisation is tested. The one
remaining step is named as a blocker.

**"Where can a student still hesitate?"** Two places, both known. Registration asks for a password before
the student has seen anything they own — that is a V17 question about the auth model, not a payment one. And
`/explore`'s filter row is dense at 1024.

**"What still looks unfinished?"** Three things, stated rather than hidden: the near-black page-head band is
shorter and its arc is fixed, but thirteen screens still open on it and it is still the most console-like
thing in the student product; three seeded notification strings are English inside a Korean UI; and the
`v16.pay.*` strings reach 12 locales rather than 52.

## What the suite could not have caught before, and now can

Every V16 defect was invisible to a green suite, so each one got an assertion shaped like the defect:

| Defect | New assertion |
|---|---|
| A 2 px ink rule reading as a CSS bug | a dark border-top with no other border, anywhere in `#pricing` |
| A hover clipped by an ancestor | the rendered panel measured against every ancestor's clip rect, hovered, at 5 widths |
| A badge floating off its control | the badge's box inside the button's box, within 5 px of its corner, at 4 counts |
| A button painted on its own colour | foreground vs. the first opaque background behind it, every labelled control, 16 routes |
| A test-login string in a production bundle | two real `vite build`s, grepped |
| A secret in a tracked file | SHA-256 fingerprints, so the scanner is not itself a leak |
| A block that is present but unstyled | the divider's rule, the hint's alignment, the role list's markers and indent — all measured, because the colour/order/wording checks passed on a stylesheet that was never written (§138.6b) |

menu open; fourteen student routes at five widths in both the bought and not-yet states; the payment
journey including the **real Toss 결제창**; and both console logins with the role disclosure and an
invalid-password state.

## The consoles, after the shared header changed

Agency and University do **not** use `ConsoleShell`'s `.hg-topbar` — they render the YNEX `app-header` and
place `NotificationBell` and `UserMenu` inside it. Checked after the change: the bell button measures
38 × 38 and the badge 16 × 16 in both; the badge's ring falls back to `--hg-surface` (#FFFFFF), which is
exactly what the YNEX header is painted, so it reads correctly without a token of its own; the console
keeps its own blue badge (`html[data-surface='console']`), because orange means something different there.
`qa:agency` and `qa:university` are unchanged and green.

## Native (brief Part 23)

`apps/student-mobile` has **no purchase flow** — it is a companion app (home, explore, applications,
documents, messages, visa, profile) and never had a services screen. So there is nothing to duplicate and
nothing to migrate: the payment state machine is the server's, and when the native app needs to sell, it
should open the same `/services` route in a system browser and return through a deep link to the same
success route. Building that now would be building a second client for a flow with no caller.

# 147. V17 Independent Product Audit

Written **before** any code changed, against the running stack at `:3100`–`:3103` and the repository as it
stands after V16. Where this disagrees with an earlier section, the measurement below is what the browser
actually does today.

V16 closed the defects it set out to close and said so with evidence. V17's brief is not a defect list —
it is a change of what the product *is*: a free discovery product that sells a paid managed service, priced
in USD, to students who are not in Korea and do not hold Korean cards. Measured against that, the product
has four structural gaps and a set of smaller ones.

## The four structural gaps

| # | Gap | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **There is no paywall.** | Signing in as `student.new@demo.hangyul.kr` (no paid plan) lands on the full Student dashboard, and `/applications`, `/documents`, `/essays` and `/visa` all render their real screens. The managed service is free to anyone with an account |
| 2 | **The free product is inside the paid app.** | The quick check lives at `student-web /start`, and its results link to `/explore?tab=foryou` — a Student route. A visitor who wants "which Korean universities fit me" is sent into the product they have not bought |
| 3 | **A university page is a registry record, not a reason to go.** | `/universities/pusan-national-university` renders four sections: a name, a 4-row table (지역 · 학교 구분 · 설립 구분 · 공시 학과 수), two IEQAS notes and an official-links block. No hero image, no logo, no identity sentence, no philosophy, no campus life, no video |
| 4 | **The currency the product advertises cannot be charged.** | See §152. `PLANS` is typed `currency: 'KRW'`, and the supplied `HANGYUL` test MID is a KRW MID — verified against the live provider, not inferred |

## The smaller ones, all reproduced

| Area | What the browser does |
|---|---|
| Motion | One duration for everything cinematic: `--hg-motion-reveal: 640ms` drives `rise`, `fade` and `stagger`; `media` adds a `760ms` clip-path; the hero is `1400ms`; the stagger step is `80ms`. A heading, a 1440 px photograph and a 13 px caption all arrive in 640 ms |
| Mobile nav | The bottom bar holds **four** items (홈 · 대학 · 지원 현황 · 메시지) and **더보기 is in the top bar** — the one control the brief says must move down |
| Language sheet | At 390 × 844 the sheet's scroller measures `scrollHeight 1180 === clientHeight 1180`: nothing is constrained, so the box is 1180 px tall inside an 844 px viewport and the entries below the fold are unreachable. `overflow-y: auto` is set and does nothing, because there is no `max-height` for it to act against |
| Markets | **31**, not 32. `MARKETS` in `packages/i18n/src/markets.ts` has 31 entries and `apps/flags` holds 31 SVGs. **Nepal is absent**, and `docs/qa/v14/LOCALE_MATRIX.md` already records the missing 32nd market as an open question |
| Locale selector | Exposes every bundle it finds, not the approved market set — the consumer picker and the 31-market manifest disagree |
| University data | 425 institutions in `server/app/data/korean_institutions.json`. Of those: **302** carry an English name, **281** a website URL, **0** a logo, **0** a mission or philosophy, **0** media, **0** official video |
| Refunds | Still not implemented. `Order` has no cancellation path and `/v1/payments/cancel` is never called — V16 §144's stated blocker, unchanged |
| Review build | Does not exist. Every app's data comes from `/api/v1` at runtime; with FastAPI down there is nothing to share |

## What is genuinely working and is not to be touched

The Koreanasha marketing identity and the white editorial homepage; the pricing composition as recomposed
in V15 b and corrected in V16 (one shared hairline, no clipping, a legible comparison); the university
marquee; the student journey model; the Agency operating system and the University decision/analytics
model; the entitlement architecture; the **server-owned Order/Payment state machine** and its idempotency,
ownership and amount-integrity guarantees; URL locale persistence; test-login gating and its build-time
boundary; and every gate from `qa:v12` through `qa:v16`.

V17 changes the commercial model and the access model. It does not re-open any of the above.

# 148. V17 Conversion & Journey Audit

## The journey today, measured

```
homepage  유학 준비 ──▶ student-web /start  (3 questions)
                          ├─ signed out ──▶ /register?next=/services?plan=…
                          └─ results ─────▶ /explore?tab=foryou      ← inside the paid app
pricing CTA ──▶ /start?plan=… ──▶ register ──▶ /services ──▶ Toss 결제창 (KRW)
```

Two things are wrong with it, and they are the same thing twice: **the free product and the paid product
are the same application.** A visitor who has bought nothing is given an account, a dashboard, a document
locker and a visa case. There is nothing left to sell, and nothing to pay for.

## What the free product has to be

The brief states it plainly (§19): nationality, study type, language qualification → recommended Korean
universities, no payment, no dashboard. That is a **public** experience and it belongs on the marketing
site, where it can be indexed, shared, and opened without an account.

```
marketing /  ──▶ /start (3 questions, public) ──▶ /start results
                                                    └─▶ /universities/<slug>?lang=…&from=recommendation
                                                          └─▶ "이 대학으로 유학 준비하기" ──▶ #pricing
                                                                └─▶ auth ──▶ /services ──▶ USD checkout
```

## Where a visitor can currently bypass payment

| Entry | Today | Must become |
|---|---|---|
| `student-web /` signed in, no plan | Full dashboard | `/services` — choose a plan |
| `/applications`, `/documents`, `/essays`, `/visa`, `/housing`, `/arrival`, `/messages` | Render | Redirect to `/services` with the reason |
| `/profile`, `/settings`, `/services`, `/more`, `/support` | Render | **Stay reachable** — an account is not a purchase, and a student must be able to see and delete their own data |

The split matters: the paywall is on the **managed service**, not on the account. Locking a student out of
their own profile because they have not paid is a different product decision, and a worse one.

## Upgrade

There is no upgrade path at all today: `/services` offers the two other plans as flat alternatives with no
notion of a difference in price, and nothing in the product knows that a Basic student has just tried to do
something All-in-One includes. §24 asks for the opposite of a banner — an offer that appears **only** at
the moment a capability is refused. That requires the refusal to be a product event rather than a 403.

# 149. V17 Global Localization Audit

## The manifest problem

There are three lists and they disagree:

| Source | Count | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/i18n/src/markets.ts` → `MARKETS` | **31** | Country + flag asset + served locale + three names |
| `apps/flags/*.svg` | **31** | The owner's flag files |
| `packages/i18n/locales/*` | **52** | Every translation bundle that exists, including ~20 at 0 % |

The consumer selector renders from the **locale bundles**, so a student sees entries for markets the
business does not serve and bundles that are empty. The brief's requirement is exactly one list of
**32** markets, consumed by marketing, student web and student native alike.

Two filenames in `apps/flags` do not match the country they depict — the French tricolour ships as `GP.svg`
and the Polish flag as `ID2.svg` — and `markets.ts` already handles this by keeping `asset` (the owner's
filename) separate from `code` (the real ISO country). That separation is correct and stays.

## Nepal

Absent from `MARKETS`, absent from `apps/flags`. The `ne` locale bundle exists and is the **third
best-covered student bundle in the product at 99 %**, behind only `en` and `ko` — so Nepali is already
translated and simply has no market entry or flag to be selected by. This is a wiring gap, not a
translation gap.

Nepal's flag is the only non-rectangular national flag in the world — two stacked pennons. Every other
asset in `apps/flags` is a 3:2 or 4:3 rectangle, and `.hg-flag` renders at `width: 20; height: 14` with
`object-fit` behaviour inherited from the img default. Dropping a Nepal SVG into that will stretch it.
The flag component needs a per-asset aspect ratio, not a crop.

## The flag-rendering complaint

The owner reports flags failing while names render. Reproduced at 390 in the student sheet: **17 of 17
flags loaded**, so it is not failing in that path. The paths where it plausibly does, and which this pass
must check rather than assume:

1. `flagUrl()` returns `/flags/<code>.svg` — an **absolute** path, which breaks under any non-root base,
   including a static review build served from a subdirectory.
2. `scripts/media/sync-flags.mjs` copies `apps/flags` into each app's `public/flags`; an app that is not
   in that script's list has no flags at all.
3. The native app cannot serve from `public/` — Metro resolves assets through `require`, so a URL-based
   flag renders nothing in React Native.

(3) is almost certainly the owner's report: the selector is the same component, the names come from the
manifest and render, and the flags are URLs that Metro never bundles.

## Translation completeness, measured

`npm run i18n:check`, student namespace: `en`/`ko` 100 %, `ne` 99 %, `ar`/`mn`/`my`/`uz`/`vi` 98 %,
`zh-Hans` 97 %, `ja` 89 %, `ru` 88 %, `zh-Hant` 87 %, then a cliff — `bn`/`es`/`fil`/`fr`/`hi`/`kk`/`ky`/
`tr`/`ur` at 71 %, `id`/`th` at 68–69 %, and `agency`/`university` at **0 %** for every non-en/ko locale.

The agency and university consoles are staff tools and their English fallback is defensible. The critical
consumer flows are not, and §16 names them: marketing, the free recommendation, university detail, student
core, pricing, plan selection, payment and upgrade.

# 150. V17 University Content Coverage Audit

## What exists

`server/app/data/korean_institutions.json` — 425 active institutions, generated from 대학알리미
(academyinfo.go.kr, survey year 2025) and cross-checked against Study in Korea's IEQAS list.

| Field | Coverage |
|---|---|
| `name_ko`, `institution_type`, `establishment`, `region`, `major_count`, `ieqas` | 425 / 425 |
| `name_en` | 302 / 425 (71 %) |
| `website_url` | 281 / 425 (66 %) |
| `wikidata_id`, `latitude`/`longitude` | partial |
| logo · hero media · gallery · mission/philosophy · founding year · international office page · official YouTube · official intro video | **0 / 425** |

Composition: 218 universities, 163 junior colleges, 44 graduate universities. 173 IEQAS-certified, 43
IEQAS-excellent, 118 with a certified language programme.

## What the public page renders from it

Four sections, all of them registry fields. The first thing a prospective student reads about 부산대학교 is
a table row that says `공시 학과 수 — 142개`. The brief's test ("Can I imagine myself studying here?")
cannot be met by this data no matter how it is styled: **the content is missing, not the design.**

## The honest shape of the work

This is a data-acquisition project, and the brief is explicit that it must not be met by inventing facts or
by copying images that are not licensed. The constraints that decide what is achievable:

- **Facts** can be sourced at scale. Wikidata is CC0 and carries, for Korean universities, official
  website (P856), inception (P571), logo image (P154), motto/mission (P1451), student count (P2196),
  coordinates and **official YouTube channel ID (P2397)** — all machine-queryable, all attributable.
- **Logos are trademarks.** A Commons file being *hosted* does not make it redistributable; many Korean
  university logos there are non-free. Each candidate's licence has to be read per file.
- **Campus photography** is the hardest. "Official university photo" is not a licence (§29). The
  defensible sources are CC0/CC-BY-SA Commons images of the campus, assets the university publishes under
  an explicit reuse licence, and nothing else.
- **Official video** can be *embedded* without redistribution rights — that is what the YouTube embed is
  for — but the channel must be verified as the university's own, not a vlog (§30).

So the plan is a **pipeline plus honest coverage**, not a claim of 425/425: enrich every institution with
every CC0 fact available, resolve logos and media only where the licence permits, verify official channels
where they can be verified, and publish the exact per-field coverage in
`docs/qa/v17/UNIVERSITY_ENRICHMENT.csv`. A page with four sourced facts and no photograph, laid out
honestly, is worth more than a page with a stolen hero image.

## Mobile web

| | Today | Required |
|---|---|---|
| Bottom bar | 4 items: 홈 · 대학 · 지원 현황 · 메시지 | 5, and **더보기 must be one of them** |
| 더보기 | A `<Link to="/more">` in the **top** bar (`AppLayout.tsx` `MoreMenu`, `hg-mobile-only`) | Gone from the top bar |
| Top bar at 390 | logo · nav · 더보기 · locale · bell · avatar | logo · locale · bell · avatar |
| `/more` | A page of three grouped lists | Keep, as the destination of the new tab |

The top bar currently carries six controls at 390 px. The brief's instruction and the measurement agree.

## Page heads

V16's own hostile audit named this and did not fix it: thirteen student screens open with a near-black band
carrying a radial tangerine disc. V16 made it shorter and fixed the arc's geometry; it is still the same
band thirteen times, and it is still the most console-like thing in the consumer product. §38 asks for it
to stop being a template.

## Native

`apps/student-mobile` is a companion: home, explore, universities, applications, documents, messages,
visa, tasks, notifications, saved, matches, profile. There is **no services screen, no plan, no payment,

The constraint that must not be relaxed: **one backend state machine.** Native gets screens; it does not
get a second definition of what a plan is or when a payment succeeded.

# 152. V17 Payment Contract / USD Audit

## What the provider documentation says, re-verified today

From Toss Payments' current 해외결제 guide (`docs.tosspayments.com/guides/v2/learn/foreign-payment`),
read 2026-10-20:

1. **Overseas card payment requires a separate contract.** Registration takes ~2 business days after the
   request.
2. **An additional card-company review follows**, stated as **영업일 10–14일** (10–14 business days),
   before overseas cards are enabled.
3. **Overseas cards settle in KRW by default.** Multi-currency (USD, JPY …) requires **another separate
   contract**; the supported currencies and terms are a sales-team question (1544-7772).
4. **One MID holds exactly one currency** — "하나의 MID는 하나의 통화만 가질 수 있어요." A KRW MID and a
   USD MID are different merchant IDs. Foreign currency is configured under 이용서비스 → 외화결제.

(4) is the finding that decides the architecture, and it is the one V16 could not have known because V16
was not selling in USD.

## What the supplied merchant configuration actually does — verified, not assumed

The `HANGYUL` test MID (client key `test_ck_PBal…`) was driven directly against the live sandbox with the
same call the product makes, changing only the currency:

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `amount: { value: 499000, currency: 'KRW' }` | The real 결제창 renders: All-in-One, 499,000원, 간편결제 and nine card issuers, Toss's own test badge (V16 §142 evidence) |
| `amount: { value: 349, currency: 'USD' }`, `card.useInternationalCardOnly: true` | The window opens and **fails**: `일시적인 오류가 발생했습니다 / 처리 중 오류가 발생했습니다` |

Evidence: `docs/qa/v17/payment/toss-usd-refused-testmid.png`.

**Conclusion: the supplied test MID is a KRW MID and cannot take a USD payment.** This is consistent with
the documentation rather than a transient fault — a KRW MID is contracted for one currency and USD is not
it. Sending `currency: 'USD'` from code does not create a USD merchant.

A second, independent constraint points the same way: the `test_ck_…` key family drives 결제창(구버전),
whose `requestPayment` reference states that 일반결제 supports **KRW only**. USD overseas payment is a
주문서형/결제창형 product, which needs a `test_gck_…` key that this merchant has not been issued.

## What this means for V17

The brief's rule (§5) — *do not silently charge KRW for a USD product* — is therefore not a style
preference, it is the only correct behaviour available. The product must:

- price in USD, everywhere, as the canonical commercial model;
- **refuse to open a live USD checkout** until the contracts exist, behind explicit server-owned readiness
  flags (§9);
- never substitute a KRW order for a USD price;
- and record the contract status as **UNKNOWN — OWNER ACTION REQUIRED** where it cannot be verified from
  this machine, because merchant-admin access is not available here.

`docs/payments/TOSS_FOREIGN_CARD_REVIEW.md` carries the full record, including the four requests Hangyul
has to make of Toss.

## Refunds

Still absent, still the stated launch blocker. V17 builds the **technical** path — an authorised
cancellation endpoint, the provider cancel call, refund state, amount, timestamp, provider reference,
audit and idempotency — and deliberately does **not** invent the legal policy. `release:check` must keep
failing on the policy until a person approves one.

# 153. V17 Server-Free Review Strategy

## The requirement

A stakeholder must be able to open links on **2026-10-21** and walk marketing, student, agency and
university with FastAPI, Postgres and Redis all switched off.

## Why the obvious approaches are wrong

- **Scattering `if (reviewMode)`** through components contaminates production logic with a second
  behaviour per screen, and every component then has two states nobody tests together. The brief rules it
  out and it is right to.
- **A mock service worker** intercepts at the network layer, which is closer, but it ships an interceptor
  into the production bundle and fails on the first request it does not know about.
- **A second codebase** diverges within a week.

## The architecture

There is already exactly one boundary where product code meets the server: `@hangyul/api-client`'s
`createClient()`, which every app constructs once and passes into `AuthProvider`. That is the seam.

```
build time   scripts/review/export-fixtures.mjs
             → signs in as each seeded persona against a live dev stack
             → captures every GET the review routes need
             → writes packages/api-client/fixtures/<persona>.json

run time     createClient({ transport: REVIEW ? fixtureTransport(bundle) : fetchTransport })
             REVIEW = import.meta.env.VITE_REVIEW_MODE === 'true'   ← folded at build time
```

One `transport` seam, one build-time constant, zero component changes. A production build leaves
`VITE_REVIEW_MODE` unset, the constant folds to `false`, and Vite drops the fixture bundle exactly as it
drops the test-login chunk today — the pattern V16 §138.6b arrived at the hard way, reused deliberately.

Fixtures are captured from the real API against seeded data, so the review build shows the real product
with real shapes, not hand-written mock objects that drift.

## Payment in review mode

The brief is precise and the reasoning is sound: reviewers must be able to inspect plan selection, the
order surface, and the success and failure screens, but the build must not **fake a successful
transaction**. So the deterministic preview states are reachable by route, and the one place that would
contact a provider — the pay button — shows a restrained line at that boundary and nowhere else. The rest
of the build looks like the product, because it is the product.

## Deployment

The repository has no hosting credentials and this pass will not create a paid account. The deliverable is
therefore the complete static artefact plus the single remaining step, written down — and if no link
exists, §162 will say no link exists.

# 154. V17 Simplification Plan

Ordered by what it removes. Every addition below states what it replaces and why it needs no new nav item.

| # | Change | Replaces | Why no new nav item |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Move the quick check to marketing** as the public free product | `student-web /start` as the entry point | It is reached from the homepage's existing primary CTA |
| 2 | **Recommendations link to the public university page** | Links into `/explore?tab=foryou` | It is a link, not a destination in a menu |
| 3 | **Paywall the managed service** | An unpaid dashboard that sells nothing | It *removes* reachable surfaces |
| 4 | **Contextual upgrade sheet** | Nothing — this is new | It appears only on refusal, never in navigation |
| 5 | **더보기 moves to the bottom bar** | 더보기 in the top bar | It is the same destination, one bar lower; the top bar loses a control |
| 6 | **One market manifest** consumed by three apps | Three disagreeing lists | Data, not UI |
| 7 | **University page becomes an editorial composition** | The four-section registry table | Same route, same link |
| 8 | **USD replaces KRW in the manifest** | `currency: 'KRW'` | Data, not UI |
| 9 | **Refund API** | Nothing | Server-side; the only UI is a status line in the existing history |
| 10 | **Review transport** | Nothing | Invisible; a build flag |
| 11 | **Differentiated motion durations** | One 640 ms for everything | Tokens |

**Deliberately not done**: no new top-level navigation anywhere; no KRW/USD toggle or FX display; no
billing keys or subscriptions; no second payment state machine; no webhook; no redesign of Agency or
University beyond regression; no upgrade banners; no comparison table in the upgrade sheet.

# 155. V17 Implementation Log

Ordered by what each change removes or decides, not by file.

## 155.1 Motion — four entrance durations instead of one

`packages/design-tokens/src/index.ts`. V14 shipped one entrance duration and every non-media reveal used
it, so a 42 px section heading, a paragraph of supporting copy and a 15 px tick all arrived in 640 ms. That
reads as a sweep rather than a composition, because **a duration that is right for a small element is too
short for a large one** — the eye tracks distance.

| | before | after | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `small` (stagger children, ticks, cards) | 640 ms | **780 ms** | +22 % |
| `copy` (ledes, supporting text) | 640 ms | **880 ms** | +38 % |
| `reveal` (section headings — the default) | 640 ms | **920 ms** | +44 % |
| `media` (photography, masked wipes) | 760 ms | **1080 ms** | +42 % |
| `hero` (first-load settle) | 1400 ms | **1400 ms** | already cinematic |
| `stagger` step | 80 ms | **120 ms** | at 80 ms a row of three read as simultaneous |
| `fast` / `base` / `slow` (hover, menus, forms, payment) | 120/180/260 | **unchanged** | a slow interface feels broken; a slow entrance feels composed |

`SectionHead`'s lede moved from `rise` to `fade` with its beat from 120 → 180 ms: against a 920 ms heading,
120 ms made the two read as one event. The marquee's three loops went 46/54/50 → **53/62/58 s** (+15 %,
inside the brief's 10–20 %), keeping their different durations so the rows do not lock into one wall.

## 155.2 USD is the commercial model

`PlanDef.currency` is typed `'USD'` and `amount_minor` is **cents**. $179 / $349 / $599 are fixed list
prices, not a conversion of the won figures.

What was *not* changed, and this is the distinction the brief leaves implicit: **Korean universities still
charge in won.** Tuition, dormitory fees, application fees and the money plan are all still KRW throughout,
because that is what a student will actually be billed by a university. Only Hangyul's own service fee is
in dollars. `money.py`'s `when_totals` already refused to convert between currencies, so the budget shows
a USD line beside KRW lines and sums neither into the other.

Two presentation rules came with it:

- `formatMoney` drops the cents on a whole amount — `$179`, not `$179.00`. A price with `.00` on a card
  reads as a database column rather than as a number somebody chose.
- The thin space that `gap` inserts is now applied **only** to ₩ and ¥. It exists because ₩'s two
  crossbars collide with digits at display size; `$` does not, and `$ 349` was a space nobody asked for.

Korean renders `US$179` and Vietnamese `179 US$` — Intl's own locale-correct forms, which double as the
currency clarification the brief permits.

**Upgrade pricing** is a declared policy (`UPGRADE_POLICY`), not numbers in a component: the difference
between list prices, $170 / $250 / $420, with `status: 'PENDING_APPROVAL'` so a live launch cannot inherit
it silently.

## 155.3 The access model

| | |
|---|---|
| `apps/student-web/src/lib/access.ts` | The line between an account and a purchase, and why it is drawn there |
| `AppLayout.PlanGate` | Redirects an unpaid student from the managed service to `/services?gate=<route>` |
| `components/Upgrade.tsx` | `GateNotice` (why you are here) and `UpgradeSheet` (what you just tried, what it costs) |

The paywall is on the **service**, not on the account. The rule, stated once rather than kept as a list:
**a plan buys Hangyul's labour, not access to your own information or to public facts.** A counsellor, a
document review, an essay review, a managed application and a visa case are work people do; a saved
university, a budget built from published tuition, a scholarship listing and a student's own profile are
not. Nine routes stay open, the two `<Navigate>` aliases of `/explore` among them (§155.15), and the gated
set is exactly `/` plus the eight managed-service routes.

Locking a student out of their own profile because they have not paid is a different and worse product;
locking them out of a counsellor, a document review and a visa case is the product.

One small thing worth recording because it is the kind of detail that makes an interface read as machine
output: the gate notice interpolates a noun into a Korean sentence, so it needed the right postposition.
`koParticle()` (`@hangyul/utils`) computes 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 와/과 and 으로/로 from the final consonant of
the preceding syllable — 지원 관리**는**, 기숙사 지원**은** — instead of printing `은(는)`, which is the Korean
equivalent of "1 item(s)".

## 155.4 The free product moved to the marketing site

`apps/marketing-web/src/pages/Start.tsx`, route `/start`. Three questions, anonymous, no payment, and its
results link to `/universities/<slug>?lang=…&from=recommendation` — the **public** page, not `/explore`
inside the app nobody has bought.

The homepage's two CTAs now differ, which is the point:

```
내 유학 준비 (undirected)  →  /start                              free answer first
plan CTA (decided)        →  /register?next=/services?plan=…      brief §23: plan → auth → checkout
```

V15's rule sent *both* through the quick check. That principle — a conversion action must not open a
password field — still holds for the undirected one. Applying it to the plan button made a visitor who had
already chosen answer three questions in order to buy.

## 155.5 Markets: 31 → 32, and the flag system

| | |
|---|---|
| `markets.ts` | One canonical manifest: market code, flag asset, locale, country names ×3, **language names ×3**, direction, `flagRatio`, products |
| `localeOptions` | Exposes **exactly the 32 markets**, not the 52 bundles |
| `<Flag>` | Sized by height with its own width, inside a fixed-width slot |
| `apps/flags/NP.svg` | Nepal, public domain, with `NP.PROVENANCE.md` beside it |

**The flag bug the owner reported was the selector's, not the asset pipeline's.** The picker rendered from
the locale bundles; a bundle with no market row has no country, so `<Flag code={undefined}>` drew the grey
placeholder. A third of the rows had no flag and some were 0 % translated. The fix is not a fallback image
— it is to stop offering markets the business does not serve, so **every exposed row has a flag by
construction**.

Nepal's flag is the only non-quadrilateral national flag in the world and is portrait at ~0.82 : 1. The old
`20 × 14` with `object-fit: cover` would have cropped it into a rectangle. Every market now declares its own
`flagRatio`, flags size by height, and a pennon gets a `drop-shadow` that follows its silhouette instead of
a rectangular ring. Nepal renders **11.5 × 16**, uncropped.

**Two locales are deliberately not markets**: `my` (Burmese, 98 % — the fourth best-covered student bundle,
with a seeded persona and its own visa-route data) and `zh-Hant` (87 %). Neither has ever had a market row.
V17 did not add one, because the brief names **32** and names **Nepal** as the addition — inventing two
further target markets is a commercial decision, not a wiring fix. §157 flags them for the owner.

## 155.6 The language selector scrolls

`.hg-locale__sheet` was `display: grid` with `max-height: min(78svh, 620px)`, and the scroller inside it
declared `max-height: none`. The list won: at 390 × 844 the scroller measured `scrollHeight 1180 ===
clientHeight 1180` — never a scroller at all, just a very tall box hanging off the bottom of the screen with
`overflow-y: auto` doing nothing. With 32 markets the bottom third was unreachable.

The sheet is a **column flexbox** now and the list is `flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0`. `min-height: 0` is the
load-bearing half: a flex item's automatic minimum size is its content, so without it the scroller still
refuses to be smaller than its list. The selected row also scrolls into view on open, because a reader's own
language is rarely the first row — Nepali is third of 32, Swedish is last.

## 155.7 Mobile: 더보기 moved down

The bottom bar was four items and 더보기 was a link in the **top** bar, which carried six controls at
390 px. The rail stays the four fixed destinations it has been since V11; 더보기 is the fifth tab, pointing
at the `/more` page that already existed. The top bar lost a control and the phone gained one.

## 155.8 Payments: overseas card, USD, and a contract gate

| | |
|---|---|
| `config.py` | Four readiness flags, `usd_readiness`, `live_usd_checkout_enabled` |
| `payments.py` | `useInternationalCardOnly: true`, `methods: ['CARD']`, window language from the reader's locale, and `cancel()` for refunds |
| `student.py` | The currency gate **before an order exists**, `POST /me/orders/{id}/refund`, readiness in `/me/payments/config` |

The currency gate is the heart of it. §152 established that Toss holds **one currency per MID** and that the
supplied `HANGYUL` test MID is a KRW MID — verified by driving a USD `requestPayment` at the live sandbox
and watching the window fail. So a USD price on that merchant is a contract that does not exist, and the
server answers `503 CURRENCY_NOT_CONTRACTED` and **creates nothing**.

Two bugs were found by writing the tests for this, both of which would have surfaced only after the
contract landed — i.e. after a student had already paid:

1. `toss_confirm` still read `if order.currency != "KRW": 409 "Only KRW one-time payments are supported."`
   — a V16 line that would have rejected every confirmation the moment USD went live.
2. The first version of the currency gate ran *after* `db.add(order)`, so a refused checkout left a PENDING
   order behind for the recovery sweep to find. The gate now runs before the order exists.

**Refunds** (`POST /me/orders/{id}/refund`) are the technical path only. `amount_minor` is **required** —
no default, no pro-rata — because Hangyul has no approved refund policy and a request handler is the worst
place to invent one. The idempotency key carries how much has already been refunded, so a retry is a no-op
while a genuine second partial refund is not swallowed as a duplicate of the first.

## 155.9 University content

`scripts/catalog/enrich_universities.py` — one SPARQL query for every Korean higher-education institution
Wikidata knows, matched to the 425-row registry, with each media candidate's licence read from the Commons
API and **anything not reusable dropped rather than downgraded to a warning**.

Three bugs in the pipeline, each of which produced a confidently wrong number, and all three worth
recording because they are the same mistake in different clothes — *trusting a value's shape without
checking it*:

1. A 50-title Commons batch of percent-encoded Hangul filenames ran past the server's URI limit and lost a
   batch to `HTTP 414`. Now POSTed, 25 at a time.
2. MediaWiki normalises underscores to spaces in the titles it echoes back; Wikidata's P154 uses
   underscores. Keying on the raw value missed every multi-word filename.
3. **P154 and P18 do not hold a filename at all** — they hold a `Special:FilePath` URL with the name
   percent-encoded. Taking the raw value as a title meant every lookup was for a page that does not exist.

Before fix 3 the script reported **0 reusable logos** while KAIST's was plainly public domain. After:
14 logos and 38 hero images with verified licences. §158 has the full coverage.

The page composition changed too: 학교 개요 — a four-row registry table whose opening fact about 부산대학교
was `공시 학과 수 — 142개` — was the first content section. The aspirational blocks (logo, founded/size/city,
교육 이념, official video, the recommendation thread) come first now and the table follows them. Nothing was
deleted, and every block renders only when it has a source, so pages are genuinely different lengths.

## 155.10 The server-free review build

`packages/api-client/src/review.ts` · `scripts/review/export-fixtures.mjs` · `scripts/review/build.mjs`.

One seam: `createApiClient` already took a `fetchImpl`, and every app builds its client once in
`bootWebApp`. Review mode is a different `fetch` and **no component knows it exists**. `VITE_REVIEW_MODE` is
a build-time literal, so a production build folds it away and drops both the transport and the fixtures —
the boundary V16 §138.6b arrived at for the test-login chunk, reused deliberately.

Four bugs, found by actually opening the thing rather than by trusting the build:

1. Every app rendered its 404 page at its own root — the routers had no `basename`, so nothing under
   `/marketing/` matched. All four now read Vite's `BASE_URL`.
2. The apps booted to a sign-in screen: the fixture stored a trimmed session object, but `auth.restore()`
   POSTs `/auth/refresh` and hands the result to `setSession`, which needs `access_token`.
3. Then they *still* booted to a sign-in screen, because `import(\`…/fixtures/${client}.json\`)` is not
   statically analysable across a package boundary, so Vite never emitted the chunk and the failure fell
   silently into a `catch`. Four literal imports; the catch now logs.
4. The capture put a seeded account's **real refresh token** into a shared static artefact. Tokens are
   stripped and replaced with a placeholder — the transport never authenticates anything.

Payments are the one place the preview admits what it is: any write answers `503 REVIEW_MODE`, and nothing
else in the build says DEMO, FIXTURE or MOCK anywhere.

## 155.11 The upgrade sheet is wired to a real refusal

`apps/student-web/src/lib/upgrade.tsx`. The sheet existed at §155.3 and nothing raised it, which made it
the weakest thing in this pass — a surface that had never been seen by the event it exists for.

The event already existed on the server. `app/services/entitlements.py` refuses work outside the purchased
plan with `409 { error: 'entitlement_exceeded', entitlement_key, limit, used, add_on_available }`, and two
student actions reach it: moving an application out of DRAFT (`max_managed_applications` — Basic sells 0)
and sending an essay for 첨삭 (`essay_review_rounds` — Basic 0, All-in-One 1, Premium 2). Both landed in
the generic error toast, which told a Basic student that something had gone wrong when nothing had: they
had asked for a thing they had not bought.

`useUpgradeOnRefusal()` claims a mutation failure only when **all** of three things hold — the server said
`entitlement_exceeded` (not a guess from a status code), a higher plan includes it (`planThatUnlocks`), and
there is a sentence for it. Otherwise it returns `false` and the toast handles it as before. Two of those
conditions are there for the same case: a **Premium** student who exhausts a Premium allowance has nothing
above them to buy, and a sheet offering a plan they already own is worse than the plain message it
replaced. The third keeps `max_managed_applications` out of a heading a student reads.

## 155.12 The native app became a product

New: `app/(tabs)/more.tsx` (the fifth tab), `app/services.tsx` (the plan, and the payment hand-off),
`app/settings.tsx`, and `src/plan.ts`. Moved: `profile.tsx` out of the tab group. §160 has the whole
account; the two decisions worth recording here are the ones that constrain everything else.

**The app does not implement payment.** It opens the web checkout in the *system* browser and comes back
by deep link. One payment state machine is the rule that must not bend, and `qa:v17` proves the absence by
walking every source file for the SDK, `requestPayment`, a confirm call, a `paymentKey`, a provider key and
`POST /me/orders`.

**The way back is validated.** `?return=` comes off a query string, so `apps/student-web/src/lib/apphandoff.ts`
accepts only this app's own scheme, keeps it in `sessionStorage` for the length of the Toss round trip, and
*offers* it as a link rather than navigating to it.

And `scripts/i18n/generate-flag-module.mjs` closes the native flag gap §149 recorded: 32 flags inlined into
34.2 KB of generated TypeScript, rendered through `SvgXml` with each market's own ratio, because Metro has
no `public/` directory and the URL the web uses resolves to nothing on a phone. `--check` fails if the
module drifts from `apps/flags/`.

## 155.14 The three English notifications, and what two of them turned out to be

V16's hostile audit recorded "three seeded notification strings are English inside a Korean UI" and
classed them as seed content. Checking each against the bundles: **two of the three are not seed content.**

| Key | Raised by | In any locale? |
|---|---|---|
| `notify.addonOffered` | `api/v1/agency.py` — a counsellor offering an extra service | **no locale at all, including `en`** |
| `notify.documentRequest.fulfilled` | `services/document_requests.py` — the applicant sent what was asked for | **no locale at all, including `en`** |
| `notify.applicationStatus` | the seed only | no — and real transitions raise `notify.application.<STATUS>`, which every locale has |

Because neither existed even in `en`, i18next had nothing to fall back to but the server's English
`fallback_text`, in every language, for as long as the feature has existed. Both are now written in the 12
tier-1 locales; the seed is corrected to the key real transitions use, and the three rows already in the
database were repointed so the running environment matches.

The add-on sentence deliberately does **not** name the service. `{{key}}` is an entitlement key
(`mock_interviews`), its label lives in the student namespace, and `$t()` across namespaces only resolves
when that namespace happens to be loaded. The notification announces and `/services` names it — which it
already did, with the proper label.

**Why V16 got this wrong is the part worth keeping**: the three were found by eye, in a Korean UI, and the
one that looked most like a bug (an application status in English) was the only one that *was* seed-only.
The two real ones looked like seed strings because their `fallback_text` reads like prose. A bundle
lookup settles in a second what staring at a screen cannot.

## 155.13 Two fixes that came from walking the product rather than reading it

Both are small, both were invisible to every check that existed, and both were found the same way — by
opening a page nobody had opened.

**`LegalLayout` called `window.matchMedia` unguarded.** jsdom has none, so `/privacy` and `/terms` rendered
React's error boundary instead of the page whenever the live smoke test ran — and that test is skipped
unless `HG_LIVE_API` is set, so it had not run. Guarded, along with the same hole on a click path in
`Universities.tsx`. The live smoke test is 22 / 22 now, for the first time. §162.1.

**`reviewFetch` could not serve a list page.** Its fallback chain was *exact key → bare path → 404*, and a
list asks for a query the capture does not hold while nothing was ever captured at the bare path. Three of
the review bundle's sixteen links were a 404 as a result. A fourth step now matches any capture of the same
path, preferring the shortest query so an unfiltered request does not land on `?region=Seoul`. §162.2.

## 155.16 A paywall that would not let a student give up

Taking the screenshot for §155.11 found the worst bug of this pass, and it was mine.

`applications.py` has rationed "an application leaving DRAFT" since V15, because a managed application is
what the plan sells. `WITHDRAWN` also leaves DRAFT. So a student whose plan includes **no** managed
applications could not withdraw their own draft — and after V17 wired the upgrade sheet, the refusal they
met offered them a paid plan **so that they could delete something**.

The allowance rations the work Hangyul takes on. Giving a draft up is the opposite of asking for work, and
a boundary that traps someone is not a boundary. `S.WITHDRAWN` is excluded now.

**How the gate missed it, and what that says.** The gate's upgrade-sheet check clicked the first action on
the application page. That page offers a forward action only once the checklist is far enough along, so the
first — and only — action was 지원 철회, and the sheet duly appeared. The assertion passed *because of* the
bug. A check that proves a surface exists will happily be satisfied by the wrong road to it.

The gate drives the sheet through the **essay** now — 검토 요청 on a personal statement spends an
`essay_review_rounds` allowance that Basic sells none of, and it is one click from a screen a student is
already on. The withdrawal rule is asserted where server rules belong, in
`test_withdrawing_a_draft_is_not_rationed`: the same Basic student, the same draft, the forward transition
refused with its numbers and the withdrawal allowed. It is **not** in the browser gate, because driving it
there would leave a withdrawn application behind on every run — the first attempt did, and the next run
failed with *"You already started an application for this intake."* A gate that accumulates rows eventually
fails for reasons that are not the product's.

## 155.17 And the slot it had already spent

Opening the withdrawal path immediately exposed the next layer of the same mistake. The gate's refusal came
back `max_managed_applications **1/0**` for a student who had drafted one application and withdrawn it
without Hangyul ever touching it.

`_used()` counted every application whose status is not `DRAFT`, and `WITHDRAWN` is not `DRAFT`. So a
student who drafted, changed their mind and started again had **permanently burned a slot on work that
never happened**. On Basic (0 slots) it changes nothing; on All-in-One (2) it means withdrawing one draft
costs half of what they bought.

The allowance measures work delivered, not applications once opened, so the test is the history rather than
the status: a withdrawal whose `application_status_history` records nothing but `DRAFT` and `WITHDRAWN`
never left the student's own desk. One that was managed to a real stage and then withdrawn still counts —
that work happened.

This is the second defect in a row that existed only because the first one hid it: a student who could not
withdraw could never reach the miscount. **Opening a path is also a way of testing one**, and both are now
asserted in `test_v17_usd_refunds.py`.

## 155.15 What the e2e suite said about the paywall, and what it changed

The 67-test Playwright suite had not been run in this pass. Run against V17 it produced **11 failures**, and
they sort into three kinds — only one of which was a test needing an update.

**A real defect in the access model (1).** `/matches` and `/saved` are `<Navigate>` aliases of
`/explore?tab=…`. `/explore` was open and the two aliases were not, so a student following a link to their
own saved universities met a paywall at one URL and the page itself at another. That is not a stricter rule,
it is an incoherent one, and no gate caught it because the gate checked `/explore`.

Fixing it properly meant stating the rule rather than patching the list: **a plan buys Hangyul's labour, not
access to your own information or to public facts.** The gated set is now exactly the nine that are labour —
`/` and the eight managed-service routes — and `/matches`, `/saved`, `/compare`, `/budget`, `/scholarships`,
`/help` and `/family` joined the open set. `qa:v17` asserts both halves and the two aliases by name.

**Two real product defects, neither of them V17's (2).**

- `/start` — the free product, and the destination of the site's one conversion action — had **no `h1`**.
  `SectionHead` defaults to `h2`, which is right for a section of the homepage and wrong for a page.
- The profile's section control was labelled **"Add"** and announced **"Edit education"**: `aria-label`
  overrode the visible text unconditionally. A sighted reviewer never sees that; a screen-reader user hears
  it on every incomplete section. `profile.addSection` now exists in the 12 tier-1 locales.

**Journeys the paywall or the contract genuinely ends (8).** Seven specs begin by buying a plan, and the
currency gate refuses — correctly. `e2e/helpers.ts` gained `activatePlan()`, which returns the reason
instead of throwing, so each spec skips with that reason named rather than failing over a contract nobody in
this repository can sign. Nothing is deleted and nothing is faked; the moment the contract lands, or the
stack runs the demo provider, all of them run again untouched. The Nepal flow (`v5-flow-a`) was restructured
rather than skipped wholesale: the plan is activated at the **UI boundary**, so a refusal costs the two
rendering checks and not the consular-legalization evidence that is the point of the test.

Two more specs encoded V17's own deliberate changes and were updated to them: the marketing CTA now opens
`/start` on the marketing origin (§155.4), and the V16 purchase journey is **three clicks** rather than five
because the plan button no longer passes through the quick check (brief §23).

# 156. V17 Marketing & Conversion Validation

**Motion.** Measured from the tokens and the compiled CSS, not asserted: entrance durations 780/880/920/
1080 ms, stagger 120 ms, interface durations unchanged at 120/180/260 ms. `prefers-reduced-motion` is
untouched — the reveal still never arms under it, so nothing moves and nothing is left half-faded.

**Prices.** `qa:v17` reads the rendered card, not the manifest:

```
ko: US$179 · US$349 · US$599
en:   $179 ·   $349 ·   $599
vi: 179 US$ · 349 US$ · 599 US$
no retired KRW plan price (249,000 / 499,000 / 849,000) renders on the homepage
```

**Conversion flow**, verified end to end at a real browser:

```
/ ──내 유학 준비──▶ /start (3 questions, anonymous)
                    └─▶ 6 universities, each a fit in words
                         └─▶ /universities/<slug>?lang=ko&from=recommendation
                              └─▶ 이 대학 유학 준비하기 ──▶ #pricing ──▶ /register?next=/services?plan=…
```

Asserted: three questions and no more; every result links to a **public** university page; the language and
the recommendation context survive the link; **no percentage anywhere** and no 합격/guarantee string.

**Visual defects fixed on the way**: the university header reserved a photograph's worth of empty space when
no licensed photograph existed (V12 gave the typographic variant the immersive variant's `min-height`), and
the new story blocks had no bottom margin, so the video block's provenance line sat on top of the next
section's heading.

**One structural defect, found by the e2e suite**: `/start` — the free product, and the destination of this
site's one conversion action — had **no `h1`**. `SectionHead` defaults to `h2`, which is correct for a
section of the homepage and wrong for a page of its own. `/start` is in the axe route list now, which is
the other half of the fix.

# 157. V17 32-Market Localization Validation

```
markets.ts: 32 rows · Nepal is a market · every asset exists and is published to the web apps
 390px · 32 languages · 32/32 flags · scrolls · Nepal 11.5×16 (portrait)
1440px · 32 languages · 32/32 flags · scrolls · Nepal 11.5×16 (portrait)
```

Zero `hg-flag--none` placeholders at either width — which is the measurement that matters, because the
placeholder *was* the reported bug.

**Translation coverage** for the V17 strings (gate notice, upgrade sheet, quick check, university story,
payment, and the native app's own namespace): **12 locale bundles** — ko, en, vi, ne, my, uz, mn, ar,
zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ja, ru. Every locale whose student bundle is above 85 %.

**But 12 bundles is not 12 markets, and the difference is worth stating rather than rounding.** The 32
markets map to 32 distinct locales; two of the twelve (`my`, `zh-Hant`) are not markets at all. So the V17
strings reach **10 of the 32 markets** — Korea, Vietnam, Nepal, Uzbekistan, Mongolia, China, Japan, the
United States, Saudi Arabia and Russia — and the other **22 fall back to English**, as ~30 % of the student
namespace already does. Those 10 are the markets Hangyul actually recruits from, which is why they were
first; the 22 are a translation task, named as a blocker in §164 and §167 rather than papered over.

**Nepali specifically** is complete for every critical flow added in V17 — the quick check, the results, the
university story, the gate, the upgrade sheet and the payment copy — and `ne` was already the third
best-covered student bundle at 99 %.

Adding Nepal as a market then found something nobody had looked for, because nobody had been sent there:
`ne/marketing.json` carried **no `v11` block at all**, so the homepage a Nepali reader lands on was partly
in English — the hero, the FAQ, the closing CTA and the university rail. V17 translated all 49 strings,
with the markup and placeholders (`<br>`, two `class` attributes, `{{count}}`, `{{n}}`) carried over byte
for byte and asserted identical to English before the file was written. `ne/marketing` went 77 % → 80 %,
and `qa:v14`'s locale pass is clean at 390 px and 1440 px.

This is worth recording as a pattern rather than a fix: **the bundle percentages did not predict it.**
`ne` read 99 % on `student` and 77 % on `marketing`, and the 23 % that was missing happened to be the
homepage. A coverage number tells you how much is translated, not whether what a reader sees first is.

**The native picker is the same list now.** §149 recorded it as a separate defect: the app listed the 52
locale bundles filtered by the V9 native gate, with no flags, so the app and the website offered different
languages. It lists the same 32 markets from the same manifest, with the same flags and the same ratios —
§160.4 has how, and why the cause was never the one the web picker's identical-looking bug had.

**Two locales for the owner to decide on**: `my` (98 %, seeded persona, visa-route data) and `zh-Hant`
(87 %) are translated but are not markets and therefore are not offered. Adding either is a go-to-market
call, not an engineering one.

# 158. V17 University Enrichment Validation

`docs/qa/v17/UNIVERSITY_ENRICHMENT.csv` — 425 rows, one per institution, with the blocking reason on each.

| Field | Coverage | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Registry facts (name_ko, type, establishment, region, major count, IEQAS) | **425 / 425** | 대학알리미 2025 + Study in Korea |
| Matched to an authoritative external record | **325 / 425** (76 %) | Wikidata (CC0) |
| English name | **323 / 425** (76 %) | registry + Wikidata |
| Official website | **298 / 425** (70 %) | registry + Wikidata P856 |
| Founding year | **290 / 425** (68 %) | Wikidata P571 |
| **Licensed logo** | **14 / 425** (3 %) | Commons, licence verified per file |
| **Licensed hero image** | **38 / 425** (9 %) | Commons, licence verified per file |
| **Verified official YouTube channel** | **10 / 425** (2 %) | Wikidata P2397 |
| Mission / 교육 이념 | **5 / 425** (1 %) | Wikidata P1451 |
| Student count | **8 / 425** (2 %) | Wikidata P2196 |

**This is not 425/425 and the brief said not to claim it is.** The three numbers that matter most are the
three lowest, and the reason is the same for all of them: **the data is not publicly licensed, not that it
was not looked for.** 139 media candidates were found and every one's licence was read; 53 resolved on
Commons and 52 of those were reusable, while the remainder live on language-specific Wikipedias under
non-free terms — which is the expected outcome for Korean university logos, and precisely why §29 says an
official photo is not a licence.

So the page is built to be good **without** them: a university with no logo, no photograph and no video
renders as a clean typographic header, an identity line, the registry facts and its official links — and
two universities' pages are genuinely different lengths. A page padded to a fixed shape with empty sections
tells a reader that Hangyul does not know the difference.

**To raise these numbers**, the work is acquisition, not code: a media-use request to each university's
communications office, or a licensing agreement. The pipeline re-runs in one command once assets exist.

# 160. V17 Student Native Validation

The companion app became a product in this pass. What it did **not** become is a second place where money
moves, and that is deliberate.

## 160.1 Five tabs, and 더보기 is one of them

```
홈 · 대학 · 지원 현황 · 메시지 · 더보기
```

The fifth tab used to be 프로필, which is how everything occasional — documents, visa, tasks, saved,
notifications, settings, the plan — ended up as a list at the bottom of a screen with an avatar on it. 프로필
is now one row inside 더보기, which is the same move the mobile web made in this pass and for the same
reason: a drawer should be named a drawer.

## 160.2 Seventeen screens

| | |
|---|---|
| Tabs | 홈 · 대학 (explore) · 지원 현황 · 메시지 · **더보기** |
| Detail | university, application, document, thread |
| Work | documents, visa, tasks, saved, notifications, matches |
| **New in V17** | **플랜** (`app/services.tsx`) · **설정** (`app/settings.tsx`) · 프로필 (pushed, no longer a tab) |

**플랜** shows what was bought and what is left of each allowance, or the plans and a price when nothing is.
**설정** is language, the three things only the web can change (as links, not as duplicate forms), sign-out
and the build version. Each is asserted by `qa:v17` as a file, so the gate fails if one is deleted.

## 160.3 The payment hand-off, and the rule it keeps

**One backend state machine.** `qa:v17` walks every `.ts`, `.tsx` and `.json` file under
`apps/student-mobile/app` and `src` and fails on any of: the Toss SDK, a `requestPayment` call, a payment
confirmation, a `paymentKey`, a provider key, or `POST /me/orders`. **None of them appears.**

What the app does instead:

```
플랜 → 결제하기
  → Linking.openURL(`${web}/services?plan=…&lang=ko&return=hangyul-student://services&from=app`)
  → the system browser, where the web session and the 결제창 live
  → Toss → /services/payment/success → the web app confirms the order
  → "앱으로 돌아가기" → hangyul-student://services
  → useFocusEffect refetches /me/services, and the plan is simply there
```

The **system** browser, not a WebView: 3-D Secure and an overseas issuer's own app both need to leave the
page and come back, and a WebView is where that breaks.

Three details that are the actual work in that diagram:

- **Toss decides where the browser lands**, so the `?return=` the app passed is gone by the time the
  student sees a confirmation. It is kept in `sessionStorage` for the length of the round trip
  (`apps/student-web/src/lib/apphandoff.ts`) and no longer.
- **It is offered, never followed.** A confirmation page that navigates itself to a custom scheme is
  blocked by most browsers, and in the rest it looks like a hijack. `qa:v17` fails on a
  `window.location =` in that file for exactly this reason.
- **`?return=` is attacker-controlled.** A page that forwards a student to any scheme it is handed is an
  open redirect with a payment confirmation for cover. Only `hangyul-student://` and Expo's
  `exp+hangyul-student://` are accepted, plus Expo's LAN form off a production build.
  `apps/student-web/src/lib/v17.test.ts` asserts the refusals one by one — `https://evil.example/collect`,
  `javascript:`, `data:`, `intent://`, `//evil.example/`, `hangyul-agency://`, `hangyul-studentX://`.

## 160.4 The native flag gap is closed

§149 recorded that the native picker showed language names with an empty space where the flag should be,
and that the cause was **not** the one the web picker's identical-looking bug had: the web assets are
published as URLs and Metro has no `public/` directory, so on a phone that URL resolves to nothing.

`scripts/i18n/generate-flag-module.mjs` inlines the 32 flags into `packages/mobile-ui/src/flags.generated.ts`
— **34.2 KB for all of them**, which is cheaper than any loader — and `<MarketFlag>` renders them through
`react-native-svg`'s `SvgXml` with each market's own `flagRatio`, so Nepal is a narrow flag rather than a
cropped rectangle, exactly as on the web.

The picker itself changed with it: `surface="student"` now lists **the 32 markets** from the same manifest
the web reads, with each language named in that language and the country beside it (two markets share
`en`; the country is what tells them apart). It used to list the 52 locale bundles filtered by the V9
native gate — which meant the app and the website offered different languages. The footer note that said
"a language appears here once every student screen is translated" was removed rather than reworded: it
stopped being true, and the rows that are not fully translated already say so, on the row.

Profile **editing**, the essay editor, the full 플랜별 비교표, receipts and plan history. Each is a link

**What this pass did not do**: the native app has no offline cache and no local draft, so a student on a
