# 162. V17 Server-Free Review Validation

Built: `npm run review:build` → `dist-review/` — **2,125 files, 102.1 MB**, four apps plus an index.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `localhost` / loopback in any emitted file | **0** |
| Requests to any API origin while walking all four apps at 390 and 1440 | **0** |
| Marketing root | renders the real homepage |
| University deep link (`/marketing/universities/kaist`) | renders, with real content |
| Student / Agency / University | render **signed in**, with real seeded data |
| DEMO / FIXTURE / MOCK anywhere in the UI | **none** |
| Payment action | `503 REVIEW_MODE`, at that boundary only |
| Tokens in the bundle | **0 JWT-shaped strings** |
| Review mode in a **production** build | **0 references** to `REVIEW_MODE`, `reviewFetch`, `REVIEW_MISS`, the placeholder token or the fixture imports, in all four apps' `dist/` |
| The bundle's own index | a tour of 16 named links across the four apps, not four app roots |
| Every tour link renders | **yes** — 4 roots + 1 deep link + 11 paths, asserted by `qa:v17` |

**Hosting requirement**, and it is the one thing a reader must not miss: the four apps are SPAs, so the
host must fall back to each app's `index.html` for unknown paths. The build emits `404.html` per app, which
covers GitHub Pages, S3 website hosting, Netlify and Cloudflare Pages without configuration. A bare
`python -m http.server` has no fallback and 404s on deep links — verified both ways.

## Deployment

**No link exists, and this section will not pretend one does.** The brief asked for a server-free review
build with working links by **2026-10-21**. The build exists, every link on it has been clicked, and it is
a day early — but a link a stakeholder can open needs a host, and a host needs credentials this repository
does not have and that §4 of the brief forbids creating. That step is §167.6.

The repository has no hosting credentials and this pass did not create a paid account. The artefact is
complete and verified. The single remaining step is external:

```
# any static host; the bundle is self-contained and origin-relative
npx wrangler pages deploy dist-review          # or
aws s3 sync dist-review s3://<bucket> --delete # or drag dist-review/ onto Netlify
```

If the bundle is served from a subdirectory rather than an origin root, rebuild with
`BASE=/your-path/ npm run review:build` so each app's router gets the right basename.

**Against the 2026-10-21 date**: the artefact is ready a day early. The deployment is blocked only on
credentials, which are the owner's to supply.

**One addition for the reviewer's sake.** The bundle's root used to be four links — the four app roots —
which left a stakeholder to find their own way around a product they have not seen. It is now a named tour
of sixteen routes: the homepage, the free quick check, the 425-university directory, one university as a
story, the pricing section, and the five screens of each console worth looking at. Every path on it is one
the fixtures answer. The brief asked for "working links", and four roots is not that.

## 162.2 Three of the sixteen links were a 404, and the fallback was why

Publishing a tour meant walking it, and walking it found that `/marketing/universities`,
`/agency/students` and `/university/applicants` — the three **list** pages — rendered the apps' 404 state.

Not a routing bug: the transport's miss. A list page asks for `?page=1&page_size=24&sort=…`; the capture
holds `?page=1&page_size=24`. Resolution was *exact key → path with no query → 404*, and the middle step
cannot bridge a query that differs, because nothing was ever captured at the bare path. So a reviewer
clicking the 425-university directory met "we couldn't find that page" in a build that contains all 425.

`reviewFetch` has a fourth step now: **any** capture of the same path, whatever query it carries, choosing
the one with the **shortest** query — so a request with no filter falls back to the unfiltered capture
rather than to `?region=Seoul`. The index is built once per bundle and only consulted on a miss.

Walked again: every link on the index renders real content, with **0 requests to any API origin**. The
three that failed now show the directory, the agency's students and the university's applicants. `qa:v17`
walks it on every run — the four app roots, a university deep link and the **11** remaining tour paths;
the sixteenth link is `#pricing`, which is the homepage with an anchor rather than a page of its own.

This is the second thing in this pass that only a walk would find (§162.1 is the first), and both were in
the same place: a surface nobody had opened. The gate opened four app roots and one deep link, all five of
which were fine; the pages that were broken were the ones no check had asked for.

## 162.1 One real bug the review work found

`npm run test:web` skips `apps/marketing-web/src/test/smoke.live.test.tsx` unless `HG_LIVE_API` is set, so
it had not been run in this pass. Run against the live API, **two of its 22 routes failed**: `/privacy` and
`/terms` rendered React's error boundary, not the page.

`LegalLayout` called `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 1200px)')` unguarded, and jsdom has no `matchMedia`.
Every other call site in the product guards it — `usePhone`, the locale selector — and these two did not
(`Universities.tsx` had the same hole on a click path). It is pre-V17 code and a browser never sees it, but
it is not only a test problem: any environment without `matchMedia` takes the **whole legal page** down,
and the legal pages are the two the product is legally obliged to show. Guarded now, and the live smoke
test is **22 / 22** — which is the first time all of it has been green, because the two failures were
hidden behind a skip.

Worth recording as the lesson rather than the fix: **a test that is skipped by default is not a test.**
This one had been in the repository for several passes, and the thing it would have caught was sitting in
the two pages nobody clicks.

Each of these is expanded, with who can clear it, in **§167 — V17 Owner Actions**.

# 165. V17 Final Hostile Audit

**"You found four product bugs by taking screenshots and running tests that already existed. What does
that say about the gates?"** That a check written to prove a surface exists will be satisfied by the wrong
road to it, and that a test skipped by default is not a test. Both halves showed up in one afternoon: the
upgrade-sheet check passed *because* withdrawal was wrongly refused (§155.16), and `/privacy` and `/terms`
had been rendering an error boundary behind a default skip for several passes (§162.1). The honest reading
is that this pass's gates are better than its predecessors' and still not a substitute for opening the
product — which is how the remaining two were found: a review index whose own links 404'd (§162.2) and an
allowance spent on work never done (§155.17).

**"Slower motion is just sluggish."** It would be if one multiplier had been applied to everything — which
is what the first draft of this change would have been. The durations differ *by what is entering*, 780 to
1080 ms, and interface motion is untouched at 120/180/260 ms. A button still responds in 120 ms. If the
homepage feels slow, the number to change is `reveal`, not all seven.

**"You priced in USD but you cannot charge USD. That is a fake feature."** It is an honest half-feature, and
the alternative was dishonest. The brief's §5 forbids silently charging KRW for a USD product, and §152
established *why* that is not a preference: Toss holds one currency per MID, so the fallback would charge an
amount nobody quoted. The product advertises what it will charge and refuses to take money it cannot take
in that currency. The readiness flags make which contract is missing visible rather than discoverable.

**"Did the code just send `USD` and call it done?"** No — and the evidence is a provider refusal, not an
assertion. A USD `requestPayment` on the supplied MID opens the window and fails; the screenshot is in the
repository. §161 says no real USD transaction has occurred.

**"3 % logo coverage is a failure."** It is a *licensing* result, and reporting it as 3 % is the point. 139
candidates were found, every licence was read, and the ones that may not be redistributed were dropped
rather than used. The brief's §29 asks for exactly this and §33 forbids claiming 425/425. What would have
been a failure is 425 pages with stolen hero images.

**"Then the university pages are empty."** They are *shorter*, and differently shaped. KAIST opens with
`1971년 설립 · 재학생 10,249명 · 대전광역시`, its official channel with the date it was verified, and the
registry facts below. Seoul National adds a licensed logo and a campus gallery. Neither leads with a
deadline or a document checklist, which is what the brief actually asked to change.

**"Does Nepal really work, or does it just appear?"** 11.5 × 16, portrait, uncropped, with a drop-shadow
following the pennon silhouette rather than a rectangle drawn around it — asserted by the gate at two
widths, which fails if the rendered width ever exceeds the height.

**"Can I scroll all 32?"** `scrollHeight > clientHeight` and the sheet's bottom inside the viewport, both
measured at 390 and 1440. The bug was that neither was true: the box was 1180 px tall in an 844 px viewport.

**"Can an unpaid user sneak into the paid product?"** Eight managed routes redirect, nine account and
discovery routes do not, and both halves are asserted — because a paywall that also locks a student out of
their own profile is a different bug, not a stricter version of the same one.

**"Did the paywall break anything?"** Twice, and both are recorded rather than buried. It gated `/matches`
and `/saved`, which are `<Navigate>` aliases of a page that stayed open — found by the e2e suite (§155.15).
And the managed-application allowance refused a **withdrawal**, so a student on the smallest plan could not
delete their own draft and was offered an upgrade in order to (§155.16). The second is the worse of the two
and my gate had been passing *because of* it: the check clicked the first action on the page, and on an
unfinished draft the only action is 지원 철회.

**"Where could this still be sold badly?"** Two places. The plan CTA now skips the free quick check, which
is right for someone who has chosen but means a visitor who clicks a price before understanding the product
meets a registration form — the homepage has to carry that understanding, and it does, but it is the seam
to watch. The upgrade sheet was the other one, and it is wired now: a Basic student moving a draft application
forward, or sending an essay for 첨삭, gets the server's own `entitlement_exceeded` turned into the next
plan instead of an error toast (`apps/student-web/src/lib/upgrade.tsx`). `qa:v17` produces that refusal
against the running server and reads what the student sees — *자기소개서 첨삭은 올인원에서 이용할 수
있어요.*, 현재 플랜 베이직, US$170 1회 결제, one CTA, no comparison table. It is narrow on purpose: when a **Premium** student
exhausts a Premium allowance there is nothing above them to sell, so the hook declines the error and the
plain message stands, because the counsellor's add-on is the real next step there.

**"The native app is a shell with five tabs."** It has 17 screens, every one against the API the web uses,
and it bundles — `expo export` produces a 19 MB Hermes bundle. What it does not have is a payment of its
own, and `qa:v17` proves the absence rather than asserting it: no SDK, no `requestPayment`, no confirm, no
`paymentKey`, no provider key, no `POST /me/orders` in any file. A student pays in the system browser and
comes back by a deep link that is validated against an allowlist, because the alternative — a native
payment path — is how a second answer to "has this student paid" gets created.

**"What still looks unfinished?"** University photography (9 %, licensing); V17's strings missing in 22
of the 32 markets; the native app's lack of any offline cache, so a poor connection shows loading states instead of
last-known data; and the student page-head band, which V16's own hostile audit named and V17 did not get
to either. The first two are acquisition and translation work; the last two are real engineering I did not
do in this pass.

Of V16's three leftovers, one is closed and two are reclassified. The **English notification strings** are
fixed (§155.14), and two of the three were never seed content — they existed in no bundle at all. The
`v16.pay.*` strings still reach 12 locales rather than 52, which V16 reported as a gap; it is the same 12
every V17 string reaches, so it is not a payment-specific gap but the one translation blocker in §164.4.
The page-head band is simply not done.


## 165.1 The four defects this pass found in itself

Recorded together because the pattern matters more than any one of them, and because three were V17's own.

| # | Defect | Found by | Why no check had it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `/matches` and `/saved` paywalled while `/explore` was open | the e2e suite | the gate checked the destination, not its aliases |
| 2 | Withdrawing a draft refused by the managed-application allowance | taking a screenshot | the gate's own check passed *because of* it |
| 3 | A never-managed withdrawal spending a managed slot | #2's fix, immediately | the path did not exist to walk |
| 4 | The review bundle's own index linking to three 404s | publishing the index and clicking it | the gate opened four app roots, all fine |

Plus two that predate V17 and had been invisible for the same reason: `/privacy` and `/terms` rendering an
error boundary behind a test skipped by default, and a profile button labelled "Add" that announced "Edit
education".

What they have in common is that **every one was on a road nobody had driven**. The assertions are now
shaped like the defects (§166), but the honest conclusion is the one in §165's first answer: gates are
cheaper than opening the product, and they are not a substitute for it.

## What the suite could not have caught before, and now can

Every V17 defect that mattered was invisible to a green suite, so each one got an assertion shaped like it:

| Defect | New assertion |
|---|---|
| A 1,180 px "scroller" in an 844 px viewport | `scrollHeight > clientHeight` **and** the sheet's bottom inside the viewport, at 2 widths |
| A flag cropped into the wrong shape | the rendered flag measured — Nepal must be taller than it is wide |
| A market offered with no flag | `hg-flag--none` placeholders counted; must be 0 of 32 |
| A paywall that locks a student out of their own data | both halves asserted, and the two `<Navigate>` aliases of `/explore` by name |
| A refused checkout leaving a PENDING order | `pending_order_id` compared **before and after**, not against an empty table |
| A hardcoded currency in a confirm handler | 13 server tests with the contract declared present, so the USD path is exercised at all |
| An upgrade sheet nothing could raise | the gate **produces** a real `entitlement_exceeded` from a screen a student is actually on, and reads what they see |
| A paywall that refuses a *withdrawal* | a server test: the forward transition refused with its numbers, the withdrawal allowed (§155.16) |
| An allowance spent on work never done | the usage count compared before and after a never-managed withdrawal (§155.17) |
| Payment reimplemented in the native app | every native source file scanned for the SDK, `requestPayment`, a confirm, a `paymentKey`, a key, `POST /me/orders` |
| A deep link that forwards a student anywhere | 8 refusals asserted one by one, including `javascript:`, `data:` and `//evil.example/` |
| A review bundle with 404s on its own index | all 16 tour links walked in a browser, with the API origin switched off |
| A generated flag module drifting from `apps/flags` | `--check` mode, run by the gate |
| A stale enrichment claim | the coverage CSV is 425 rows and the gate reads the stored counts, not the script's log |

Everything V17 could not do, in the order it blocks things, with who can do it. Nothing here is engineering
work that was skipped; each one needs an account, a signature or a decision that is the owner's.

|---|---|---|---|

| 8 | **Commission translation** of V17's strings into the other 22 markets | 10 of 32 markets carry them; the rest fall back to English | §157, §164.4 |
| 9 | **Request media-use permission** from university communications offices | 3 % logo and 9 % photo coverage is a licensing result, not a pipeline one | `docs/qa/v17/UNIVERSITY_ENRICHMENT.csv` |
| 10 | **Open Apple and Google developer accounts** | The native app bundles; it cannot be signed or listed | §160.5, §164 |
| 11 | **Verify the 66 published programmes** against official sources | `release:check` MARKETING PREVIEW blocker; V17 verified *institutions*, which is a different object | §164.6 |

**Four of these (1–3, 10) require creating or paying for a third-party account, which §4 of the brief

# 168. V18 Independent Final Product Audit

> **On the honesty of this section.** The V18 brief asks for the audit to be written before implementation.
> It was written *during* the pass, as each finding was verified against the running system, and several
> fixes were applied before the section was committed to the file. Findings whose fix had already landed by
> the time this was written are marked **(fixed in this pass)**; the rest carry their status plainly. An
> audit that claims a sequence it did not follow is worth less than one that reports what happened.
>
> Every finding below was reproduced against the actual repository or the actual running product. Nothing
> here is inferred from a previous section of this report.

### 168.1 The API port was never 8001

- **SCREEN** — none; the whole dev and QA stack.
- **USER QUESTION** — *(engineer)* "Which port is the Hangyul API on?"
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — the brief states the intended API port is **8001**. Every active Hangyul
  configuration used **8000**: `scripts/dev.mjs`, `scripts/api.mjs`, the Vite proxy in
  `packages/config/vite.ts`, `playwright.config.ts`, `e2e/helpers.ts`, the v15/v16/v17 QA gates, the review
  fixture exporter, and `extra.apiUrl` in all three Expo app configs. 28 source references in total.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — the port was never a token. It was a literal repeated in every file that needed it, so
  there was no single place to change and no gate that could notice the disagreement.
- **SEVERITY** — **P1.** Nothing was broken, but the documentation and the brief disagreed with the code, and a
  reader following the brief would have started the stack on a port nothing talked to.
- **FIX** *(fixed in this pass)* — migrated all 28 references to 8001, including the `10.0.2.2:8000`
  Android-emulator hints inside translated strings, and corrected `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and
  `docs/FRONTEND_CONVENTIONS.md`. Historical QA logs under `docs/qa/v8/` and `docs/qa/v9/` were deliberately
  left alone: they are records of what those passes ran against.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — one port, one answer. The alternative (an env var everywhere) adds a layer
  of indirection to a value that changes once a year.
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — the API was started on 8001 and `GET /healthz` returned
  `{"ok":true,"env":"development"}`; `qa:v18` greps the tree for a live `:8000` Hangyul reference.

### 168.2 The front of this report described a product that no longer existed

- **SCREEN** — `docs/REPORT.md`, §1.
- **USER QUESTION** — *(new engineer)* "What is this system, today?"
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — the first screenful claimed the API runs on `:8000`, that payments run through a
  "demo provider … Stripe/Toss adapters exist but are not enabled", and that the mobile apps have "no
  document upload". By V17 all three were false: Toss one-time checkout is the live path, and native upload
  shipped before V17.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — the document is explicitly append-only for audits, which is correct, but *nothing* was
  append-only-exempt. There was no current-state section, so "the top of the file" doubled as both the
  oldest audit and the introduction.
- **SEVERITY** — **P1.** This is the file the brief calls the living source of truth.
- **FIX** *(fixed in this pass)* — added **§0 Current state**, placed above the table of contents, covering
  ports, products, native state, payments, measured localization and launch readiness; annotated the two
  hard-stale lines in §1 in place rather than rewriting the 2026-09-28 audit.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — one section to update per pass, instead of a rule that every historical
  section must be kept true forever (which is what made it drift).
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — §0 exists and names 8001, 33 markets and the Toss test-merchant state;
  `qa:v18` fails on a current-documentation `:8000` reference.

### 168.3 The translation status file could not see V17's own strings

- **SCREEN** — every market's quick check, paywall and payment handoff.
- **USER QUESTION** — *(owner)* "Are we actually translated into the markets we sell to?"
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — `locales/_student_status.json` reported `100 %` and `missing: 0` for a dozen
  locales while V17's own 69 strings existed in exactly **10 of 32** markets. 22 markets rendered the quick
  check and the paywall in English.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — coverage was measured against `_student_manifest.json`, generated **2026-10-14**, before
  V17 added its strings. A manifest is a snapshot; measuring completeness against a snapshot means every new
  string is invisible to the gate that is supposed to find missing strings.
- **SEVERITY** — **P0.** It is the failure mode that hides every other localization failure.
- **FIX** *(fixed in this pass)* — `scripts/qa/v18-locale-coverage.mjs` measures **against English at run
  time**, so a string added today is counted today. The 1,518 missing translations were written.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — deletes a generated artifact from the trust chain. English is already the
  source of truth for keys; nothing needs regenerating or remembering.
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — `npm run qa:v18-locales` prints core and full coverage per market and exits
  non-zero if any exposed market falls back to English on a core flow. It currently reports **33/33**.

### 168.4 Burmese was translated into a market nobody could select

- **SCREEN** — the language/market picker, web and native.
- **USER QUESTION** — *(student in Yangon)* "Is this in my language?"
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — `my` was one of the best-covered student bundles in the product **and already had
  every V17 string**, but Myanmar had no row in `MARKETS` and no flag asset, so it was unreachable.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — a wiring gap left open as a commercial question. V17 recorded it (§157) and correctly
  declined to invent a target market.
- **SEVERITY** — **P2** as a defect, **P1** as waste: the translation was paid for and shipped dark.
- **FIX** *(fixed in this pass, on the owner's V18 decision)* — Myanmar added to `MARKETS` (**33**) and to
  `RESEARCH_MARKETS`, the latter because the research was already there too: a visa playbook sourced to the
  Korean embassy in Yangon (verified 2026-10-10) and `docs/qa/v13/country-simulations/mm-myanmar.md`. The
  public-domain flag was fetched from Wikimedia Commons, licence-checked via the Commons API, scanned for
  script/external references, and documented in `apps/flags/MM.PROVENANCE.md` following the Nepal precedent.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — one canonical list gains one row. The alternative was a permanent footnote
  explaining why a translated language is not offered.
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — `sync-flags.mjs` publishes 33 × 4 apps; the flag module regenerated to 33;
  `qa:v18-locales` reports Myanmar at 100 % of the core surface.

### 168.5 The market count was hardcoded in the gate that guards it

- **SCREEN** — CI.
- **USER QUESTION** — *(engineer)* "Why did the V17 gate fail when I opened a market?"
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — `scripts/qa/v17-gate.mjs` asserted `rows.length !== 32` and that
  `public/flags` had at least 32 files. Adding Myanmar failed the gate for doing exactly what the brief asked.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — the gate encoded a business number as a magic literal in three places.
- **SEVERITY** — **P2.**
- **FIX** *(fixed in this pass)* — one named `EXPECTED_MARKETS` constant, the flag-count check derived from
  the table's own row count, and an assertion that both Nepal and Myanmar are present.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — opening a market is now a one-line change in the gate instead of a hunt.
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — `qa:v17` passes at 33 markets.

# 169. V18 Visual Quality Audit

### 169.1 Twenty student screens opened with the same dark band

- **SCREEN** — Documents, Applications, Visa, Services, Messages, Tasks, Housing, Arrival, Notifications,
  Profile, Explore, Scholarships, Support, Family, Settings, Budget, Help, Compare (×2), Essays, More.
- **USER QUESTION** — "What do I need to do on this screen?"
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — every one of them opened with a near-black `#16130f` band carrying a radial
  tangerine disc and white text, ported from the marketing breadcrumb band. On a 390 px phone it occupied
  the first ~160 px of every screen before any content. It is the single thing that made the student product
  read as admin software, and V16 and V17 both recorded it and both only made it *smaller*.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — a marketing surface reused as a product chrome. Once twenty screens shared it, changing it
  felt like a redesign, so each pass tuned its padding instead.
- **SEVERITY** — **P1.** It is the first impression of every paid screen.
- **FIX** *(fixed in this pass)* — the band is gone. `PageIntro` now renders typography on the page's own
  paper: the screen name in ink at `clamp(25px, 2.4vw, 31px)`, one quiet line of context at a 62ch measure,
  and the page action on the same baseline. The V7 white-on-dark repaint rules and the V16 disc-geometry
  rules were **deleted**, not overridden.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — it removes a surface, a decoration, and two blocks of CSS whose only job was
  to make text legible on that surface. It also removes the defect class behind REPORT §130 #5 (the
  `:not(.hg-btn)` rule that shipped `/applications`' only action white-on-white from V7 to V16) — because
  the dark background that rule existed to compensate for no longer exists.
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — measured in-browser at 390 and 1440 across five screens: header background
  `rgba(0,0,0,0)`, `::after` content `none`, title colour `rgb(40,40,40)`, zero console errors.
  Screenshots in `result/screenshots/student-web/`.

### 169.2 The editorial entrance was too quick to read as a composition

- **SCREEN** — marketing homepage.
- **USER QUESTION** — *(owner)* "Does this feel considered?"
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — V17's entrance durations (small 780 / copy 880 / reveal 920 / media 1080 / hero
  1400 / stagger 120 ms) were an improvement but still read as *appearing* rather than *arriving*.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — not a defect; a tuning judgement the owner wanted moved.
- **SEVERITY** — **P3.**
- **FIX** *(fixed in this pass)* — small 840 / copy 950 / reveal 1020 / media 1180 / hero 1450 /
  stagger 140 ms. The *shape* of V17's decision is preserved rather than rescaled: +6 – 9 %, largest in
  absolute terms where the element is largest, so `small < copy < reveal < media` still holds. `hero` moves
  only 50 ms — past ~1.5 s a first-load settle stops reading as cinematic. Interface motion is untouched at
  120 / 180 / 260 ms.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — six numbers in one token file, regenerated into CSS; no component changed.
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — `qa:v18` asserts each entrance token sits in its V18 range **and** that
  `fast`/`base`/`slow` have not drifted, so "make it feel slower" can never leak into the interface.

### 169.3 Remaining visual issues this pass did *not* fix

Recorded rather than quietly dropped:

- **Student page header, desktop.** With `align-items: flex-end`, a page action beside a two-line subtitle
  sits low against the title. It reads as slightly disconnected at 1440. **P3**, unfixed.
- **Gap below the header.** ~75 px between the new header and the first content block on some screens —
  inherited from the band's old bottom margin. **P3**, unfixed.
- **Native login screen.** At 1080 × 2400 the composition is vertically centred with large empty regions
  above and below, and both inputs render with no placeholder text, which reads as unfinished. **P3**,
  unfixed — see `result/screenshots/android/01-login-cold-start.png`.

# 171. V18 Student Native Audit

### 171.1 The app had no memory between launches

- **SCREEN** — Home, Applications, Documents, Messages, saved universities, visa, plan.
- **USER QUESTION** — "What's my application status?" — asked on the subway, underground.
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — every query lived in memory only. Killing the app and reopening it without a
  connection showed a spinner and then an error, for data the student had already read that morning.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — React Query was configured with `staleTime`/`gcTime` but no persister, and
  `onlineManager` was never wired, so the client assumed the network was always up and burned its retries
  into a dead radio.
- **SEVERITY** — **P1** for a product whose users are often on prepaid mobile data in another country.
- **FIX** *(fixed in this pass)* — `packages/mobile-ui/src/bootstrap/offline.ts`: an AsyncStorage-backed
  persister restoring the last successful result of **allowlisted** queries, plus `onlineManager` driven by
  `@react-native-community/netinfo`. An **allowlist**, not a denylist, because the next pass is exactly when
  somebody adds a query holding a payment result. Payment, checkout, order, document *bodies*, downloads,
  uploads, session and auth keys are additionally refused outright. The cache is busted by app version and
  cleared on sign-out, so the next account cannot see the previous student's applications.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — no bespoke cache layer; it reuses the query client that already holds this
  data, and the security decision is one readable list.
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — `qa:v18` asserts the allowlist exists and that no forbidden prefix is
  cacheable; typecheck clean; the APK was rebuilt with it and relaunched.

### 171.2 The status bar style was silently ignored on Android 15+

- **SCREEN** — every native screen.
- **USER QUESTION** — "Does this look like a real Android app?"
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — logcat on the installed release APK showed, on every launch:
  `StatusBarModule: Ignored status bar change, current activity is edge-to-edge.` The app's
  `<StatusBar style="dark" />` did nothing.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — Android 15 enforces edge-to-edge for apps targeting SDK 35+, and the runtime
  `StatusBarModule` call is a no-op under it. The bar's appearance has to be set on the **theme** at build
  time. The same root cause produced prebuild's `userInterfaceStyle: Install expo-system-ui` warning.
- **SEVERITY** — **P2.** Cosmetically harmless today (dark icons happen to be correct on the light canvas)
  but the app had no actual control over its own status bar.
- **FIX** *(fixed in this pass)* — installed `expo-system-ui`, and configured the **`expo-status-bar` config
  plugin** with `{ style: 'dark' }`, which writes `android:windowLightStatusBar` into the app theme and the
  matching `UIStatusBarStyleDarkContent` on iOS. A first attempt used `androidStatusBar` in `app.json`;
  prebuild reported it **deprecated and without effect** in SDK 57, which is recorded here because it is
  exactly the kind of config that looks applied and is not.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — declarative, applied at build time, and verifiable in the generated theme.
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — logcat after the V18 rebuild; the warning should no longer appear.

### 171.3 Secure storage — audited, no defect

`packages/mobile-ui/src/bootstrap/api.ts` already keeps the refresh token in the OS keychain/keystore via
`expo-secure-store` with `AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY`, and the access token in memory only. No
AsyncStorage use for credentials anywhere in the tree. **No change needed** — recorded because §23 asked and
a clean result is a result.

### 171.4 Native work this pass did *not* do

Stated plainly: no native **profile editing** (§19), no native **essay** list or editor (§20), no native
typography-scale rationalisation (§26), no accessibility sweep (§27), and no deep-link replay / malicious
return-URL testing (§24). These remain open; see §189.

# 172. V18 33-Market Translation Audit

*(The brief says "32-market". The owner's V18 decision made it **33** — see §168.4.)*

### 172.1 The measured position, before and after

Measured against English at run time by `scripts/qa/v18-locale-coverage.mjs`.

| | Before V18 | After V18 |
|---|---|---|
| Exposed markets | 32 | **33** |
| Markets with the **core conversion surface** complete | **10** | **33** |
| V17 strings missing across markets | 1,518 | **0** |
| Markets with the **full** user-facing surface complete | 1 (en) | 1 (en) |
| Full-surface strings outstanding | ~70,000 | **70,702** |

The last two rows are the honest part of this section and the reason it exists.

### 172.2 What "core conversion surface" means here

71 keys per market, chosen as the surface a prospective or paying student cannot proceed without:

- `marketing:v17.quick.*` — the three-question quick check, its degree/language options, its fit verdicts,
  its result copy and the "this is not an offer" disclaimer.
- `marketing:v17.uni.*` — university detail: founding, student count, mission and its Wikidata provenance,
  official video, and "this university matched your answers".
- `student:v17.gate.*` — the paywall, including the seventeen names for *what* is gated.
- `student:v17.upgrade.*` — upgrade copy, plan names, the "you only pay the difference" promise.
- `student:v17.pay.*` — the Toss handoff, the overseas-card refusal, and the return-to-app result.
- `mobile:v18.offline.*` — the native offline state (new in V18).

### 172.3 The gap this pass did not close

- **SCREEN** — the deep product surface in 13 markets.
- **USER QUESTION** — *(student in Warsaw, Prague, Lisbon, Belgrade…)* "Why is half of this in English?"
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — against the full `common` + `student` + `mobile` + `marketing` surface, Serbian sits
  at **3.8 %**, eleven markets (pl, cs, hu, ro, el, it, pt, de, nl, sv, uk) at **31–32 %**, Spanish and
  French at **63 %**. Visa-route detail, the concierge, the writing/essay surface and the dossier are
  English for all of them.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — markets were opened ahead of translation. Exposure is a flag in one file; translation is
  tens of thousands of strings.
- **SEVERITY** — **P1 commercially**, and explicitly **not fixable in one pass**: 70,702 strings at the
  quality standard the brief itself sets (§9's three review passes, §10's native personas) is a funded
  programme with native reviewers, not a generation run. Bulk-generating it would produce exactly the
  machine-translation register §9 forbids, while making the report *look* finished.
- **FIX** — the owner's V18 decision: complete the core conversion surface in every exposed market (done),
  and carry the remainder as a costed, measured owner action rather than a silent fallback.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — the gate now tells the truth per market, so the decision to open a market can
  be taken against a number instead of a claim.
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — `qa:v18-locales` prints both columns every run; the full-surface column is
  reported, never gated, and §189 carries it as an external dependency.

### 172.4 Translation method and its honest label

Each of the 1,518 V17 strings and 64 new offline strings was written, not machine-translated
sentence-by-sentence, with three concerns held at once: product meaning (plan limits, the payment/legal
distinction, admission uncertainty preserved), native register for an 18–25-year-old reader, and a calm,
concise product tone.

Three decisions worth recording because they are where mechanical translation fails:

1. **Grammatical case.** `v17.gate.named` interpolates `{{what}}` into a sentence. Turkish needs the
   accusative (`başvurularınızı`), Kazakh and Kyrgyz likewise; Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Romanian, Greek,
   Ukrainian and Serbian were restructured so the fragment lands in the nominative
   (`{{what}} to część planu Hangyul.`) rather than forcing a case the fragment cannot carry in every slot.
2. **Plurals were avoided, not faked.** English `v17.quick.resultTitle` has no plural forms, so adding
   `_one`/`_few`/`_many` to Slavic locales would be a plural-shape mismatch against the source. Those
   locales were phrased to be count-agnostic (`Kierunki otwarte dla kandydatów takich jak Ty: {{count}}`),
   which is what a professional localiser does with a non-plural-aware key.
3. **Relative time is the platform's job.** The native "last updated" stamp uses
   `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with the active locale rather than four translated strings per market —
   Polish's *5 minut* vs *2 minuty* and Arabic's dual are exactly where hand-translated relative time ships
   plural bugs.

**Status label: `SYNTHETIC_NATIVE_REVIEWED`.** No native speaker reviewed this copy. It is not labelled
`HUMAN_REVIEWED` and must not be until one does. Confidence is honestly uneven: it is highest for
es/fr/pt/it/de/nl/sv/pl/cs/tr/id/el/ro/hu/uk and lowest for fil/bn/hi/th/kk/ky/sr, which should be the
first sent for native review.

### 172.5 Translation QA the brief asked for and this pass did not build

`qa:v18-locales` gates missing keys, English fallback on core flows, and placeholder parity (directionally —
an English placeholder may never be dropped; Korean's extra `{{particle}}`/`{{particleRo}}`, fed by
`koParticle()` for 은/는 and 으로/로 agreement, is allowed by name). **Not built:** raw-key detection, HTML
markup parity, script/mixed-language detection, currency and date placement, and automated text-overflow and
button-truncation capture across 33 locales × 390/768/1440. RTL beyond the existing `qa:v8-rtl` was not
re-swept. These are listed in §189.

# 173. V18 Error / Edge-Case Audit

### 173.1 A broken NDK made the native build impossible, silently

- **SCREEN** — CI / any developer's first `assembleRelease`.
- **USER QUESTION** — "Why won't the app build?"
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — `[CXX1101] NDK at /root/android-sdk/ndk/27.1.12297006 did not have a
  source.properties file`. The directory existed and was **12 KB** — a previous session's download had been
  interrupted, leaving a directory that looked installed.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — a partial SDK install is indistinguishable from a complete one by directory existence,
  which is how every tool decides whether to install it.
- **SEVERITY** — **P0 for release**; the build could not produce a binary at all.
- **FIX** *(fixed in this pass)* — removed the directory and reinstalled via `sdkmanager`; verified
  `source.properties` reports `Pkg.Revision 27.1.12297006 / r27b`.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — a real install instead of a guard for a broken one.
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — the build then succeeded twice end to end.

### 173.2 Release signing was a hand-edit that the next prebuild would erase

- **SCREEN** — the release pipeline.
- **USER QUESTION** — "Is this APK actually signed with our key?"
- **OBSERVED FAILURE** — the first V18 attempt patched `android/app/build.gradle` directly after prebuild.
  `expo prebuild --clean` regenerates that folder, so the signing config would vanish and the next
  "release" build would be **debug-signed, with no error saying so**. The first patch attempt also matched
  the wrong `release {` block (the template has no `signingConfigs.release`) and corrupted `buildTypes`.
- **ROOT CAUSE** — treating generated output as source.
- **SEVERITY** — **P1.** A silently debug-signed release is worse than a failed build.
- **FIX** *(fixed in this pass)* — `apps/student-mobile/plugins/withReleaseSigning.js`, a config plugin that
  re-applies the signing config on **every** prebuild and **throws** if the Expo template changes shape
  under it. The keystore moved out of `android/` to `apps/student-mobile/credentials/` so `--clean` cannot
  delete it; both are gitignored; gradle falls back to the debug keystore when the properties are absent so
  a fresh checkout still builds.
- **WHY THE FIX IS SIMPLER** — the project stays CNG: `app.json` is the source of truth and `android/` is
  disposable output.
- **HOW IT WILL BE VERIFIED** — prebuild log prints the injected config; `apksigner verify --print-certs`
  reports `CN=Hangyul Univ` on the produced APK.

### 173.3 The full student error-state matrix was not run

The brief (§44) asks every high-value screen to be exercised under loading / empty / partial / offline /
401 / 403 / 404 / 409 / 422 / 429 / 500 / timeout. **This was not done in V18.** What was verified: the five
student web screens above produced zero console and zero page errors signed in; `ErrorState` already
distinguishes forbidden / not-found / offline / generic and always offers a retry; the native app now has a
real offline path. The matrix itself is open — §189.

### 173.4 `test:release` was not built

§43 asks for an `npm run test:release` that either runs the required release tests or fails loudly with
`MISSING REQUIRED TEST ENVIRONMENT` rather than silently skipping. **Not built in V18.** The default-skip
risk V17 identified (e.g. `HG_LIVE_API`-gated smoke tests) therefore remains. §189.

# 174. V18 Native Build & Distribution Audit

### 174.1 Environment, inspected before anything was asked of the owner

| Thing | State found | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Java | OpenJDK 21.0.12 | fine |
| Android SDK | **absent** (`ANDROID_HOME` unset, no `adb`, no `gradle`) | installed cmdline-tools, platform-tools, `platforms;android-36`, `build-tools;36.0.0` |
| NDK | present but **corrupt**, 12 KB | reinstalled — §173.1 |
| Emulator + system image | already present (`android-35 google_apis x86_64`), 3 AVDs | usable |
| `/dev/kvm` | **present** | hardware acceleration, so a real emulator run was possible |
| `eas` CLI / login | **not logged in** | **all EAS cloud builds blocked** |
| macOS / Xcode | not applicable — Linux (WSL2) | **no local iOS build possible** |
| RAM | 5 GB total | gradle pinned to `-Xmx2048m`, daemon off, no parallel |

### 174.2 `expo-doctor`

Started at **2 of 21 checks failing**:

1. **Patch-level Expo package drift** (expo, expo-constants, expo-document-picker, expo-linking,
   expo-notifications, expo-router) — fixed with `expo install --fix`.
2. **`splash` is no longer a valid top-level config field** in SDK 57 — moved to the `expo-splash-screen`
   plugin.
3. **`android.edgeToEdgeEnabled` is not an allowed property** — removed; edge-to-edge is unconditional in
   SDK 57.
4. **TypeScript**: doctor wants `~6.0.3`; the monorepo is pinned to `~5.9.3`. **Not followed.** TS 6 is a
   breaking major across seven workspaces and was rejected in an earlier pass for Expo incompatibility. It
   is declared in `expo.install.exclude` **with the reason written next to it**, which is the "documented
   with a concrete reason" the brief allows — not an ignored warning.

Now **21/21**, with one expected exception while `android/` exists on disk: doctor warns that a non-CNG
project will not sync `app.json` native fields. That warning is a consequence of `android/` being present as
local build output; it disappears in a clean checkout, and the folder is gitignored for that reason.

### 174.3 Build profiles

`apps/student-mobile/eas.json` created with `base`, `development`, `preview`, `production`, `android-apk`
and `ios-simulator`. `production` builds an **`app-bundle`**; `preview` and `android-apk` build **APKs**;
`ios-simulator` sets `ios.simulator: true`. `base.env` is deliberately **empty**: there is no production API
origin defined anywhere in this repo, and inventing `api.hangyul.kr` would have put a fabricated hostname in
a shipped artifact. The owner supplies it — §189.

### 174.4 iOS — blocked, with the exact blocker

- **No local build.** This is Linux (WSL2); an iOS build requires macOS and Xcode. Not a configuration
  problem and not fixable here.
- **No cloud build.** `eas whoami` → **`Not logged in`**. EAS cloud builds, including the simulator build
  that needs no Apple Developer membership, require an authenticated Expo account.
- Therefore: **`IOS_SIMULATOR_BLOCKED_BY_EAS_LOGIN`** and **`SIGNED_IPA_BLOCKED_BY_APPLE_CREDENTIALS`**.
- **No placeholder artifact was created.** `result/student-mobile/ios/` does not exist.

# 181. V18 Android Build Validation

**Both Android artifacts exist, are signed, and are real binaries.** Full detail, including exact sizes,
checksums and the build command line, is in `result/student-mobile/metadata/BUILD_REPORT.md`.

| | APK | AAB |
|---|---|---|
| Built | `gradle :app:assembleRelease` | `gradle :app:bundleRelease` |
| Path | `result/student-mobile/android/hangyul-univ-preview.apk` | `result/student-mobile/android/hangyul-univ-production.aab` |
| Size | 120.1 MB (125,903,361 B) | 79.2 MB |
| SHA-256 | `bb9f7bde672c5fec…93526f7` | `3311ee704a509382…436c62ae7` |
| Signature | `apksigner verify` → **Verifies**, v2 scheme, `CN=Hangyul Univ` | `jarsigner -verify` passes, same key, valid to 2054-03-07 |
| Format check | installs on a device | `bundletool validate` → well-formed `base` module, 5 dex, per-ABI libs |
| Store-ready | internal distribution only | **no** — local keystore, dev API origin |

### 181.1 Runtime — what "verified" means here

**Verified** on an Android 16 (API 36) x86_64 emulator, hardware-accelerated via `/dev/kvm`, with the
**signed release APK** installed: `adb install -r` → `Success`; cold start reaches
`topResumedActivity=kr.hangyul.univ.student/.MainActivity`; `ReactNativeJS: Running "main"`; the sign-in
screen renders correctly; both fields accept keyboard input; **zero fatal exceptions**.

**Not verified:** everything behind sign-in. The Expo Android template puts
`android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"` in the **debug** manifests only, so a `targetSdk 36` **release**
build refuses plaintext HTTP — including the emulator's `http://10.0.2.2:8001`. That is correct behaviour
for a shipping binary, and it is why the release APK cannot be driven against a local HTTP dev stack.

So this pass claims **ANDROID BUILD VERIFIED** and **launch/render RUNTIME VERIFIED**, and explicitly does
**not** claim signed-in runtime verification for the release artifact. The §38 checklist (login, language
change, bottom tabs, university detail, documents, upload, messages, notifications, services, deep link,
logout) is therefore **not** complete — see §189.

### 181.2 Two real defects found by running it rather than testing it

1. **The status bar was not under the app's control.** logcat showed
   `StatusBarModule: Ignored status bar change, current activity is edge-to-edge` on every launch.
   Fixed at the theme level — the shipped APK's `styles.xml` now carries
   `<item name="android:windowLightStatusBar">true</item>`, verified in the generated resources. The
   runtime `<StatusBar>` was then scoped to iOS, because on Android it was asking for work the theme had
   already done; that last change is **in the source but not in the artifact above** — it landed after the
   build and is not claimed as verified.
2. **A self-contradicting error message.** The login failure read *"Can't reach the server at
   http://10.0.2.2:8001 … On an Android emulator use http://10.0.2.2:8000"* — the string still named the
   old port while the code used the new one. Fixed in **21 locale bundles**. No test could have caught
   this; it needed someone to read the screen.

### 181.3 Secret scan

1,371 files from inside the APK — JS bundle, assets, resources — scanned for Toss secret keys, JWT secrets,
database URLs, private-key blocks, AWS keys, Google API keys, the demo password and the keystore password.
**No server secrets in the APK.**

# 184. V18 Programme Verification

`docs/qa/v18/PROGRAM_VERIFICATION.csv` — 66 rows, one per active programme, with university (English and
Korean), programme name, degree level, language of instruction, tuition, status, source, the university's
official site, and exactly what remains unverified.

**Verified against an official source: 0 of 66.**

This is worse than "unverified" sounded in V17, and the CSV says so. Every active programme has
`verification_status = 'DEMO'` and a `source_url` of
`https://github.com/hangyul/hangyul-univ#demo-data` — the repository's own demo-data anchor. The
`verified_at` timestamps in the database are **seed times, not verifications**, so the CSV leaves that
column empty rather than reproducing a number that looks like evidence.

The distinction REPORT flagged earlier holds and is now quantified: **325 institution records** carry a
real source and verified date; **0 of 66 programmes** do. Institution-level verification does not transfer
to programme level — a university's existence and address being verified says nothing about whether it runs
a Business Administration BBA in English, at that tuition, with that intake.

No requirement was invented to fill a gap. Each row names the official site to check and lists what must be
confirmed: that the programme exists, its degree level, its language of instruction, its tuition per
semester, its intake terms and its admission requirements — against the university's 모집요강 or
international-office page. That is the worklist; it is operations work, not a code change.

guards them, but **nobody watched the new entrance**. "Calm, cinematic, deliberate" is an intention, not a
finding. Section spacing, image crops, CTA emphasis, text measure, the logo marquee, pricing and the footer
were not touched or re-checked.

**Translation.** 33/33 on the core surface is real and measured. But **thirteen markets are still mostly
English** one screen deeper, and the gate reports it rather than hiding it. Nothing was reviewed by a native
speaker. No overflow or truncation testing was done in any locale, so a long German or Greek string could
be breaking a button right now and this pass would not know.

**Student web.** The band is gone and that is the biggest single improvement in V18. But only **five
screens** at **two widths** were opened. The brief named nine widths and four products. The agency and
university consoles were not opened at all — §49 and §50 were not done.

**Native.** It installs, launches and renders with no crashes, and it now survives a lost connection. It is
**not** release-grade against the brief's own list: no native profile editing, no essay surface, no
accessibility sweep, no typography-scale work, and **no signed-in runtime testing at all** — the release
build correctly refuses the cleartext dev API, and the debug build that would have allowed it ran out of
memory on this 5 GB machine. Claiming "the app works" from a login screen and a logcat with no fatals would
be dishonest.

**Android.** The APK and AAB are genuine, signed and verified by their own tooling. The APK is **120 MB**,
which is a universal build with four ABIs; nobody optimised it. The AAB is not Play-ready for two concrete
reasons, both stated.

**iOS.** Nothing exists. Two independent blockers, neither solvable here.

**Errors.** The §44 matrix was not run, the §42 click-map was not built, and `test:release` was not
created — so V17's silent-skip risk is **still open**. V18 found two real defects by *running* the product
(the ignored status bar; the error message that named the wrong port) and both were invisible to every
existing test, which is the strongest argument that the unrun checks matter.

**Gates.** The honest headline: **`qa:v12`–`qa:v17` were not validly run this pass** because the full dev
stack was not up. `qa:v18` passing 38/38 is a real result for what it covers, and is not a substitute.

**The one thing that would most change this product next:** not a feature. Running the existing gates
properly, end to end, with all four web apps up — and then the §44 error matrix.

# 191. V19 Navigation & Scroll Audit

## 191.1 `/start` — measured, not estimated

The gap between the floating pill's real bottom edge and the top of the first heading, before any change:

| width | 320 | 360 | 390 | 430 | 768 | 1024 | 1280 | 1440 | 1728 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/start` | **−14** | **−14** | **−14** | **−14** | **−6** | **−6** | +2 | +2 | +2 |
| `/universities` | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 33 | 41 | **30** | **30** | **30** |
| `/privacy`, `/terms` | 62 | 62 | 62 | 62 | 65 | 73 | 66 | 66 | 66 |

A negative number is an overlap: the heading is *behind* the pill. On a 390 px phone the top half of
"어떤 한국 대학이 나와 맞을까요?" was covered by the header. The owner's word was "collides"; it was literal.

## 191.2 Root cause — three different ideas about one number

The header is `position: fixed`, so it takes no space in the flow and every page must reserve its footprint
itself. Three pages did, one did not, and the one that did got it wrong:

- **`/start`** reserved nothing. It is a `<Band>`, whose `padding-block` is the section rhythm
  (`--kn-band`: 56 / 72 / 100 px), and at 320 px that 56 px is 14 px less than the pill's 70 px footprint.
- **`/universities`, `/universities/:slug`, legal** used `--mk-headclear: calc(var(--kn-header-top) + 68px)`.
  The literal `68` is the **desktop** pill's height. Below 1200 px the pill is 56 px tall, so the page
  cleared 12 px too much; at and above 1200 px the pill plus its border is 70 px, so it cleared 2 px too
  little. Because each page then added a `clamp()` that *grew* with the viewport while the error flipped
  sign at the breakpoint, the measured gap went 26 → 33 → 41 → **30**: the clearance got *smaller* as the
  window got bigger, between 1024 px and 1280 px.

## 191.3 The scroll defect — reproduced, then explained

`scripts/qa/v19/_scroll-probe.mjs` reproduces the owner's report and prints the mechanism:

```
[2. home scrolled to bottom] /?lang=ko
  scrollY=6209   history.scrollRestoration=manual
  CTA href=/start?lang=ko   CTA is a plain <a> (full document load) = true
[3. after clicking 유학 준비] /start?lang=ko
  scrollY=833    scroll-positions: {"default":6209}
```

The cause is one line of state, shared by every page in the origin:

1. `SiteLayout` rendered react-router's `<ScrollRestoration />`. It saves scroll offsets into
   `sessionStorage` keyed by `location.key`.
2. `location.key` is the literal string **`"default"`** for the *first* history entry of **every** document.
3. The site's one conversion action was `<a href="/start">` — a plain anchor, so a **full document load**.
4. Home saved `{"default": 6209}` on unload. `/start` loaded as a new document, whose first entry is also
   `"default"`, found 6209, and restored it. `/start` is 1,733 px tall, so the browser clamped to 833.

This is not a missing `scrollTo`. It is one storage slot shared by every page, so **any** full-document
navigation inherited the previous page's offset. A `window.scrollTo(0, 0)` in the button's `onClick` — the
fix the brief forbids — would have hidden exactly one of its symptoms.

## 191.4 The other three apps

| app | before V19 |
|---|---|
| Marketing | `<ScrollRestoration />` — the defect above |
| Student | its own `useEffect(() => window.scrollTo({top: 0}), [pathname])`. Resets on every pathname change and **can never restore**, so Back from an application always landed at the top of the applications list |
| Agency | **nothing at all** |
| University | **nothing at all** |

Opening an applicant from halfway down a list in either console put the reader halfway down the applicant.
V18 did not find this because V18 did not open either console.

# 192. V19 Marketing Visual Audit

## 192.1 Motion — watched this time

V18 moved the editorial duration tokens and added a gate over their values; nobody looked at the result.
`scripts/qa/v19/_motion-trace.mjs` installs a `requestAnimationFrame` recorder *inside* the page at document
start and reports what a visitor experiences. Two things had to be right before the numbers meant anything,
and the first draft got both wrong:

- **Measure the node the CSS moves.** `SectionHead` wraps its heading in a `<Reveal>`, so the heading's own
  opacity is always 1; a `<Reveal variant="stagger">` is the opposite — the container stays at 1 and its
  children animate. Resolving this as "walk up to the first ancestor with an opacity transition" lands on
  the stagger container and reports a page with no animation anywhere, which is what the first run claimed.
- **Start before React.** The hero plays on mount; a recorder installed after `domcontentloaded` has missed it.

### What the entrances actually do (1440 px, after the §199 fix)

| element | dead time | perceptual settle | travel |
|---|---|---|---|
| services heading | 66 ms | 716 ms | 20 px |
| services media photo | 66 ms | 716 ms | 12 px |
| university marquee | 83 ms | 700 ms | 0 px |
| pricing heading | 83 ms | 733 ms | 20 px |
| pricing cards | 83 ms | 616 ms | 18 px |
| FAQ heading | 66 ms | 716 ms | 20 px |
| closing CTA | 216 ms | 867 ms | 20 px |

"Dead time" is how long an element is still invisible *after* it is on screen — what reads as a broken page.
"Settle" is when it reaches rest.

**The durations are right and V19 did not change them.** The tokens say 1020 ms for a `rise`, but the easing
(`cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`) front-loads it, so opacity reaches 0.99 at roughly 60 % of the nominal
duration — 616–733 ms in practice. Against a normal trackpad flick (~1,000 px/s) that finishes well before
the reader has passed the section, and 66–83 ms of dead time is imperceptible. This is the owner's
"slightly slower, clearly perceptible, not slow", and the honest finding is that V18's numbers already
delivered it. Changing them again would have been the third pass in a row to move a number without looking.

### The defect the trace found instead

**The hero never animated.** Frame capture at 65 / 116 / 151 / 298 / 401 / **604** ms: absent, absent,
absent, absent, absent, then fully opaque, with no intermediate value. `Reveal` sets `armed` in an effect
and the IntersectionObserver fires on the very next frame for anything already in the viewport, so React
batched both state updates into one render — the element entered the DOM already carrying `--armed` *and*
`is-in`, and the browser had no previous computed value to interpolate from. The entire entrance existed in
the stylesheet and never ran. No duration token could have revealed this.

**The closing CTA band had no entrance at all** — the only section on the page without one. On a page where
every heading, photograph and price arrives, the conversion moment simply existed.

## 192.2 Spacing, alignment and colour

- The three subpage families used three different header-clearance rules, one of them wrong in both
  directions (§191.2). Now one derived token.
- A disabled primary button was `opacity: 0.45` over tangerine with white text — roughly 1.9:1, and the
  first thing a visitor meets on `/start`, where the CTA is disabled until three questions are answered. It
  reads as broken rather than as not-yet-available.
- `/start` put a **centred** 760 px head above a **left-aligned** 640 px form: two measures and two
  alignments in the first viewport. That, more than any spacing value, is why a page with three questions
  on it read as a generic form.
- `/start`'s three-option questions used `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(150px, 1fr))`, which gave three options
  **four** tracks at 1440 (one empty, so the row stopped short of the measure for no reason) and **two**
  tracks at 390 (so the third option sat alone, half-width, under the other two).
- The page said "no account needed" **three times**: in the lede, beside the button, and in a standing hint
  below the form that was the lede again in different words.

| `android/` project directory | absent — managed workflow, so `expo prebuild` must run before any Gradle build |

## 194.2 The V18 gaps, one by one

| V18 gap | V19 |
|---|---|
| Native profile editing | **Still open** — not attempted |
| Native essay surface | **Still open** — not attempted |
| Typography rationalisation | **Audited (§194.7): largely already right.** A closed 7-size/3-weight scale with 193 of 200 usages going through it; one genuine off-scale value |
| Accessibility sweep | **Static half done (§194.6): 0 real findings.** The device half — reading order, what TalkBack announces, 200 % font scale — is still open |
| Payment deep-link matrix | **Still open** — needs a running app |
| Signed-in runtime verification | **Attempted (§194.8)** |
| APK size (120 MB) | **Answered (§194.4)** with measured numbers |
| Artifact rebuild | **Attempted, blocked on the keystore (§194.5)** |

## 194.3 The artifact is now definitely out of step with source

V18 noted that one Android status-bar fix landed after the artifact was built. V19 makes that worse and
must say so plainly: **this pass changed `packages/api-client`**, which the native app bundles — the request
deadline in §199.6. The committed artifacts

```
result/student-mobile/android/hangyul-univ-preview.apk     125,903,361 B  sha256 bb9f7bde…526f7
result/student-mobile/android/hangyul-univ-production.aab   83,095,350 B
```

were built at `2026-10-20T06:16:29Z`, before those changes. They are **stale** and must be rebuilt. No
rebuild was attempted here, so no new checksum is offered and the old ones are left in place rather than
being re-presented as current.

V19 added a gate for precisely this (`qa:v19` check F, §208.1). It fails right now, by design, and will
keep failing until the artifacts are rebuilt — so this can no longer be a paragraph somebody skips.

## 194.4 Why the APK is 120 MB — audited, read-only

The brief asks why, and that can be answered without rebuilding anything: the artifact is a zip, so it can
simply be opened. Uncompressed bytes in `hangyul-univ-preview.apk`:

| group | size | note |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/x86` | 22.4 MB | **emulator only** |
| `lib/x86_64` | 22.0 MB | **emulator only** |
| `lib/arm64-v8a` | 21.4 MB | every current phone |
| `lib/armeabi-v7a` | 14.8 MB | older phones |
| `classes*.dex` | **42.8 MB** | unminified |
| `assets/index.android.bundle` | 18.2 MB | Hermes **bytecode** (magic `c6 1f bc 03`), not raw JS |
| `res/` | 6.3 MB | |
| other | 2.2 MB | |
| **total** | **149.2 MB** uncompressed → 121 MB on disk | |

Three findings, in order of size:

1. **Native libraries are 80.6 MB — 54 % of the artifact — and 44.4 MB of that is x86/x86_64**, which no
   shipping Android phone uses. They are in there because this is a *universal* APK with no `abiFilters`.
   For a direct-install preview build, restricting to `arm64-v8a` (plus `armeabi-v7a` if old devices
   matter) removes roughly a third of the file on its own.
2. **42.8 MB of dex is unminified.** `app.json` declares no `expo-build-properties` plugin, so
   `enableProguardInReleaseBuilds` sits at the React Native template default of `false` and R8 never runs.
3. **18.2 MB of Hermes bytecode** is large but is already compiled — and it carries all 33 locale bundles.
   This is the one number that is *earned*, and the least worth attacking.

**And the 120 MB figure is not what a user downloads.** The Play artifact is the AAB (83 MB), from which
Play generates a per-device split: one ABI instead of four, and only the matching density resources. The
universal APK exists so the owner can side-load a build onto any device without Play.

None of this was changed, because changing it means rebuilding, and the rebuild is blocked below. It is a
specification for whoever does: add `expo-build-properties` with R8 on, and `abiFilters` on the preview
profile only — the AAB must keep every ABI, because Play does the splitting.

## 194.5 The rebuild was attempted, and is blocked on a credential

Late in the pass, with the web work finished, V19 **did** start the rebuild, following V18's documented
recipe (`result/student-mobile/metadata/BUILD_REPORT.md`) and its memory tuning for this 5.9 GB host.

```
$ npx expo prebuild --platform android --clean --no-install
✔ Created native directory
✔ Finished prebuild
```

Prebuild succeeded, and `withReleaseSigning.js` correctly re-applied the release signing block to the
regenerated `android/app/build.gradle` — the plugin V18 wrote for exactly this reason works.

It stops there. That signing block is deliberately conditional:

```gradle
release {
    if (project.hasProperty('HANGYUL_UPLOAD_STORE_FILE')) { storeFile file(HANGYUL_UPLOAD_STORE_FILE); … }
    else { storeFile file('debug.keystore'); storePassword 'android'; … }
}
```

The keystore itself is present (`apps/student-mobile/credentials/hangyul-release.keystore`), but its
**password, key alias and key password are not recorded anywhere in this repository** — correctly, since
`qa:v16` scans the tree against a fingerprint of that very password. V18 supplied them as Gradle
properties in an untracked `android/gradle.properties`, and `prebuild --clean` regenerates that directory,
so they are gone.

Building without them would not fail. It would **silently produce a debug-signed APK labelled "release"** —
the precise trap `withReleaseSigning.js`'s own comment names — and publishing that over a correctly
release-signed artifact would be strictly worse than leaving the stale one in place. Generating a *new*
keystore is not an option either: changing the upload key is an irreversible Play decision that belongs to
the owner, not to a QA pass.

So the rebuild is blocked on one secret, and that is a far more useful answer than "not attempted". The
generated `android/` directory was removed again rather than left half-prepared; it is gitignored build
output and `scripts/release/v19-android-build.sh` regenerates it in about thirty seconds once the
properties are available.

**To finish this, the owner supplies four values** and the scripted path takes it from there:

```
HANGYUL_UPLOAD_STORE_FILE  HANGYUL_UPLOAD_STORE_PASSWORD  HANGYUL_UPLOAD_KEY_ALIAS  HANGYUL_UPLOAD_KEY_PASSWORD
  → bash scripts/release/v19-android-build.sh     # prebuild → assembleRelease → bundleRelease → verify signature
  → node scripts/release/v19-build-info.mjs       # recompute sizes + SHA-256 into BUILD_INFO.json
  → npm run qa:v19                                # check F goes green
```

The rest of the native workstream — profile editing, essays, typography, accessibility, the deep-link
matrix, signed-in runtime testing — needs no credential and was simply not reached; §209.3 carries it.

## 194.6 Accessibility — the static half, and what it does not cover

The brief's §33 asks for an accessibility sweep. A real one needs a device, TalkBack or VoiceOver and a
human listening to the reading order; none of that was available. What *was* possible is a static audit of
the native source for the defects a screen reader certainly trips over —
`npm run qa:v19-native-a11y` (`scripts/qa/v19/native-a11y.mjs`).

**Result: no statically-detectable accessibility defect.** That is the honest answer, and it took three
corrections to the instrument to reach it:

| run | findings | why they were wrong |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 88 | Flagged every `<Button>` call site. `@hangyul/mobile-ui`'s `<Button>` already sets `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel={accessibilityLabel ?? label}`, `accessibilityState` and `hitSlop` — the script had audited a component it had not read |
| 2 | 31 | The JSX tag regex stopped at the first `>`, which in `style={({ pressed }) => …}` sits inside an arrow function, so every multi-line component looked bare. Replaced with a brace- and quote-aware `tagBody()` scanner |
| 3 | 6 | All six opened by hand, all six false: two decorative icon wrappers (`width: 28`, `width: 32`) whose **row** carries the real 56 px target, an `<Image>` inside a `<View accessible accessibilityRole="progressbar" accessibilityLabel>` that is itself the accessibility element, and a `<Pressable accessibilityRole="button">` whose children arrive through a variable |
| 4 | **0** | — |

So the shared native components do this properly, which is a genuinely good result and is worth saying
after three sections of defects. It is also a **narrow** result: static analysis says nothing about reading
order, focus order, what TalkBack actually announces, contrast in context, or behaviour at 200 % font
scale. §33 is **not** discharged, and §209.3 still carries the accessibility sweep as outstanding.

The pattern is the same one as §207 and §196.2, and by now it is the most reliable finding of this whole
pass: **a new instrument is wrong before it is right, and its first output is a hypothesis, not a result.**
## 194.7 Typography — audited, and largely already right

V18 listed "typography rationalisation" as an open native gap. Read against the source, most of it is not
a gap. `packages/mobile-ui/src/components/AppText.tsx` already defines a closed scale:

| variant | size / line | weight |
|---|---|---|
| display | 26 / 32 | semibold |
| metric | 24 / 30 | semibold |
| title | 20 / 26 | semibold |
| heading | 17 / 24 | semibold |
| subheading · body · bodyStrong | 15 / 22 | semibold · regular · semibold |
| caption | 13 / 18 | regular |
| label | 12 / 16 | semibold |

Nine variants over **seven sizes and three weights**, with bold reserved for display numbers, and
`maxFontSizeMultiplier = 1.6` so the OS text-size setting is honoured up to 1.6×. That is a limited,
intentional hierarchy, and 193 of the 200 text usages in the app go through it.

**Seven `fontSize:` literals bypass it, and six of the seven are defensible**: `DevAccess` (10 px) is
compiled out of production; `Badge.dotText` (11), `Patterns.markBang` (10) and `Messages.time` (11) are
glyph-and-counter cases that are deliberately smaller than the smallest reading size; and the two 16 px
values are both on `TextInput`, which is a comfort convention rather than a scale step.

The seventh is a real finding: **`Button.smallText: 14`** sits between `caption` (13) and `body` (15) for
no stated reason. It was not changed — moving a button's label size without being able to look at the
button is how a one-pixel fix becomes a wrapped label — and it is carried in §209.3.

The first sweep reported **clipped tables** on `/retention` and `/graduation` — a table wider than its

```
/retention   table scrollWidth=153  parent clientWidth=1  overflow-x:hidden  parent class "hg-sr-only"
/graduation  table scrollWidth=197  parent clientWidth=1  overflow-x:hidden  parent class "hg-sr-only"
```

Those are the screen-reader data tables that accompany each chart — the text alternative for a
visualisation, clipped to a 1 px box **by design**. The instrument was wrong, not the page; it was fixed to

drops its own false positives is not one.

# 198. V19 Zero-Defect Plan

Written before the implementation below. In priority order, with the rule that a fix must remove the
*cause*, not the symptom the owner happened to see.

1. **One derived header footprint.** `--kn-header-h` → `--kn-header-space` → `--kn-page-top`, defined once
   in `koreanasha.scss`, consumed by a `Band pageTop` prop and by the three hand-rolled page heads. No page
   may restate the pill's height.
2. **One route-scroll policy** in `@hangyul/ui`, mounted by all four apps, implementing push/pop/hash/
   query-only/anchor correctly — and leaving `history.scrollRestoration` alone so the browser keeps doing
   cross-document restoration, which is the coupling that broke.
3. **One shared page intro**, left-aligned, so a subpage's heading sits on the same axis as its content.
4. **Make the hero actually animate**, then re-measure rather than retune.
5. **Run every gate V18 left unrun**, fix what they find, and update a gate only where a later product
   decision genuinely invalidated it — with the reason written down.
6. **Run the error matrix and the click-map**, and fix the instrument when it is the instrument that is wrong.
7. **Create `test:release`** such that a missing dependency fails the run instead of skipping a test.
8. **Report native as untouched** rather than part-done.
