# 199. V19 Implementation Log

## 199.1 One derived header footprint

`packages/koreanasha-ui/src/scss/koreanasha.scss` — the pill's footprint is now computed from the two
variables that position it, and the page-top rhythm is computed from that:

```scss
--kn-header-h: 56px;                                                   /* .kn-header__inner min-height */
--kn-header-space: calc(var(--kn-header-top) + var(--kn-header-h) + 2px);   /* + the 1px border, twice */
--kn-page-breathe: 32px;                                               /* the owner's optical target */
--kn-page-top: calc(var(--kn-header-space) + var(--kn-page-breathe));
```

`--kn-page-breathe` **steps** rather than scaling continuously — 32 / 38 (≥576) / 44 (≥768) / 60 (≥1200) —
because the pill's own height steps at 1200 px, and a `vw` curve crossing that step is what produced a gap
that *shrank* as the window grew. `--kn-header-h` steps to 68 px in the same media query as
`.kn-header__inner`, and `qa:v19` parses both and fails if they ever disagree.

Consumers: a new `pageTop` prop on `<Band>` (`.kn-band--pagetop`), used by `/start`; and `.mk-dir__head`,
`.mk-uni__head` and `.mk-legal__grid`, which now read `var(--kn-page-top)` directly. **`--mk-headclear` is
deleted**, and the gate fails if any per-page clearance variable reappears.

`.mk-uni__head--visual` keeps `padding-block-start: 0` — where the header floats over a photograph the
image is the clearance, and reserving space there would put a white strip across the design.

## 199.2 A shared, left-aligned page intro

New `PageIntro` in `apps/marketing-web/src/components/blocks.tsx`, with `.mk-pagehead` in `styles.css`.
`/start` used the homepage's **centred** `SectionHead`; it now uses the same left-aligned anatomy the
directory and the legal pages already had. Centred is right for a section a reader scrolls *into*; it is
wrong at the top of a page where everything below it — a form, a search field, a list — is left-aligned.

## 199.3 One route-scroll policy — `packages/ui/src/route-scroll.tsx`

| navigation | behaviour |
|---|---|
| PUSH/REPLACE to a different pathname | top, `behavior: 'instant'` |
| POP, same document | restore the remembered offset for that entry |
| POP across documents | **left to the browser** |
| a location with a `#hash` | untouched |
| same pathname, different search (`?lang=`, filters, sort, a drawer on the URL) | untouched |

Mounted by `SiteLayout` (marketing), `StudentShell` and `YnexShell` (agency + university). The student
app's own `ScrollToTop` is deleted; the gate fails if it returns.

Three things had to be right, and the first two attempts got them wrong:

- **`history.scrollRestoration` is left at `'auto'`.** react-router sets it to `'manual'`; at the browser
  default the engine restores a *cross-document* entry from its own per-entry store, which is more accurate
  than anything reconstructable in JS. We own same-document navigation, the browser owns cross-document,
  and neither needs the shared key that broke.
- **The saved offset is captured when the navigation *starts*, not when it commits.** Reading
  `window.scrollY` in a layout effect looks right and is not: React has already committed the new route, so
  if the incoming page is shorter the browser has **already clamped** the scroll. Leaving the bottom of a
  7,109 px Home for a 1,733 px `/start` recorded 833 px as "where Home was" — the restoration then worked
  perfectly and returned the reader to the wrong place. All four apps use `createBrowserRouter`, so
  `useNavigation().state` leaves `idle` while a lazy chunk resolves and the outgoing page is still in the
  DOM; that is the moment the offset is taken. A scroll sampler is the fallback for navigations that never
  leave `idle`.
- **A restored offset is re-applied each frame until it sticks.** On a POP the route has rendered but its
  images and observers have not settled, so the document is still short and the browser silently clamps.
  The first version restored the directory to 107 px instead of 1,400: the number was right and there was
  nowhere to put it. The loop stops when the offset holds, after one second, or the moment the reader
  scrolls themselves — wheel, touch and keyboard only, because a programmatic `scrollTo` also fires
  `scroll` and listening for that would cancel the restoration with its own first attempt.

Separately, the marketing CTA is now a client-side `<Link>` when `prepareAction` returns a local path, and
stays a real `<a>` for the cross-origin student-platform URL. A full document reload for a route in the
same SPA threw away the React tree and the query cache for no reason.

## 199.4 `/start` composition

One axis, one measure. The container is centred at 36 rem on wide screens and everything inside drops its
own max-width, so the heading, the lede, every question and the button share one left edge. The rhythm is
deliberately coarse — one large step between questions (30–44 px), one small step inside a question — so
three questions read as three questions rather than six fields. Question labels moved from the 13 px
tertiary `.hg-label` to a 17 px semibold ink legend: a question is a question, not a micro-label above a
field in a dense console.

The three-option grids are now an explicit 3-up that becomes a 1-up below 560 px, instead of
`repeat(auto-fill, minmax(150px, 1fr))` and whatever happened to fit. The selected card carries a tangerine
inset ring and a 6 % tint instead of the shared near-black, which at a glance was indistinguishable from
the hover border. The CTA owns its row and goes full-width on a phone; the reassurance line sits under it.
The standing hint below the form is **deleted** — it was the lede again in different words, and the page
made the same promise three times.

## 199.5 Localization

49 Burmese strings written for the marketing homepage (`packages/i18n/locales/my/marketing.json › v11`):
the hero, the three "why Hangyul" sections, three service rows with their image alt text, all ten FAQ
question/answer pairs, and the closing band. Placeholders (`{{count}}`, `{{n}}`) and inline markup
(`<br>`, `<em>`, `<span class="text-blue">`, `<h2 class="mb-4">`) were diffed token-by-token against
English before the file was written; the register follows the existing `v10`/`v17` Burmese, and the brand
stays Latin "Hangyul" as it is in the other 70 occurrences in that bundle.

Marketing coverage for `my`: 1,250 → **1,299 / 1,632**. Status remains `SYNTHETIC_NATIVE_REVIEWED`.

## 199.6 Product-wide behaviour fixes found by the error matrix

**An unknown entitlement is not "unpaid".** `PlanGate` guarded on `q.isLoading` only. The moment
`GET /me/plan` *failed*, the query left the loading state with no data, `paid` evaluated false, and a
student who had paid was redirected to `/services?gate=documents` — told to buy something they already
owned because the server returned a 500 or the train went into a tunnel. It now requires a definite answer
(`!isLoading && !isError && data !== undefined`); an error lets the page render and show its own error
state, because a student who cannot reach the API has a connectivity problem, not an entitlement problem.

**`fetch` has no timeout, so now the client does.** A connection that opens and stalls left the promise
pending for as long as the OS kept the socket: react-query never left `isPending` and the screen showed
skeletons forever. `packages/api-client` now carries a 20 s deadline (180 s for uploads, because a passport
scan on a slow connection legitimately takes longer and cancelling one would be a worse bug), composed
manually rather than with `AbortSignal.any`, which Hermes does not ship and this client runs in the native
app too. A timeout surfaces as `ApiError(408)` — the real status for it, and one the existing retry policy
does not retry, so a stalled request fails once and shows a retry button instead of stacking three more
twenty-second waits behind it. A caller's own abort still throws `AbortError`, so a cancelled query is not
recorded as a failure.

## 199.7 Smaller fixes

- **Disabled buttons are neutral**, not faded brand colour: `--btn-bg: surface-sunken`,
  `--btn-fg: text-tertiary`. The shape, size and position are unchanged so nothing moves when the button
  activates — which is what makes the moment it turns tangerine mean something. Two source-order traps had
  to be closed: `.hg-btn[disabled]` and `.hg-btn--primary` have *equal* specificity, so the disabled rule
  had to move below every variant; and `.ed .hg-btn--primary` in the Eduan glue sets `background` directly,
  carries two classes, and loads later still — so it is now guarded with `:not([disabled])`. Every variant
  hover/active is guarded the same way, or a disabled button lit up under the cursor.
- **`OptionCards` is a real radiogroup**: one tab stop, arrow keys with selection following focus, Home/End.
  It also takes a `className` now.
- **`Reveal` paints its armed state before showing** — two `requestAnimationFrame`s — so an element already
  in the viewport at mount actually animates. Below-fold elements are unaffected: their observer fires
  seconds later and ~33 ms is invisible.
- **The closing CTA band has an entrance**, `rise`, like the section heads it follows.
- **Student Home's journey strip** lost its bespoke 24 px / 12 px inset and now sits on the page's own
  gutter with its caption; on phones the six-tile scroller is replaced by a progress line (stage name,
  "2/6", a bar) and the stage sentence, in one card. The tiles stay in the DOM and the progress line is
  `aria-hidden`, so a screen reader still gets the real list rather than a decorative summary.
- **Student and Agency 404 pages** pass `headingLevel={1}`, so the document has a heading.
- **Documents lost its badge wall.** Every list on that page is built with `rows.filter(r => r.state === s)`
  and rendered under a heading that names that state, so the per-row status pill was identical on every row
  of its group and repeated the heading directly above it — eight rows of "할 일 있음" under a section
  called "직접 해야 할 일". A badge on every row of a list carries no information. `DossierRowItem` now
  takes `stateInHeading`, which drops the pill *and gives its 140 px column back to the content* (leaving
  an empty column where a badge used to be is how a removal starts looking like a bug); the state text
  stays in the row as `hg-sr-only`, because a screen-reader user who jumped straight to a row by its title
  never heard the heading. The pill remains wherever rows of different states can sit together.

- **Student Home's "다가오는 일정" rows are bounded.** Each row joins every *other* requirement falling on
  the same date with ` · `. The title above it was clamped to two lines; that line was not, so a date
  carrying four requirements rendered a four-line run-on inside a 320 px column — the densest thing on the
  screen, and the clearest instance of the wall-of-text the owner means by "does not feel premium". It now
  gets the same two-line budget as the title.
- **Agency Writing Insights stops offering dead controls.** The page is managers-only and the API answers
  403 to everyone else, which renders as a clear "you don't have access · ask your organization's admin".
  The period picker sat in the page header above that message, so a counsellor was offered three date
  ranges, each of which fetched another 403 and changed nothing. The header omits them when the query is
  forbidden.

## 199.8 Gates

- **`scripts/qa/v17-gate.mjs`**: three hardcoded `32`s replaced with `EXPECTED_MARKETS`. V18 corrected that
  literal in one place and missed three others, so opening Myanmar as the 33rd market left `qa:v17` red —
  on the language selector count, on the printed line, and on the native flag module. The gate now tests
  what it is for (that the generated flag module is *in step with* `apps/flags`) rather than that it holds
  a particular number. **This is a gate updated because a deliberate product decision invalidated it, with
  the reason recorded — not a test weakened to go green.**
- **New: `npm run qa:v19`** (`scripts/qa/v19-gate.mjs`) — 66 checks.
- **New: `npm run test:release`** (`scripts/release/test-release.mjs`).
- **New instruments**: `scripts/qa/v19/{error-matrix,click-map,student-sweep,console-sweep,locale-shots,
  journey,native-a11y}.mjs` — all wired to `npm run qa:v19-*` — plus the probes `_motion-trace`,
  `_scroll-probe`, `_measure-top`, `_align`, `_perf`, `_ovf`, `_tbl`, `_403`, `_inert`, `_pay`,

- **New release scripts**: `scripts/release/v19-android-build.sh` and `scripts/release/v19-build-info.mjs`,

- **New e2e**: `e2e/v19-scroll.spec.ts`, seven cases.

## 200.2 Motion

Re-traced after the fix (§192.1 table). The hero now animates — the frame strip shows the stagger running,
and the closing CTA settles at 867 ms where before it had no transition at all. **No duration token was
changed in V19**, because watching the result showed V18's numbers were already right.

Interface motion is untouched and `qa:v18` still asserts it: `fast` 120 ms, `base` 180 ms, `slow` 260 ms.

## 200.3 The recommendation results, audited against the brief's §27

The answer screen is the free product's payoff, so it was driven and photographed rather than reasoned
about (`docs/qa/v19/screenshots/marketing/after-start-results@{390,1440}.png`, Mongolia / bachelor's / no
language score).

What it does right, measured against "a student should think *I can see a path to Korea*":

- It **leads with possibility**: "지금 지원할 수 있는 과정이 31개 있어요" — a count of open courses, not a
  rejection, not a deadline, not a tuition figure.
- Six rows, each carrying the university, the programme, the city and a fit **in words**. No percentage,
  no 합격, nothing that reads as a prediction.
- The unlock line is a fact rather than a warning: "TOPIK 3이면 21개 과정이 더 열려요".
- The conversion CTA comes **after** the value, and the disclaimer after that.
- The CTA was correctly disabled until all three questions were answered — the capture script failed on
  its first run for exactly that reason, which is the feature working.

Two gaps against §27, both **specified and not implemented**, and both carried in §209.3:

1. **No university image or logo.** §27 names it. `POST /public/quick-eligibility` returns
   `university_slug` but no crest, so this needs either an API field or a client-side lookup against the
   marquee crest manifest — and that manifest covers the marquee set, not all 425 institutions, so a
   partially-populated logo column would look broken rather than rich. Left alone deliberately.
2. **No "why" per row.** The API already returns `reason` and `reason_code`
   (`LANGUAGE_BELOW`, `LANGUAGE_GAP_SMALL`, `S_BLOCKED`), and the UI shows neither. `reason` is English
   prose, so it cannot be rendered directly into 33 locales; `reason_code` is the right hook, but there
   are no `v17.quick.reason.*` strings and inventing them means new copy in 33 markets, which §24
   explicitly warns against doing to make a pass look fuller. It is a wire-up plus 3 × 33 strings for
   whoever picks it up.

One observation that is data-shaped rather than a defect: with *no* language score every row returns the
same `NOT_YET` tier, so the list shows six identical fit badges under a headline promising 31 open
courses. It is accurate, and a student with TOPIK 4 sees a mix — but the all-identical case is the one a
first-time visitor is most likely to hit, and it is worth a product decision rather than a code change.

## 200.4 Rendering

`qa:v19` section D opens `/`, `/start`, `/universities`, `/privacy`, `/terms` and a deliberate 404 at 390
and 1440 — twelve screens — and checks for console errors, uncaught exceptions, horizontal overflow, raw

## 205.1 The per-locale sweep found one more defect — introduced by this pass

`npm run qa:v19-locales` renders `/start` and `/universities` in **all 33 market locales at 390 and 1440**
— 132 screenshots in `docs/qa/v19/screenshots/locales/` — and checks each for document overflow and for
clipped controls. The first run was not clean:

```
✗ ja start@390: overflow=408>390
```

Japanese `/start` overflowed the viewport by 18 px, and nothing else in 33 locales did. The cause was
`word-break: keep-all` on the new `.mk-pagehead` — written **in this pass**, in §199.2.

`keep-all` is a **Korean** rule, not a CJK one. Korean has spaces, so it stops a line breaking inside a
어절 and makes a heading break where it would be spoken. Japanese and Chinese have no spaces, so the same
declaration turns a whole sentence into one unbreakable token: the intro block measured 392 px inside a
358 px container. Unscoped, a rule that looks like it was written for CJK breaks exactly the two CJK
markets. It is now `:lang(ko)`-scoped, and the sweep is clean:

```
132 screenshots → docs/qa/v19/screenshots/locales
No overflow and no clipped control on any market locale.
```

Worth stating plainly: this was a **regression V19 created and V19's own new instrument caught**, which is
the argument for the per-locale sweep the brief asked for and V18 skipped. No existing gate would have seen
it — `qa:locales` tests the homepage, not `/start`.

Long tail unchanged and ungated. `npm run qa:v18-locales`, run this pass:

```
V18 CORE complete:  33/33 markets
FULL core complete: 1/33 markets (not gated)
FULL core gap:      70653 strings across all markets
PASS — every exposed market owns the V18 core conversion surface.
```

70,702 → **70,653**: exactly the 49 strings V19 wrote, and not one more. Myanmar's full-surface coverage
moved to 93.3 %. Per-locale numbers in `npm run i18n:check`. No `HUMAN_REVIEWED` claim anywhere.

## 206.1 The whole journey, as one user

`npm run qa:v19-journey` walks the path a stranger actually takes and counts what the brief asks about —
clicks, scroll surprises, dead ends, unexpected route jumps, lost context. It is a step of `test:release`
from now on; this pass ran it standalone, after the recorded release run had already started. Run in
Korean and in Vietnamese:

```
step                                clicks  scrollY   route
1 homepage                               0        0   /?lang=vi
2 scrolled to the closing band           0     6209   /?lang=vi
3 click 유학 준비                           1        0   /start?lang=vi
4 nationality                            2        0   /start?lang=vi
5 study level                            3        0   /start?lang=vi
6 language score                         4        0   /start?lang=vi
7 see my universities                    5      978   /start?lang=vi
8 open a recommended university          6        0   /universities/yonsei-university?lang=vi&from=recommendation
9 plan CTA target                        7        0   http://localhost:3101/register?next=%2Fservices%3Fplan%3Dbasic&lang=vi

7 clicks from landing to the plan handoff · 6 recommendations returned
No scroll surprise, no dead end, no unexpected route jump, no lost context.
```

Seven clicks from a cold landing to the authenticated plan handoff. The language survives all nine steps
including the cross-origin hop; `from=recommendation` reaches the university page so it can carry the
thread; the chosen plan rides inside `next=` through registration. The 978 px at step 7 is deliberate —
the page moves to the answer, which is the point of the free product.

One more instrument correction, for the same reason as the others: the first run reported "the plan CTA
carries no plan". The plan is there, percent-encoded inside `next=%2Fservices%3Fplan%3Dbasic`; the
assertion was matching the raw href. It decodes first now.

# 207. V19 Error-Matrix Validation

V17 named this. V18 said "the §44 matrix was not run". It is run.

`scripts/qa/v19/error-matrix.mjs` — **10 high-value Student pages × 12 conditions × 2 widths = 240 cells.**
Each cell loads the page with that failure forced on its own data calls (auth is left alone except on the
`401` row, where the redirect *is* the behaviour under test), with the react-query cache cleared first so a
previous healthy result cannot answer for it.

**Zero acceptance**, applied as assertions: raw JSON or a raw API error on screen · a blank page · an
endless spinner · layout collapse · an uncaught console exception · a toast hidden behind the mobile
bottom navigation · a 401 that does not reach the sign-in page.

```
Error matrix @ 1440px — 10 pages × 12 conditions
page         load empt part offl  401  403  404  409  422  429  500 time
home           ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·
explore        ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·
applications   ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·
documents      ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·
essays         ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·
messages       ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·
visa           ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·
services       ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·
notifications  ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·
profile        ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·    ·
120 cells, 0 failing.        (390 px: 120 cells, 0 failing.)
```

That is the **final** state. The first run was not clean, and what it found is the point of the exercise:

| first-run failure | verdict |
|---|---|
| `documents/offline`, `documents/500` → the **paywall**, plus 10 spinners | **Real, serious.** A failed plan query downgraded a paying student to the sales page. Fixed in §199.6 |
| `documents/timeout` → 8 skeletons still animating | **Real.** No client-side deadline. Fixed in §199.6 |
| `409/422/429` → "toast behind bottom nav" at **1440 px** | **Instrument.** A `display: none` tab bar reports a zero-height rect at the top of the viewport, so every desktop row matched. Now only a bar that is actually on screen counts |
| `empty`/`partial` → "layout collapse" | **Instrument.** The route error boundary deliberately replaces the shell with a human message and a Reload button. A handled failure is not a collapse |
| `home/loading` → "blank" with 6 skeletons present | **Instrument.** A loading screen has no text and is not blank |
| `home/404` → "blank" at 15 characters | **Instrument.** "페이지를 찾을 수 없습니다." is a correct, concise empty state; a flat character count called it a defect |

Four of six first-run failures were the harness. They are listed rather than quietly deleted, because the
difference between a defect and a bad assertion is the whole value of the exercise, and a pass that only
reports the findings that survived is not showing its work.

A seventh appeared later and is worth recording for the same reason. Run *concurrently* with the rest of
`test:release`, the matrix reported `profile/partial: LAYOUT-COLLAPSE | BLANK` once; two clean re-runs
showed the page had simply not finished rendering inside a 5 s budget on a contended machine. A harness
that reports a defect when the CPU is busy is not measuring the product, so it now waits for the app to
have *said something* — text, a skeleton, or a handled state — before starting its settle clock, with the
fixed period on top. A page that never says anything is still the finding.

Evidence: `docs/qa/v19/evidence/error-matrix-1440.json`, `error-matrix-390.json`; failure screenshots in
`docs/qa/v19/screenshots/student/errors/`.

# 208. V19 QA Ledger

## 208.1 Every gate, run with the full stack alive

V18's honest headline was "`qa:v12`–`qa:v17` were not validly run this pass because the full dev stack was
not up". They are run. API :8001, Marketing :3100, Student :3101, Agency :3102, University :3103 and the
review bundle on :4173 were all verified by HTTP first.

| gate | result | note |
|---|---|---|
| `qa:v12` | **PASS** | data-map · legal · leak — 72 rendered routes scanned, 0 leaks |
| `qa:v13` | **PASS** | composition · 14-country probe |
| `qa:v14` | **PASS** | **was FAILING** — 8 Myanmar English leaks; fixed by translating the homepage (§197) |
| `qa:v15` | **PASS** | pricing · entitlements · handoff · agency · university |
| `qa:v16` | **PASS** | 1 documented skip (the order contract needs a contracted currency; covered by 12 server tests) |
| `qa:v17` | **PASS** | **was FAILING** — three hardcoded `32`s and an unserved review bundle (§199.8) |
| `qa:v18` | **PASS** | 38 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| `qa:v19` | **FAIL** | **66 passed, 1 failed** — new. The single failure is deliberate: check F (below) |

One ordering flaw in `test:release` was found by watching it run and has been corrected for future runs:
`qa:v17` renders pages out of `dist-review/` to check the server-free stakeholder build, but
`review:build` was scheduled in the *last* group — so on the run recorded above, `qa:v17` validated a
bundle built before any V19 change. The step now runs **before** the gates. A release check that validates
a stale artifact is the same class of mistake as one that skips a test, and it is the second time in this
pass that the thing being checked was older than the thing it was checked against (§194.3 is the first).

`npm run release:check` is run by `test:release` and **reported rather than gated**. It is a
business-readiness checklist — does the company legally exist in the product, is a payment provider
contracted, has Korean counsel reviewed the terms, are documents on encrypted production storage, were
usability sessions run with real students — and it fails on 2/6, 10/14 and 24/29 requirements across its
three tiers. Every one of those is an owner or external blocker (§209.2) that no code change can turn
green, so counting it as a code failure would make `test:release` permanently red for reasons unrelated to
the tree, and a check that is always red is a check nobody reads. It is still executed on every run and
its three tier summaries are printed in full: that is the opposite of a silent skip.

Two of the eight were red when this pass started, and both were red because V18 did not run them.

### The one red gate at the end of V19, and why it is left red

```
F. The native artifacts match the source they were built from
  ✗ the Android artifacts predate their source by 3.8h — newest change: packages/i18n/locales/_meta.json.
    Rebuild and recompute the checksums (REPORT §194.3).
```

`qa:v18` verifies that each listed SHA256 matches the binary on disk and that `BUILD_INFO.json` is
complete. Both of those can be true of a binary built from code that no longer exists — which is exactly
what V18 reported about its own status-bar fix, and exactly what V19 did again by changing
`packages/api-client`. **Nothing in the suite could see it**, so `qa:v19` now compares the recorded build
time against the newest source file the native bundle actually compiles.

It fails. That is the correct result and it is not being worked around. A release check that goes green
while the shipped binary predates the code is the failure mode this entire pass exists to attack, and the
alternative — leaving the check out so the ledger reads 8/8 — would be the V18 mistake with a V19 label on
it. It stays red until somebody rebuilds the artifacts.

**So the honest headline is seven of eight gates green, and the eighth red on one check that says "the
native work in §209.3 has not been done".**

### The gate was mutation-tested, because a gate that cannot fail is decoration

`qa:v19` is 66 green assertions written by the same pass that made the code green, which is the easiest
way in the world to write a gate that asserts nothing. So the central one was deliberately broken:
`--kn-page-breathe` was changed from `32px` to `4px` and the gate re-run.

```
✗ /start?lang=ko @320: 4px clear after the pill, want 28–40px
✗ /start?lang=ko @360: 4px clear after the pill, want 28–40px
✗ /start?lang=ko @390: 4px clear after the pill, want 28–40px
✗ /start?lang=ko @430: 4px clear after the pill, want 28–40px
✗ /start?lang=en @320 … (and the rest)
```

It catches the regression on the first width it measures, and names the number and the band. The token was
restored immediately and re-verified at 32 px / 390 and 60 px / 1440.

**And it contaminated the release run, which is worth admitting rather than tidying away.** The mutation
was applied while `test:release` happened to be executing its own `qa:v19` step, so that step recorded
**58 passed, 9 failed** — the eight page-top assertions plus check F — instead of the 66/1 the tree
actually produces. The first version of this paragraph claimed the run was clean, on the strength of
grepping the release log for "clear after the pill" and finding nothing; that was wrong, because
`test:release` prints only the last fourteen lines of a failing step and the page-top failures had scrolled
off the top of its own output. The authoritative figure below is a standalone re-run on the restored tree.
Two lessons, both earned the hard way in this pass: do not mutate a tree while a suite is reading it, and
do not verify an absence with a grep against truncated output.

### 22 e2e tests did not run, and all 22 are one blocker

`test:e2e` exits 0 with **22 of 74 tests skipped**, which is the kind of green tick V17 was criticised for.
They are not *silent* skips — every one carries a reason at its `test.skip()` — but the release summary
was not surfacing them, so `test:release` now prints any step that passed while withholding tests.

Listing them shows a single cause. Every skipped test needs a **paid case**, and a plan cannot be bought:
the merchant is not contracted for USD, so `POST /me/orders` answers `503 CURRENCY_NOT_CONTRACTED` and
`buyPlan()` stands the test down with that reason. The affected journeys are the purchase itself, document
review, all five writing/essay flows, guided submission, visa, arrival, and the three agency-acting-on-
behalf-of-a-student cases.

So the honest reading is: **52 of 52 runnable tests pass, and 30 % of the suite is gated behind
§209.2 row 1.** That is one owner action away from running, not a gap in the tests, and it is the single
largest piece of untested behaviour in the product.

## 208.3 The click-map

V17 asked for it, V18 did not build it. `scripts/qa/v19/click-map.mjs` enumerates every visible interactive
control on 20 primary routes, activates it, and puts it in exactly one bucket. No silent coverage holes:
the bucket totals are the coverage claim.

**596 controls across 20 routes at 1440 px — 366 tested · 2 intentionally disabled · 217 unreachable ·
11 inert · 0 broken.**

"Unreachable" is a coverage fact, not a defect: the great majority are the university marquee's cloned
`aria-hidden inert` logos (which exist precisely so a reader meets each university once), the
visually-hidden skip link that only materialises on focus, and footer links inside collapsed `<details>`.
An earlier version of this map called 11 of those "broken" because a Playwright click timeout fell through
to the wrong bucket; that was corrected rather than reported.

Of the 11 inert, nine are **self-links** — the logo on Home, the "홈" tab while on Home, the "메시지" tab
while on Messages, the already-selected 전국 region chip. A nav item for the page you are already on doing
nothing is correct. The tenth is the header's 유학 준비 CTA on `/start`, which points at `/start`: harmless,
and noted rather than changed because the header is shared by every page.

**The eleventh was a real defect, and a commercial one.** On `/services`, "프리미엄으로 변경" did nothing —
no panel, no navigation, no toast, no console error, for ever. `OrderBlock` was rendered only when
`!d.plan`, so for anyone who already owned a plan there was nothing for the upgrade button to reveal. The
same held for `?upgrade=<plan>`, the deep link the contextual upgrade sheet uses when a student is refused
a capability. **The entire upgrade path was unreachable for exactly the people who had already paid once.**
Fixed in §199; verified end to end afterwards: the order block now opens on Premium US$599 and the pay
button reaches the honest refusal "해외카드 USD 결제가 아직 활성화되지 않았어요. 다른 통화로 청구하지
않습니다".

   essay surface, the typography scale, the accessibility sweep, the payment deep-link matrix and
   signed-in runtime testing need no credential and were simply not reached; the Android SDK, NDK and
   three AVDs are all present on this host, so the constraint was time, not tooling. **This is the single
   largest outstanding item.** The *artifact rebuild* specifically is blocked on the keystore password
   (§194.5, §209.2 row 9a) and has moved to the externally-blocked list.
2. **Student Web beyond Home and Documents.** The brief asked for a question/action/failure/removal/fix
   record on 26 screens and three documented design passes. What was done is a structural pass on Home and
   on Documents, fixes to the shared controls every screen uses, and a complete defect sweep of all 30
   routes. Documents' remaining duplication — the summary line restating the counts its own group headings
   carry, and one row mixing a Korean label with an English body from seed data — is specified in §193.3
   and not implemented. The other 24 screens got a defect sweep, not a design pass.
3. **Student Home's right-hand column** still truncates its *titles* at two lines in a 320 px track — the
   clamp is working, but the column is narrow for the content it is given, and that is a layout decision
   rather than a bug. One seeded item also renders English inside a Korean screen. The dense secondary
   line below each title **was** fixed (§199.7).
3a. **The recommendation rows carry no logo and no "why"** — both named in the brief's §27, both
   specified in §200.3 with the exact reason each was left alone.
4. **`/start`'s header CTA points at `/start`.** Harmless, and left alone because the header is shared by
   every page and special-casing one route in it is a worse trade than a no-op button.
5. **The APK size work.** §194.4 now answers *why* it is 120 MB with measured numbers — 80.6 MB of native
   libs across four ABIs, 44.4 MB of which is emulator-only x86; 42.8 MB of unminified dex because no
   `expo-build-properties` plugin enables R8. Acting on either means rebuilding, which is blocked (§194.5).

## 209.4 The honest summary

The web product is materially better and the claim is backed by measurements that can be re-run. The native
product is exactly where V18 left it, and one step worse, because shared code moved underneath its
artifacts. Anyone reading only §209.1 would get the wrong impression; §209.3 is the other half.

# 210. V19 Final Hostile Audit

Assume a competitor built this and the job is to reject it.

**"You fixed the screenshot."** Partly fair, and the defence is the method rather than the result. The
owner reported one page being too close to the header; what shipped is a derived token that three page
families consume, a gate that fails if the pill's height and the clearance variable ever disagree, and nine
measured widths per page. The scroll complaint was one button; what shipped is a policy for four apps with
seven e2e cases. Neither was solved where it was reported.

**"Student Web still is not redesigned."** True, and §209.3 says so first rather than last. Home and
Documents are recomposed and the shared controls underneath every screen are fixed — the disabled button,
the radiogroup, the 404 heading, the request deadline, the entitlement gate. Twenty-four other screens were
opened, measured and found defect-free, but *defect-free is not premium* and this pass did not make them
premium. The brief asked for three documented design passes across Student; it got one, on two screens.

**"Native is untouched."** True, and worse than untouched: `packages/api-client` changed, so the committed
APK and AAB no longer match source. The pass did not rebuild them and does not pretend the old checksums
still mean anything. Four of V18's eleven admissions are repeated verbatim in §194 as still open. That is
the correct report and a poor outcome.

Two things V19 did do about it. It made the gap impossible to lose — `qa:v19` check F compares the
artifact's build time against the newest source it bundles, so **this pass ends with a red gate**, and the
red gate says "the native artifacts are stale". Shipping a suite that reads 8/8 while §194.3 admits the
binaries predate the code would have been the exact dishonesty this section exists to catch. And it
actually started the rebuild, which is how the real blocker surfaced: the keystore password is not in this
repository, and a build without it is silently debug-signed rather than failing (§194.5). "Not attempted"
would have hidden that; it is now one named owner action with a scripted path behind it.

**"Then your own pass introduced a regression."** It did — `word-break: keep-all` on the new page head,
which broke Japanese and Chinese line-wrapping on `/start` while looking like a CJK-aware rule. V19's own
per-locale sweep caught it within the hour (§205.1). The uncomfortable part is not that it happened but
that no pre-existing gate would have: `qa:locales` tests the homepage, and the defect was on a different
page in two of thirty-three markets.

**"Your error matrix found four of its six failures in its own code."** Yes, and §207 lists them. The
alternative — quietly deleting the bad assertions and reporting only the two real defects — would have
produced a cleaner section and a less trustworthy one. The same happened to the university console: two
"clipped tables" were screen-reader alternatives behind charts, and the instrument was wrong. An audit that
never catches itself is not being run honestly.

**"Thirty per cent of your e2e suite never ran."** True, and `test:release` was reporting it as a green
tick until this pass made it print withheld tests. 22 of 74 skip, every one of them because a plan cannot
be bought while USD is uncontracted — so document review, all five essay flows, guided submission, visa,
arrival and the agency-on-behalf cases are **untested behaviour**, not passing behaviour. One owner action
unblocks all 22 at once (§209.2 row 1), and until then the product's entire paid half rests on unit tests
and manual walkthroughs.

**"How much of this would a user notice?"** The `/start` overlap and the scroll bug: immediately, on the
free product's first screen. The hero not animating: on the homepage, every visit. The paywall-on-error and
the dead upgrade button: only when something goes wrong or when they try to pay more money — which is to
say, at exactly the two moments that decide whether the product gets paid.

**"And you broke your own release run."** Also true. The mutation test that proves `qa:v19` can fail
(§208.1) was applied while `test:release` was reading the tree, so that run's `qa:v19` step recorded 58/9
instead of 66/1 — and the first draft of this report claimed the run was clean, on the strength of a grep
against output `test:release` had already truncated. The number was corrected from a standalone re-run and
the mistake is written down beside it. Two rules earned: do not mutate a tree a suite is reading, and do
not prove an absence with a grep against truncated output.

**"What is still ugly?"** Student Home's right column truncates almost every line. Documents still states
its counts twice — once in the summary, once in the group headings — even with the badge wall gone. The
journey tiles are still six near-identical boxes on desktop. Seeded content mixes English into Korean
screens. None of that is a defect any gate will catch, and all of it is what the owner means by "does not
feel premium".

**"What would most change this product next?"** Not a feature, and not another audit. Three things, in
order: get the keystore properties and rebuild the native artifacts, so the red gate goes green and the
binaries mean something; then do the signed-in native runtime testing that has now been outstanding for
two passes; then give the remaining 24 Student screens the per-screen pass that Home and Documents got.

**Not claimed:** that the product is finished, that Student Web is premium, that native is release-grade,
that any translation has been reviewed by a native speaker, or that live payment works.

# 211. V20 University Experience Audit

Read first: §86 (V12 directory and detail), §150 and §158 (V17 enrichment), §192 (V19 marketing visual).
Then the running product at `localhost:3100`, which is newer than all three.

## 211.1 What `/universities` is today

Two text columns, 24 rows a page, 18 pages. Each row is a name, an alternate name, three grey words
(region · kind · establishment) and up to two IEQAS chips. **There is no image anywhere on the page** —
not a logo, not a thumbnail, not a mark. The comment at the top of `InstitutionTile` records why: V14
built a 16:10 thumbnail per row, discovered that 424 of 425 rows drew the same peach placeholder, and
removed it. That was the right call then and it is the wrong state now, because the conclusion it reached
— *no picture is better than the same picture* — is only one of the four tiers §19 asks for.

Secondary defects, all visible in `docs/qa/v20/before/dir-1440.png`:

- **Ragged vertical rhythm.** Rows are different heights because some carry chips and some do not, and the
  two columns are independent, so the hairlines across the page never line up. At 1440 the eye reads a
  broken grid before it reads a university.
- **The map owns a third of the first screen and answers one question.** It is good, it is keyboard
  operable, and below it 425 institutions are listed alphabetically from "ACTS University" — which is the
  least informative possible first row.
- **No ordering a prospective student would choose.** Alphabetical-within-type. There is no way to see the
  institutions that actually have something to show.

## 211.2 What `/universities/:slug` is today

Two different pages, depending on one boolean (`resolveVisual(...).media !== null`):

| | universities | what the page is |
|---|---|---|
| with a photograph | **1** (Seoul National) | photo band → breadcrumb → logo → name → facts → CTA → gallery → video → table → IEQAS → sources |
| without | **424** | breadcrumb → name → facts → CTA → table → IEQAS → sources |

The 424-case is `docs/qa/v20/before/ks-1440.png`: at 1440 the content occupies the left 56 % of the page
and the right 44 % is empty white from the breadcrumb to the footer. The first thing under the name is
`Busan · University · Private`; the second is a four-row table whose rows are Region, Institution,
Established as, Majors disclosed. The brief's test — *remove the Hangyul logo, would this page still
obviously belong to THIS university?* — fails for all 424. Nothing on the page is specific to Kyungsung
except the name, the founding year and the website link.

The 1-case (`snu-1440.png`) is better and still not what §10 describes. The photograph is a 420 px band
the page scrolls past; the logo, name and location sit **below** it on white, so the hero is a picture and
a header rather than one composition. The gallery is two 300 px images left-aligned in a column that ends
at 50 % of the viewport. There is no identity sentence, no "why this university", no education philosophy,
no international-student section, no city, no dormitory.

## 211.3 Section inventory against §12

| §12 section | present today | source available |
|---|---|---|
| 01 hero | partial — photo band, not a composition | — |
| 02 why this university | **no** | not collected |
| 03 campus experience | 1 of 425 | 1 institution has ≥2 attribution-free photos |
| 04 academic identity | **no** (`major_count` only) | registry has counts, not fields |
| 05 education philosophy | 5 of 425 (`motto`) | Wikidata P1451 only; official sites unread |
| 06 international student life | IEQAS chips only | not collected |
| 07 campus & city life | region word only | `city_ko` 304/425, no city writing |
| 08 dormitory | **no** | not collected |
| 09 official video | 10 channels, **0 videos** | Wikidata P2397 only |
| 10 official links | yes | registry + Wikidata |
| 11 CTA | yes | — |

Four of eleven sections exist. Three of the four that matter most for desire (02, 05, 06) have no data
behind them at all.

## 211.4 Student / marketing divergence (§30, §54)

`apps/student-web/src/pages/University.tsx` (620 lines) is a **different content system** on a different
model: `UniversityDetail` from the programme catalogue, five tabs (overview / admissions / costs / life /
sources), `summary` quoted from catalogue text in English only. It shares no component, no resolver and no
media rule with the public page, and it is reachable only for institutions Hangyul holds catalogue data
for. Two public-facing descriptions of the same institution can therefore disagree, and the signed-in one
is the weaker of the two.

## 211.5 Hostile questions, answered honestly

- *Would a 19-year-old want to click another photo?* On 424 pages there is no photo to click.
- *Can they imagine studying there?* No. The page describes a record, not a place.
- *Does it look better than the university's own admissions site?* No — the university's own site has
  photography, a campus map and a video.
- *Does anything look generated?* Yes: the four-row table reads as a database dump, and
  `공시 학과 수 — 80개` is the single most prominent fact about Kyungsung University.

# 212. V20 University Content Coverage Audit

Measured from the committed data, not from a page: `server/app/data/korean_institutions.json` (425 rows,
survey year 2025) joined to `server/app/data/university_enrichment.json` (325 matched records) and
`apps/marketing-web/src/media/credits.json` (26 assets).

| field | coverage | source |
|---|---|---|
| TOTAL UNIVERSITIES | **425** | 대학알리미 (218 university · 163 junior college · 44 graduate) |
| authoritative record matched | 325 / 425 (76 %) | Wikidata |
| LOGO | **14 / 425 (3 %)** | Wikidata P154 → Commons |
| HERO IMAGE | 38 / 425 (9 %) *recorded*, **0 rendered** | Wikidata P18 → Commons |
| GALLERY (≥2 of the same institution) | **1 / 425** | Hangyul media manifest |
| OFFICIAL WEBSITE | 298 / 425 (70 %) | registry 281 + Wikidata 17 |
| MISSION / EDUCATION PHILOSOPHY | **5 / 425 (1 %)** | Wikidata P1451 |
| INTERNATIONAL OFFICE | **0 / 425** | not collected |
| OFFICIAL YOUTUBE CHANNEL | **10 / 425 (2 %)** | Wikidata P2397 |
| OFFICIAL INTRODUCTION VIDEO | **0 / 425** | not collected |
| CAMPUS / CITY (city name) | 304 / 425 (72 %) | Wikidata P131 |
| DORMITORY | **0 / 425** | not collected |
| founding year | 290 / 425 (68 %) | Wikidata P571 |
| coordinates | 276 / 425 (65 %) | Wikidata P625 |
| student count | 8 / 425 (2 %) | Wikidata P2196 |

**The ceiling is the source, not the pipeline.** Wikidata carries almost nothing about Korean junior
colleges: of the 100 institutions with no matched record, 78 are 전문대학. Every remaining field the brief
asks for — 교육이념, international office, dormitory, academic strengths, an introduction video — exists
only on the institution's **own website**, which no pipeline in this repository has ever read.

This is the finding that shapes the plan: V17's enrichment reached its ceiling at Wikidata and the honest
way past it is to read the official sites, which §6 lists as source number one.

# 213. V20 University Media & Rights Audit

## 213.1 What may actually be served

The V14 owner decision stands: **no customer-visible photo attribution**, therefore only
`HANGYUL_OWNED`, `OWNER_AUTHORISED`, `COMMERCIAL_NO_ATTRIBUTION` and `CC0_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` may be hosted
(`scripts/qa/v14-media-licence.mjs`). Against 26 manifest assets:

| | count | of those, **a specific university** |
|---|---|---|
| servable (attribution-free) | 13 | **3** — `snu-main-gate`, `snu-law-library`, `kyunghee-main-building` |
| attribution-required, not served | 13 | 4 — Yonsei ×2, Ewha, KAIST, Kyung Hee library |

`kyunghee-main-building` is CC0, is already encoded at 640/1200/2400 in
`apps/marketing-web/public/media`, and **is not wired to Kyung Hee University.** It is downloaded,
licensed, paid-for work that no page renders. That is the single cheapest coverage gain in this pass.

## 213.2 A live rights defect the gate does not catch

`UniversityStory.UniversityLogo` renders `enrichment.logo.url` **directly from
`upload.wikimedia.org`**. Of the 14 logos recorded:

| licence | n | may be shown with no credit? |
|---|---|---|
| Public domain | 9 | yes |
| CC BY-SA 4.0 | 4 | **no** |
| CC BY-SA 3.0 | 1 | **no** |

So five institutions — Global Cyber, Kumoh, Sungkyul, UNIST, Hansung — are currently serving an
attribution-required image on a customer page with no attribution. `qa:v14` does not see it because it
inspects `credits.json` and the `public/` directories, and these are external URLs in a JSON blob on the
institution row. **The gate's blind spot is that it checks where media is stored, not where media is
rendered from.** V20 closes both: the rights rule moves into the content record, and the gate reads the
content record.

Two further problems with the same code path: the asset is hot-linked from Wikimedia (an uptime and
latency dependency on a third party, in the hero, eagerly loaded), and `hansung-university`'s "logo" is
`Authority.jpg`, which §49's quality gate should refuse on sight.

## 213.3 The cross-assignment rule

`resolveVisual()` already honours §8 — a university's own photograph, else the **region's** photograph
*labelled as the region*, else nothing. No university currently displays another university's campus. That
property must survive this pass, and it is now a gate rather than a convention.

Region photography is a one-row table: `Seoul` only. The Busan pair is CC BY and therefore unusable. So
tier C has imagery for 1 of 17 regions, covering 85 of 425 institutions.

## 213.4 Where media can honestly come from

1. **Commons, CC0/PD only**, searched per institution and per city — the existing `fetch_cc0.py` already
   refuses anything else and records provenance. Unharvested so far.
2. **The official YouTube thumbnail** (`i.ytimg.com`) for an institution with a verified channel and a
   verified introduction video. This is YouTube serving the channel's own artwork as part of an embed
   facade, not Hangyul redistributing a file.
3. **Nothing.** For an institution with neither, a designed typographic composition — which must be good
   enough that it is a choice rather than a gap.

Commissioned photography remains the real fix and remains a launch dependency
(`docs/MEDIA_LICENSE_AUDIT.md`).

# 214. V20 Pricing Presentation Audit

## 214.1 The defect, measured in the running product

`apps/marketing-web/src/pages/home/pricing.tsx` renders
`formatMoney(plan.amount_minor, 'USD', locale, { minor: true })`, which is
`Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' })`. That API's default
`currencyDisplay` is `'symbol'`, and for most non-US locales CLDR's "symbol" for USD **is** `US$` or
`USD`. Read off the live pricing card:

| locale | rendered today | wanted |
|---|---|---|
| `ko` | `US$179` | `$179` |
| `zh-Hans` | `US$179` | `$179` |
| `th` | `US$179` | `$179` |
| `id` | `US$179` | `$179` |
| `vi` | `179 US$` | `179 $` |
| `ms` | `USD 179` | `$179` |
| `en`, `ja`, `tr`, `hi`, `ur`, `tl`, `mn`, `ky`, `uz` | `$179` | unchanged |

Korean is the product's default locale, so **the default reading of the pricing card is the wrong one.**

## 214.2 Scope

This is one call site for the headline, and the same function serves ~20 other call sites where the
currency label is wanted (agency payments mixes KRW and USD in one table; a receipt and a payment history
row must say which currency was charged). So the fix is a *mode*, not a change to `formatMoney`'s default.

## 214.3 Internal currency — nothing to change, and that is checked

`currency: 'USD'` in `packages/types/src/plans.ts`, the order currency, the payment validation, the API
contract and the Toss provider currency are all unchanged by this pass. §152 and §161 recorded the V17
decision; `qa:v15-pricing` and `test_v17_usd_refunds.py` already assert it. V20 adds the inverse assertion:
that the *presentation* layer never prints `US$`/`USD` beside a headline price.

# 215. V20 Primary Button Design-System Audit

## 215.1 Reproduced, with the computed values

`scripts/qa/v20/_orange-probe.mjs` walks every `a` / `button` / `[role=button]` on a page, forces rest,
hover, focus and active, and reports any element whose computed background is a Hangyul tangerine and
whose computed foreground is not a light colour.

Marketing, every public route, 1440 and 390 — **the header "Get started" button fails in `:focus` and
`:active`**:

```
.kn-btn.kn-btn--primary.kn-btn--sm   background rgb(204, 78, 0)   color → rgb(24, 26, 31)
```

`rgb(24,26,31)` is `--hg-text`. White-on-#CC4E00 is 4.5:1; near-black-on-#CC4E00 is **2.4:1**. The probe
caught it mid-transition at `rgb(69,71,75)` because `.kn-btn` animates `color` over 150 ms, which is also
why it reads to the eye as the label *going dark* rather than as a different button.

Student, Agency and University: **0 findings** at rest, hover, focus and active. The defect is specific to
the marketing site, and the reason is specific too.

## 215.2 Root cause

`packages/eduan-ui/src/scss/eduan/abstracts/_common.scss:81`, unscoped, from the licensed template:

```scss
a:focus,
a:hover { color: inherit; text-decoration: none; }
```

Eduan's stylesheet is imported **last** in `apps/marketing-web/src/main.tsx`. Specificity decides the rest:

| selector | specificity | sets |
|---|---|---|
| `.kn-btn--primary` | (0,1,0) | `color: var(--hg-text-on-primary)` |
| `.kn-btn--primary:hover` | (0,2,0) | `color: var(--hg-text-on-primary)` |
| `.kn-btn--primary:active` | (0,2,0) | background **only** |
| `a:focus, a:hover` | (0,1,1) | `color: inherit` |

`:hover` survives because somebody wrote the hover rule. `:focus` and `:active` do not, because
`(0,1,1) > (0,1,0)` and no rule was written for those states. The button inherits from the white header
pill, so "inherit" is near-black.

The same trap is set for `.hg-btn`, which carries its foreground as `color: var(--btn-fg)` on the **base**
class at (0,1,0): any `<a class="hg-btn hg-btn--primary">` rendered inside the marketing site loses its
foreground on `:hover` as well as `:focus`. It does not fail today only because no marketing surface
currently renders one.

**This is a contract that depends on nobody ever writing an `a:pseudo` rule, in a product that imports two
third-party templates.** Patching the two missing states would make the screenshot green and leave the
contract exactly as fragile. §32 asks for the cascade fixed properly, so the fix is both: scope the
template reset so it stops reaching out of the template, *and* make the primary-solid foreground
state-complete and specificity-proof.

## 215.3 Contrast

`--hg-primary #CC4E00` against `#FFFFFF` is **4.51:1** — AA for normal text, AA Large for ≥18.66 px bold,
and it already passes. `--hg-primary-hover #B34400` is 5.4:1 and `--hg-primary-pressed #9E3C00` is 6.4:1,
so the button gets *more* contrast as it is pressed. **No background shade change is needed** and §34's
conditional does not fire.

## 215.4 Variants — what must not be touched

Only the solid tangerine surface takes white. `--outline` (white on `--hg-border-control`, tangerine label
on hover), `--onphoto` (white pill, dark label), `--quiet-onphoto` (dark translucent, white label),
`--soft`, `--ghost`, `--link` and `[disabled]` (V19's neutral surface, tertiary text) all keep their own
foregrounds. A blanket "white text on buttons" rule would destroy four of those.

## 215.5 Native

`packages/mobile-ui/src/components/Button.tsx` is already correct for the enabled states: `primary` takes
`theme.color.textOnPrimary` (`#FFFFFF`) and both icons are rendered with `color={p.fg}`, so label and icon
are white at rest, pressed and loading. **One defect:** `disabled` is `{ opacity: 0.5 }` over the
tangerine fill — the same washed-out brand colour V19 removed from the web for being at roughly 1.9:1 and
reading as broken. Native was not brought along. §38 permits a neutral disabled surface and that is the
fix.

# 216. V20 Implementation Plan

Three goals, in the order they will be done, smallest first so the university work gets the rest.

## 216.1 Pricing — presentation only

1. `formatMoney` gains `currencyDisplay`-aware behaviour through one new option, `symbolOnly`, which
   (a) asks Intl for `narrowSymbol` and (b) if the locale *still* emits letters in the currency part
   (Arabic has no narrow symbol for USD), substitutes the canonical symbol taken from `en`. Built from
   `formatToParts`, so a locale that puts the symbol after the number keeps its own order.
2. The marketing pricing card, the Student services/plan prices and the Student upgrade sheet pass it.
   Checkout, receipts, payment history and the agency payments table **do not** — a line that says what
   was charged needs the code.
3. `qa:v20` asserts `$179 / $349 / $599` on the rendered card in all 33 locales and asserts the string
   `USD` is still present in the plan type, the order payload and the payment contract.

## 216.2 Primary button — one contract, enforced

1. **Scope the template reset.** `a:focus, a:hover { color: inherit }` becomes `:where(.ed) a:focus,
   :where(.ed) a:hover` — the same `:where(.ed)` wrapper `_hangyul-glue.scss` already uses for Eduan's
   `a` rule, so it keeps zero specificity and stops applying outside Eduan markup.
2. **Make the contract state-complete.** `.kn-btn--primary` and `.hg-btn--primary` declare their
   foreground for rest, `:link`, `:visited`, `:hover`, `:focus`, `:focus-visible` and `:active`, and the
   icon takes `currentColor`. Written as one grouped rule each, next to the variant, with the reason.
3. **Make it provable.** `scripts/qa/v20/button-matrix.mjs` sweeps all four products at two widths,
   forces the four states on every control, and fails on any solid-tangerine surface whose computed
   foreground or icon colour is not light. It also renders a 5-variant × 5-state × 2-width sheet to
   `docs/qa/v20/buttons/`.
4. Native `disabled` moves to the neutral surface.

## 216.3 University — the centrepiece

**Data first.** A repeatable pipeline under `scripts/universities/`, because §41 forbids one-off JSX:

| script | what it does | source order |
|---|---|---|
| `research-official.mjs` | robots-aware read of each institution's own site: 교육이념/건학이념/교훈, international-office URL, admissions URL, dormitory URL, outbound YouTube link | §6 steps 1–5 |
| `harvest-media.mjs` | Commons search per institution and per city, **CC0/PD only**, focal point per asset | §7 |
| `verify-youtube.mjs` | a channel counts as official only if the institution's own site links to it, or Wikidata P2397 asserts it; then pick one introduction video | §16 |
| `audit-content.mjs` | the coverage table and `docs/qa/v20/UNIVERSITY_CONTENT_COVERAGE.csv` | §44 |

Output is one canonical record per institution in `server/app/data/university_content.json`, every value
carrying `source_url`, `verified_at` and `verification_status`, every asset additionally carrying
`media_source`, `license_or_permission`, `official_asset`, `attribution_requirement` and
`local_path`/`external_url` (§42). The seeder merges it onto `Institution.enrichment`, which is JSONB, so
there is no migration.

**One model, one resolver.** `packages/university-content` exports the content type, the four-tier visual
resolver (§19) and the city/region editorial layer — written once, by hand, for 17 regions and the
cities that actually carry institutions, factual rather than touristic (§28). Marketing imports it;
Student's university page imports the same identity components above its operational tabs (§30, §54).

**Then the pages.** The detail page is rebuilt as an editorial composition — full-bleed hero with the
logo, name, place and one identity line over a controlled gradient; then why-this-university, campus,
academic identity, philosophy, international life, city, dormitory, official video, official links, CTA —
rendered as full-width media, two-column stories and hairlines rather than eleven cards (§13). The
directory gets the four-tier visual, a result card with real identity and the search/region/type controls
it has now.

**Honesty rules that do not bend:** no cross-university imagery; no invented prestige language; no
attribution-required asset on a customer surface; no internal provenance in the visible UI; a section with
no verified source does not render. The final coverage report distinguishes FULLY ENRICHED / TEXT COMPLETE
— MEDIA LIMITED / OFFICIAL DATA LIMITED / RIGHTS BLOCKED and does not round any of them up.

**What this pass will not do:** commission photography, write per-university prose for 425 institutions
from unsourced knowledge, add a map layer (§22 — the existing region map is kept and left alone), or ship
a second university content system anywhere.

# 217. V20 Implementation Log

## 217.1 Pricing — one option, four call sites, nothing else

`packages/utils/src/index.ts` — `formatMoney` gains `symbolOnly`, which asks Intl for
`currencyDisplay: 'narrowSymbol'` and then, **only if the currency part still contains letters**,
substitutes the canonical glyph taken from `en`. Built from `formatToParts`, so a locale that puts the
symbol after the number keeps its own order and spacing; the one residual case (Arabic, where CLDR has
no narrow symbol for USD at all) also gets the space the two-glyph `US$` used to occupy collapsed, so
the price is one typographic unit.

Four headline call sites take it: the marketing plan card, Student's service price, Student's current
plan, and the upgrade sheet. **Checkout, the payment-history row, the add-on approval amount and the
agency payments table do not** — a line that says what was charged needs the code, and the agency table
can hold KRW and USD in the same column.

Nothing in the money model moved. `currency: 'USD'` in `packages/types/src/plans.ts`, the order
currency, the payment validation and the Toss provider currency are byte-for-byte what V17 left, and
`qa:v20` asserts both halves: no `US$`/`USD` beside a headline price in any of the 55 locale bundles,
and `USD` still present in the plan type and absent from the symbol-only call sites' neighbours.

## 217.2 The primary-button contract — root cause, then contract, then proof

**The cascade fix.** `packages/eduan-ui/src/scss/eduan/abstracts/_common.scss` shipped three *global*
element rules from the licensed template, and the marketing app imports that stylesheet last:

```scss
a:focus, a:hover { color: inherit; }                      /* (0,1,1) — outranks a bare class */
a:focus, .button:focus { outline: none; }
button:focus, input:focus, textarea:focus { outline: 0; }
```

All three are now `:where(.ed) …`, which keeps their specificity exactly as upstream wrote it and
confines them to Eduan markup — the same wrapper `_hangyul-glue.scss` already used for `a` and the
heading scale. **Two defects fell out of that one change beyond the one we were looking for:** the
second and third rules were removing the focus ring from *every* anchor, button, input and textarea on
the marketing site, because `a:focus` (0,1,1) outranks the shared base's `:focus-visible` (0,1,0) and
nothing replaced it. The `outline: none` is deleted rather than scoped.

**The contract.** `.kn-btn--primary` and `.hg-btn--primary` now declare their foreground as one grouped
rule across rest, `:link`, `:visited`, `:hover`, `:focus`, `:focus-visible` and `:active`, at (0,2,0),
with the icon on `currentColor` so label and glyph cannot drift apart. This is belt *and* braces on
purpose: scoping the template fixes today's cascade, declaring every state fixes the next one. The
comment in both files says so and says not to collapse them back.

`.kn-btn` also gained a disabled state, which it had never had — the QA sheet is what showed it, because
the primary/disabled cell was indistinguishable from primary/rest. Same treatment the shared `.hg-btn`
took in V19: a neutral surface, not a faded brand one.

**Contrast.** Computed rather than asserted, in the gate: white on `#CC4E00` is **4.51:1**, on
`#B34400` 5.43:1, on `#9E3C00` 6.42:1. The button gains contrast as it is pressed, so §34's "darken the
surface instead" conditional never fires and no token changed.

**Native.** `packages/mobile-ui/src/components/Button.tsx` was already correct for every *enabled* state
and wrong for disabled — `opacity: 0.5` over tangerine, the ~1.9:1 wash V19 removed from the web and
never carried across. Disabled is now a neutral surface, border and tertiary text; `loading` deliberately
keeps the brand colour, because the action was accepted and is in flight.

## 217.3 The university content pipeline — `scripts/universities/`

Five commands, wired to npm, each doing one thing and writing one file:

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run uni:research` | reads each institution's **own** site, robots-aware, ≤4 pages, for the philosophy page, the international office, international admissions, the dormitory and any YouTube link in its own markup |
| `npm run uni:youtube` | resolves every candidate channel to its canonical id, keeps only the one whose title names the institution, and takes the channel's **own featured video** when its title says it is an introduction |
| `npm run uni:media` | wires the owner's 23 authorised crests, re-checks every Commons logo's licence against the API, downloads what survives, refuses what does not |
| `npm run uni:curate` | merges the hand-written, source-checked editorial layer and the institution↔photograph map |
| `npm run uni:audit` | the coverage table and `docs/qa/v20/UNIVERSITY_CONTENT_COVERAGE.csv` |

Output is one record per institution in `server/app/data/university_content.json`, merged onto
`Institution.enrichment` at seed time (JSONB — no migration). The seeder names the keys the content
record **owns outright** (`logo`, `hero`, `youtube`, `media`, `education_philosophy`) and refuses to let
the V17 cache fill one of them back in, because the absence of a key is how V20 expresses "this failed
the licence re-check".

Three decisions inside the pipeline are worth recording because the first attempt at each was wrong:

- **The philosophy *statement* is not auto-extracted any more.** The naive version returned navigation:
  Korean university menus list 건학이념 / 교육이념 / 교육목표 as siblings, so the text after the heading
  is four more menu items — which reads as a sentence to a regex and as nonsense to a person. The
  extractor now refuses a candidate that contains a second heading keyword, that carries chrome
  vocabulary, or that does not parse as prose, and it only ever reads the dedicated philosophy page with
  the nav/header/footer containers stripped first. What survives is stored as `SOURCE_CAPTURED` and
  **never rendered**. 11 strings survived; 4 of those are still wrong; none is on a page.
- **A footer link is not a channel.** The first run recorded "TU – The Head Office of International
  Affairs" as Tongmyong University's official channel, with a language-programme episode as its
  introduction video. A channel is now kept only when its own title names the institution.
- **A channel trailer is not automatically an introduction.** Three of the first eight were a cafeteria
  short with eight hashtags, a language-programme episode, and a promo for a different (affiliated)
  institution. The title must now match an introduction pattern *and* clear the avoid-list; 37 trailers
  were refused on that basis and those institutions link their channel and embed nothing.

## 217.4 Media and rights

- **23 owner-authorised crests wired.** `apps/marketing-web/public/media/universities` has held them
  since V13 — transparent, audited for bbox fill and stray geometry by `normalize_crests.py`, joined to
  registry slugs by `build_marquee_manifest.py` — and only the homepage marquee ever drew them. They are
  now the primary logo source and outrank anything from Commons.
- **Five attribution-required logos removed from a customer surface.** Global Cyber, Kumoh, Sungkyul,
  UNIST and Hansung were serving CC BY-SA images with no credit (§213.2). Every remaining logo is
  re-checked against the Commons API, classified, **downloaded to Hangyul's own origin** and capped at
  640 px; the hot-link to `upload.wikimedia.org` in the hero is gone. Hansung's `Authority.jpg` is also
  refused by the quality gate on its filename.
- **Seven CC0/PD city photographs added**, each chosen by eye against §49 before download: Busan ×2
  (Gwangan Bridge at night, Gamcheon Culture Village), Daejeon (Expo Bridge), Ulsan (Ulsan Bridge),
  Gangwon (Sokcho under Seoraksan), Jeonbuk (Jeonju hanok rooftops), Gyeongbuk (Bulguksa). Twelve further
  candidates were **rejected**: a bus, a city hall, a hospital, a car park, a coast guard cutter, three
  grey-sky landmarks. Region photography now covers 7 of 17 regions, up from 1.
- **`kyunghee-main-building` is finally wired.** CC0, downloaded and encoded in V14, attached to no
  institution for two versions.

## 217.5 The shared model — `@hangyul/types` + `@hangyul/utils` + `@hangyul/ui`

`UniversityContent` and `UniversityMedia` live in `packages/types`; the four-tier resolver, the region
media table, the monogram and the city-key map live in `packages/utils`; the rendering components live
in `packages/ui/src/university.tsx` with `styles/university.css`. Marketing and Student both import all
three, which is §54's "one canonical public university content model" made concrete rather than
promised.

**A client cannot choose a photograph.** `resolveUniversityVisual` reads `content.media.hero` from the
institution's own record and returns one of four tiers; there is no parameter that takes an image. That
is how §8 stops being a rule people remember and becomes a property of the system.

`monogramOf` takes the **Korean** name whatever script the page is in. Latin initials are not
distinctive at tile scale — ACTS, Ajou and Anyang are all "AU", and three identical tiles in one column
read as a rendering fault; 아신 / 아주 / 안양 are three different marks.

## 217.6 The detail page

Rebuilt as an editorial composition in the order a person decides in — hero → why here → campus →
philosophy → international → city → official film → the record → official links → one action. The
registry table is **ninth**, not first.

- **The hero is one composition, not a photograph with a header underneath.** Full-bleed image, a
  two-stop scrim plus a flat wash, the mark on a plate, the name, the place line, one identity sentence
  and one call to action. Where there is no licensed photograph it is the *same* composition on a
  region-tinted field with the institution's monogram bled off the right edge — same anatomy, same
  rhythm, same scale, so a university with no imagery reads as a different design decision rather than
  as a page with a hole in it. That case is 368 of 425.
- **The identity sentence is composed, not written.** Place, who runs it, what kind of institution, when
  it opened, how wide the course list is — all disclosed registry fields, so the sentence is specific
  for all 425 and asserts nothing the register does not. Four shapes rather than one with optional
  clauses, and the course-breadth clause is dropped below three majors rather than printing "teaching
  across 1 majors".
- **"Why here" is three points at most, from facts.** IEQAS status first because it is the one fact that
  changes whether an application is *possible*; then the language certification, state funding, a
  contactable international office, university housing, course breadth, multiple campuses, founding
  date. Fewer than two and the section does not render.
- **The city is written once per region**, factual and student-facing (what the rent is like, how far
  Seoul is, what the weather does), attached to the place and never to the institution.
- **No section renders without a source**, so two universities' pages are different lengths.

## 217.7 The directory

Every result now gets the same shape through the four tiers. What it is **not** is a wall of the same
photograph: the first build let tiers C and D fall through to the region's picture, and the Seoul page
drew the Han River eight times in one screen — the exact failure §19 names. On a card, §19's "logo +
editorial city composition" is now the **typographic** composition: the institution's Korean monogram,
its mark where one is licensed, and the region named underneath. Those differ for every row. City
photography stays on the detail page, where it appears once and is labelled as the city.

Also: a kind filter (university / junior college / graduate institution) beside the count, the map
behind a disclosure below 992 px so results are the first thing under the search field, and a 340 px
picker column at ≥1200 px so the results grid fits three tiles instead of two.

## 217.8 The thread back from the free quick check (§29)

`?from=recommendation` already existed and said one sentence. §29 asks for **one to three actual
reasons** and forbids a percentage, so the result row now also carries `fit` (the API's own
STRONG / POSSIBLE / NOT_YET verdict for that programme) and `degree` (what the reader typed), and the
detail page turns them into at most three lines:

> **This university matched your answers**
> · Programmes here fit the answers you gave.
> · It teaches at the level you chose — Bachelor's degree.
> · Its Korean-language course is on the certified list, so you can start with the language.

Every line is the reader's own input, the API's own verdict, or a certification on the public register.
There is no score, because a score would be a number Hangyul invented about a decision Hangyul does
not make.

## 217.9 Student

`apps/student-web/src/pages/University.tsx` renders `UniversityPhilosophy`, `UniversityVideo` and
`UniversityOfficialLinks` — the same components the public page uses, reading the same record from the
same public endpoint — in the Housing & campus tab for a catalogued institution and under the interest
card for one that is not. The student app keeps everything that is its own (saving, match explanation,
cost, deadlines, the next action) and no longer maintains a second, poorer description of the place.
`marketing` joins its i18n bundle, because one set of components has to have one set of strings.

## 217.10 Fixes found by looking at the rendered page, not the stylesheet

Recorded because each one was correct in source and wrong on screen:

- **The hero scrim was painting behind the photograph.** `.hg-uni-hero__media` is its own stacking
  context and the scrim had `z-index: -1` while the image was at `auto`. Both layers are numbered
  explicitly now.
- **Every `<p>` in the hero lockup was near-black on a dark photograph.** `:where(.ed) p { color: … }`
  *matches* the element, and a matching rule always beats a colour the element would otherwise inherit
  from `.hg-uni-hero__inner { color: #fff }`. Every text node in the component now declares its own
  colour. Same class of defect as the button cascade.
- **The card's mark lost its corner.** `.mk-unicard__visual img` (0,2,0) overrode
  `.mk-unicard__logo { position: absolute }` (0,1,0) — the logo is an `<img>` in the same box. The image
  rule is now `> img:not(.mk-unicard__logo)`.
- **The breadcrumb was pushing the hero lockup out of the readable half of the scrim.** With
  `align-items: end`, the ~160 px of header clearance the crumb needs moved the name to 45 % of the
  hero's height, where the ramp is ~0.3. The crumb is its own absolutely positioned block now and the
  lockup reserves nothing.
- **A two-photograph gallery drew an empty grey quarter**, because the 2 × 2 lead rule was written for
  three or more. One, two and three-or-more are three layouts.
- **A monogram's second syllable was clipped off the right edge** — 안양 at 360 px is 720 px wide in a
  460 px column. The column is 560 px and the glyph 260 px.

## 217.11 Dead code removed

`UniversityStory.tsx`, `UniversityVisual.tsx` and `media/university-media.ts` are **deleted**, along
with 73 CSS rules in `v12.css` and `v17.css` that could no longer match anything. Leaving them would
have left a second university content system in the tree — which is the thing §54 is about — and one
of them still contained the hot-linking logo component that caused §213.2. The Korean `keep-all`
treatment those rules carried moved into `packages/ui/src/styles/university.css`, so it travels with
the components into the student app instead of living in the marketing app's CSS.

## 217.12 Gates and instruments

- **New: `npm run qa:v20`** (`scripts/qa/v20-gate.mjs`) — 39 static checks plus a rendered pass over
  four products at two widths.
- **New: `npm run qa:v20-buttons`** (`scripts/qa/v20/button-matrix.mjs`) — the 5 × 5 × 2 QA sheet, and
  `matrix.json` recording every cell's computed background and foreground.
- **New: `npm run qa:v20-shots`** (`scripts/qa/v20/capture.mjs`) — discovery at four widths and the
  §46 representative set at two.
- **New: `npm run uni:*`** — the five pipeline commands above.
- **New evidence**: `docs/qa/v20/UNIVERSITY_CONTENT_COVERAGE.csv` (425 rows),
  `docs/qa/v20/buttons/` (8 sheets + matrix.json), `docs/qa/v20/screenshots/` (62 captures).
