# 218. V20 University Discovery Validation

## 218.1 Before and after, at the same four widths

| | before (V19) | after (V20) |
|---|---|---|
| visual per result | **none** — a text row | one of four tiers, resolved from this institution's own record |
| results per screen at 1440 | 2 columns of text rows | 3 tiles |
| results carrying their own media | 0 | **37** (2 photograph, 35 official-video poster) |
| results carrying their own mark | 0 | **29** |
| results carrying a place label | region word in the row | region word **and** a label in the composition |
| controls | search, map, region chips | search, map (behind a disclosure below 992 px), region chips, institution kind |
| vertical rhythm | ragged — rows differed in height by whether they carried IEQAS chips | uniform: every tile is 16:10 + three lines |

Captured at **390 / 768 / 1440 / 1728** in `docs/qa/v20/screenshots/discovery-*.png`.

## 218.2 The Seoul test

Seoul has 85 institutions and Hangyul holds three attribution-free photographs of Seoul. The first
build let tiers C and D fall through to the region's picture, and the result was the Han River eight
times in one screen — §19's named failure, reached by following §19's own tier list. The rule now is
that a **result tile never uses city photography**: the city photograph belongs on the detail page,
where it appears once and is labelled. One screen of Seoul results is now 총신 · 추계 · 중앙 · 사이 ·
디지 · 동국 · 이화 · 강서 · 한국 as nine different marks, with Cyber University of Korea, Dongduk and
Duksung carrying their own film posters.

## 218.3 Monogram distinctiveness

Cut from the **Korean** name, after dropping the institutional suffix. The Latin alternative was tested
and rejected: ACTS / Ajou / Anyang are three consecutive rows and three identical "AU" tiles.

**Then fixed again by the Busan page.** Three consecutive results — 부산교육대학교, 부산장신대학교,
부산외국어대학교 — all gave 부산, and the two Catholic universities both gave 가톨. A leading place
name or denominational prefix is now dropped before the cut **when at least two syllables remain**, so
those five give 교육 · 장신 · 외국 · 관동 · 꽃동. 부산대학교 keeps 부산, because removing the prefix
would leave nothing: there, the place name *is* the name.

**Residual:** 한국외국어대학교 and 부산외국어대학교 both give 외국. They are in different regions, the
region is printed inside the composition and the full name is directly under it, so this is a graphic
collision rather than an ambiguous one.

## 218.4 Honesty

- No institution shows another institution's campus: asserted statically by `qa:v20` over the content
  record, not by inspection.
- No city photograph is presented as a campus anywhere in discovery, because no city photograph appears
  in discovery.
- No fee, deadline, requirement, document count or match score is on a result tile.

## 219.2 Accuracy fixes the rendered page exposed

- **KAIST was described as "a private university".** The register's three-way `establishment` collapses
  특별법법인 to PRIVATE, which is right for 368 rows and wrong for the twelve institutions created by
  their own statute (KAIST, UNIST, KENTECH and four others; plus 특별법국립 and 국립대법인). The page
  now reads the finer `establishment_source` and names a fourth category, and the sentence drops the
  adjective entirely rather than printing "a statutory university in Daejeon".
- **"now teaching across 1 majors"** — the course-breadth clause is dropped below three majors, and
  pluralised properly where it survives.

## 219.3 Mobile — 390

The hero is immersive and the lockup sits in the readable half of the scrim; the logo plate keeps the
mark sharp; the headline clamps from 60 px to 32 px on one curve; the gallery becomes a scroll-snapped
swipe row at 88 % viewport width rather than three squeezed columns; the video facade keeps 16:9; the
CTA is full width; the two-column story sections become one column at 900 px. `qa:v20` asserts zero
horizontal overflow at 390 on the directory and on both a tier-A and a tier-D detail page.

## 219.4 What is still not good enough

- **One institution in 425 has more than one photograph.** The gallery section is correct and almost
  never renders. This is a licensing problem, not a design one, and commissioned photography remains
  the fix (`docs/MEDIA_LICENSE_AUDIT.md`).
- **"Academic identity" (§12 section 04) is not built.** The register carries a *count* of disclosed
  majors, not a list of colleges or named strengths, and nothing in this pass found an authoritative
  machine-readable source for them. Inventing "강점 분야" from a university's homepage navigation is
  exactly what §23 and §24 forbid, so the section does not exist rather than existing with made-up
  content.
- **History (§26) is a founding year, not a milestone.** Same reason.

# 220. V20 University Content Coverage Result

Measured by `npm run uni:audit`; the per-institution detail is
`docs/qa/v20/UNIVERSITY_CONTENT_COVERAGE.csv` (425 rows).

| field | V19 | V20 | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| TOTAL UNIVERSITIES | 425 | **425** | 대학알리미 2025 |
| LOGO (servable, locally hosted) | 14 *hot-linked, 5 of them a rights breach* | **29** (7 %) | 23 owner-authorised crests + 6 Commons PD |
| HERO IMAGE | 1 | **2** | CC0 Commons |
| GALLERY ≥2 | 1 | **1** | — |
| OFFICIAL WEBSITE | 298 | **298** (70 %) | registry + Wikidata |
| EDUCATION PHILOSOPHY, Hangyul-reviewed | 0 | **13** (3 %) | each institution's own page, read |
| MOTTO, registry-asserted | 5 | **4** (1 %) | Wikidata P1451 |
| philosophy page located (link only) | 0 | **82** (19 %) | own site |
| INTERNATIONAL OFFICE | 0 | **60** (14 %) | own site |
| INTERNATIONAL ADMISSIONS | 0 | **96** (23 %) | own site |
| DORMITORY | 0 | **64** (15 %) | own site |
| OFFICIAL YOUTUBE CHANNEL | 10 | **84** (20 %) | 77 own-site, 7 Wikidata P2397 |
| OFFICIAL INTRODUCTION VIDEO | **0** | **35** (8 %) | channel's own featured film |
| CAMPUS / CITY | 425 (region word) | **425**, 7 regions with photography (was 1) | — |

**Discovery visual tier**: A 2 · B 35 · C 20 · D 368.

**Honest status (§45)**, and it does not round up:

| status | n | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| FULLY ENRICHED | **4** | reviewed philosophy *and* a contactable international office *and* (a photograph or a verified film) |
| TEXT COMPLETE — MEDIA LIMITED | **92** | the page has real sourced content and no photograph of its own |
| OFFICIAL DATA LIMITED | **326** | the institution's own site could not be read, or carries none of the four things we look for |
| RIGHTS BLOCKED | **3** | media exists and may not be served |

**Why 326 is the largest number, measured rather than guessed.** 127 of 425 institutions have no website
in either source. Of the 298 that do: 203 answered, **37 forbid robots outright** (`Disallow: /` under
`User-agent: *` — honoured, not worked around), and 58 were unreachable even after retrying `https://`
and the bare origin. That is the ceiling of what can be collected without a commercial data supplier or
writing to 425 international offices, and both of those are outside a software pass.

**Not claimed:** that every university is complete, that the philosophy coverage is adequate (13 of 425
is not), or that 8 % video coverage makes the video section a feature rather than a bonus.

cafeteria short with eight hashtags, and a promotional film for a *different* institution on an

this channel from its own pages" and "the institution's own Wikidata item carries the channel id".

# 222. V20 Global Button Validation

## 222.1 Root cause, restated in one line

An element-plus-pseudo-class selector from a licensed template — `a:focus, a:hover { color: inherit }`,
specificity (0,1,1) — outranked the single-class rule that carried the primary button's foreground, in
the two states nobody had written a rule for.

## 222.2 Before and after, by product

Measured by `scripts/qa/v20/_orange-probe.mjs`, which forces rest, hover, focus and active on **every**
`a` / `button` / `[role=button]` and reports any solid-tangerine surface whose computed label or icon
is not light.

| product | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Marketing | **8** — `.kn-btn--primary` "Get started", label **and** icon, on 4 routes, in `:focus` and `:active` | **0** |
| Student | 0 | 0 |
| Agency | 0 | 0 |
| University | 0 | 0 |

The failing computed value was `rgb(24, 26, 31)` on `rgb(204, 78, 0)` — **2.41:1**. The probe caught it
mid-transition at `rgb(69, 71, 75)` because `.kn-btn` animates `color` over 150 ms, which is also why
it reads to the eye as the label *going dark* rather than as a different button.

Student, Agency and University were clean before this pass and are clean after. They were clean by
luck: none of them imports the Eduan template, and `.hg-btn` carries its foreground on the same
single-class selector that failed on the marketing site. That is now fixed in all four.

## 222.3 The design-system rule, as enforced

`npm run qa:v20` asserts, statically:

- the Eduan anchor reset is scoped to `:where(.ed)` and an unscoped `a:hover`/`a:focus` has not returned;
- `.kn-btn--primary` and `.hg-btn--primary` each declare their foreground on `:link`, `:visited`,
  `:hover`, `:focus`, `:focus-visible` and `:active` — twelve separate checks;
- the primary icon is `currentColor` in both;
- **no non-solid variant takes a light foreground** — `--outline`, `--ghost`, `--soft`, `--onphoto`
  and `--link` are checked for the opposite, because "white text on buttons" applied blanket would
  destroy four of them;
- white on `--hg-primary` / `--hg-primary-hover` / `--hg-primary-pressed` clears 4.5:1, computed from
  the tokens rather than asserted: **4.51 / 5.43 / 6.42**;
- native primary uses `theme.color.textOnPrimary`, passes it to both icon slots, and disabled is the
  neutral surface rather than a faded brand one.

…and, rendered: every control in four products at 390 and 1440, in four states.

## 222.4 The visual matrix (§40)

`npm run qa:v20-buttons` → `docs/qa/v20/buttons/<app>-<width>.png`, eight sheets, five variants × five
states each, plus `matrix.json` recording every cell's computed background, foreground, border and icon
colour. **A picture proves it looked right; the JSON proves it was.**

The sheet is rendered **inside each running app**, with the body's own classes kept, so the real
cascade applies — including Eduan and Koreanasha on the marketing site, which is where the defect
lived. A sheet built from a standalone HTML file with the tokens imported would have been green
throughout. The first run of the sheet proved the point by printing three blank cells, because
`--kn-accent` is declared on `.kn` and the matrix had been injected outside that scope.

Two things the sheet found that no screenshot of a real page would have:

- **`.kn-btn` had no disabled state at all** — primary/disabled was pixel-identical to primary/rest, so
  a disabled marketing CTA looked enabled. Now a neutral surface.
- **Two marketing variants are white pills for use on photographs** and were invisible on a white QA
  sheet, which is why the sheet's ground is grey.

# 223. V20 Performance & Accessibility Validation

## 223.1 Loading

| rule | state |
|---|---|
| §48 only the above-the-fold hero loads eagerly | enforced — `qa:v20` fails on any image with `loading != "lazy"` below the fold, on three detail pages |
| gallery images lazy | ✓ |
| YouTube iframe created only on click | ✓ — `qa:v20` asserts **0 iframes** before the click on all three pages |
| video poster lazy, with a `maxresdefault` → `hqdefault` fallback | ✓ |
| explicit `width`/`height` on every photograph | ✓ — reserved from the asset's own recorded dimensions |
| responsive `srcset` at 640 / 1200 / 2400 with per-surface `sizes` | ✓ |
| logo hot-link to a third-party origin | **removed** — 14 → 0 |

**One §48 defect found and fixed outside the university pages**: the footer Hangyul lockup
(`logo-combined.png`, 456 × 96) was loading eagerly ~3,600 px down **every page in the product**. The
`Logo` component takes a `below` prop now; the marketing footer passes it. The header's lockup keeps
the default, because it is the LCP candidate on several routes.

## 223.2 Accessibility

| check | state |
|---|---|
| exactly one `h1` per detail page | ✓ asserted at three tiers |
| every section has an accessible name (`aria-labelledby`) | ✓ asserted, ≥3 named sections per page |
| the mark's `alt` | **empty + `aria-hidden`** — the logo *is* the name as a mark, and the visible `h1` carries it; an alt would make a screen reader say the name twice |
| a campus photograph's `alt` | names the institution |
| a city photograph's `alt` | names the **city**, never the institution — and the visible caption says so too |
| the horizontal gallery is reachable from the keyboard | ✓ `tabIndex={0}` + `aria-label`, no `role="group"` (which would orphan the `<li>`s) |
| focus ring on the video facade | ✓ 3 px tangerine, offset 3 |
| `prefers-reduced-motion` | every transform and transition in `university.css` is disabled |
| horizontal overflow at 390 and 1440 | **0 px**, asserted on the directory and two detail pages |
| RTL (`?lang=ar`) | `dir="rtl"` and **0 px** overflow on the directory and the detail page, at 390 and 1440 — every rule in `university.css` and `v20.css` is written in logical properties |
| raw i18n keys on screen | **0** across five university routes × ko / en / vi |
| console errors on the university surfaces | **0**, asserted |

**One accessibility defect found and fixed outside this pass's scope**: the Eduan template's
`a:focus { outline: none }` and `button:focus, input:focus, textarea:focus { outline: 0 }` were
*global*, and `a:focus` (0,1,1) outranks the shared base's `:focus-visible` (0,1,0). Every anchor,
button, input and textarea on the marketing site had no focus ring, and nothing replaced it. Scoping
the reset to `:where(.ed)` and deleting the `outline: none` restores it product-wide.

## 224.2 Two gates were edited, and here is exactly why

All of them are **renames, not relaxations.** The V20 detail page moved to the shared university
presentation, so its elements changed class and four gates were still looking for the old ones:

| gate | selector before | after | what the assertion tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| `e2e/v12-directory-legal.spec.ts` | `.mk-uni__checked` | `.hg-uni-checked` | the date the official information was checked is on the page — unchanged |
| `scripts/qa/v17-gate.mjs` | `.mk-uni__from` | `.hg-uni-hero__from` | `?from=recommendation` is carried onto the page — unchanged |
| `scripts/qa/v17-gate.mjs` | `.mk-uni__head` | `.hg-uni-hero` | the first viewport does not lead with a deadline — unchanged |
| `scripts/qa/v14-marquee-details.mjs` | `.mk-uni__title, .mk-uni__alt` | `.hg-uni-hero__name, .hg-uni-hero__alt` | every crest in the homepage band opens a page that **names that university** — unchanged |
| `scripts/qa/v14-marquee-details.mjs` | `.mk-uni__where` | `.hg-uni-hero__where` | …and gives its location — unchanged |
| `scripts/qa/v19/_unidetail.mjs` | `.mk-uni__head(--visual)` | `.hg-uni-hero(--photo)` | header clearance probe — unchanged |

One further change to `v14-marquee-details.mjs` is **not** a rename: the placeholder list contained a
bare `'['`, standing in for an unfilled template slot. V20 attached verified official introduction
films to 35 institutions and a Korean university's brand film is very often titled
`[Brand Film] 단국에서 단국으로…`, so Dankook's page failed the check on real, sourced content. The
bracket is replaced by a regex for an actual unsubstituted slot — `[TODO]`, `[placeholder]`, `[이름]`,
`{{…}}`, `${…}`, `[[…]]`. That narrows a heuristic that was firing on correct content; an actual
unfilled template on a customer page still fails.

**The V14 story is worth dwelling on, because the first draft of this report called `qa:v14` green and
it was not.** The run printed `Marquee → detail integrity: 47 problem(s)` and exited 1; the summary line
was grepped for `OK —`, which four of the eleven sub-gates printed, and the chain's non-zero exit was
read off a wrapper that always exits 0. The gate was doing exactly its job — catching a silent rename
on the path from the homepage crest band to 23 university pages — and the reporting missed it. The
number in §224.1 is from a clean re-run, and the rule from §199.8 stands: **check the exit code, not
the prose.**

V17 also failed its *server-free review bundle* section on the first run, because `dist-review/` had
been built before this pass. Rebuilt with `npm run review:fixtures && npm run review:build` and re-run;
that is a stale artifact, not a weakened check.

## 224.3 The one failure that is not fixed, and why

`qa:v19` F — *"the Android artifacts predate their source by 11.8 h"*. This is §194.3's outstanding
blocker: the signed native artifacts cannot be rebuilt without the keystore properties, which the owner
has not supplied, so any source change in the repository re-opens this check. It was red before this
pass for the same reason and this pass did not make it worse or better. It is **not** claimed green.

# 225. V20 Final Hostile Audit

## 225.1 The brief's own questions, answered against the screenshots

**"If I removed the Hangyul logo, would this page still obviously belong to THIS university?"**

For the 57 institutions at tier A, B or C: yes — the page carries their photograph or their own film,
their mark, their city and, for thirteen, their own statement of what they are for. For the other 368:
**partly.** The monogram, the name, the place, the founding year, the course breadth, the certification
status and the city writing are all specific; the *imagery* is not, because there is none. A reader
would know they were looking at Anyang University and not Ajou. They would not know what Anyang
University looks like.

**"Would a 19-year-old want to click another photo?"** On 2 pages there is a second photo. On 35 there
is a film they can play. On 388 there is not. This is the honest headline of the pass.

**"Would they want to watch the official video?"** For the 35 where one is verified: it is the
university's own featured film, with its real title and channel named under it, behind a facade that
costs nothing until they press play. Yes.

**"Can they imagine studying there?"** More than before, and not yet enough. The city sections do real
work — a reader now learns that Daejeon is where the laboratories are, that Jeonju is cheap and that
Gangwon has real winters — but that is the *place*, not the campus.

**"Can they understand its academic character?"** For thirteen institutions, yes, from their own
educational philosophy. For the rest, no: the register carries a count of disclosed majors and nothing
about fields, and §12's "academic identity" section is **not built** rather than built from invention.

**"Does this page look more appealing than the university's own old admissions site?"** For a
photographed or filmed institution, yes. For an unphotographed one it is cleaner, faster and better
written, and it has fewer pictures. That is a fair draw and not a win.

**"Does anything look generated or fabricated?"** Three things were, and were removed:

- the auto-extracted "교육이념" that was actually a navigation menu — *no* captured statement renders;
- "TU – The Head Office of International Affairs" recorded as Tongmyong University's official channel;
- a promotional film for a different institution offered as a university's own introduction.

What remains is composed rather than written — the identity sentence is five registry fields in a
sentence shape. It reads as specific because the fields are specific, and it will read as a template to
anyone who opens twenty pages in a row. That is a real limitation and it is the price of refusing to
write 425 paragraphs from unsourced knowledge.

## 225.2 Button hostile audit (§57)

| search | expected | found |
|---|---|---|
| solid orange + dark text, any of 4 products, any of 4 states | 0 | **0** |
| solid orange + dark icon | 0 | **0** |
| the same, before this pass | — | 8 (marketing header, label and icon, `:focus` and `:active`) |

## 225.3 Currency hostile audit (§58)

| searched for, beside a headline price | found |
|---|---|
| `US $179` / `US$179` / `USD 179` / `179 USD` / `$179 USD`, and the same for 349 and 599 | **0**, across every locale bundle |
| before: `ko` `US$179` · `zh-Hans` `US$179` · `th` `US$179` · `id` `US$179` · `vi` `179 US$` · `ms` `USD 179` | — |

Legitimate currency metadata is untouched and was checked for: `currency: 'USD'` in the plan model, the
order payload, the payment contract and the provider call; `USD` still printed in the checkout order
block, the payment-history row and the agency payments table.

## 225.4 What this pass did **not** achieve

Stated plainly, because §62 asks for it:

1. **Photography.** 2 of 425 institutions have a licensed photograph of their own campus. Every tier
   below A exists because of that number. Commissioned photography is the fix and it is not a software
   task.
2. **Education philosophy at 3 %.** Thirteen institutions have a Hangyul reading of their own stated
   philosophy, because thirteen are what a person actually read in this pass. Eighty-two more have a
   located philosophy page waiting to be read; the pipeline makes each one a ten-minute job rather than
   a research project, but somebody has to do them.
3. **95 institutions could not be read at all** — 37 forbid robots, 58 are unreachable. Those pages
   carry registry facts and city writing and nothing from the institution itself.
4. **Academic identity and history are absent**, not thin. No authoritative machine-readable source for
   either was found and neither was invented.
5. **The monogram collides** for institutions sharing a Korean name prefix (three 부산, two 가톨).
6. **`qa:v20` takes about half an hour** because the rendered button sweep is a real pointer move per
   control per state. It is correct and it is slow.
7. **The native artifacts are still unbuilt** (§194.3), so `qa:v19` is still red on one check.
8. **Two runs did not finish inside the pass** — a confirming full-chain `qa:v14` and the
   `test:release` wrapper. Every gate inside both was run standalone and is reported in §224.1; what
   is missing is the single serial sweep that proves they are green *together*, and it is not claimed.

**Not claimed:** that the university experience is finished, that coverage is adequate, that any
translation outside en/ko has been reviewed by a native speaker, or that the 368 typographic pages are
as persuasive as a photographed one. What is claimed is that the architecture now makes every one of
those a data problem with a named pipeline, rather than a design problem with no answer.

§226 lists what the owner has to do for those numbers to move.

# 226. V21 University Discovery Hostile Audit

The owner's screenshots are the finding. V20's gates were green and the page is not good, which means the
gates measured the wrong thing: they asserted that **a** visual resolved for every institution, never that
the visual was worth looking at.

## 226.1 What the first screen of `/universities` actually shows

Nine tiles above the fold at 1440. **Eight of them are a two-syllable fragment of the university's own
name set at 90 px in 20 %-opacity tangerine**: 아신 · 아주 · 안양 · 백석 · 교육 · 장신 · 외국 · 칼빈. The
ninth is a real video poster.

That is not a design, it is wallpaper generated from a string. Three specific failures:

- **It reads as machine output**, because it is. A human designer does not crop "교육" out of
  부산교육대학교 and set it as the identity of a 78-year-old teachers' college.
- **Several fragments are meaningless or wrong as identity.** 교육 means "education". 외국 means
  "foreign". 장신 is a syllable pair with no referent. They are not abbreviations the institutions use.
- **It defeats its own purpose.** V20 introduced the monogram to make tiles *distinct*; at a glance a
  grid of identical peach rectangles with two faint glyphs is less distinguishable than the V12 text
  list it replaced, because the text list at least put the full name at full contrast.

I fixed a monogram collision in V20 (부산 ×3 → 교육/장신/외국) and recorded it as a win. Looking at the
rendered page, the collision was never the problem. **The concept was the problem**, and improving the
algorithm made the page worse by making the fragments more arbitrary.

## 226.2 The rest of the first screen

- **The map takes the entire left column** — 360 px wide, ~560 px tall, the full height of the first
  three result rows. It is a selector for one attribute, given a third of the opening viewport, on a page
  whose job is to make someone want to study somewhere. It makes the product read as a data explorer.
- **The headline is weak.** "Where in Korea do you want to study?" / "한국에서 어디에서 공부하고 싶나요?"
  presumes the reader has already decided on Korea *and* only needs to pick a province, which is the map's
  question again in words.
- **The first results are arbitrary.** ACTS · Ajou · Anyang · Baekseok — alphabetical by English name, so
  the opening impression of Korean higher education is four institutions almost no applicant is looking
  for. Not wrong, just useless as a first screen.
- **The kind filter is a bare `<select>`** sitting between the heading and the count, styled as a form
  control rather than as part of the composition.

## 226.3 Verdict

Delete the monogram. Not tune it — delete the concept, including the resolver tier that produces it, the
CSS, and the gate check that currently *certifies* it as an intentional visual tier.

---

# 227. V21 University Detail Hostile Audit

Measured on `catholic-kkottongnae-university`, a fair example of the 368 institutions with no photograph.

## 227.1 The hero

A **230 px-tall "꽃동"** occupies the right half of the first viewport. It is the first graphic element a
prospective student sees on this university's page and it is two syllables chopped out of
가톨릭꽃동네대학교. The owner named this exact case. It is indefensible and there is no version of it
worth keeping.

## 227.2 The prose

> "A private university in Cheongju, opened in 1998 and now teaching across 3 majors."
> "청주에 있는 사립 대학교. 1998년에 문을 열었고 지금은 3개 학과를 두고 있습니다."

V20 defended this as "composed from registry facts, not invented". That defence is true and beside the
point. It reads as a database row read aloud, the clause order is identical on all 425 pages, and
"3개 학과를 두고 있습니다" is not a reason to study anywhere. §11 of this brief is right: a shorter honest
page beats generated filler.

The city section has the same problem at paragraph scale. "Living in Cheongju" is a heading over text
about **North Chungcheong province**, written once and shown on every institution in the province. It is
accurate, it is not about this university, and the heading implies it is.

## 227.3 What is actually good and must survive

Said plainly so this pass does not throw it away:

- the section-renders-only-when-sourced rule;
- the official-destinations block (international office / admissions / dormitory), from the institution's
  own site;
- the education-philosophy block for the 13 institutions that have a reviewed one — this is the only
  content on the whole surface that sounds like a person wrote it about that specific university;
- the video facade, and the refusal to embed an unverified film;
- the per-asset focal points and the lazy-loading discipline.

## 227.4 Verdict

The hero, the identity sentence and the city heading all go. The information architecture stays.

# 228. V21 University Visual-Identity Audit

| tier | institutions | what the tile/hero actually is | verdict |
|---|--:|---|---|
| A — own photograph | **2** | Seoul National, Kyung Hee | keep |
| B — official film poster | **35** | the channel's own featured film | keep |
| C — logo + region tint | 20 | mark over a tinted field | keep, improve |
| D — **monogram** | **368** | two chopped syllables | **delete** |

**86 % of the register renders a fragment of its own name as its identity.** Any honest reading of this
table says the visual system was built around a fallback and the fallback is not acceptable.

## 228.1 Why media coverage is 2 and what was never tried

V20 asked Wikidata for exactly two properties per institution — `P154` (logo) and `P18` (image) — and
treated the answer as the ceiling. It is not the ceiling. A Korean university's media on Commons lives in
its **category** (`P373`), which routinely holds ten to eighty files. A twelve-institution probe of the
category route found **servable photographs for 3 of 12** against V20's 2 of 425 overall.

The same under-search applies to video: V20 accepted only the channel's **featured** film, so 84 verified
channels yielded 35 films and 37 refusals. The channels' uploads were never listed.

## 228.2 Logos

29 of 425, of which 23 are the owner's own crest drop and 6 are Commons public domain. The Commons
category route was not tried for logos either, and Korean institutional wordmarks are frequently
`PD-textlogo`.

# 229. V21 Foreign-Card Billing Architecture Audit

Everything below is a **measured response from Toss's sandbox**, obtained with the owner's own
`bill_talkoab1` TEST credentials by `server/scripts/v21_toss_billing_probe.py` and
`scripts/qa/v21/_billingauth-probe.mjs`. No secret, no card number and no billing key appears in any
output, here or in the scripts.

## 229.1 Do the four TEST secret keys authenticate at all?

`GET /v1/payments/orders/<nonexistent>` → **HTTP 404 `NOT_FOUND_PAYMENT`** on all four (a bad key gives
401). So every configuration is live and reachable; nothing below is an authentication problem.

## 229.2 `POST /v1/billing/authorizations/card` — the card-direct billing-key route the brief specifies

| MID | result |
|---|---|
| `bill_talkoab1` (foreign) | **400 `INVALID_BILL_KEY_REQUEST`** — for *every* card tried |
| `bill_talko18s0` (domestic) | 400 `NOT_SUPPORTED_CARD_TYPE` / `INVALID_CARD_NUMBER` |
| `bill_talkspm0` (easy pay) | 400 `NOT_SUPPORTED_CARD_TYPE` |
| `HANGYUL` (one-time) | 400 `INVALID_BILL_KEY_REQUEST` |

Eleven card numbers were tried on the foreign MID — Luhn-valid and invalid, Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Amex,
Korean and foreign BINs. **Every one returned the same error, before any card validation.** The same key
on the same endpoint returns `INVALID_REQUEST — 필수 파라미터가 누락되었거나 null입니다: cardNumber`
when the field is omitted, so the endpoint is reachable and schema-validated for us.

The asymmetry is the diagnosis: the *domestic* MID reaches card-level validation (it tells us the card
type is unsupported, which for a foreign BIN on a domestic MID is correct), while the *foreign* MID is
rejected **before** the card is looked at. **키인 billing-key issuance is not enabled on
`bill_talkoab1`.** This is the §45 "contract/method error", diagnosed rather than converted into a false
boolean.

## 229.3 `POST /v1/payments/key-in` — card-direct **one-time** payment

| MID | result |
|---|---|
| `bill_talkoab1` (foreign) | **HTTP 200 · `status: DONE` · `currency: "USD"`** |
| `HANGYUL` (one-time) | 400 `NOT_SUPPORTED_CARD_TYPE` |
| `bill_talko18s0` / `bill_talkspm0` | 400 `NOT_SUPPORTED_CARD_TYPE` |

This is the finding that re-shapes the pass. `bill_talkoab1` accepts a **plain foreign Visa, with no
`cardPassword` and no `customerIdentityNumber`, and settles in USD.** A request sent with
`amount: 179, currency: "USD"` came back `totalAmount: 179.0, currency: "USD", status: "DONE"`; a
request sent with no `currency` at all *also* came back `currency: "USD"`. The configuration is a
**foreign-card 키인 결제 (key-in) MID contracted in USD** — which is exactly Hangyul's product: a
one-time $179 / $349 / $599 purchase by someone who is not in Korea.

The returned `card.number` is **masked by Toss** (`########****###*`), `cardType`/`ownerType` are
`미확인` for a foreign card, and `issuerCode`/`acquirerCode` are returned. Cancellation works
(`POST /v1/payments/{paymentKey}/cancel` → `CANCELED`), so the probe charges were reversed.

## 229.4 The SDK billing-key window

`payment().requestBillingAuth({ method: 'CARD' })` with the foreign client key first returned
**400 `INCORRECT_SUCCESS_URL_FORMAT`** — because the probe used a made-up origin, not because of the
contract. With a real `successUrl` the route returns **200** and the window opens. So a billing key
*is* obtainable on this MID, by the hosted-window route.

## 229.5 What the evidence means for the brief

| brief | evidence | what V21 ships |
|---|---|---|
| §26 Hangyul card form, **not** a Toss popup | key-in accepts raw card data server-side | **shipped as specified** |
| §27 `POST /v1/billing/authorizations/card` → billingKey | **refused on this MID** | replaced by `POST /v1/payments/key-in`, with the evidence above |
| §28 secret key server-side only | — | shipped |
| §29 raw card never persisted or logged | — | shipped |
| §32/§33 encrypted credential store | key-in returns **no** reusable credential | the store, the AES-256-GCM envelope, the `customerKey` and the lifecycle are **built**; what they hold for this MID is the safe card metadata, and the billing-key column stays empty until a route that issues one is contracted |
| §37 upgrade reuse / §41 "pay with this card" / §42 delete at Toss | needs a billing key | **not deliverable on this MID today** — the card is re-entered for a second purchase, and this is stated in the UI rather than faked |
| §46 USD | provider returns `currency: "USD"` | USD, unconverted |

The honest summary: **the owner's described experience is fully deliverable and the owner's described
mechanism is not.** Hangyul renders the card form, the student never leaves Hangyul, the backend holds
the secret, the charge is USD and immediate. The one thing that cannot be done on `bill_talkoab1` today
is storing a credential that can be charged again without the card.

# 230. V21 Existing Payment-Gate Root Cause

Why the student could not pay, in one sentence: **the gate is keyed to `live`, and the plans are priced
in USD, so no test transaction of any kind could ever run.**

`server/app/core/config.py`:

```python
@property
def live_usd_checkout_enabled(self) -> bool:
    return self.toss_env == "live" and all(self.usd_readiness.values())
```

`server/app/api/v1/student.py:713`, before an Order even exists:

```python
if settings.payment_provider == "toss" and price.currency != "KRW" and not settings.live_usd_checkout_enabled:
    raise HTTPException(503, detail={"code": "CURRENCY_NOT_CONTRACTED", ...})
```

Three compounding causes:

1. **`toss_env` is `test`, so the first conjunct is false by construction.** Not "the flags are off" —
   even with all four readiness flags true, a test environment refuses. There was no test path at all.
2. **Every plan price is USD** (V17 owner decision), so `price.currency != "KRW"` is always true. The
   refusal therefore fires on 100 % of plan purchases.
3. **The four readiness flags describe the wrong merchant configuration.** They were written for the
   `HANGYUL` one-time MID, whose 결제창 is KRW. `bill_talkoab1` is a *different* configuration that
   §229.3 shows already settles USD. The flags gate a contract Hangyul does not need for this route.

The V19/V20 statement **"the three `bill_*` configs … must never be wired to a plan"** rested on one
premise — that a `bill_*` MID can only register billing keys for recurring charges. §229.3 disproves it
for `bill_talkoab1`, which performs a one-time USD card payment. **The premise was wrong, so the
conclusion is void.** The historical analysis stays in §135 and §152; this section is the correction.

What does *not* change: the secret key never reaches the browser; the server prices the order; the
amount sent to Toss is the server's number; `qa:v16`'s fingerprint scan stays.

1. **Media, properly searched.** Commons `P373` category per institution, one level of subcategory,
   every file's licence read from the API. Measured on all 325 matched institutions: **19 with a
   servable photograph** under the attribution-free rule, **66** if attribution-bearing licences are
   supported — which §15 of this brief permits "if its attribution terms are intentionally supported".
   So V21 builds real attribution into the design and takes the 66.
2. **Video, properly searched.** List each verified channel's uploads rather than only its featured
   film, and match the same introduction vocabulary.
3. **Four tiers, none of them invented**: own photograph → official film poster → logo on a neutral

## 231.3 Payment

1. `HG_TOSS_FOREIGN_BILLING_*` already exists in `server/.env` and already holds `bill_talkoab1`'s TEST
   triple. No new secret, no rename — the brief's requested names are these names minus the project's
   `HG_` settings prefix.
2. New `foreign_billing_test_ready` / `foreign_billing_live_ready`, independent of the four live flags.
3. `StudentPaymentMethod` with an AES-256-GCM envelope, a random server-side `customerKey`, and safe
   card metadata only.
4. `POST /me/payment-methods/toss/card` → Toss `/v1/payments/key-in` → Order PAID → plan active, in one
   authenticated, rate-limited, idempotent call that never persists or logs a PAN.
5. A Hangyul-rendered card form. No Toss window, no domestic or easy-pay methods.
6. Prove it end to end against the sandbox, through the product, and record the real result.

## 231.4 What this pass will not do

Fabricate a reusable card credential that the merchant configuration does not issue; convert USD to KRW;
ship live payment on test credentials; or keep any visual that is generated from a string.

# 234. V21 Media Acquisition

## 234.1 What V14's rule was costing

V14 required **no attribution** for any served image. Running the Commons sweep over 325 institutions
with reasons recorded:

```
files found and refused on rights/quality   718
  of which refused on licence alone         676
```

676 of 718. The rule, not the supply, was the reason hero coverage was 2 of 425. V21 §15 permits a
credited photograph where the credit is rendered, so `ATTRIBUTION_SUPPORTED` was added as a servable
rights class with `PhotoCredit` as its condition, and the sweep was re-run.

## 234.2 What was taken, and what was refused

| | |
|---|---:|
| institutions with a campus photograph | 2 → **44** |
| institutions with an official intro film | 35 → **81** |
| university assets under a credit-bearing licence | 33 |
| university assets under CC0 / public domain | 9 |

Licences in play: CC BY-SA 4.0 ×14, CC BY-SA 3.0 ×13, CC0 ×6, public domain ×3, CC BY 4.0 ×2,
CC BY 3.0, CC BY 2.5, CC BY 2.0 kr, Attribution ×1 each.

Every file is **resized, never cropped**, and `credits.json` carries author, licence, licence URL and
source URL per asset. Nothing was taken from a university's own website: being published there is not
a licence to redistribute, and 37 institutions additionally return `Disallow: /`.

The widest free file is not the right file. Reviewing a contact sheet of the automatic choices
rejected a stage performance (Pusan National), a 1900s map (Dong-A), several wordmarks, portraits of

the pipeline rather than a note about it.

One institution, `dong-eui-university`, failed to download and has no photograph.

Channel ownership is established from the institution's own site or Wikidata P2397 and recorded as
`verified_via`; a channel that cannot be tied to the institution is not stored, and no video is
stored without its channel. In-channel search (`/channel/<id>/search?query=…` with an oEmbed
`author_name` check) raised intro-film coverage from 35 to 81.

# 236. V21 Foreign-Card Billing Implementation

## 236.1 What the owner described, and what the merchant account can do

The brief specifies:

> FOREIGN CARD → HANGYUL CARD REGISTRATION UI → TOSS FOREIGN-CARD BILLING API → BILLING KEY →
> STORED SECURELY → CHARGE PLAN

Measured against the real sandbox on `bill_talkoab1` (§229):

| endpoint | result |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/billing/authorizations/card` (issue a billing key from a card) | refused for this MID |
| `POST /v1/payments/key-in` (charge a card directly) | **approves, settles in USD** |

`bill_talkoab1` is a **foreign-card key-in MID**, not a billing-key MID. The diagnosis is not an
inference from an error string: the same endpoint returns `INVALID_REQUEST: cardNumber` for a missing
field, and the *domestic* MID reaches card-level validation on it, so the refusal is merchant
configuration rather than a malformed request.

So the owner's described **experience** is delivered in full and the described **mechanism** is not
available on this account:

* Hangyul's own card form, no Toss popup, immediate charge, plan active — all shipped.
* A stored, reusable billing key — the infrastructure is built and unused, because this MID issues
  no credential to store.

The encrypted credential column, the envelope, the revoke-at-provider path and the saved-card
endpoint are all built and tested anyway, so that enabling a billing-key contract later is a
configuration change rather than a rebuild. `reusable` is `false` on every stored card today, and
`/me/orders/{id}/pay-with-saved-card` answers `CARD_NOT_REUSABLE` — the honest answer. Re-prompting
for the card from an endpoint whose name promises otherwise would be the dishonest one.

## 236.2 The blocker that made testing impossible

`live_usd_checkout_enabled` is `toss_env == "live" and all four contract flags`. Every plan is priced
in USD, so that refused 100 % of purchases — and because its first conjunct is `live`, it refused
them **in test too**. There was no path on which a USD order could be created at all (§230).

V21 gives foreign billing its own two states, independent of the four 결제창 contract flags:

```python
foreign_billing_test_ready  = toss_env == "test" and credentials paired and crypto.configured()
foreign_billing_live_ready  = toss_env == "live" and credentials paired and keys are not test_ and crypto.configured()
```

A USD order is allowed when **either** route can take it. `test_v17_usd_refunds.py` asserts both
directions: refused when neither route exists, accepted when the foreign-card route does.

## 236.3 The obsolete assumption is deleted

V16 asserted that a `bill_*` MID must never be wired to a plan purchase. That was right when the only
`bill_*` MIDs on the account were Korean 자동결제 products. `bill_talkoab1` is not one of those, and
the assertion had become a statement that the product must not work. The test is **rewritten, not
deleted** — it now asserts that exactly one configuration is wired to plan purchase, that the listing
agrees with itself about which, that each MID is still labelled with the product it really is, and
that no key of any kind is served to a browser.

## 236.4 The form

`apps/student-web/src/components/CardForm.tsx` — three fields (number, expiry, name), Hangyul's own
markup, `autocomplete="cc-number|cc-exp|cc-name"`, `data-hg-no-capture` on every field, state cleared
on unmount, Luhn checked client-side so an obvious typo costs no round trip, and one button that says
what it will do: **Pay with this card · $599**.

No domestic card option, no 토스페이 / 네이버페이 / 카카오페이, no 계좌이체, no easy-pay. `qa:v21`
fails if any of those strings appears in the purchase UI. The
"해외카드 USD 결제가 아직 활성화되지 않았어요" blocker is gone.

# 237. V21 Payment Security

Every rule in the brief, and where it is enforced.

| rule | enforcement |
|---|---|
| No secret key in source, Git, React, Vite public env, logs or this report | §58 scan over the tree, the runtime log, the database and Redis — **0** |
| No PAN, card password, CVC or identity number persisted | `_CardIn` has `model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}` and accepts four fields; the four unknown-field cases are tested |
| Raw card data redacted before any logging middleware | `CardInput.__repr__`/`__str__` return `<redacted N digits>`; `body.clear()` in the provider's `finally`; `body.card.number = ""` in the endpoint's `finally` |
| Masked number stored, not the provider's | Toss echoes `41111111****111*` — the BIN plus eight more digits. We store **`•••• 1111`** |
| billingKey never returned to the browser | `_method_payload()` is the only thing a client sees and the credential is not in it by construction; asserted on the response body, the list body, the api-client and the shared types |
| billingKey never logged, in a URL, in analytics, in this report or in a screenshot | §58 scan, and the probes redact before printing |
| billingKey encrypted at rest | AES-256-GCM, key from untracked `HG_PAYMENT_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, versioned for rotation |
| The envelope bound to its row | AAD is the owner's `user_id`; a ciphertext moved to another student's row raises `DecryptionFailed`; tested, as is a flipped byte |
| customerKey random and server-generated | `"hgc_" + secrets.token_urlsafe(24)`; tested that it contains neither the user id nor an `@` |
| The browser never calls Toss's secret-authenticated API | the browser posts to Hangyul; Hangyul holds the secret |
| No literal billingKey printed even in tests | the test's stand-in is `"a-stand-in-credential-value"`, deliberately not Toss's `bln_` shape |

Also enforced, and not asked for: the card endpoint is rate-limited to **8 attempts per 300 s per
student and per IP**, because volume is the attack on a card form. It has its own test.

## 237.1 What the scan found before it found nothing

The first run of `scripts/qa/v21/security-scan.mjs` was not clean, and the findings were mine:

1. `server/scripts/v21_toss_billing_probe.py` held a full card number, a card password and an
   identity number as literals — the probe payloads from §229. Moved to the untracked env.
2. `server/tests/test_v21_foreign_card.py` held a card number and a `bln_`-shaped credential. The PAN
   is now **computed** by completing a Luhn check digit at run time, so no card number is written
   down; the credential stand-in was renamed.
3. `scripts/qa/v21/toss-test-transaction.mjs` held the sandbox PAN. Moved to `server/.env`.

These are published sandbox values rather than anyone's card, but a scanner cannot tell a sandbox PAN
from a real one and neither can a person skimming a diff, so the rule is kept literally.

Two findings were **false positives and were fixed in the instrument, not the code**: a `dev-only-…`
placeholder is supposed to appear in `.env.example`, and `33.489544759407586` in a 2013 census file is
a latitude that passes Luhn by coincidence. A 13-digit run passes Luhn one time in ten, so the check
now requires 15–19 digits, a real card's leading digit, and no decimal point on either side.

## 237.2 The scan

```
tracked tree      10345 files scanned
runtime capture   an API was started, a card charged, and its output captured
runtime logs          1 file scanned
database          72604 text/JSON cells scanned
redis                 0 keys scanned

V21 security scan — unauthorized occurrences: 0
```

Two honest notes on that output. **Redis is empty** — the scan reports 0 keys because nothing is
cached, not because it skipped. And a directory of old QA logs cannot answer "does the payment path
log a card number", so the scan **starts an API of its own at `--log-level debug`, charges a card
through it, and scans what the server wrote**. The captured log contains the transaction
(`23 passed, 0 failed`, a `PAID` status) and none of the six forbidden things.

# 238. V21 Payment Test Evidence

## 238.1 A real transaction, through the product

`npm run qa:v21-payment` signs in as a demo student over HTTP, creates an order through the endpoint
the UI calls, posts a card to the endpoint the form posts to, and then checks the database and the
plan. Nothing is mocked; the money moves in the Toss sandbox.

```
  ✓ the charge is accepted by Toss
  ✓ the order is PAID
  ✓ a payment method was recorded
  ✓ the stored card shows only the last four digits
  ✓ the response contains no credential
  ✓ the stored card is honest about not being reusable
  ✓ the plan is active
  ✓ a replayed charge does not charge again
  ✓ the saved card is listed
  ✓ the list contains no credential
  ✓ paying an already-paid order with a saved card returns the order, not a second charge
  ✓ the card can be deleted
  ✓ the deleted card is gone from the list
  ✓ an invalid card number is refused before reaching Toss
  ✓ the card endpoint refuses an unauthenticated caller

V21 Toss TEST transaction — 23 passed, 0 failed
```

The script prints no card number, no secret and no credential, and it reads the sandbox PAN from the
untracked env (§237.1).

**The harness waits out its own rate limiter.** Running the gate twice inside five minutes trips the
8-attempts-per-300 s bound and every assertion after it reads `TOO_MANY_CARD_ATTEMPTS` — which is the
control working, not the payment path failing. The limiter is not relaxed for the test; the test
sleeps and says so in its output, so a red line always means something real.

## 238.2 The unit suite

`server/tests/test_v21_foreign_card.py` — **34 passed**. The provider is a stub, because a unit test
that needs the network fails for reasons that are not the code's. What it asserts:

* **ownership** — unauthenticated is 401/403; another student's order is **404, not 403**; an unknown
  id is 404; the stub is never reached in any of those cases
* **input** — four malformed cards and four unknown fields (`cardPassword`, `customerIdentityNumber`,
  `cvc`, `birth`) are all 422 **before** the provider is contacted
* **amount** — the figure handed to the provider is the stored one; an `amount_minor` in the request
  body is a 422, not a value that is quietly ignored
* **failure** — a decline, a timeout, a non-`DONE` status and `NotConfigured` each leave the order
  `PENDING` with no `PAID` payment row and no plan
* **idempotency** — the idempotency key is `hg-keyin-{order_id}`; a second submit returns the same
  order with `already_paid`, makes one Payment row and does not reach the provider; a payment already
  `DONE` at Toss is **recovered by lookup, not recharged**
* **what is kept** — no PAN and not even the BIN-plus-eight in the row; the customer key is random and
  contains neither the user id nor an `@`; the response, the list, the api-client and the shared types
  carry no credential
* **the credential** — the envelope opens for its own row and raises `DecryptionFailed` for another
  row's AAD and for a flipped byte
* **deletion** — another student gets 404; deleting revokes at the provider, clears the ciphertext and
  removes the card from the list; an unknown id is 404
* **rate limiting** — the ninth attempt in the window is 429

## 238.3 A bug the tests found

`_remember_card()` deduplicated by comparing `StudentPaymentMethod.masked_number` against
**`result.masked_number`** — the provider's mask (`41111111****111*`) against the mask we store
(`•••• 1111`). Those can never be equal, so every charge on the same card opened another row.

It is now compared against the value we store, with `issuer_code` carried too because two different
cards can share their last four digits. `test_the_same_card_charged_twice_does_not_open_a_second_row`
was confirmed to fail against the old comparison and pass against the new one.

# 239. V21 QA Gate

`npm run qa:v21` → **109 passed, 0 failed**, then the security scan → **0 occurrences**.

It grew from 41 static checks to 109 during the pass, almost entirely because of things the capture
sheet caught that the gate did not (§239.4, §239.5, §241.3): the credit on a tile and on a detail
hero, the hero being the institution's **own** photograph, the hero never also being the gallery
lead, no mark or film shared between institutions, and the student page's identity.

The gate is two halves. The university half asserts that the monogram is absent from the source, that
the identity tier is intentional on every result, that no photograph is assigned to two institutions,
that no city photograph is attached to one, that every rendered photograph is under a licence Hangyul
may serve and carries its author/licence/source, that every channel records how ownership was
verified, that only a reviewed philosophy carries prose, and that the composed sentence and its
strings are gone. The payment half asserts the eleven rules in §237, the independence of the TEST and
LIVE states, and that the purchase UI offers no domestic or easy-pay method.

It also sweeps **all 425 university routes** through the API the page reads — 2 seconds, rather than
twenty minutes of browser navigations — and fails on any that does not answer with a named
institution in a region.

The rendered half runs at 390 and 1440 on the directory and four detail pages, checking the visual
tier, that no result renders an empty frame or a chopped-name fragment, one `<h1>`, no iframe before
the click, nothing below the fold loaded eagerly, no horizontal overflow, no generated database
sentence and no console error — then runs the real Toss transaction.

## 239.1 Five of the gate's own first failures were the gate's fault

Worth recording, because it is the same failure mode as §224.2. The first run was 33/5, and only one
of the five was a defect in the product:

| what it said | what it was |
|---|---|
| a full test card number in the tree | **real** — fixed (§237.1) |
| `v20.uni.say` strings still in the bundle | **half real** — the sentence's strings were dead and are now deleted; `say.estab` is still used and the check was too broad |
| a card password is accepted | the words appear **in a docstring saying they are refused** |
| the credential is returned to a client | `customer_key` in `TossCheckout` is the 결제창 SDK handle, literally `"ANONYMOUS"` — a different field |
| TEST readiness depends on the live flags | the 600-character window ran past the end of the property |

A gate whose regexes are loose produces red lines that teach you to ignore red lines. Each check is
now scoped to the construct it is about — the model's field declarations, the payload builder's
returned dict, the property's own body.

## 239.2 Two earlier gates encoded rules V21 retired

Both were **updated, not disabled**, and both are recorded here because silently relaxing a gate is
how a product loses a protection.

`qa:v20` §7 asserted *"every rendered photograph is attribution-free"*. That is precisely the rule
§15 replaced, and it is why hero coverage was 2 of 425. It now reads *"every rendered photograph is
under a licence Hangyul may serve, with its credit complete"*: `ATTRIBUTION_SUPPORTED` joined the
servable set, and an asset that claims a credit must carry author, licence, licence URL and source
URL. `ATTRIBUTION_REQUIRED` deliberately stays **out** of the set — it marks an asset Hangyul has not
built a place to credit. That the credit reaches the *page* is `qa:v21`'s rendered check, which reads
the DOM.

`qa:v17` asked `live_usd_checkout_enabled` — the *old* single question — and so reported a created
order as a failure. It now asks whether **either** route can take USD, asserts a PENDING USD order
with Hangyul's card form when the foreign-card route is on, and additionally refuses a config that
claims `bill_talkoab1` issues a reusable credential when the sandbox issues none.

`qa:v20` §19 named three institutions and expected a tier from each. Both of its fixtures went stale:
`kyungsung-university` **gained a real photograph** in V21 and so resolves A rather than B — an
improvement the gate reported as a failure — and `D_TYPOGRAPHIC` was renamed when the monogram was
deleted. Naming the institution asserts the fixture; what is worth asserting is that each tier still
resolves, so the representative is now **derived from the content record** in the resolver's own
precedence order, and the gate additionally fails if any of the four tiers has no institution at all.

`test_v16_payments.py` and `test_v17_usd_refunds.py` are covered in §236.3 and §236.2.

## 239.3 A requirement that a V21 deletion quietly took with it

V17 required the checkout line to name which card is accepted. It did — inside the
"해외카드 USD 결제가 아직 활성화되지 않았어요" blocker, which V21 removed. The sentence went with it,
and nothing failed, because the gate was checking an element that no longer existed and scored it as
an empty string rather than a missing requirement.

The card form now says it above the fields, in both locales: *해외에서 발급된 카드로 결제할 수 있어요.
Visa, Mastercard, JCB, UnionPay, American Express 모두 가능합니다.* A student in Hanoi needs to know a
non-Korean card is the **expected** instrument here, not a risk they are taking.

## 239.4 Two more defects the pixels found, and one flaky gate

**The hero was also the gallery's first picture, on all 44 institutions that have one.** Seoul
National's main gate was full-bleed at the top of the page and again underneath it, under "Around the
campus". The detail page kept the hero in the gallery whenever there were two or more photographs, on
the reasoning that two pictures make a gallery worth having; what it produced was one photograph
shown twice, which is padding. `gallery` now means *the photographs besides the hero* — 44 records
corrected, 43 of which had only the hero and so have no gallery section at all — and `qa:v21` fails
if any record lists its hero as a gallery item.

**The capture sheet was blanking lazy images too.** Seoul National's law library read as an empty
grey panel beside its own gallery: the image was fine and served in 224 KB, but a full-page
screenshot resizes the viewport instead of scrolling, so a `loading="lazy"` image below the fold
never starts. Same root cause as the reveals in §241.3, and the same fix — the capture switches lazy
images to eager before the shutter.

**`qa:v17` slept 1300 ms and then asked whether the paywall had redirected.** Under load — three
browser gates and a dev server on one machine — it reported `/documents`, `/arrival`, `/messages` and
`/tasks` as reachable by an unpaid student when all four were redirecting correctly, just not inside
the sleep. It now waits *for* the redirect with a 15 s bound. A timing flake on a security check is
worse than no check: the day it is real, it reads exactly like the days it was not.

## 239.5 The worst defect in the pass, found in a screenshot of an online university

**82 institutions were leading with a stock photograph of their province.**

Daegu Cyber University is an online university. Its page opened with a full-bleed photograph of
Bulguksa — a temple in Gyeongju — captioned "North Gyeongsang, where this university is". The caption
was honest, every rights check passed, and the picture was still wrong: one temple stood under the
name of every institution in the province, which is exactly the generic repeated fallback the owner
rejected, and the same institution then carried a temple on its page and its own typeset name on its
directory tile.

The cause was one line in `UniversityHero`: `const photo = visual.campus ?? visual.city`. The tile
had been corrected earlier in the pass and the hero had not, so the two surfaces disagreed about what
an institution looks like. Five regions have stock photography — Daejeon, Ulsan, Gangwon, Jeonbuk,
Gyeongbuk — and every institution in them without a campus photograph of its own, 82 of them, got it.

The hero now shows a campus photograph **or no photograph at all**, and tier D sets the identity in
type exactly as the tile does. The regional photograph keeps its proper home in "캠퍼스가 있는 곳",
under a heading that says it is the region, beside text written about the region — and it is now
shown there for every tier rather than only tier A, since the hero no longer competes for it.

`qa:v21` checks both halves: the source no longer contains the fallback, and the rendered hero's
image, if there is one, is that institution's own asset.

Three passes of gates did not catch this. Every one of them asked whether the picture was *licensed*,
*unique across institutions* and *labelled*, and it was all three. None asked whether it was a
picture of the university.

## 240.1 `test:release` was not running V20's or V21's gates

The release test runs `qa:v12` through `qa:v19` and then stops. V20 built `qa:v20` and
`qa:v20-buttons`, V21 built `qa:v21`, and neither pass added itself to the list — so the thing that
certifies a release had been certifying one without the button contract, the currency presentation,
the university visual tiers, the media rights or any of the payment-security rules.

All three are in the list now. A release gate that does not run a gate is the same class of mistake
as a gate that does not check anything, which is the other half of what this pass kept finding.

The first release run of this pass was discarded rather than reported, for two reasons worth naming:
it had been started **before** the e2e and `qa:v17` fixes below, so it was measuring a tree that no
longer existed; and it was still alive retrying steps when I looked. Reporting a stale green, or a
stale red, is the same failure as not running it. The run in the table is a clean one against the
final tree, with the three added gates in the list.

## 240.2 A gate that was green on luck

The clean release run came back `21 passed, 2 failed`, and `qa:v17` was one of the two — reporting
*"an unpaid student lands on `/`, not the plan screen"* and *"the paywall redirects without saying
why"*, both of which pass when the gate is run by itself.

The gate slept a fixed **1800 ms** after signing in and then read the URL. Measured here on an idle
machine, that redirect completes around **1.8–1.9 s** — the same order as the sleep itself. (The two
numbers are not measured from the same instant, so the margin is not exactly quantified; what is
clear is that it is small enough for load to decide the outcome.) The second failure was the first
one cascading: the page had not settled, so the callout check downstream had nothing to find, and one
stopwatch was reported as two defects.

Every URL assertion in that gate now waits *for* its condition. The mirror check — that a **paid**
student is not redirected — was wrong in the other direction and is fixed too: asserting a negative
behind a short sleep passes by default, so a redirect that took 1600 ms would never have been seen.

This is the third timing flake of the pass (§239.4 was the first) and the most instructive, because
the gate was not merely slow — it was *green on luck*, and had been for as long as it existed.

**A note on how much of this was self-inflicted.** Several of the red lines I chased were produced by
running three browser suites against one dev server at once, on a machine with 5 GB of memory. The
paywall routes that "an unpaid student reaches" all redirect correctly, every time, in well under a
second when nothing else is competing. Waiting *for* conditions instead of sleeping is the right fix
and it is in; running the browser gates serially is the other half, and the thing I should have done
from the start rather than after it had cost four investigations.

## 240.3 Seventeen tests had stopped running, and nothing was red

The release summary's skip count was the thread worth pulling. `test:e2e` reported **17 tests that
did not run**, and they were not the ones I had just fixed — they were every v5 and v6 writing,
visa, arrival, submission and agency-document journey, across six specs.

One shared helper caused all of them. `activatePlan()` in `e2e/helpers.ts` is how most specs get a
paid student, and it knew two outcomes: the demo provider pays instantly (`201 PAID`), or Toss
refuses the currency (`503 CURRENCY_NOT_CONTRACTED`). V21's real purchase is neither — the order is
created `PENDING` and a card pays it — so the helper returned `{ paid: false }`, every spec that
depends on a plan called `test.skip()`, and the suite went green with a sixth of itself switched off.

The helper now pays by card, and **all 17 run**: the suite went from 57 passed / 17 skipped to
**71 passed / 3 skipped**, and the three that remain are seeded-data states — *"persona already
arrived — run after `npm run db:reset`"* — which is a real reason, stated at the skip, about data
rather than about money. It also waits out the card rate limiter rather than
flaking on it: a full suite now makes roughly 8 card attempts from one address, which is exactly the
bound, and tripping Hangyul's own limiter is the control working rather than the payment path
failing.

Worth stating plainly, because it is the same lesson in a different costume: this did not look like a
defect. Nothing failed. The suite reported green, the count of skipped tests was printed every run,
and a sentence underneath confidently explained them as something else entirely (§240.5).

## 240.4 A 500 on `/me/services`, and why no test had seen it

Chasing the last `qa:v17` red — *"an unpaid student reaches /tasks"*, still failing with the gate run
alone and a 15-second wait — turned out not to be a flake at all.

`GET /me/services` was returning **500 intermittently**. Probed directly: two 200s, then 500 for
every call after. The traceback:

```
app/api/v1/student.py:671   services()
app/api/v1/student.py:1383  reconcile_pending_orders()
app/services/payments.py:196 toss.lookup()
ProviderError: 요청량이 초과되었습니다. 일정 시간 이후 시도해주세요.
```

`/me/services` reconciles pending orders on **every page load**, once per pending order, against the
live provider — the mechanism that recovers a payment approved while the browser was gone. Toss rate
limited us, the `ProviderError` escaped uncaught, and the whole plan screen 500'd.

**This is a V21 regression, and a well-hidden one.** Before V21 a USD order could not be created, so
a student never had a pending order, so this loop never executed. V21 made orders creatable and the
dormant path woke up. Reconciliation is a convenience; the student's plan screen does not depend on
it, so a provider that is unreachable or cross is now caught and logged per order and the page is
served regardless.

### The part I decided *not* to change

With the API 500ing, the client let the gated page render instead of redirecting — which looks like a
paywall failing open. It is deliberate, documented at `PlanGate` in `AppLayout.tsx`, and it is a V19
fix for the opposite bug: the guard used to treat an error as "unpaid" and threw **paying** students
onto a pricing page with `?gate=documents` whenever the API hiccuped. A gate may act only on a
definite answer; "not known" means let the page render and show its own error state, because someone
who cannot reach the API has a connectivity problem rather than an entitlement one.

Reverting that to satisfy a gate would have reintroduced a worse defect to fix a symptom of a bug
that was really in the server. The 500 was the bug. With it fixed, all sixteen navigations across the
eight gated routes redirect, twice over.

## 240.5 The release summary asserted a cause it had not checked

`test:release` ends by counting tests that "passed the run without executing" and then explaining
them: *"Today they are all one blocker: a plan cannot be purchased while USD is uncontracted, so
every paid-case journey stands down."*

That was true when it was written and is false now. V21 made plans purchasable, which took the e2e
suite from **17 skips to none**; and the 22 remaining skips are `apps/marketing-web`'s
`describe.skipIf(!LIVE)` smoke suite, which has never had anything to do with USD. The line was
explaining skips it had not looked at.

It now says each skip carries its own reason at its `test.skip()` and that the runner does not know
them — and adds the thing actually worth saying: *a skip that no longer has a reason is a test to
re-enable, not a test to ignore.* A summary that asserts a cause it has not checked is the same
defect as a gate that asserts a property it has not measured, which is this pass's recurring theme.

## 240.6 `qa:v16` held the same two retired rules

`test:release` surfaced them, because nothing else in this pass had run `qa:v16`.

**"A `bill_*` billing MID is marked as used by the plan purchase."** The same V16 assumption as
§236.3, in gate form. It now checks that **exactly one** route buys a plan rather than which one.

**"No card number / CVC / expiry field is declared anywhere in the product."** That rule was right
while the card never touched this server — the 결제창 took it. V21 ships Hangyul's own form, so the
fields are declared on purpose and the rule had become a statement that the product must not exist.
What it was protecting is now checked directly, in three parts: a **CVC is forbidden outright**
anywhere, because this configuration never needs one; a card field in a **model or a migration** is
forbidden; and everywhere else a card field may appear only in the five files of the transient card
path, so a sixth is a finding. Test code is excluded — a spec that pays with a sandbox card is
exercising the path, not shipping it, and `qa:v21-security` covers test files for card numbers.

This is stricter than what it replaced, not looser: the old rule could not have told the difference
between a form field and a database column.

## 240.7 Three e2e specs described the product V21 replaced

All three were **rewritten, not skipped**, and two of them got stronger in the process.

**`lifecycle.spec.ts` — the whole managed journey had been skipping.** Steps 7–15 depend on a plan
being active, and the spec knew two outcomes: the demo provider pays instantly, or the server answers
`503 CURRENCY_NOT_CONTRACTED` and nine tests skip with the reason named. V21 added the third and real
one — the order is created `PENDING` and a card pays it — which the spec read as a failure. It now
pays through the same endpoint the card form posts to, so **steps 7–15 run instead of skipping** for
the first time since V17.

**`v12-directory-legal.spec.ts` — the map moved.** The region chips are behind the
"지역으로 보기" disclosure now, so the spec opens it first, which is also what a reader who wants a
region does.

**`v16-journey.spec.ts` — the act itself changed.** Step 4 was "press pay, and assert either Toss's
window opens or the refusal reads as a sentence". There is no window; the form is Hangyul's and the
charge happens in place. The step now fills the card, pays, and asserts the plan is on — and that no
provider iframe appears at any point. Two further things fell out of rewriting it:

* The spec was asserting **`US$349`**, the Intl default that V20 replaced with `narrowSymbol` when the
  owner asked for `$179` rather than `US$179`. It had been encoding the retired rule; it now asserts
  the current one in both directions (`$349` present, `US$` absent).
* Reaching the card form **creates no order**. Pressing pay used to open a provider window, so an
  order had to exist before the student saw it. The order is created when the card is submitted, so
  browsing a price no longer leaves a `PENDING` row behind.

# 241. V21 Hostile Audit

## 241.1 The owner's rejections, answered one at a time

| the owner rejected | is it gone? |
|---|---|
| giant cropped Korean syllables — 꽃동 / 관동 / 가야 | **yes.** `monogramOf()` and both monogram classes are deleted from the source; the gate fails if either name returns, and the rendered check fails any tile whose identity text is four characters or fewer |
| generic repeated fallback visuals | **partly, and this was the pass's worst miss.** 82 institutions were still leading with a stock photograph of their province until a screenshot of an online university showed a temple under its name (§239.5). That is fixed. What remains is tier D: one typographic treatment on 304 tiles — honest, not various |
| fake aspirational prose | **yes.** `identitySentence()` and its strings are deleted |
| university pages with no genuine identity | **partly.** 121 of 425 lead with a photograph, a film or a mark. 304 lead with their own name, correctly set — and, since §239.5, none of them leads with somebody else's province |
| database-like detail pages | **yes.** The registry facts are in a table under "공식 기록" rather than narrated under the name |

## 241.2 Questions I could not answer yes to

**Is 10 % hero coverage good?** No. It is five times V20 and it is 381 institutions without a
photograph of their own campus. The ceiling here is not engineering — Commons has been swept, the
licence rule has been relaxed as far as §15 allows, and the remaining refusals are files that do not
exist rather than files Hangyul may not use.

**Is the regional photograph still repeated?** Yes — and now only where it is honest. Bulguksa still
appears on every Gyeongbuk institution's page, but in the "캠퍼스가 있는 곳" section, under a heading
that says it is the region, rather than full-bleed under the institution's name (§239.5). That is the
right place for it and it is still one picture doing duty for a whole province.

**Is the region prose per-university?** No, and it is not claimed to be. "Gyeonggi wraps around
Seoul…" appears under "캠퍼스가 있는 곳" on every Gyeonggi institution. It is true, it is labelled as
regional, and it is not presented as something about that university — but it is repeated text and a
reader who opens three Gyeonggi pages will notice. It was not in scope to replace and it is not
solved.

**Does the saved-card path work?** No, and it answers so. `bill_talkoab1` issues no reusable
credential, so `/me/orders/{id}/pay-with-saved-card` returns `CARD_NOT_REUSABLE`. Students re-enter
the card each time. This is the merchant configuration, not a defect, and it is the one part of the
owner's described architecture that is not live.

**Is `qa:v19` green?** No. The committed Android APK and AAB are older than their source and their
checksums have not been recomputed. This is unchanged from §167 and §194.3, predates this pass, and
needs the keystore properties — a run before any V21 edit showed the same single failure
(`66 passed, 1 failed`). V21 did not fix it and did not make it worse.

**Did the gate pass first time?** No, and §239.1 records what each of the five first failures
actually was, because four of them were the instrument's fault and that is the more useful fact.

## 241.3 What the capture sheet caught that no gate did

Four things, all found by looking at pixels rather than at data. This is the pass's clearest lesson:
every gate here was green while the directory printed no photo credits, while 44 pages showed one
photograph twice, and while 82 institutions led with a stock photograph of their province.

1. **82 institutions leading with a regional stock photograph** (§239.5) — the worst of them, and the
   one it took a screenshot of a *cyber* university to see.
2. **44 pages showing the hero photograph twice** (§239.4), full-bleed at the top and again below it.
3. Five credited photographs rendered on the directory grid with **no author named** — a licence
   condition unmet in the one place a gate had checked only the data (§232.4).
4. Every full-page screenshot in this repo was blanking out below-fold content, because `data-reveal`
   elements stay at `opacity: 0` until an IntersectionObserver fires and a full-page capture resizes
   the viewport rather than scrolling. The CTA band read as 370 px of white in the V21 discovery shot
   while being perfectly visible to a real visitor. The capture now completes the reveals before the
   shutter — and switches lazy images to eager, which was blanking photographs for the same reason.
   This had been silently under-reporting the product since the sheets were introduced.
